title: The Heroes: Greek Fairy Tales
author: Charles Kingsley
original_title: The Heroes; Or, Greek Fairy Tales for My Children

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: PREFACE

translation.en: [Preface]
translation.kr: [머리말]

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: MY DEAR CHILDREN,

translation.en: My dear children,
translation.kr: 사랑하는 나의 아이들에게,

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: Some of you have heard already of the old Greeks; and all of you, as you grow up, will hear more and more of them.  Those of you who are boys will, perhaps, spend a great deal of time in reading Greek books; and the girls, though they may not learn Greek, will be sure to come across a great many stories taken from Greek history, and to see, I may say every day, things which we should not have had if it had not been for these old Greeks.  You can hardly find a well-written book which has not in it Greek names, and words, and proverbs; you cannot walk through a great town without passing Greek buildings; you cannot go into a well-furnished room without seeing Greek statues and ornaments, even Greek patterns of furniture and paper; so strangely have these old Greeks left their mark behind them upon this modern world in which we now live.  And as you grow up, and read more and more, you will find that we owe to these old Greeks the beginners of all our mathematics and geometry—that is, the science and knowledge of numbers, and of the shapes of things, and of the forces which make things move and stand at rest; and the beginnings of our geography and astronomy; and of our laws, and freedom, and politics—that is, the science of how to rule a country, and make it peaceful and strong.  And we owe to them, too, the beginning of our logic—that is, the study of words and of reasoning; and of our metaphysics—that is, the study of our own thoughts and souls.  And last of all, they made their language so beautiful that foreigners used to take to it instead of their own; and at last Greek became the common language of educated people all over the old world, from Persia and Egypt even to Spain and Britain.  And therefore it was that the New Testament was written in Greek, that it might be read and understood by all the nations of the Roman empire; so that, next to the Jews, and the Bible which the Jews handed down to us, we owe more to these old Greeks than to any people upon earth.

translation.en: Some of you have already heard of the ancient Greeks.
translation.kr: 여러분 중 몇몇은 이미 고대 그리스인들에 대해 들어보았을 것입니다.

translation.en: As you grow up, you will hear much more about them.
translation.kr: 여러분이 자라면서 그들에 대해 훨씬 더 많은 것을 듣게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: The boys among you might spend a great deal of time reading Greek books.
translation.kr: 소년들은 아마도 그리스 책을 읽는 데 많은 시간을 보낼지도 모릅니다.

translation.en: The girls may not learn the Greek language, but you will certainly come across many stories from Greek history.
translation.kr: 소녀들은 그리스어를 배우지 않을 수도 있지만, 틀림없이 그리스 역사의 많은 이야기들을 접하게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: In fact, you will see things every day that we wouldn't have without these ancient Greeks.
translation.kr: 사실, 여러분은 고대 그리스인들이 없었다면 존재하지 않았을 것들을 매일 보게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: You can hardly find a well-written book that doesn't include Greek names, words, or proverbs.
translation.kr: 그리스의 이름이나 단어, 혹은 속담이 포함되지 않은 잘 쓰인 책을 찾기란 거의 불가능합니다.

translation.en: You can't walk through a large city without passing buildings designed in the Greek style.
translation.kr: 큰 도시를 걷다 보면 그리스 양식으로 설계된 건물들을 지나치지 않을 수 없습니다.

translation.en: You can't enter a well-furnished room without seeing Greek statues, ornaments, or even furniture patterns.
translation.kr: 잘 꾸며진 방에 들어가면 그리스 조각상이나 장식품, 심지어 가구의 무늬라도 반드시 보게 됩니다.

translation.en: These ancient people have left a remarkable, lasting mark on our modern world.
translation.kr: 이 고대 사람들은 우리가 사는 현대 세계에 놀랍고도 영구적인 자취를 남겼습니다.

translation.en: As you grow and read more, you'll discover just how much we owe them.
translation.kr: 여러분이 자라서 더 많은 책을 읽게 되면, 우리가 그들에게 얼마나 많은 빚을 지고 있는지 깨닫게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: They laid the foundation for our mathematics and geometry—the study of numbers, shapes, and the forces that move objects.
translation.kr: 그들은 숫자와 모양, 그리고 사물을 움직이는 힘을 연구하는 학문인 수학과 기하학의 기초를 다졌습니다.

translation.en: They started our sciences of geography and astronomy.
translation.kr: 그들은 지리학과 천문학이라는 과학을 시작했습니다.

translation.en: They also shaped our ideas of law, freedom, and politics, which teach us how to govern a peaceful and strong country.
translation.kr: 또한 평화롭고 강한 나라를 다스리는 방법을 가르쳐 주는 법, 자유, 정치에 대한 우리의 개념도 형성했습니다.

translation.en: We even owe them our logic, the study of reasoning and words, and our metaphysics, the study of our own thoughts and souls.
translation.kr: 심지어 추론과 언어를 연구하는 논리학과, 우리 자신의 생각과 영혼을 연구하는 형이상학 역시 그들의 덕분입니다.

translation.en: Finally, they made their language so beautiful that foreigners often preferred it to their own.
translation.kr: 마지막으로, 그들은 자신들의 언어를 매우 아름답게 가꾸어 외국인들조차 모국어보다 그것을 더 선호할 정도였습니다.

translation.en: Greek eventually became the common language of educated people across the ancient world, stretching from Persia and Egypt all the way to Spain and Britain.
translation.kr: 그리스어는 결국 페르시아와 이집트에서부터 스페인과 브리튼에 이르기까지 고대 세계 전역에 걸쳐 교육받은 사람들의 공용어가 되었습니다.

translation.en: Because of this, the New Testament was written in Greek so that people across the entire Roman Empire could read and understand it.
translation.kr: 이러한 이유로, 로마 제국 전역의 사람들이 읽고 이해할 수 있도록 신약성경은 그리스어로 쓰였습니다.

translation.en: Aside from the Jewish people and the Bible they passed down to us, we owe more to the ancient Greeks than to anyone else on earth.
translation.kr: 유대인들과 그들이 우리에게 전해준 성경을 제외한다면, 우리는 세상 그 누구보다도 고대 그리스인들에게 더 많은 것을 빚지고 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: Now you must remember one thing—that ‘Greeks’ was not their real name. They called themselves always ‘Hellens,’ but the Romans miscalled them Greeks; and we have taken that wrong name from the Romans—it would take a long time to tell you why.  They were made up of many tribes and many small separate states; and when you hear in this book of Minuai, and Athenians, and other such names, you must remember that they were all different tribes and peoples of the one great Hellen race, who lived in what we now call Greece, in the islands of the Archipelago, and along the coast of Asia Minor (Ionia, as they call it), from the Hellespont to Rhodes, and had afterwards colonies and cities in Sicily, and South Italy (which was called Great Greece), and along the shores of the Black Sea at Sinope, and Kertch, and at Sevastopol.  And after that, again, they spread under Alexander the Great, and conquered Egypt, and Syria, and Persia, and the whole East.  But that was many hundred years after my stories; for then there were no Greeks on the Black Sea shores, nor in Sicily, or Italy, or anywhere but in Greece and in Ionia.  And if you are puzzled by the names of places in this book, you must take the maps and find them out.  It will be a pleasanter way of learning geography than out of a dull lesson-book.

translation.en: You must remember one important thing: 'Greeks' was not their real name.
translation.kr: 여러분은 한 가지 중요한 사실을 기억해야 합니다. '그리스인'은 그들의 진짜 이름이 아니었습니다.

translation.en: They always called themselves 'Hellens.
translation.kr: 그들은 언제나 스스로를 '헬렌인'이라고 불렀습니다.

translation.en: The Romans misnamed them Greeks, and we adopted that incorrect name from the Romans.
translation.kr: 로마인들이 그들을 그리스인이라고 잘못 불렀고, 우리는 로마인들로부터 그 잘못된 이름을 받아들인 것입니다.

translation.en: It would take a long time to explain exactly why.
translation.kr: 정확히 그 이유를 설명하려면 아주 오랜 시간이 걸릴 것입니다.

translation.en: The Hellens were made up of many different tribes and small, independent states.
translation.kr: 헬렌인들은 여러 다양한 부족과 작고 독립적인 국가들로 이루어져 있었습니다.

translation.en: When you read in this book about the Minuai, the Athenians, and others, remember that they were all part of the one great Hellen race.
translation.kr: 이 책에서 미누아이나 아테네인 등에 대해 읽게 될 때, 그들이 모두 하나의 위대한 헬렌 민족의 일부였다는 것을 기억하십시오.

translation.en: They lived in the area we now call Greece, scattered across the islands of the Aegean Sea, and along the coast of Asia Minor (which they called Ionia), from the Hellespont to the island of Rhodes.
translation.kr: 그들은 오늘날 우리가 그리스라 부르는 지역에 살았으며, 에게해의 여러 섬들과 헬레스폰트에서 로도스 섬에 이르는 소아시아 연안(그들은 이오니아라 불렀습니다)에 흩어져 살았습니다.

translation.en: Later, they built colonies and cities in Sicily and Southern Italy, a region known as Great Greece.
translation.kr: 훗날 그들은 대그리스라 불리는 시칠리아와 남이탈리아 지역에 식민지와 도시들을 건설했습니다.

translation.en: They even settled along the shores of the Black Sea at places like Sinope, Kerch, and Sevastopol.
translation.kr: 심지어 그들은 시노페, 케르치, 세바스토폴 같은 흑해 연안에도 정착했습니다.

translation.en: Centuries later, they spread under the rule of Alexander the Great, conquering Egypt, Syria, Persia, and the entire East.
translation.kr: 수백 년이 흐른 후, 그들은 알렉산더 대왕의 지배 아래 퍼져나가 이집트, 시리아, 페르시아, 그리고 동방 전체를 정복했습니다.

translation.en: But all of that happened hundreds of years after my stories take place.
translation.kr: 하지만 이 모든 일은 제 이야기들이 일어난 지 수백 년 뒤의 일입니다.

translation.en: In the time of these tales, there were no Greeks on the Black Sea shores, in Sicily, in Italy, or anywhere outside of Greece and Ionia.
translation.kr: 이 이야기들이 펼쳐지던 시절에는 흑해 연안이나 시칠리아, 이탈리아, 혹은 그리스와 이오니아 밖 그 어디에도 그리스인들은 없었습니다.

translation.en: If you ever feel puzzled by the place names in this book, pull out a map and track them down.
translation.kr: 이 책에 나오는 지명들이 혼란스럽게 느껴진다면 지도를 꺼내어 찾아보십시오.

translation.en: It will be a much more pleasant way to learn geography than staring at a dull textbook.
translation.kr: 따분한 교과서를 들여다보는 것보다 훨씬 즐겁게 지리를 배우는 방법이 될 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: Now, I love these old Hellens heartily; and I should be very ungrateful to them if I did not, considering all that they have taught me; and they seem to me like brothers, though they have all been dead and gone many hundred years ago.  So as you must learn about them, whether you choose or not, I wish to be the first to introduce you to them, and to say, ‘Come hither, children, at this blessed Christmas time, when all God’s creatures should rejoice together, and bless Him who redeemed them all. Come and see old friends of mine, whom I knew long ere you were born. They are come to visit us at Christmas, out of the world where all live to God; and to tell you some of their old fairy tales, which they loved when they were young like you.’

translation.en: I love these ancient Hellens deeply.
translation.kr: 저는 이 고대 헬렌인들을 깊이 사랑합니다.

translation.en: I would be very ungrateful if I didn't, considering everything they have taught me.
translation.kr: 그들이 제게 가르쳐 준 모든 것을 생각하면, 그렇지 않는 것이 오히려 매우 배은망덕한 일일 것입니다.

translation.en: They feel like brothers to me, even though they died hundreds of years ago.
translation.kr: 비록 그들은 수백 년 전에 세상을 떠났지만, 제게는 마치 형제처럼 느껴집니다.

translation.en: Since you have to learn about them anyway, I want to be the first to introduce you.
translation.kr: 어차피 여러분도 그들에 대해 배워야 하니, 제가 가장 먼저 여러분에게 그들을 소개해 주고 싶습니다.

translation.en: I say to you, Come here, children, at this wonderful Christmas time.
translation.kr: 저는 이렇게 말하고 싶습니다. 이 놀라운 크리스마스 시기에 이리 오렴, 아이들아.

translation.en: It is a season when all of God’s creatures should rejoice together and bless Him who saved us all.
translation.kr: 지금은 하나님의 모든 피조물이 함께 기뻐하고, 우리 모두를 구원하신 그분을 축복해야 할 계절입니다.

translation.en: Come and meet my old friends.
translation.kr: 와서 저의 오랜 친구들을 만나보십시오.

translation.en: I knew them long before you were born.
translation.kr: 저는 여러분이 태어나기 훨씬 전부터 그들을 알고 있었답니다.

translation.en: They have come to visit us at Christmas from the eternal world.
translation.kr: 그들은 크리스마스를 맞아 영원한 세계에서 우리를 찾아왔습니다.

translation.en: They want to tell you some of the fairy tales they loved when they were young like you.
translation.kr: 그들은 여러분처럼 어렸을 때 사랑했던 몇 가지 옛날이야기를 들려주고 싶어 합니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: For nations begin at first by being children like you, though they are made up of grown men.  They are children at first like you—men and women with children’s hearts; frank, and affectionate, and full of trust, and teachable, and loving to see and learn all the wonders round them; and greedy also, too often, and passionate and silly, as children are.

translation.en: Nations begin as children, just like you, even though they are made up of grown adults.
translation.kr: 국가란 비록 다 자란 어른들로 이루어져 있지만, 여러분처럼 처음에는 아이들로서 시작됩니다.

translation.en: At first, they are men and women with the hearts of children.
translation.kr: 처음에 그들은 어린아이의 마음을 가진 남녀들입니다.

translation.en: They are open, affectionate, trusting, and eager to learn about all the wonders around them.
translation.kr: 그들은 마음이 열려 있고, 다정하고, 잘 믿으며, 주변의 모든 경이로운 것들을 배우고 싶어 합니다.

translation.en: Too often, they are also greedy, passionate, and silly, exactly as children can be.
translation.kr: 또한 그들은 아이들이 그럴 수 있듯 탐욕스럽고, 충동적이며, 어리석을 때도 너무나 많습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: Thus these old Greeks were teachable, and learnt from all the nations round.  From the Phoenicians they learnt shipbuilding, and some say letters beside; and from the Assyrians they learnt painting, and carving, and building in wood and stone; and from the Egyptians they learnt astronomy, and many things which you would not understand.  In this they were like our own forefathers the Northmen, of whom you love to hear, who, though they were wild and rough themselves, were humble, and glad to learn from every one.  Therefore God rewarded these Greeks, as He rewarded our forefathers, and made them wiser than the people who taught them in everything they learnt; for He loves to see men and children open-hearted, and willing to be taught; and to him who uses what he has got, He gives more and more day by day.  So these Greeks grew wise and powerful, and wrote poems which will live till the world’s end, which you must read for yourselves some day, in English at least, if not in Greek. And they learnt to carve statues, and build temples, which are still among the wonders of the world; and many another wondrous thing God taught them, for which we are the wiser this day.

translation.en: These ancient Greeks were eager to learn from all the nations around them.
translation.kr: 이 고대 그리스인들은 주변의 모든 국가들로부터 배우기를 열망했습니다.

translation.en: From the Phoenicians, they learned shipbuilding and perhaps the alphabet.
translation.kr: 그들은 페니키아인들로부터 배 만드는 법과 어쩌면 알파벳을 배웠을 것입니다.

translation.en: From the Assyrians, they learned painting, carving, and how to build with wood and stone.
translation.kr: 아시리아인들로부터는 그림 그리는 법, 조각하는 법, 그리고 나무와 돌로 건축하는 법을 배웠습니다.

translation.en: From the Egyptians, they learned astronomy and many other complex subjects.
translation.kr: 이집트인들로부터는 천문학과 그 밖의 많은 복잡한 학문들을 배웠습니다.

translation.en: In this way, they were like our own ancestors, the Northmen.
translation.kr: 이런 점에서 그들은 우리의 조상인 북유럽인들과 같았습니다.

translation.en: You love hearing about them.
translation.kr: 여러분은 그들에 대한 이야기를 듣는 것을 좋아하지요.

translation.en: Although the Northmen were wild and rough, they were humble and happy to learn from anyone.
translation.kr: 북유럽인들은 거칠고 투박했지만, 겸손하게 누구에게서든 기꺼이 배웠습니다.

translation.en: Because the Greeks were open-hearted and willing to be taught, God rewarded them just as He rewarded our ancestors.
translation.kr: 그리스인들은 열린 마음을 가지고 배우려 했기 때문에, 하나님은 우리 조상들에게 주셨던 것처럼 그들에게도 보상을 내려주셨습니다.

translation.en: He made them wiser than the very people who taught them.
translation.kr: 그분은 그들을 가르쳤던 사람들보다 그들을 더 지혜롭게 만드셨습니다.

translation.en: God loves to see men and children eager to learn.
translation.kr: 하나님은 어른들과 아이들이 배우기를 열망하는 모습을 보기 좋아하십니다.

translation.en: He always gives more to those who use what they already have.
translation.kr: 그분은 자신이 가진 것을 활용하는 자들에게 항상 더 많은 것을 주십니다.

translation.en: So the Greeks grew wise and powerful.
translation.kr: 그리하여 그리스인들은 지혜롭고 강력해졌습니다.

translation.en: They wrote poems that will last until the end of the world—poems you must read for yourselves one day, at least in English, if not in Greek.
translation.kr: 그들은 세상이 끝날 때까지 남을 시를 썼는데, 언젠가 여러분도 그리스어로는 아니더라도 최소한 영어로라도 직접 읽어보아야 할 시들입니다.

translation.en: They learned to carve statues and build temples that are still considered wonders of the world.
translation.kr: 그들은 조각상을 새기고 신전을 짓는 법을 배웠으며, 그것들은 오늘날까지도 세계의 불가사의로 여겨집니다.

translation.en: God taught them many other wondrous things, and we are still benefiting from that wisdom today.
translation.kr: 하나님은 그들에게 다른 많은 경이로운 것들을 가르쳐 주셨고, 우리는 오늘날에도 여전히 그 지혜의 혜택을 누리고 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: For you must not fancy, children, that because these old Greeks were heathens, therefore God did not care for them, and taught them nothing.

translation.en: You must not think, children, that just because these ancient Greeks were pagans, God did not care for them or teach them anything.
translation.kr: 아이들아, 이 고대 그리스인들이 이교도였다고 해서 하나님이 그들을 돌보지 않으셨다거나 아무것도 가르치지 않으셨다고 생각해서는 안 됩니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: The Bible tells us that it was not so, but that God’s mercy is over all His works, and that He understands the hearts of all people, and fashions all their works.  And St. Paul told these old Greeks in after times, when they had grown wicked and fallen low, that they ought to have known better, because they were God’s offspring, as their own poets had said; and that the good God had put them where they were, to seek the Lord, and feel after Him, and find Him, though He was not far from any one of them. And Clement of Alexandria, a great Father of the Church, who was as wise as he was good, said that God had sent down Philosophy to the Greeks from heaven, as He sent down the Gospel to the Jews.

translation.en: The Bible tells us otherwise.
translation.kr: 성경은 우리에게 그렇지 않다고 말합니다.

translation.en: It says that God's mercy covers all His creations, and that He understands the hearts of all people and shapes their work.
translation.kr: 하나님의 자비는 그분의 모든 피조물을 덮으며, 그분은 모든 사람의 마음을 이해하시고 그들의 일을 빚어내신다고 성경은 말합니다.

translation.en: Later, when the Greeks had grown wicked and fallen into decline, St.
translation.kr: 훗날 그리스인들이 악해지고 쇠퇴의 길을 걷게 되었을 때, 성(聖)

translation.en: Paul told them they should have known better.
translation.kr: 바울은 그들에게 그들이 더 잘 알았어야 했다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: After all, they were God's own children, just as their own poets had written.
translation.kr: 결국 그들 자신들의 시인들이 썼던 것처럼 그들은 하나님의 친자녀들이었기 때문입니다.

translation.en: The good God had placed them where they were so they could seek the Lord and find Him, for He was never far from any of them.
translation.kr: 선하신 하나님은 그들이 주님을 구하고 찾을 수 있도록 그들을 그 자리에 두셨습니다. 그분은 결코 그들 누구에게서도 멀리 계시지 않았기 때문입니다.

translation.en: Clement of Alexandria, a wise and good Father of the early Church, even said that God sent philosophy down from heaven to the Greeks, just as He sent the Gospel down to the Jewish people.
translation.kr: 초대 교회의 지혜롭고 선한 교부였던 알렉산드리아의 클레멘스는 하나님이 유대인들에게 복음을 내려주셨듯이 그리스인들에게는 하늘에서 철학을 내려주셨다고 말하기까지 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: For Jesus Christ, remember, is the Light who lights every man who comes into the world.  And no one can think a right thought, or feel a right feeling, or understand the real truth of anything in earth and heaven, unless the good Lord Jesus teaches him by His Spirit, which gives man understanding.

translation.en: Remember that Jesus Christ is the Light who guides everyone who comes into the world.
translation.kr: 예수 그리스도는 세상에 오는 모든 사람을 인도하시는 빛이라는 사실을 기억하십시오.

translation.en: No one can think a good thought, feel the right feeling, or understand the true nature of anything on earth or in heaven unless the good Lord Jesus teaches them through His Spirit.
translation.kr: 선하신 주 예수님이 그분의 성령을 통해 가르쳐 주시지 않는다면, 누구도 선한 생각을 하거나, 올바른 감정을 느끼거나, 하늘과 땅에 있는 어떤 것의 본질도 이해할 수 없습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: But these Greeks, as St. Paul told them, forgot what God had taught them, and, though they were God’s offspring, worshipped idols of wood and stone, and fell at last into sin and shame, and then, of course, into cowardice and slavery, till they perished out of that beautiful land which God had given them for so many years.

translation.en: However, as St.
translation.kr: 하지만 성(聖)

translation.en: Paul reminded them, these Greeks eventually forgot what God had taught them.
translation.kr: 바울이 그들에게 일깨워 주었듯이, 이 그리스인들은 결국 하나님이 그들에게 가르쳐 주신 것을 잊어버렸습니다.

translation.en: Even though they were God's children, they worshipped idols made of wood and stone.
translation.kr: 하나님의 자녀였음에도 불구하고 그들은 나무와 돌로 만든 우상을 숭배했습니다.

translation.en: They fell into sin, shame, cowardice, and slavery.
translation.kr: 그들은 죄악, 수치, 비겁함, 그리고 노예 상태로 전락했습니다.

translation.en: Ultimately, they were driven out of the beautiful land God had given them for so many years.
translation.kr: 결국 그들은 하나님께서 아주 오랫동안 그들에게 주셨던 아름다운 땅에서 쫓겨나고 말았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: For, like all nations who have left anything behind them, beside mere mounds of earth, they believed at first in the One True God who made all heaven and earth. But after a while, like all other nations, they began to worship other gods, or rather angels and spirits, who (so they fancied) lived about their land.  Zeus, the Father of gods and men (who was some dim remembrance of the blessed true God), and Hera his wife, and Phoebus Apollo the Sun-god, and Pallas Athené who taught men wisdom and useful arts, and Aphrodite the Queen of Beauty, and Poseidon the Ruler of the Sea, and Hephaistos the King of the Fire, who taught men to work in metals.  And they honoured the Gods of the Rivers, and the Nymph-maids, who they fancied lived in the caves, and the fountains, and the glens of the forest, and all beautiful wild places.  And they honoured the Erinnues, the dreadful sisters, who, they thought, haunted guilty men until their sins were purged away.  And many other dreams they had, which parted the One God into many; and they said, too, that these gods did things which would be a shame and sin for any man to do.  And when their philosophers arose, and told them that God was One, they would not listen, but loved their idols, and their wicked idol feasts, till they all came to ruin.  But we will talk of such sad things no more.

translation.en: Like all great nations that leave behind more than just mounds of dirt, the Greeks initially believed in the One True God who created heaven and earth.
translation.kr: 단순한 흙더미 이상의 것을 남긴 모든 위대한 국가들처럼, 그리스인들도 처음에는 천지를 창조하신 유일하고 참된 하나님을 믿었습니다.

translation.en: But over time, like other nations, they began to worship other gods.
translation.kr: 하지만 시간이 흐르면서 다른 국가들처럼 그들도 다른 신들을 숭배하기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: These were actually angels and spirits who they believed lived across their land.
translation.kr: 사실 이들은 그들이 자신들의 땅 곳곳에 살고 있다고 믿었던 천사와 영혼들이었습니다.

translation.en: They worshipped Zeus, the Father of gods and men, who was a faint memory of the true God.
translation.kr: 그들은 신과 인간의 아버지인 제우스를 숭배했는데, 그는 참된 하나님에 대한 희미한 기억이었습니다.

translation.en: They also worshipped Hera, his wife;
translation.kr: 그의 아내인 헤라와,

translation.en: Apollo, the Sun-god;
translation.kr: 태양의 신 아폴로,

translation.en: Athena, the goddess of wisdom and useful arts;
translation.kr: 지혜와 실용적인 기술의 여신 아테나,

translation.en: Aphrodite, the Queen of Beauty;
translation.kr: 아름다움의 여왕 아프로디테,

translation.en: Poseidon, the Ruler of the Sea;
translation.kr: 바다의 지배자 포세이돈,

translation.en: and Hephaestus, the King of Fire, who taught men how to work with metals.
translation.kr: 그리고 인간에게 금속을 다루는 법을 가르쳐 준 불의 왕 헤파이스토스를 숭배했습니다.

translation.en: They honored the gods of the rivers and the Nymphs, the nature spirits they imagined living in caves, fountains, forest glens, and beautiful wild places.
translation.kr: 그들은 강들의 신들과, 동굴, 분수, 숲속의 골짜기, 아름다운 야생의 장소에 산다고 상상했던 자연의 정령들인 님프들을 섬겼습니다.

translation.en: They also feared the Furies, dreadful sisters who they believed haunted guilty men until their sins were forgiven.
translation.kr: 또한 그들은 죄지은 인간들이 죄를 용서받을 때까지 그들을 쫓아다닌다고 믿었던 무시무시한 자매들인 복수의 여신들을 두려워했습니다.

translation.en: The Greeks had many other dreams that split the One God into many different figures.
translation.kr: 그리스인들은 유일하신 하나님을 여러 다른 인물로 쪼개는 다른 많은 꿈들을 꾸었습니다.

translation.en: They even claimed these gods did terrible things that would be considered sinful for any human to do.
translation.kr: 그들은 심지어 이 신들이 인간이 하면 죄로 여겨질 끔찍한 일들을 저질렀다고 주장하기까지 했습니다.

translation.en: When their own philosophers rose up and told them that God was One, they refused to listen.
translation.kr: 그들 자신의 철학자들이 일어나 하나님은 한 분이시라고 말했을 때, 그들은 듣기를 거부했습니다.

translation.en: They loved their idols and wicked feasts until it brought them to ruin.
translation.kr: 그들은 결국 파멸에 이를 때까지 자신들의 우상과 사악한 축제를 사랑했습니다.

translation.en: But we will not talk about such sad things anymore.
translation.kr: 하지만 우리는 더 이상 그런 슬픈 이야기들은 하지 않을 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: But, at the time of which this little book speaks, they had not fallen as low as that.  They worshipped no idols, as far as I can find; and they still believed in the last six of the ten commandments, and knew well what was right and what was wrong.  And they believed (and that was what gave them courage) that the gods loved men, and taught them, and that without the gods men were sure to come to ruin.  And in that they were right enough, as we know—more right even than they thought; for without God we can do nothing, and all wisdom comes from Him.

translation.en: At the time this little book takes place, they had not fallen that low.
translation.kr: 이 작은 책의 배경이 되는 시절에는 그들이 그렇게까지 타락하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: As far as I can tell, they did not worship idols.
translation.kr: 제가 아는 한, 그들은 우상을 숭배하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: They still followed the moral rules of the last six commandments and knew right from wrong.
translation.kr: 그들은 여전히 십계명 중 마지막 여섯 개의 도덕적인 규칙을 따랐고 옳고 그름을 알았습니다.

translation.en: They drew their courage from the belief that the gods loved men and taught them.
translation.kr: 그들은 신들이 인간을 사랑하고 가르친다는 믿음에서 용기를 얻었습니다.

translation.en: They believed that without the gods, humanity would surely face ruin.
translation.kr: 그들은 신들이 없다면 인류가 분명 파멸에 직면할 것이라고 믿었습니다.

translation.en: In that respect, they were absolutely right—more right than they even realized.
translation.kr: 그 점에 있어서는 그들이 전적으로 옳았습니다. 심지어 그들이 깨달았던 것보다도 더 옳았습니다.

translation.en: Without God, we can do nothing, because all wisdom comes directly from Him.
translation.kr: 모든 지혜는 그분으로부터 직접 나오기 때문에 하나님이 없다면 우리는 아무것도 할 수 없습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: Now, you must not think of them in this book as learned men, living in great cities, such as they were afterwards, when they wrought all their beautiful works, but as country people, living in farms and walled villages, in a simple, hard-working way; so that the greatest kings and heroes cooked their own meals, and thought it no shame, and made their own ships and weapons, and fed and harnessed their own horses; and the queens worked with their maid-servants, and did all the business of the house, and spun, and wove, and embroidered, and made their husbands’ clothes and their own.  So that a man was honoured among them, not because he happened to be rich, but according to his skill, and his strength, and courage, and the number of things which he could do.  For they were but grown-up children, though they were right noble children too; and it was with them as it is now at school—the strongest and cleverest boy, though he be poor, leads all the rest.

translation.en: You must not picture the people in this book as the highly educated men who lived in the great cities of later times, creating beautiful works of art.
translation.kr: 이 책에 나오는 사람들을 훗날 위대한 도시에 살면서 아름다운 예술 작품을 창조했던 고등 교육을 받은 사람들로 상상해서는 안 됩니다.

translation.en: Instead, imagine them as country people living a simple, hardworking life in farms and walled villages.
translation.kr: 대신 그들을 농장이나 성벽으로 둘러싸인 마을에서 소박하고 부지런하게 살아가는 시골 사람들로 생각하십시오.

translation.en: The greatest kings and heroes cooked their own meals and felt no shame in it.
translation.kr: 가장 위대한 왕들과 영웅들도 스스로 식사를 요리했으며, 그것을 전혀 부끄럽게 여기지 않았습니다.

translation.en: They built their own ships, forged their own weapons, and fed and harnessed their own horses.
translation.kr: 그들은 직접 배를 만들고, 무기를 벼려냈으며, 자신들의 말에게 먹이를 주고 마구를 채웠습니다.

translation.en: The queens worked right alongside their maidservants.
translation.kr: 여왕들은 하녀들 곁에서 함께 일했습니다.

translation.en: They managed the household, spun yarn, wove fabric, embroidered, and made clothes for themselves and their husbands.
translation.kr: 그들은 집안일을 돌보고, 실을 잣고, 옷감을 짜고, 자수를 놓고, 자신과 남편의 옷을 만들었습니다.

translation.en: A man was honored not because he happened to be rich, but because of his skill, strength, courage, and the sheer number of things he could do.
translation.kr: 사람이 존경받은 것은 우연히 부유해서가 아니라 그의 기술과 힘, 용기, 그리고 그가 할 수 있는 수많은 일들 때문이었습니다.

translation.en: They were essentially grown-up children, but very noble ones.
translation.kr: 그들은 본질적으로 다 자란 아이들이었지만, 매우 고결한 아이들이었습니다.

translation.en: Just like at school today, the strongest and cleverest boy led the rest, even if he was poor.
translation.kr: 마치 오늘날 학교에서처럼, 비록 가난하더라도 가장 강하고 똑똑한 소년이 나머지 모두를 이끌었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: Now, while they were young and simple they loved fairy tales, as you do now.  All nations do so when they are young: our old forefathers did, and called their stories ‘Sagas.’  I will read you some of them some day—some of the Eddas, and the Voluspà, and Beowulf, and the noble old Romances. The old Arabs, again, had their tales, which we now call the ‘Arabian Nights.’  The old Romans had theirs, and they called them ‘Fabulæ,’ from which our word ‘fable’ comes; but the old Hellens called theirs ‘Muthoi,’ from which our new word ‘myth’ is taken.  But next to those old Romances, which were written in the Christian middle age, there are no fairy tales like these old Greek ones, for beauty, and wisdom, and truth, and for making children love noble deeds, and trust in God to help them through.

translation.en: While they were a young and simple civilization, they loved fairy tales just as much as you do now.
translation.kr: 그들이 어리고 순수한 문명이었을 때, 그들은 지금의 여러분만큼이나 옛날이야기를 사랑했습니다.

translation.en: All nations do when they are young.
translation.kr: 모든 국가가 어릴 때는 그렇게 합니다.

translation.en: Our own ancestors told stories they called 'Sagas.
translation.kr: 우리 조상들은 '사가'라고 부르는 이야기들을 전해주었습니다.

translation.en: I will read you some of those one day—tales from the Eddas, the Voluspá, Beowulf, and the noble old romances.
translation.kr: 언젠가 제가 에다, 볼루스파, 베오울프, 그리고 고결한 옛 로맨스 같은 이야기들을 여러분에게 읽어주겠습니다.

translation.en: The ancient Arabs had their tales, which we now call the 'Arabian Nights.
translation.kr: 고대 아랍인들에게도 자신들의 이야기가 있었는데, 오늘날 우리는 그것을 '아라비안나이트'라고 부릅니다.

translation.en: The ancient Romans had theirs, called 'Fabulæ,' which gives us our word 'fable.
translation.kr: 고대 로마인들에게는 '파불라'라고 불리는 이야기들이 있었고, 여기서 우리의 '우화'라는 단어가 나왔습니다.

translation.en: But the ancient Hellens called their stories 'Muthoi,' which is where we get the modern word 'myth.
translation.kr: 하지만 고대 헬렌인들은 자신들의 이야기를 '무토이'라고 불렀으며, 여기서 '신화'라는 현대 단어가 생겨났습니다.

translation.en: Next to the old romances written during the Christian Middle Ages, there are no fairy tales quite like these ancient Greek ones.
translation.kr: 기독교가 지배하던 중세에 쓰인 옛 로맨스들을 제외한다면, 이 고대 그리스 이야기들만 한 옛날이야기는 없습니다.

translation.en: They are unmatched in beauty, wisdom, and truth.
translation.kr: 그것들은 아름다움, 지혜, 그리고 진리에 있어 비할 데가 없습니다.

translation.en: They inspire children to love noble deeds and to trust that God will help them through.
translation.kr: 그것들은 아이들이 고결한 행동을 사랑하고 하나님께서 그들이 이겨내도록 도우실 것임을 신뢰하게 영감을 줍니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: Now, why have I called this book ‘The Heroes’?  Because that was the name which the Hellens gave to men who were brave and skilful, and dare do more than other men.  At first, I think, that was all it meant: but after a time it came to mean something more; it came to mean men who helped their country; men in those old times, when the country was half-wild, who killed fierce beasts and evil men, and drained swamps, and founded towns, and therefore after they were dead, were honoured, because they had left their country better than they found it.  And we call such a man a hero in English to this day, and call it a ‘heroic’ thing to suffer pain and grief, that we may do good to our fellow-men.  We may all do that, my children, boys and girls alike; and we ought to do it, for it is easier now than ever, and safer, and the path more clear.  But you shall hear how the Hellens said their heroes worked, three thousand years ago. The stories are not all true, of course, nor half of them; you are not simple enough to fancy that; but the meaning of them is true, and true for ever, and that is—Do right, and God will help you.’

translation.en: Why have I called this book 'The Heroes'?
translation.kr: 그렇다면 저는 왜 이 책의 제목을 '영웅들'이라고 지었을까요?

translation.en: Because that was the name the Hellens gave to men who were brave, skilled, and dared to do more than others.
translation.kr: 그것은 헬렌인들이 용감하고 솜씨가 뛰어나며 다른 사람들보다 더 많은 것을 감히 행하는 사람들에게 붙여준 이름이었기 때문입니다.

translation.en: At first, I think that was all the word meant.
translation.kr: 처음에는 그 단어의 의미가 그것뿐이었던 것 같습니다.

translation.en: But over time, it came to mean something more.
translation.kr: 하지만 시간이 흐르면서 그것은 더 많은 의미를 가지게 되었습니다.

translation.en: It came to mean men who helped their country.
translation.kr: 그것은 조국을 도운 사람들을 의미하게 되었습니다.

translation.en: In those ancient times, when the land was half-wild, these men killed fierce beasts and evil criminals, drained swamps, and founded towns.
translation.kr: 나라가 반쯤 야생 상태였던 그 옛날, 사나운 짐승과 악한 범죄자들을 죽이고 늪의 물을 빼고 마을을 세운 사람들 말입니다.

translation.en: After they died, they were honored because they left their country better than they found it.
translation.kr: 그들이 죽은 후 사람들은 그들이 조국을 처음보다 더 살기 좋은 곳으로 남겨두었기 때문에 그들을 존경했습니다.

translation.en: We still call such a person a hero in English today.
translation.kr: 오늘날 우리는 영어로 그런 사람을 여전히 영웅이라고 부릅니다.

translation.en: We call it a 'heroic' act to suffer pain and grief just to do good for our fellow human beings.
translation.kr: 우리는 동료 인간들에게 선을 행하기 위해 고통과 슬픔을 겪는 것을 '영웅적'인 행동이라고 부릅니다.

translation.en: We can all do that, my children, boys and girls alike.
translation.kr: 소년 소녀 할 것 없이 우리 아이들 모두가 그렇게 할 수 있습니다.

translation.en: We ought to do it, because it is easier and safer now than ever before, and the path is much clearer.
translation.kr: 이제는 그 어느 때보다 더 쉽고 안전하며 그 길이 훨씬 더 명확하기 때문에, 우리는 마땅히 그렇게 해야 합니다.

translation.en: But you are going to hear how the Hellens believed their heroes worked three thousand years ago.
translation.kr: 이제 여러분은 헬렌인들이 자신들의 영웅들이 3천 년 전에 어떻게 활약했다고 믿었는지 듣게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: Of course, the stories are not entirely true—not even half of them.
translation.kr: 물론 그 이야기들이 전부 사실은 아니며, 심지어 절반도 사실이 아닐 것입니다.

translation.en: You are smart enough to know that.
translation.kr: 여러분은 그것을 모를 만큼 어리석지 않습니다.

translation.en: But the meaning behind them is true forever: do what is right, and God will help you.
translation.kr: 하지만 그 이면에 담긴 의미는 영원히 진실이며, 그것은 바로 '옳은 일을 행하라, 그러면 하나님이 너를 도우실 것이다'라는 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Preface: To My Children
paragraphs.raw: FARLEY COURT, _Advent_, 1855.

translation.en: Farley Court, Advent, 1855.
translation.kr: 1855년 대림절, 팔리 코트에서.

chapters.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: PART I HOW PERSEUS AND HIS MOTHER CAME TO SERIPHOS

translation.en: [Part 1: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos]
translation.kr: [1부: 페르세우스와 그의 어머니가 세리포스 섬에 오다]

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: Once upon a time there were two princes who were twins.  Their names were Acrisius and Prœtus, and they lived in the pleasant vale of Argos, far away in Hellas.  They had fruitful meadows and vineyards, sheep and oxen, great herds of horses feeding down in Lerna Fen, and all that men could need to make them blest: and yet they were wretched, because they were jealous of each other.  From the moment they were born they began to quarrel; and when they grew up each tried to take away the other’s share of the kingdom, and keep all for himself.  So first Acrisius drove out Prœtus; and he went across the seas, and brought home a foreign princess for his wife, and foreign warriors to help him, who were called Cyclopes; and drove out Acrisius in his turn; and then they fought a long while up and down the land, till the quarrel was settled, and Acrisius took Argos and one half the land, and Prœtus took Tiryns and the other half.  And Prœtus and his Cyclopes built around Tiryns great walls of unhewn stone, which are standing to this day.

translation.en: Once upon a time, there were twin princes named Acrisius and Proetus.
translation.kr: 옛날 옛적에 쌍둥이 왕자 아크리시오스와 프로이토스가 있었습니다.

translation.en: They lived in the pleasant valley of Argos, far away in ancient Greece.
translation.kr: 그들은 아득히 먼 고대 그리스의 평화로운 아르고스 계곡에 살았습니다.

translation.en: They had fertile meadows, rich vineyards, sheep, oxen, and great herds of horses grazing down in the Lerna Fen.
translation.kr: 그들에게는 비옥한 목초지와 풍성한 포도원, 양과 소, 그리고 레르나 늪지대에서 풀을 뜯는 엄청난 말 떼가 있었습니다.

translation.en: They had everything a man could need to be happy, yet they were miserable because they were intensely jealous of each other.
translation.kr: 그들은 사람이 행복해지는 데 필요한 모든 것을 갖추고 있었음에도 불구하고 서로를 몹시 질투했기 때문에 불행했습니다.

translation.en: They began to quarrel from the moment they were born.
translation.kr: 그들은 태어나는 순간부터 다투기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: When they grew up, each tried to steal the other's share of the kingdom to keep it all for himself.
translation.kr: 어른이 되자 그들은 왕국을 모두 차지하기 위해 서로의 몫을 빼앗으려 했습니다.

translation.en: First, Acrisius drove Proetus out.
translation.kr: 먼저 아크리시오스가 프로이토스를 쫓아냈습니다.

translation.en: Proetus fled across the sea and returned with a foreign princess for a wife and an army of massive foreign builders known as Cyclopes.
translation.kr: 프로이토스는 바다 건너로 달아났다가 외국 공주를 아내로 맞이하고 키클롭스라 불리는 거대한 이방인 건축가들의 군대를 이끌고 돌아왔습니다.

translation.en: Proetus then drove Acrisius out.
translation.kr: 그러고는 프로이토스가 아크리시오스를 쫓아냈습니다.

translation.en: The two fought back and forth across the land for a long time until they finally settled the quarrel.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 다툼을 완전히 끝낼 때까지 오랫동안 영토를 오가며 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: Acrisius took the city of Argos and half the land, while Proetus took the city of Tiryns and the other half.
translation.kr: 마침내 아크리시오스는 아르고스 시와 영토의 절반을 차지했고, 프로이토스는 티린스 시와 나머지 절반을 차지했습니다.

translation.en: Proetus and his giant Cyclopes built massive walls of rough, uncarved stone around Tiryns, which are still standing to this day.
translation.kr: 프로이토스와 그의 거인 키클롭스들은 티린스 주변에 깎지 않은 거친 돌로 거대한 성벽을 쌓았으며, 그 성벽은 오늘날까지도 남아 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: But there came a prophet to that hard-hearted Acrisius and prophesied against him, and said, ‘Because you have risen up against your own blood, your own blood shall rise up against you; because you have sinned against your kindred, by your kindred you shall be punished.  Your daughter Danae shall bear a son, and by that son’s hands you shall die.  So the Gods have ordained, and it will surely come to pass.’

translation.en: One day, a prophet came to the hard-hearted King Acrisius and delivered a dark warning.
translation.kr: 어느 날, 예언자 한 명이 냉혹한 아크리시오스 왕에게 와서 어두운 경고를 전했습니다.

translation.en: Because you have risen up against your own blood, your own blood shall rise up against you, the prophet said.
translation.kr: 당신이 자신의 핏줄을 거슬러 일어났으니, 당신의 핏줄이 당신을 거슬러 일어날 것이오, 하고 예언자는 말했습니다.

translation.en: Because you have sinned against your family, your family will punish you.
translation.kr: 당신이 당신의 가족에게 죄를 지었으니, 당신의 가족이 당신을 벌할 것이오.

translation.en: Your daughter, Danae, will bear a son, and you will die by that boy's hands.
translation.kr: 당신의 딸 다나에가 아들을 낳을 것이며, 당신은 그 소년의 손에 죽게 될 것이오.

translation.en: The gods have ordained it, and it will surely come to pass.
translation.kr: 신들께서 그렇게 명하셨으니, 이 일은 반드시 일어날 것이오.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: And at that Acrisius was very much afraid; but he did not mend his ways. He had been cruel to his own family, and, instead of repenting and being kind to them, he went on to be more cruel than ever: for he shut up his fair daughter Danae in a cavern underground, lined with brass, that no one might come near her.  So he fancied himself more cunning than the Gods: but you will see presently whether he was able to escape them.

translation.en: Acrisius was terrified, but he did not change his ways.
translation.kr: 아크리시오스는 몹시 두려웠지만, 자신의 방식을 고치지는 않았습니다.

translation.en: He had always been cruel to his family, and instead of repenting and showing kindness, he became even more vicious.
translation.kr: 그는 항상 가족에게 잔인하게 굴었고, 회개하고 다정함을 보여주는 대신 더욱더 악랄해졌습니다.

translation.en: He locked his beautiful daughter, Danae, in an underground cavern lined with solid bronze so that no one could ever come near her.
translation.kr: 그는 아름다운 딸 다나에를 튼튼한 청동으로 덧댄 지하 동굴에 가두어 아무도 그녀 곁에 갈 수 없게 만들었습니다.

translation.en: He thought he was outsmarting the gods, but you will soon see if anyone can truly escape them.
translation.kr: 그는 자신이 신들보다 영리하다고 생각했지만, 정말로 신들을 피할 수 있는 사람은 아무도 없다는 것을 여러분은 곧 알게 될 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: Now it came to pass that in time Danae bore a son; so beautiful a babe that any but King Acrisius would have had pity on it.  But he had no pity; for he took Danae and her babe down to the seashore, and put them into a great chest and thrust them out to sea, for the winds and the waves to carry them whithersoever they would.

translation.en: In time, Danae gave birth to a son.
translation.kr: 시간이 흘러 다나에는 아들을 낳았습니다.

translation.en: The baby was so beautiful that anyone but King Acrisius would have felt pity for him.
translation.kr: 그 아기는 너무나도 아름다워서 아크리시오스 왕만 아니었다면 누구라도 불쌍히 여겼을 것입니다.

translation.en: But the king had no mercy.
translation.kr: 하지만 왕에게는 자비가 없었습니다.

translation.en: He dragged Danae and her infant down to the seashore, locked them inside a massive wooden chest, and shoved them out to sea.
translation.kr: 그는 다나에와 아기를 바닷가로 끌고 가 거대한 나무 궤짝 안에 가두고는 바다로 밀어버렸습니다.

translation.en: He left them for the winds and waves to carry wherever they pleased.
translation.kr: 그는 바람과 파도가 마음대로 그들을 실어가도록 내버려 두었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: The north-west wind blew freshly out of the blue mountains, and down the pleasant vale of Argos, and away and out to sea.  And away and out to sea before it floated the mother and her babe, while all who watched them wept, save that cruel father, King Acrisius.

translation.en: A brisk northwest wind blew out of the blue mountains, sweeping down the pleasant valley of Argos and out across the water.
translation.kr: 상쾌한 북서풍이 푸른 산맥에서 불어와 평화로운 아르고스 계곡을 휩쓸고 탁 트인 바다로 빠져나갔습니다.

translation.en: The mother and her baby floated away over the open sea.
translation.kr: 어머니와 아기는 망망대해 위로 떠내려갔습니다.

translation.en: Everyone who watched them go wept for them, except for that cruel father, King Acrisius.
translation.kr: 그들이 떠나는 모습을 지켜본 모든 이들이 그들을 위해 눈물을 흘렸지만, 그 잔인한 아버지 아크리시오스 왕만은 예외였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: So they floated on and on, and the chest danced up and down upon the billows, and the baby slept upon its mother’s breast: but the poor mother could not sleep, but watched and wept, and she sang to her baby as they floated; and the song which she sang you shall learn yourselves some day.

translation.en: They floated on and on.
translation.kr: 그들은 끊임없이 떠내려갔습니다.

translation.en: The chest danced up and down upon the rolling waves, and the baby slept peacefully against his mother's breast.
translation.kr: 궤짝은 굽이치는 파도 위에서 위아래로 춤을 추었고, 아기는 어머니의 가슴에 안겨 평화롭게 잠들었습니다.

translation.en: But the poor mother could not sleep.
translation.kr: 하지만 가엾은 어머니는 잠들 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: She stayed awake, watching the water and weeping.
translation.kr: 그녀는 깨어난 채로 바다를 바라보며 눈물을 흘렸습니다.

translation.en: As they drifted, she sang a lullaby to her baby—a song you might learn yourselves one day.
translation.kr: 그들이 떠내려가는 동안 그녀는 아기에게 자장가를 불러주었습니다. 이 노래는 언젠가 여러분도 직접 배우게 될지도 모릅니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: And now they are past the last blue headland, and in the open sea; and there is nothing round them but the waves, and the sky, and the wind. But the waves are gentle, and the sky is clear, and the breeze is tender and low; for these are the days when Halcyone and Ceyx build their nests, and no storms ever ruffle the pleasant summer sea.

translation.en: Soon they drifted past the last blue headland and out into the open sea.
translation.kr: 머지않아 그들은 마지막 푸른 곶을 지나 탁 트인 바다로 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: There was nothing around them but waves, sky, and wind.
translation.kr: 그들 주위에는 파도와 하늘, 그리고 바람뿐이었습니다.

translation.en: Thankfully, the waves were gentle, the sky was clear, and the breeze was soft.
translation.kr: 다행히도 파도는 잔잔했고, 하늘은 맑았으며, 산들바람은 부드러웠습니다.

translation.en: These were the calm halcyon days of summer, a time when no storms ever ruffle the pleasant waters of the sea.
translation.kr: 이때는 어떤 폭풍우도 즐거운 여름 바다를 흔들지 않는, 평온한 할시온 데이즈(할키오네의 날들)였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: [Picture: Danae and her babe]

translation.en: [Illustration: Danae and her baby adrift in the chest]
translation.kr: [삽화: 궤짝에 실려 바다를 떠도는 다나에와 아기]

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: And who were Halcyone and Ceyx?  You shall hear while the chest floats on.  Halcyone was a fairy maiden, the daughter of the beach and of the wind.  And she loved a sailor-boy, and married him; and none on earth were so happy as they.  But at last Ceyx was wrecked; and before he could swim to the shore the billows swallowed him up.  And Halcyone saw him drowning, and leapt into the sea to him; but in vain.  Then the Immortals took pity on them both, and changed them into two fair sea-birds; and now they build a floating nest every year, and sail up and down happily for ever upon the pleasant seas of Greece.

translation.en: Who were Halcyone and Ceyx?
translation.kr: 할키오네와 케윅스가 누구일까요?

translation.en: You shall hear their story while the chest floats on.
translation.kr: 궤짝이 떠내려가는 동안 그들의 이야기를 들려드리겠습니다.

translation.en: Halcyone was a fairy maiden, a daughter of the beach and the wind.
translation.kr: 할키오네는 해변과 바람의 딸인 요정이었습니다.

translation.en: She fell in love with a young sailor named Ceyx, and they were married.
translation.kr: 그녀는 케윅스라는 젊은 선원과 사랑에 빠져 그와 결혼했습니다.

translation.en: No one on earth was as happy as they were.
translation.kr: 이 세상 그 누구도 그들만큼 행복하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: But one day, Ceyx was shipwrecked.
translation.kr: 하지만 어느 날, 케윅스는 난파를 당했습니다.

translation.en: Before he could swim to shore, the massive waves swallowed him.
translation.kr: 그가 기슭으로 헤엄쳐 가기도 전에 거대한 파도가 그를 삼켜버렸습니다.

translation.en: Halcyone saw him drowning and leaped into the sea to save him, but it was too late.
translation.kr: 할키오네는 그가 물에 빠지는 것을 보고 그를 구하기 위해 바다로 뛰어들었지만, 이미 너무 늦고 말았습니다.

translation.en: The gods took pity on the tragic lovers and transformed them into two beautiful sea-birds.
translation.kr: 신들은 이 비극적인 연인들을 가엾게 여겨 그들을 두 마리의 아름다운 바닷새로 변하게 해주었습니다.

translation.en: Now, they build a floating nest every year and sail happily together forever upon the calm summer seas of Greece.
translation.kr: 이제 그들은 매년 물에 뜨는 둥지를 짓고 그리스의 잔잔한 여름 바다 위를 영원히 행복하게 항해합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: So a night passed, and a day, and a long day it was for Danae; and another night and day beside, till Danae was faint with hunger and weeping, and yet no land appeared.  And all the while the babe slept quietly; and at last poor Danae drooped her head and fell asleep likewise with her cheek against the babe’s.

translation.en: A night passed, and then a long, exhausting day for Danae.
translation.kr: 다나에에게는 하룻밤, 그리고 지루하고 고단한 하루가 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: Another night and day went by.
translation.kr: 또다시 하루와 하룻밤이 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: Danae grew weak and faint from hunger and weeping, yet there was still no land in sight.
translation.kr: 다나에는 굶주림과 눈물로 쇠약해지고 기절할 지경이 되었지만, 여전히 육지는 보이지 않았습니다.

translation.en: The baby slept quietly through it all.
translation.kr: 아기는 그 모든 시간 동안 조용히 잠을 잤습니다.

translation.en: Finally, poor Danae let her head droop and fell asleep with her cheek resting against her child's.
translation.kr: 마침내 가엾은 다나에는 고개를 떨구고 아이의 뺨에 자신의 뺨을 기댄 채 잠이 들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: After a while she was awakened suddenly; for the chest was jarring and grinding, and the air was full of sound.  She looked up, and over her head were mighty cliffs, all red in the setting sun, and around her rocks and breakers, and flying flakes of foam.  She clasped her hands together, and shrieked aloud for help.  And when she cried, help met her: for now there came over the rocks a tall and stately man, and looked down wondering upon poor Danae tossing about in the chest among the waves.

translation.en: A sudden, jarring grind woke her.
translation.kr: 갑작스럽게 삐걱거리는 마찰음이 그녀를 깨웠습니다.

translation.en: The air was filled with a roaring sound.
translation.kr: 허공에는 굉음이 가득했습니다.

translation.en: She looked up and saw massive cliffs towering over her, glowing red in the setting sun.
translation.kr: 그녀가 위를 올려다보니, 지는 해에 붉게 물든 거대한 절벽들이 그녀 위로 우뚝 솟아 있었습니다.

translation.en: Around her, the water crashed against jagged rocks, sending flakes of white foam flying through the air.
translation.kr: 그녀 주위로는 뾰족한 바위들에 부딪힌 물결이 부서지며 하얀 거품 조각들을 공중으로 날려 보냈습니다.

translation.en: She clasped her hands together and screamed for help.
translation.kr: 그녀는 두 손을 마주 잡고 살려달라고 비명을 질렀습니다.

translation.en: As she cried out, help arrived.
translation.kr: 그녀가 소리쳤을 때, 도움이 찾아왔습니다.

translation.en: A tall, stately man climbed over the rocks and looked down in wonder at poor Danae tossing in the chest among the waves.
translation.kr: 키가 크고 기품 있는 한 남자가 바위를 넘어와 파도 사이로 궤짝 안에서 흔들리고 있는 가엾은 다나에를 놀란 눈으로 내려다보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: He wore a rough cloak of frieze, and on his head a broad hat to shade his face; in his hand he carried a trident for spearing fish, and over his shoulder was a casting-net; but Danae could see that he was no common man by his stature, and his walk, and his flowing golden hair and beard; and by the two servants who came behind him, carrying baskets for his fish. But she had hardly time to look at him, before he had laid aside his trident and leapt down the rocks, and thrown his casting-net so surely over Danae and the chest, that he drew it, and her, and the baby, safe upon a ledge of rock.

translation.en: He wore a rough woolen cloak and a broad hat to shade his face.
translation.kr: 그는 거친 양모 망토를 입고 얼굴을 가리기 위해 챙이 넓은 모자를 썼습니다.

translation.en: He carried a heavy, three-pronged trident for spearing fish in one hand, and a casting net hung over his shoulder.
translation.kr: 그는 한 손에 물고기를 찌르기 위한 무거운 삼지창을 들고 있었고, 어깨에는 투망이 걸려 있었습니다.

translation.en: Two servants followed him, carrying baskets for his catch.
translation.kr: 두 명의 하인이 그가 잡은 물고기를 담을 바구니를 들고 그의 뒤를 따랐습니다.

translation.en: But Danae could tell from his impressive height, his confident walk, and his flowing golden hair and beard that he was no ordinary man.
translation.kr: 하지만 다나에는 그의 인상적인 키와 자신감 넘치는 걸음걸이, 그리고 흩날리는 금발 머리와 수염을 보고 그가 평범한 남자가 아니라는 것을 알 수 있었습니다.

translation.en: Before she could even get a good look at him, he dropped his trident, leaped down the rocks, and threw his heavy net perfectly over Danae and the chest.
translation.kr: 그녀가 그를 제대로 쳐다보기도 전에, 그는 삼지창을 내려놓고 바위 아래로 뛰어내려 다나에와 궤짝 위로 완벽하게 무거운 그물을 던졌습니다.

translation.en: With a mighty pull, he dragged the chest, the mother, and the baby to safety onto a flat ledge of rock.
translation.kr: 그는 엄청난 힘으로 그물을 당겨 궤짝과 어머니, 아기를 안전한 평평한 바위 턱 위로 끌어올렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: Then the fisherman took Danae by the hand, and lifted her out of the chest, and said—

translation.en: The fisherman gently took Danae by the hand, helped her out of the chest, and said,
translation.kr: 어부는 부드럽게 다나에의 손을 잡아 궤짝 밖으로 나오도록 도와주며 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: ‘O beautiful damsel, what strange chance has brought you to this island in so flail a ship?  Who are you, and whence?  Surely you are some king’s daughter; and this boy has somewhat more than mortal.’

translation.en: Beautiful lady, what strange accident has brought you to this island in such a fragile ship?
translation.kr: 아름다운 여인이여, 무슨 기이한 사고로 이렇게 부서지기 쉬운 배를 타고 이 섬에 오게 되었소?

translation.en: Who are you, and where did you come from?
translation.kr: 당신은 누구이며 어디서 왔소?

translation.en: Surely you must be a king's daughter.
translation.kr: 틀림없이 당신은 어느 왕의 딸일 것이오.

translation.en: And this boy seems more than just mortal.
translation.kr: 그리고 이 소년은 그저 평범한 인간 이상인 것 같구려.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: And as he spoke he pointed to the babe; for its face shone like the morning star.

translation.en: As he spoke, he pointed to the baby, whose face shone as brightly as the morning star.
translation.kr: 이렇게 말하며 그는 샛별처럼 밝게 빛나는 얼굴을 가진 아기를 가리켰습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: But Danae only held down her head, and sobbed out—

translation.en: Danae simply bowed her head and sobbed,
translation.kr: 다나에는 그저 고개를 숙이고 흐느껴 울며 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: ‘Tell me to what land I have come, unhappy that I am; and among what men I have fallen!’

translation.en: Please, tell me what land I have reached, and what kind of men I have found here!
translation.kr: 제발, 제가 어떤 땅에 도착했는지, 그리고 제가 어떤 분들을 만나게 되었는지 말씀해 주세요!

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: And he said, ‘This isle is called Seriphos, and I am a Hellen, and dwell in it.  I am the brother of Polydectes the king; and men call me Dictys the netter, because I catch the fish of the shore.’

translation.en: This island is called Seriphos," he replied. "I am a Greek, and I live here. I am the brother of King Polydectes. People call me Dictys the Netter, because I catch fish along the shore.
translation.kr: 그는 대답했습니다. 이 섬은 세리포스라 불린다오. 나는 그리스인이며 여기에 살고 있소. 나는 폴리덱테스 왕의 형제라오. 사람들은 나를 해안가에서 물고기를 잡는다고 해서 '그물 치는 딕티스'라고 부르지.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: Then Danae fell down at his feet, and embraced his knees, and cried—

translation.en: Danae fell to her knees at his feet and cried,
translation.kr: 다나에는 그의 발밑에 무릎을 꿇고 울부짖었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: ‘Oh, sir, have pity upon a stranger, whom a cruel doom has driven to your land; and let me live in your house as a servant; but treat me honourably, for I was once a king’s daughter, and this my boy (as you have truly said) is of no common race.  I will not be a charge to you, or eat the bread of idleness; for I am more skilful in weaving and embroidery than all the maidens of my land.’

translation.en: Oh, sir, please have pity on a stranger driven to your land by a cruel fate!
translation.kr: 오, 어르신, 잔인한 운명에 이끌려 당신의 땅으로 오게 된 이방인을 제발 불쌍히 여겨 주세요!

translation.en: Let me live in your house as a servant, but treat me with honor.
translation.kr: 저를 당신의 집에 하녀로 살게 해주시되, 저를 명예롭게 대우해 주세요.

translation.en: I was once a king's daughter, and this boy, as you guessed, comes from a noble bloodline.
translation.kr: 저는 한때 왕의 딸이었고, 이 아이는 당신이 짐작하신 대로 고귀한 핏줄을 타고났습니다.

translation.en: I will not be a burden to you or eat your food without earning it.
translation.kr: 저는 당신에게 짐이 되거나 일하지 않고 당신의 음식을 먹지는 않을 것입니다.

translation.en: I am more skilled at weaving and embroidery than any maiden in my homeland.
translation.kr: 저는 제 고향의 어떤 처녀보다 베 짜기와 자수에 능숙합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: And she was going on; but Dictys stopped her, and raised her up, and said—

translation.en: She would have continued, but Dictys gently stopped her. He raised her to her feet and said,
translation.kr: 그녀가 계속 말하려 했으나, 딕티스가 그녀를 부드럽게 멈춰 세웠습니다. 그는 그녀를 일으켜 세우며 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: ‘My daughter, I am old, and my hairs are growing gray; while I have no children to make my home cheerful.  Come with me then, and you shall be a daughter to me and to my wife, and this babe shall be our grandchild. For I fear the Gods, and show hospitality to all strangers; knowing that good deeds, like evil ones, always return to those who do them.’

translation.en: My daughter, I am old and my hair is gray.
translation.kr: 내 딸이여, 나는 늙었고 머리는 희끗희끗하다오.

translation.en: I have no children of my own to bring joy to my home.
translation.kr: 내 집을 즐겁게 해줄 내 자식은 없소.

translation.en: Come with me.
translation.kr: 나와 함께 가시구려.

translation.en: You shall be a daughter to me and my wife, and this baby will be our grandson.
translation.kr: 당신은 나와 내 아내에게 딸이 될 것이고, 이 아기는 우리의 손자가 될 것이오.

translation.en: I fear the gods and always offer hospitality to strangers.
translation.kr: 나는 신들을 경외하며 낯선 이들에게 항상 환대를 베푼다오.

translation.en: I know that good deeds, just like evil ones, always return to the people who do them.
translation.kr: 나는 악한 일과 마찬가지로 선한 일도 항상 그것을 행한 사람에게 돌아간다는 것을 알고 있소.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Perseus and His Mother Came to Seriphos
paragraphs.raw: So Danae was comforted, and went home with Dictys the good fisherman, and was a daughter to him and to his wife, till fifteen years were past.

translation.en: Danae was deeply comforted. She went home with Dictys, the good fisherman, and lived happily as a daughter to him and his wife for fifteen long years.
translation.kr: 다나에는 깊은 위로를 받았습니다. 그녀는 선량한 어부 딕티스와 함께 집으로 돌아가 그와 그의 아내에게 친딸처럼 지내며 15년이라는 긴 세월 동안 행복하게 살았습니다.

chapters.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: PART II HOW PERSEUS VOWED A RASH VOW

translation.en: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
translation.kr: [2부: 페르세우스가 경솔한 맹세를 하다]

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Fifteen years were past and gone, and the babe was now grown to be a tall lad and a sailor, and went many voyages after merchandise to the islands round.  His mother called him Perseus; but all the people in Seriphos said that he was not the son of mortal man, and called him the son of Zeus, the king of the Immortals.  For though he was but fifteen, he was taller by a head than any man in the island; and he was the most skilful of all in running and wrestling and boxing, and in throwing the quoit and the javelin, and in rowing with the oar, and in playing on the harp, and in all which befits a man.  And he was brave and truthful, gentle and courteous, for good old Dictys had trained him well; and well it was for Perseus that he had done so.  For now Danae and her son fell into great danger, and Perseus had need of all his wit to defend his mother and himself.

translation.en: Fifteen years passed, and the baby grew into a tall sailor.
translation.kr: 15년의 세월이 흘러 아기는 훌쩍 자라 늠름한 선원이 되었습니다.

translation.en: He traveled on trading voyages to nearby islands.
translation.kr: 그는 무역선에 올라 인근 섬들을 오갔습니다.

translation.en: His mother named him Perseus.
translation.kr: 어머니는 그를 페르세우스라 불렀습니다.

translation.en: But the people of Seriphos thought he was no mortal.
translation.kr: 하지만 세리포스 사람들은 그가 평범한 인간이 아니라고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: They called him the son of Zeus, king of the gods.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그를 신들의 왕인 제우스의 아들이라 불렀습니다.

translation.en: At just fifteen, he stood a head taller than any man on the island.
translation.kr: 불과 열다섯 살이었지만 그는 섬의 어떤 성인 남성보다 머리 하나는 더 컸습니다.

translation.en: He excelled at running, wrestling, and boxing.
translation.kr: 달리기와 레슬링, 권투에 누구보다 뛰어났습니다.

translation.en: He mastered the discus, the javelin, and the harp.
translation.kr: 원반과 투창, 하프 연주에도 능했습니다.

translation.en: He was brave, truthful, gentle, and courteous.
translation.kr: 그는 용감하고 진실했으며 다정하고 예의가 발랐습니다.

translation.en: The good Dictys had raised him well.
translation.kr: 선량한 딕티스가 그를 훌륭하게 키워낸 덕분입니다.

translation.en: This training came in handy, for Danae and her son soon faced great danger.
translation.kr: 이 가르침은 다나에와 아들에게 닥친 큰 위기에서 빛을 발했습니다.

translation.en: Perseus would need all his wits to protect them both.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 어머니와 자신을 지키기 위해 기지를 발휘해야만 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: I said that Dictys’ brother was Polydectes, king of the island.  He was not a righteous man, like Dictys; but greedy, and cunning, and cruel. And when he saw fair Danae, he wanted to marry her.  But she would not; for she did not love him, and cared for no one but her boy, and her boy’s father, whom she never hoped to see again.  At last Polydectes became furious; and while Perseus was away at sea he took poor Danae away from Dictys, saying, ‘If you will not be my wife, you shall be my slave.’  So Danae was made a slave, and had to fetch water from the well, and grind in the mill, and perhaps was beaten, and wore a heavy chain, because she would not marry that cruel king.  But Perseus was far away over the seas in the isle of Samos, little thinking how his mother was languishing in grief.

translation.en: Dictys had a brother named Polydectes, who ruled the island.
translation.kr: 딕티스에게는 섬을 다스리는 폴리덱테스라는 형제가 있었습니다.

translation.en: Unlike Dictys, he was greedy, cunning, and cruel.
translation.kr: 딕티스와 달리 그는 탐욕스럽고 교활하며 잔인한 폭군이었습니다.

translation.en: When he saw the beautiful Danae, he wanted to marry her.
translation.kr: 그는 아름다운 다나에를 보자마자 아내로 삼고 싶어 했습니다.

translation.en: But she refused, for she loved only her son and his father.
translation.kr: 하지만 다나에는 오직 아들과 그의 아버지 만을 사랑했기에 거절했습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, Polydectes grew furious.
translation.kr: 마침내 폴리덱테스는 분노를 터뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: While Perseus was away at sea, he kidnapped Danae from Dictys.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 바다로 나간 사이, 그는 딕티스에게서 다나에를 빼앗았습니다.

translation.en: He declared that if she refused marriage, she would become his slave.
translation.kr: 그는 결혼을 거부하면 노예로 만들겠다고 선고했습니다.

translation.en: Danae was forced to fetch water and grind grain at the mill.
translation.kr: 다나에는 우물에서 물을 긷고 맷돌을 돌려야 했습니다.

translation.en: She was chained and likely beaten for rejecting the cruel king.
translation.kr: 잔인한 왕을 거부한 대가로 쇠사슬에 묶인 채 매질을 당했을지도 모릅니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, Perseus was far away in Samos, unaware of her suffering.
translation.kr: 한편 페르세우스는 어머니의 고통을 모른 채 머나먼 사모스섬에 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Now one day at Samos, while the ship was lading, Perseus wandered into a pleasant wood to get out of the sun, and sat down on the turf and fell asleep.  And as he slept a strange dream came to him—the strangest dream which he had ever had in his life.

translation.en: One day in Samos, Perseus sought shade in a pleasant wood while his ship was loaded.
translation.kr: 어느 날 사모스섬에서 배에 짐을 싣는 동안, 페르세우스는 쾌적한 숲으로 들어가 햇빛을 피했습니다.

translation.en: He sat down on the grass and fell asleep.
translation.kr: 그는 잔디밭에 주저앉아 깜빡 잠이 들었습니다.

translation.en: As he slept, he experienced the strangest dream of his life.
translation.kr: 그리고 잠결에 평생 겪어본 적 없는 기이한 꿈을 꾸었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: There came a lady to him through the wood, taller than he, or any mortal man; but beautiful exceedingly, with great gray eyes, clear and piercing, but strangely soft and mild.  On her head was a helmet, and in her hand a spear.  And over her shoulder, above her long blue robes, hung a goat-skin, which bore up a mighty shield of brass, polished like a mirror.  She stood and looked at him with her clear gray eyes; and Perseus saw that her eye-lids never moved, nor her eyeballs, but looked straight through and through him, and into his very heart, as if she could see all the secrets of his soul, and knew all that he had ever thought or longed for since the day that he was born.  And Perseus dropped his eyes, trembling and blushing, as the wonderful lady spoke.

translation.en: A woman walked through the woods toward him.
translation.kr: 한 여인이 숲을 지나 그에게 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: She was taller than any mortal, and astonishingly beautiful.
translation.kr: 그녀는 어떤 인간보다 키가 컸고 눈부시게 아름다웠습니다.

translation.en: Her large gray eyes were piercingly clear, yet strangely gentle.
translation.kr: 커다란 잿빛 눈동자는 꿰뚫어 보듯 맑았지만 놀랍도록 부드러웠습니다.

translation.en: She wore a helmet on her head and held a spear in her hand.
translation.kr: 머리에는 투구를 쓰고 손에는 창을 들고 있었습니다.

translation.en: A goatskin hung over her long blue robes, supporting a polished brass shield.
translation.kr: 푸른 긴 옷 위로 염소 가죽을 걸쳤고, 거울처럼 빛나는 놋쇠 방패를 메고 있었습니다.

translation.en: She stood still, staring at him with her gray eyes.
translation.kr: 그녀는 우두커니 서서 잿빛 눈으로 그를 응시했습니다.

translation.en: Perseus noticed that her eyes never blinked or darted away.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그녀의 눈꺼풀이나 눈동자가 전혀 움직이지 않는 것을 눈치챘습니다.

translation.en: They looked straight through to his very heart.
translation.kr: 그녀의 시선은 그의 마음속 깊은 곳까지 꿰뚫어 보았습니다.

translation.en: It felt as though she knew every secret and desire he had ever held.
translation.kr: 마치 그가 태어난 순간부터 품어온 모든 비밀과 갈망을 아는 것 같았습니다.

translation.en: Trembling and blushing, Perseus lowered his gaze as the wondrous lady spoke.
translation.kr: 신비로운 여인이 입을 열자 페르세우스는 얼굴을 붉히며 고개를 숙였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Perseus, you must do an errand for me.’

translation.en: Perseus, you must run an errand for me.
translation.kr: 페르세우스, 나를 위해 심부름을 하나 해주어야겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Who are you, lady?  And how do you know my name?’

translation.en: Who are you, lady? And how do you know my name?
translation.kr: 누구십니까? 그리고 제 이름은 어떻게 아셨습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘I am Pallas Athené; and I know the thoughts of all men’s hearts, and discern their manhood or their baseness.  And from the souls of clay I turn away, and they are blest, but not by me.  They fatten at ease, like sheep in the pasture, and eat what they did not sow, like oxen in the stall.  They grow and spread, like the gourd along the ground; but, like the gourd, they give no shade to the traveller, and when they are ripe death gathers them, and they go down unloved into hell, and their name vanishes out of the land.

translation.en: I am Athena. I know the hearts of all men, seeing their courage or cowardice.
translation.kr: 나는 아테나입니다. 나는 모든 인간의 마음을 읽어 그들의 용기와 비겁함을 꿰뚫어 봅니다.

translation.en: I turn away from cowardly souls. They may be blessed, but not by me.
translation.kr: 나는 진흙 같은 비겁한 영혼들을 외면합니다. 그들도 축복을 받겠지만, 내 축복은 아닙니다.

translation.en: They fatten lazily like sheep in a pasture, eating what they never sowed.
translation.kr: 그들은 목초지의 양 떼처럼 편안히 살을 찌우고, 뿌리지 않은 것을 거두어 먹습니다.

translation.en: They spread across the earth like weeds, offering no shade to travelers.
translation.kr: 땅바닥을 기어가는 덩굴처럼 퍼지지만, 나그네에게 어떤 그늘도 내어주지 않습니다.

translation.en: When their time comes, death harvests them.
translation.kr: 때가 되면 죽음이 그들을 거두어 갑니다.

translation.en: They descend to the underworld unloved, and their names vanish from the world.
translation.kr: 그들은 누구의 사랑도 받지 못한 채 지하 세계로 내려가고, 그 이름도 세상에서 사라집니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘But to the souls of fire I give more fire, and to those who are manful I give a might more than man’s.  These are the heroes, the sons of the Immortals, who are blest, but not like the souls of clay.  For I drive them forth by strange paths, Perseus, that they may fight the Titans and the monsters, the enemies of Gods and men.  Through doubt and need, danger and battle, I drive them; and some of them are slain in the flower of youth, no man knows when or where; and some of them win noble names, and a fair and green old age; but what will be their latter end I know not, and none, save Zeus, the father of Gods and men.  Tell me now, Perseus, which of these two sorts of men seem to you more blest?’

translation.en: But to fiery souls, I give even more fire.
translation.kr: 하지만 불꽃 같은 영혼들에게는 더 큰 불꽃을 안겨줍니다.

translation.en: To the courageous, I grant strength beyond mortal limits.
translation.kr: 용기 있는 자들에게는 인간의 한계를 뛰어넘는 힘을 줍니다.

translation.en: These are the heroes, the children of the gods.
translation.kr: 이들이 바로 신들의 자녀인 영웅들입니다.

translation.en: I drive them down strange paths to fight monsters and enemies of the gods.
translation.kr: 나는 그들을 낯선 길로 내몰아 괴물들과 신의 적들에 맞서 싸우게 합니다.

translation.en: I push them through hardship, doubt, and battle.
translation.kr: 나는 고난과 의심, 전투 속으로 그들을 밀어 넣습니다.

translation.en: Some fall in their prime, in unknown times and places.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 젊은 날에 이름 모를 곳에서 목숨을 잃습니다.

translation.en: Others win glorious names and live to a ripe old age.
translation.kr: 또 어떤 이들은 영광스러운 이름을 얻고 평온한 노년을 맞이합니다.

translation.en: Only Zeus knows what their ultimate fate will be.
translation.kr: 오직 제우스만이 그들의 마지막 운명을 알고 있습니다.

translation.en: Tell me, Perseus, which of these two paths seems better to you?
translation.kr: 말해보십시오, 페르세우스. 이 두 가지 삶 중 어느 쪽이 더 축복받은 것 같습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus answered boldly: ‘Better to die in the flower of youth, on the chance of winning a noble name, than to live at ease like the sheep, and die unloved and unrenowned.’

translation.en: Perseus answered boldly.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 당당하게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: It is better to die young for a chance at glory than to live like a lazy sheep and die forgotten.
translation.kr: 게으른 양처럼 살다 잊힌 채 죽는 것보다, 영광을 쫓다 젊은 날에 죽는 것이 낫습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then that strange lady laughed, and held up her brazen shield, and cried: ‘See here, Perseus; dare you face such a monster as this, and slay it, that I may place its head upon this shield?’

translation.en: The strange lady laughed and raised her brass shield.
translation.kr: 신비로운 여인은 웃음을 터뜨리며 놋쇠 방패를 치켜들었습니다.

translation.en: Look here, Perseus! Would you dare slay such a monster so I can mount its head on my shield?
translation.kr: 여길 보십시오, 페르세우스! 내 방패에 머리를 달 수 있도록 이 끔찍한 괴물을 벨 용기가 있습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: And in the mirror of the shield there appeared a face, and as Perseus looked on it his blood ran cold.  It was the face of a beautiful woman; but her cheeks were pale as death, and her brows were knit with everlasting pain, and her lips were thin and bitter like a snake’s; and instead of hair, vipers wreathed about her temples, and shot out their forked tongues; while round her head were folded wings like an eagle’s, and upon her bosom claws of brass.

translation.en: A face appeared in the mirror of the shield, chilling Perseus to the bone.
translation.kr: 방패 거울에 얼굴 하나가 나타나자 페르세우스의 온몸이 얼어붙었습니다.

translation.en: It was the face of a beautiful woman, but her cheeks were pale as death.
translation.kr: 아름다운 여인의 얼굴이었지만 두 뺨은 죽음처럼 창백했습니다.

translation.en: Her brow was contorted in endless agony.
translation.kr: 이마는 끝없는 고통으로 일그러져 있었습니다.

translation.en: Her thin lips sneered like a venomous snake.
translation.kr: 얇은 입술은 독사처럼 비릿한 미소를 짓고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Instead of hair, writhing vipers hissed from her scalp with forked tongues.
translation.kr: 머리카락 대신 꿈틀거리는 독사들이 갈라진 혀를 날름거렸습니다.

translation.en: Eagle wings folded around her head, and brass claws rested on her chest.
translation.kr: 머리 주변에는 독수리 날개가 접혀 있었고, 가슴에는 놋쇠 발톱이 달려 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: And Perseus looked awhile, and then said: ‘If there is anything so fierce and foul on earth, it were a noble deed to kill it.  Where can I find the monster?’

translation.en: Perseus stared for a moment, then spoke.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 한참을 바라보다가 입을 열었습니다.

translation.en: If such a foul beast exists, killing it would be a noble deed. Where can I find it?
translation.kr: 세상에 저토록 끔찍한 괴물이 있다면, 그것을 죽이는 것은 숭고한 일일 것입니다. 어디서 찾을 수 있습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then the strange lady smiled again, and said: ‘Not yet; you are too young, and too unskilled; for this is Medusa the Gorgon, the mother of a monstrous brood.  Return to your home, and do the work which waits there for you.  You must play the man in that before I can think you worthy to go in search of the Gorgon.’

translation.en: The strange lady smiled again and answered him gently.
translation.kr: 신비로운 여인은 다시 미소를 지으며 부드럽게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Not yet. You are too young and unskilled to face Medusa the Gorgon.
translation.kr: 아직은 아닙니다. 고르곤 메두사를 상대하기에 당신은 너무 어리고 서투릅니다.

translation.en: Go home and finish the work waiting for you there.
translation.kr: 고향으로 돌아가 당신을 기다리는 일부터 끝마치십시오.

translation.en: You must prove your manhood first before you can hunt the Gorgon.
translation.kr: 고르곤을 사냥할 자격을 증명하려면 먼저 진짜 남자가 되어야 합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus would have spoken, but the strange lady vanished, and he awoke; and behold, it was a dream.  But day and night Perseus saw before him the face of that dreadful woman, with the vipers writhing round her head.

translation.en: Perseus tried to reply, but the strange lady vanished.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 대답하려 했지만 신비로운 여인은 사라져버렸습니다.

translation.en: He woke up and realized it was only a dream.
translation.kr: 잠에서 깨어난 그는 그것이 꿈이라는 것을 깨달았습니다.

translation.en: Yet the dreadful face with the writhing vipers haunted his every waking moment.
translation.kr: 하지만 독사들이 꿈틀거리는 끔찍한 여인의 얼굴은 밤낮으로 그를 괴롭혔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: So he returned home; and when he came to Seriphos, the first thing which he heard was that his mother was a slave in the house of Polydectes.

translation.en: He sailed back to Seriphos, only to hear that his mother had become Polydectes' slave.
translation.kr: 그는 세리포스로 돌아왔지만, 어머니가 폴리덱테스의 노예가 되었다는 소식을 들어야만 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Grinding his teeth with rage, he went out, and away to the king’s palace, and through the men’s rooms, and the women’s rooms, and so through all the house (for no one dared stop him, so terrible and fair was he), till he found his mother sitting on the floor, turning the stone hand-mill, and weeping as she turned it.  And he lifted her up, and kissed her, and bade her follow him forth.  But before they could pass out of the room Polydectes came in, raging.  And when Perseus saw him, he flew upon him as the mastiff flies on the boar.  ‘Villain and tyrant!’ he cried; ‘is this your respect for the Gods, and thy mercy to strangers and widows? You shall die!’  And because he had no sword he caught up the stone hand-mill, and lifted it to dash out Polydectes’ brains.

translation.en: Grinding his teeth in rage, he marched straight to the king's palace.
translation.kr: 그는 분노로 이를 갈며 곧장 왕의 궁전으로 향했습니다.

translation.en: He stormed through the halls, so terrifying in his fury that no one dared stop him.
translation.kr: 분노한 그의 모습이 너무도 두려워 아무도 앞을 막아서지 못했습니다.

translation.en: He found his mother weeping on the floor as she turned a heavy stone mill.
translation.kr: 마침내 무거운 맷돌을 돌리며 바닥에서 눈물짓는 어머니를 발견했습니다.

translation.en: Perseus lifted her up, kissed her, and told her to leave with him.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 어머니를 일으켜 세우고 입을 맞춘 뒤 함께 떠나자고 말했습니다.

translation.en: Before they could escape, an enraged Polydectes blocked their path.
translation.kr: 하지만 방을 나서기 전, 격노한 폴리덱테스가 앞을 가로막았습니다.

translation.en: Perseus lunged at the king like a guard dog attacking a boar.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 멧돼지에게 달려드는 사냥개처럼 왕에게 달려들었습니다.

translation.en: Villain and tyrant! he shouted.
translation.kr: 악당이자 폭군이여! 그가 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Is this how you honor the gods and treat widows? You will die for this!
translation.kr: 이것이 신들을 공경하고 과부들을 대하는 당신의 방식인가? 여기서 죽어라!

translation.en: Without a sword, Perseus hoisted the heavy stone mill to crush the king's skull.
translation.kr: 검이 없었던 페르세우스는 무거운 맷돌을 들어 왕의 머리를 내리치려 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: But his mother clung to him, shrieking, ‘Oh, my son, we are strangers and helpless in the land; and if you kill the king, all the people will fall on us, and we shall both die.’

translation.en: But his mother clung to him, screaming in terror.
translation.kr: 하지만 어머니가 비명을 지르며 그에게 매달렸습니다.

translation.en: Oh, my son! We are helpless strangers here!
translation.kr: 오, 아들아! 우리는 이 땅에서 힘없는 이방인일 뿐이다!

translation.en: If you kill the king, the people will slaughter us both!
translation.kr: 네가 왕을 죽이면 모든 백성이 달려들어 우리 둘 다 죽고 말 것이다!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Good Dictys, too, who had come in, entreated him.  ‘Remember that he is my brother.  Remember how I have brought you up, and trained you as my own son, and spare him for my sake.’

translation.en: The good Dictys rushed in and begged for his brother's life.
translation.kr: 선량한 딕티스도 뛰어 들어와 형제의 목숨을 구걸했습니다.

translation.en: Remember that he is my brother!
translation.kr: 그가 내 형제라는 사실을 기억해 다오!

translation.en: Remember how I raised you as my own son, and spare him for my sake!
translation.kr: 널 친아들처럼 키워준 나를 생각해서라도 부디 목숨만은 살려다오!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus lowered his hand; and Polydectes, who had been trembling all this while like a coward, because he knew that he was in the wrong, let Perseus and his mother pass.

translation.en: Perseus lowered the heavy stone.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 들고 있던 무거운 돌을 내려놓았습니다.

translation.en: Polydectes, trembling like a coward because he knew he was guilty, let them leave.
translation.kr: 자신의 잘못을 알고 비겁자처럼 떨고 있던 폴리덱테스는 두 사람을 보내주었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Perseus took his mother to the temple of Athené, and there the priestess made her one of the temple-sweepers; for there they knew she would be safe, and not even Polydectes would dare to drag her away from the altar. And there Perseus, and the good Dictys, and his wife, came to visit her every day; while Polydectes, not being able to get what he wanted by force, cast about in his wicked heart how he might get it by cunning.

translation.en: Perseus took his mother to the temple of Athena.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 어머니를 아테나 신전으로 모셨습니다.

translation.en: The priestess made her a temple sweeper to grant her sanctuary.
translation.kr: 여사제는 다나에를 신전 청소부로 받아주어 안식처를 내어주었습니다.

translation.en: Even Polydectes would not dare drag someone from the holy altar.
translation.kr: 아무리 폴리덱테스라도 신성한 제단에서 사람을 끌어낼 엄두는 내지 못했습니다.

translation.en: Perseus, Dictys, and his wife visited her every single day.
translation.kr: 페르세우스와 딕티스 부부는 매일같이 그녀를 찾아갔습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, the wicked king plotted new and cunning ways to get what he wanted.
translation.kr: 한편, 사악한 왕은 자신이 원하는 것을 얻기 위해 새롭고 교활한 음모를 꾸미기 시작했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
