paragraphs.raw: Now he was sure that he could never get back Danae as long as Perseus was in the island; so he made a plot to rid himself of him.  And first he pretended to have forgiven Perseus, and to have forgotten Danae; so that, for a while, all went as smoothly as ever.

translation.en: He knew he could never win Danae while Perseus remained on the island.
translation.kr: 그는 페르세우스가 섬에 있는 한 결코 다나에를 차지할 수 없다는 것을 알았습니다.

translation.en: So, he hatched a plot to get rid of the young man.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 그 젊은이를 제거할 음모를 꾸몄습니다.

translation.en: First, he pretended to forgive Perseus and forget about Danae.
translation.kr: 먼저 그는 페르세우스를 용서하고 다나에를 잊은 척했습니다.

translation.en: For a while, everything seemed peaceful.
translation.kr: 한동안은 모든 것이 평화로워 보였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Next he proclaimed a great feast, and invited to it all the chiefs, and landowners, and the young men of the island, and among them Perseus, that they might all do him homage as their king, and eat of his banquet in his hall.

translation.en: Next, he announced a grand feast.
translation.kr: 다음으로 그는 성대한 연회를 열겠다고 발표했습니다.

translation.en: He invited all the chiefs, landowners, and young men of the island.
translation.kr: 그는 섬의 모든 족장과 지주, 그리고 젊은이들을 초대했습니다.

translation.en: He made sure to include Perseus.
translation.kr: 그는 페르세우스도 빠뜨리지 않고 초대했습니다.

translation.en: The king wanted everyone to pay him respect and enjoy his banquet.
translation.kr: 왕은 모든 사람이 자신에게 경의를 표하고 연회를 즐기기를 원했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: On the appointed day they all came; and as the custom was then, each guest brought his present with him to the king: one a horse, another a shawl, or a ring, or a sword; and those who had nothing better brought a basket of grapes, or of game; but Perseus brought nothing, for he had nothing to bring, being but a poor sailor-lad.

translation.en: Everyone arrived on the appointed day.
translation.kr: 약속된 날에 모두가 도착했습니다.

translation.en: Following custom, each guest brought a gift for the king.
translation.kr: 관습에 따라 각 손님은 왕을 위한 선물을 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: Some brought a horse, a shawl, a ring, or a sword.
translation.kr: 어떤 이는 말이나 숄, 반지나 칼을 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: Others brought baskets of grapes or wild game.
translation.kr: 다른 이들은 포도 바구니나 사냥한 고기를 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: But Perseus arrived empty-handed.
translation.kr: 하지만 페르세우스는 빈손으로 도착했습니다.

translation.en: He was just a poor sailor boy with nothing to give.
translation.kr: 그는 가난한 선원 소년이라 줄 것이 아무것도 없었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: He was ashamed, however, to go into the king’s presence without his gift; and he was too proud to ask Dictys to lend him one.  So he stood at the door sorrowfully, watching the rich men go in; and his face grew very red as they pointed at him, and smiled, and whispered, ‘What has that foundling to give?’

translation.en: He felt ashamed to face the king without a gift.
translation.kr: 그는 선물 없이 왕을 마주하는 것이 부끄러웠습니다.

translation.en: Yet, he was too proud to borrow one from Dictys.
translation.kr: 하지만 그의 자존심이 허락하지 않아 딕티스에게 빌릴 수도 없었습니다.

translation.en: He stood sadly at the door, watching the rich men enter.
translation.kr: 그는 부자들이 들어가는 것을 지켜보며 문가에 슬프게 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: His face burned red as they pointed and whispered.
translation.kr: 사람들이 손가락질하며 속닥거리자 그의 얼굴은 붉게 달아올랐습니다.

translation.en: What does that foundling have to give?
translation.kr: 저 업둥이가 줄 게 뭐가 있겠어?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Now this was what Polydectes wanted; and as soon as he heard that Perseus stood without, he bade them bring him in, and asked him scornfully before them all, ‘Am I not your king, Perseus, and have I not invited you to my feast?  Where is your present, then?’

translation.en: This was exactly what Polydectes wanted.
translation.kr: 이것이 바로 폴리덱테스가 원하던 바였습니다.

translation.en: Hearing that Perseus was waiting outside, he ordered him brought in.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 밖에 서 있다는 소식을 듣고 그는 당장 데려오라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: He mocked the boy in front of everyone.
translation.kr: 그는 모든 사람 앞에서 소년을 조롱했습니다.

translation.en: Am I not your king, Perseus?
translation.kr: 내가 너의 왕이 아니더냐, 페르세우스?

translation.en: Did I not invite you to my feast?
translation.kr: 내가 너를 연회에 초대하지 않았느냐?

translation.en: Where is your present, then?
translation.kr: 그렇다면 네 선물은 어디에 있느냐?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Perseus blushed and stammered, while all the proud men round laughed, and some of them began jeering him openly.  ‘This fellow was thrown ashore here like a piece of weed or drift-wood, and yet he is too proud to bring a gift to the king.’

translation.en: Perseus blushed and stammered.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 얼굴을 붉히며 더듬거렸습니다.

translation.en: The proud men laughed, and some openly jeered at him.
translation.kr: 오만한 사람들은 웃음을 터뜨렸고, 일부는 대놓고 그를 비웃었습니다.

translation.en: This guy washed ashore like seaweed or driftwood.
translation.kr: 이 녀석은 해초나 유목처럼 이 해변으로 밀려왔지.

translation.en: Yet he is too proud to bring a gift to the king.
translation.kr: 그런데도 건방지게 왕에게 선물을 가져오지 않는군.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘And though he does not know who his father is, he is vain enough to let the old women call him the son of Zeus.’

translation.en: He does not even know who his father is.
translation.kr: 자기 아버지가 누군지도 모르는 주제에 말이야.

translation.en: But he is vain enough to let old women call him the son of Zeus.
translation.kr: 그런데도 늙은 여자들이 자기를 제우스의 아들이라 부르도록 내버려두는 허영심을 가졌지.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: And so forth, till poor Perseus grew mad with shame, and hardly knowing what he said, cried out,—‘A present! who are you who talk of presents? See if I do not bring a nobler one than all of yours together!’

translation.en: They continued their insults until Perseus went mad with shame.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 수치심에 미쳐버릴 때까지 그들의 모욕은 계속되었습니다.

translation.en: Barely knowing what he was saying, he cried out.
translation.kr: 그는 자신이 무슨 말을 하는지도 모른 채 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: A present! Who are you to talk of presents?
translation.kr: 선물이라고요! 선물을 논할 자격이나 있습니까?

translation.en: I will bring a nobler gift than all of yours combined!
translation.kr: 여러분의 선물을 모두 합친 것보다 더 고귀한 것을 가져오겠습니다!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: So he said boasting; and yet he felt in his heart that he was braver than all those scoffers, and more able to do some glorious deed.

translation.en: He made this boast out of anger.
translation.kr: 그는 분노에 차서 그렇게 허풍을 떨었습니다.

translation.en: Yet, deep down, he knew he was braver than all those scoffers.
translation.kr: 하지만 마음속 깊은 곳에서는 자신이 그 모든 비웃는 자들보다 더 용감하다는 것을 알고 있었습니다.

translation.en: He felt truly capable of achieving some glorious deed.
translation.kr: 그는 자신이 영광스러운 일을 해낼 수 있다고 굳게 믿었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Hear him!  Hear the boaster!  What is it to be?’ cried they all, laughing louder than ever.

translation.en: Listen to him! Listen to the boaster!
translation.kr: 저놈 말 좀 들어봐! 허풍쟁이 같으니!

translation.en: What will this great gift be?
translation.kr: 그 대단한 선물이 도대체 뭔데?

translation.en: They all cried out, laughing louder than ever.
translation.kr: 그들은 모두 평소보다 더 크게 웃으며 소리쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then his dream at Samos came into his mind, and he cried aloud, ‘The head of the Gorgon.’

translation.en: Then, his dream at Samos flashed into his mind.
translation.kr: 그때 사모스에서 꾼 꿈이 그의 머릿속을 스쳤습니다.

translation.en: The head of the Gorgon, he shouted.
translation.kr: 고르곤의 머리다, 그는 소리쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: He was half afraid after he had said the words for all laughed louder than ever, and Polydectes loudest of all.

translation.en: He felt a surge of fear right after saying the words.
translation.kr: 그는 그 말을 뱉자마자 두려움이 밀려왔습니다.

translation.en: Everyone laughed harder than before.
translation.kr: 모든 사람이 전보다 더 크게 웃어댔기 때문입니다.

translation.en: Polydectes laughed the loudest of them all.
translation.kr: 그중에서도 폴리덱테스의 웃음소리가 가장 컸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘You have promised to bring me the Gorgon’s head?  Then never appear again in this island without it.  Go!’

translation.en: You promised to bring me the head of the Gorgon?
translation.kr: 네가 나에게 고르곤의 머리를 가져오겠다고 약속했느냐?

translation.en: Then never return to this island without it.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 그것 없이는 절대 이 섬에 돌아오지 마라.

translation.en: Go!
translation.kr: 가거라!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Perseus ground his teeth with rage, for he saw that he had fallen into a trap; but his promise lay upon him, and he went out without a word.

translation.en: Perseus ground his teeth in rage.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 분노로 이를 갈았습니다.

translation.en: He realized he had walked right into a trap.
translation.kr: 그는 자신이 함정에 빠졌다는 것을 깨달았습니다.

translation.en: But he was bound by his promise.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 자신의 약속을 지켜야 했습니다.

translation.en: He turned and left without another word.
translation.kr: 그는 아무 말 없이 돌아서서 나갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Down to the cliffs he went, and looked across the broad blue sea; and he wondered if his dream were true, and prayed in the bitterness of his soul.

translation.en: He walked down to the cliffs.
translation.kr: 그는 절벽으로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He stared across the vast blue sea.
translation.kr: 그는 탁 트인 푸른 바다를 응시했습니다.

translation.en: He wondered if his dream had been real.
translation.kr: 그는 자신의 꿈이 진짜였는지 궁금해했습니다.

translation.en: In deep despair, he began to pray.
translation.kr: 깊은 절망 속에서 그는 기도를 시작했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Pallas Athené, was my dream true? and shall I slay the Gorgon?  If thou didst really show me her face, let me not come to shame as a liar and boastful.  Rashly and angrily I promised; but cunningly and patiently will I perform.’

translation.en: Pallas Athene, was my dream true?
translation.kr: 팔라스 아테나여, 제 꿈이 진실이었습니까?

translation.en: Will I truly slay the Gorgon?
translation.kr: 제가 정말로 고르곤을 죽일 수 있습니까?

translation.en: If you really showed me her face, do not let me face shame.
translation.kr: 당신이 진정 저에게 그녀의 얼굴을 보여주셨다면, 제가 수치를 당하지 않게 해주십시오.

translation.en: Do not let them call me a liar and a boaster.
translation.kr: 사람들이 저를 거짓말쟁이나 허풍쟁이라고 부르지 못하게 해주십시오.

translation.en: I made my promise in anger and haste.
translation.kr: 저는 홧김에 성급하게 약속을 해버렸습니다.

translation.en: But I will carry it out with patience and skill.
translation.kr: 하지만 인내심과 지혜를 다해 그것을 해내겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: But there was no answer, nor sign; neither thunder nor any appearance; not even a cloud in the sky.

translation.en: But there was no answer and no sign.
translation.kr: 하지만 아무런 대답도, 징조도 없었습니다.

translation.en: There was no thunder or sudden vision.
translation.kr: 천둥이 치지도 않았고 갑작스러운 환상도 나타나지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Not even a single cloud appeared in the sky.
translation.kr: 하늘에는 구름 한 점조차 보이지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: And three times Perseus called weeping, ‘Rashly and angrily I promised; but cunningly and patiently will I perform.’

translation.en: Perseus wept and called out three times.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 눈물을 흘리며 세 번을 부르짖었습니다.

translation.en: I made my promise in anger and haste.
translation.kr: 저는 홧김에 성급하게 약속을 해버렸습니다.

translation.en: But I will carry it out with patience and skill.
translation.kr: 하지만 인내심과 지혜를 다해 그것을 해내겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then he saw afar off above the sea a small white cloud, as bright as silver.  And it came on, nearer and nearer, till its brightness dazzled his eyes.

translation.en: Then, he noticed a small white cloud far out over the sea.
translation.kr: 그때 그는 바다 저 멀리 떠 있는 작은 흰 구름을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: It shone as brightly as pure silver.
translation.kr: 그것은 순은처럼 눈부시게 빛났습니다.

translation.en: It drifted closer and closer.
translation.kr: 구름은 점점 더 가까이 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: Soon, its brilliant light completely dazzled his eyes.
translation.kr: 이내 그 찬란한 빛이 그의 눈을 완전히 부시게 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Perseus wondered at that strange cloud, for there was no other cloud all round the sky; and he trembled as it touched the cliff below.  And as it touched, it broke, and parted, and within it appeared Pallas Athené, as he had seen her at Samos in his dream, and beside her a young man more light-limbed than the stag, whose eyes were like sparks of fire.  By his side was a scimitar of diamond, all of one clear precious stone, and on his feet were golden sandals, from the heels of which grew living wings.

translation.en: Perseus marveled at the strange cloud.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그 이상한 구름을 보고 경이로움을 느꼈습니다.

translation.en: There were no other clouds anywhere in the sky.
translation.kr: 하늘 어디에도 다른 구름은 없었기 때문입니다.

translation.en: He trembled as it finally touched the cliff beneath him.
translation.kr: 마침내 구름이 발아래 절벽에 닿자 그는 몸을 떨었습니다.

translation.en: As it landed, the cloud split wide open.
translation.kr: 절벽에 내려앉은 구름이 활짝 갈라졌습니다.

translation.en: Inside stood Pallas Athene, just as she had appeared in his dream at Samos.
translation.kr: 그 안에는 그가 사모스에서 꾼 꿈에 나타났던 모습 그대로 팔라스 아테나가 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: Beside her stood a young man, swifter and more graceful than a stag.
translation.kr: 그녀의 곁에는 수사슴보다 더 빠르고 우아해 보이는 한 청년이 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: His bright eyes flashed like sparks of fire.
translation.kr: 그의 빛나는 두 눈은 불꽃처럼 번쩍였습니다.

translation.en: A curved diamond sword hung at his side.
translation.kr: 그의 허리춤에는 휘어진 다이아몬드 검이 매달려 있었습니다.

translation.en: It was carved completely from a single precious stone.
translation.kr: 그것은 거대한 보석 하나를 통째로 깎아 만든 것이었습니다.

translation.en: He wore golden sandals on his feet.
translation.kr: 그는 발에 황금 샌들을 신고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Living wings fluttered directly from the heels of the sandals.
translation.kr: 샌들 뒤꿈치에서는 살아 움직이는 날개가 펄럭이고 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: They looked upon Perseus keenly, and yet they never moved their eyes; and they came up the cliffs towards him more swiftly than the sea-gull, and yet they never moved their feet, nor did the breeze stir the robes about their limbs; only the wings of the youth’s sandals quivered, like a hawk’s when he hangs above the cliff.  And Perseus fell down and worshipped, for he knew that they were more than man.

translation.en: They stared keenly at Perseus without even blinking.
translation.kr: 그들은 눈도 깜박이지 않은 채 페르세우스를 뚫어지게 바라보았습니다.

translation.en: They glided up the cliff toward him faster than a seagull.
translation.kr: 그들은 갈매기보다 더 빠른 속도로 절벽 위로 미끄러지듯 그에게 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: Yet, they never moved their feet at all.
translation.kr: 하지만 그들은 발을 전혀 움직이지 않았습니다.

translation.en: The ocean breeze did not even stir their flowing robes.
translation.kr: 바닷바람조차 그들의 펄럭이는 옷자락을 흔들지 못했습니다.

translation.en: Only the wings on the young man's sandals fluttered.
translation.kr: 오직 청년의 샌들에 달린 날개만이 퍼덕였습니다.

translation.en: They quivered like a hawk hovering high above a cliff.
translation.kr: 절벽 위를 맴도는 매처럼 날개가 파르르 떨렸습니다.

translation.en: Perseus immediately fell to his knees in awe.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 경외심에 사로잡혀 즉시 무릎을 꿇었습니다.

translation.en: He knew at once that they were divine immortals.
translation.kr: 그는 단번에 그들이 신성한 불멸의 존재라는 것을 알았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: But Athené stood before him and spoke gently, and bid him have no fear. Then—

translation.en: But Athene stood before him and spoke gently.
translation.kr: 하지만 아테나가 그의 앞에 서서 다정하게 말했습니다.

translation.en: She told him not to be afraid.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그에게 두려워하지 말라고 당부했습니다.

translation.en: Then she spoke.
translation.kr: 그리고 그녀가 입을 열었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Perseus,’ she said, ‘he who overcomes in one trial merits thereby a sharper trial still.  You have braved Polydectes, and done manfully. Dare you brave Medusa the Gorgon?’

translation.en: Perseus, she said, anyone who survives one trial deserves an even harder one.
translation.kr: 페르세우스, 하나의 시련을 이겨낸 자는 더 가혹한 시련을 마주할 자격이 있습니다.

translation.en: You have bravely faced Polydectes and acted like a true man.
translation.kr: 당신은 폴리데크테스에게 용감하게 맞서며 진정한 사내답게 행동했습니다.

translation.en: Do you dare to face Medusa the Gorgon?
translation.kr: 괴물 메두사에게 맞설 용기가 있습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: And Perseus said, ‘Try me; for since you spoke to me in Samos a new soul has come into my breast, and I should be ashamed not to dare anything which I can do.  Show me, then, how I can do this!’

translation.en: Try me, Perseus replied.
translation.kr: 저를 시험해 보십시오, 페르세우스가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Since you spoke to me in Samos, a new spirit has filled my heart.
translation.kr: 사모스섬에서 당신이 제게 말씀하신 이후로, 새로운 영혼이 제 가슴을 채웠습니다.

translation.en: I would be ashamed to avoid any challenge I am capable of facing.
translation.kr: 제가 할 수 있는 일을 피한다면 몹시 부끄러울 것입니다.

translation.en: Show me how I can accomplish this!
translation.kr: 이 일을 어떻게 해낼 수 있는지 제게 알려주십시오!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Perseus,’ said Athené, ‘think well before you attempt; for this deed requires a seven years’ journey, in which you cannot repent or turn back nor escape; but if your heart fails you, you must die in the Unshapen Land, where no man will ever find your bones.’

translation.en: Think carefully before you try this, Perseus, said Athene.
translation.kr: 시도하기 전에 신중하게 생각하십시오, 페르세우스, 아테나가 말했습니다.

translation.en: This task requires a seven-year journey.
translation.kr: 이 임무는 7년의 기나긴 여정을 필요로 합니다.

translation.en: You cannot change your mind, turn back, or escape.
translation.kr: 도중에 마음을 바꾸거나 되돌아갈 수도, 도망칠 수도 없습니다.

translation.en: If your courage fails, you will die in the Unshapen Land.
translation.kr: 만약 용기를 잃는다면 당신은 형태 없는 땅에서 죽게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: No one will ever find your bones there.
translation.kr: 그곳에서는 아무도 당신의 뼈를 찾지 못할 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Better so than live here, useless and despised,’ said Perseus.  ‘Tell me, then, oh tell me, fair and wise Goddess, of your great kindness and condescension, how I can do but this one thing, and then, if need be, die!’

translation.en: Better to die than live here useless and despised, said Perseus.
translation.kr: 쓸모없이 멸시받으며 이곳에 사느니 차라리 죽는 것이 낫습니다, 페르세우스가 말했습니다.

translation.en: Tell me, beautiful and wise Goddess, out of your great kindness.
translation.kr: 아름답고 지혜로운 여신이여, 당신의 넓은 자비로 제게 말씀해 주십시오.

translation.en: Show me how I can accomplish just this one thing.
translation.kr: 제가 이 단 하나의 일만이라도 어떻게 이룰 수 있는지 알려주십시오.

translation.en: Then I am willing to die if I must!
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 필요하다면 기꺼이 죽음을 맞이하겠습니다!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then Athené smiled and said—

translation.en: Athene smiled and spoke.
translation.kr: 아테나가 미소를 지으며 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘Be patient, and listen; for if you forget my words, you will indeed die. You must go northward to the country of the Hyperboreans, who live beyond the pole, at the sources of the cold north wind, till you find the three Gray Sisters, who have but one eye and one tooth between them.  You must ask them the way to the Nymphs, the daughters of the Evening Star, who dance about the golden tree, in the Atlantic island of the west.  They will tell you the way to the Gorgon, that you may slay her, my enemy, the mother of monstrous beasts.  Once she was a maiden as beautiful as morn, till in her pride she sinned a sin at which the sun hid his face; and from that day her hair was turned to vipers, and her hands to eagle’s claws; and her heart was filled with shame and rage, and her lips with bitter venom; and her eyes became so terrible that whosoever looks on them is turned to stone; and her children are the winged horse and the giant of the golden sword; and her grandchildren are Echidna the witch-adder, and Geryon the three-headed tyrant, who feeds his herds beside the herds of hell.  So she became the sister of the Gorgons, Stheino and Euryte the abhorred, the daughters of the Queen of the Sea. Touch them not, for they are immortal; but bring me only Medusa’s head.’

translation.en: Be patient and listen carefully.
translation.kr: 인내심을 갖고 잘 들으십시오.

translation.en: If you forget my words, you will die.
translation.kr: 제 말을 잊으면 목숨을 잃게 됩니다.

translation.en: Travel north to the land of the Hyperboreans.
translation.kr: 북쪽으로 가서 히페르보레아인들의 땅으로 향하십시오.

translation.en: They live beyond the North Pole where the freezing winds begin.
translation.kr: 그들은 매서운 북풍이 시작되는 북극 너머에 살고 있습니다.

translation.en: Keep going until you find the three Gray Sisters.
translation.kr: 세 명의 늙은 자매를 찾을 때까지 계속 가야 합니다.

translation.en: They share only one eye and one tooth among them.
translation.kr: 그들은 눈 하나와 이빨 하나를 셋이서 함께 사용합니다.

translation.en: Ask them the way to the Nymphs, the daughters of the Evening Star.
translation.kr: 그들에게 저녁별의 딸들인 요정들에게 가는 길을 물으십시오.

translation.en: These Nymphs dance around a golden tree on a western Atlantic island.
translation.kr: 그 요정들은 서쪽 대서양의 어느 섬에 있는 황금 나무 주위에서 춤을 춥니다.

translation.en: They will show you the path to the Gorgon.
translation.kr: 그들이 고르곤에게 가는 길을 알려줄 것입니다.

translation.en: Then you can slay my enemy, the mother of monstrous beasts.
translation.kr: 그러면 당신은 괴물들의 어미이자 나의 원수인 그녀를 베어버릴 수 있습니다.

translation.en: She was once a maiden as beautiful as the morning.
translation.kr: 그녀는 한때 아침처럼 아름다운 처녀였습니다.

translation.en: But she committed a sin of pride so terrible the sun hid its face.
translation.kr: 하지만 그녀는 너무나 끔찍한 오만의 죄를 저질러 태양마저 얼굴을 가릴 정도였습니다.

translation.en: From that day, her hair turned into venomous snakes.
translation.kr: 그날 이후 그녀의 머리카락은 독사로 변해버렸습니다.

translation.en: Her hands became the sharp claws of an eagle.
translation.kr: 그녀의 손은 날카로운 독수리의 발톱이 되었습니다.

translation.en: Her heart filled with shame and rage, and her lips dripped poison.
translation.kr: 그녀의 심장은 수치심과 분노로 가득 찼고, 입술에서는 독이 흘러내렸습니다.

translation.en: Her eyes became so terrible that anyone who looks at her turns to stone.
translation.kr: 그녀의 눈은 너무나 무시무시해져서, 그녀를 보는 자는 누구든 돌로 변하게 됩니다.

translation.en: Her children are the winged horse and the giant with the golden sword.
translation.kr: 그녀의 자식들은 날개 달린 말과 황금 검을 든 거인입니다.

translation.en: Her grandchildren include the witch-adder Echidna and the tyrant Geryon.
translation.kr: 그녀의 손주들은 마녀 독사 에키드나와 폭군 게리온입니다.

translation.en: Geryon has three heads and feeds his herds beside the herds of hell.
translation.kr: 머리가 셋 달린 게리온은 지옥의 무리 곁에서 자신의 가축들을 먹입니다.

translation.en: She became the sister of the horrifying Gorgons, Stheino and Euryte.
translation.kr: 그녀는 끔찍한 고르곤 자매인 스테이노와 에우리알레의 자매가 되었습니다.

translation.en: They are the daughters of the Queen of the Sea.
translation.kr: 그들은 바다의 여왕의 딸들입니다.

translation.en: Do not touch them, for they are immortal.
translation.kr: 그들은 불사신이니 절대 건드리지 마십시오.

translation.en: Just bring me the head of Medusa.
translation.kr: 오직 메두사의 머리만 내게 가져오십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘And I will bring it!’ said Perseus; ‘but how am I to escape her eyes? Will she not freeze me too into stone?’

translation.en: I will bring it to you! said Perseus.
translation.kr: 제가 그것을 가져오겠습니다! 페르세우스가 말했습니다.

translation.en: But how can I escape her deadly eyes?
translation.kr: 하지만 그녀의 치명적인 눈길을 어떻게 피할 수 있습니까?

translation.en: Will she not turn me into stone as well?
translation.kr: 저마저도 돌로 만들어버리지 않겠습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘You shall take this polished shield,’ said Athené, ‘and when you come near her look not at her herself, but at her image in the brass; so you may strike her safely.  And when you have struck off her head, wrap it, with your face turned away, in the folds of the goat-skin on which the shield hangs, the hide of Amaltheié, the nurse of the Ægis-holder.  So you will bring it safely back to me, and win to yourself renown, and a place among the heroes who feast with the Immortals upon the peak where no winds blow.’

translation.en: You will take this polished shield, said Athene.
translation.kr: 이 빛나는 방패를 가져가십시오, 아테나가 말했습니다.

translation.en: When you get close to her, do not look directly at her.
translation.kr: 그녀에게 다가갈 때 절대 그녀를 직접 쳐다보아서는 안 됩니다.

translation.en: Look only at her reflection in the brass to strike her safely.
translation.kr: 방패에 비친 그녀의 모습만 보아야 안전하게 공격할 수 있습니다.

translation.en: Once you chop off her head, turn your face away immediately.
translation.kr: 그녀의 머리를 베어낸 후에는 즉시 고개를 돌리십시오.

translation.en: Wrap the head in the goatskin that holds this shield.
translation.kr: 그리고 방패가 매달린 염소 가죽에 그 머리를 감싸십시오.

translation.en: It is the hide of Amalthea, the sacred nurse of Zeus.
translation.kr: 그것은 제우스를 키운 성스러운 유모 아말테이아의 가죽입니다.

translation.en: This way, you will bring the head safely back to me.
translation.kr: 이렇게 하면 그 머리를 제게 안전하게 가져올 수 있을 것입니다.

translation.en: You will win great fame for yourself.
translation.kr: 당신은 위대한 명성을 얻게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: You will earn a place among the heroes who feast with the gods on the windless peaks.
translation.kr: 또한 바람 없는 산봉우리에서 신들과 함께 연회를 즐기는 영웅들의 자리에 오를 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus said, ‘I will go, though I die in going.  But how shall I cross the seas without a ship?  And who will show me my way?  And when I find her, how shall I slay her, if her scales be iron and brass?’

translation.en: I will go, even if it costs my life, Perseus said.
translation.kr: 목숨을 잃는 한이 있더라도 가겠습니다, 페르세우스가 말했습니다.

translation.en: But how can I cross the seas without a ship?
translation.kr: 하지만 배도 없이 어떻게 바다를 건널 수 있습니까?

translation.en: Who will guide me on my journey?
translation.kr: 누가 제 여정을 안내해 주겠습니까?

translation.en: And when I find her, how can I kill her if she has armor of iron and brass?
translation.kr: 게다가 그녀를 찾는다 해도, 무쇠와 놋쇠 같은 비늘을 가졌다면 어떻게 죽일 수 있단 말입니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then the young man spoke: ‘These sandals of mine will bear you across the seas, and over hill and dale like a bird, as they bear me all day long; for I am Hermes, the far-famed Argus-slayer, the messenger of the Immortals who dwell on Olympus.’

translation.en: Then the young man spoke to him.
translation.kr: 그때 그 젊은 남자가 그에게 입을 열었습니다.

translation.en: These sandals of mine will carry you across the oceans.
translation.kr: 내 이 샌들이 당신을 바다 건너로 데려다줄 것입니다.

translation.en: They will fly you over hills and valleys like a bird.
translation.kr: 새처럼 언덕과 계곡을 넘어 날아갈 수 있게 해줄 것입니다.

translation.en: They carry me in this exact way all day long.
translation.kr: 하루 종일 나를 데리고 다니는 것과 똑같은 방식입니다.

translation.en: I am Hermes, the famous slayer of Argus.
translation.kr: 나는 아르고스를 물리친 것으로 유명한 헤르메스입니다.

translation.en: I am the messenger of the gods who live on Mount Olympus.
translation.kr: 나는 올림포스산에 사는 신들의 전령입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus fell down and worshipped, while the young man spoke again:

translation.en: Perseus immediately fell to his knees and worshipped him.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 즉시 무릎을 꿇고 그를 경배했습니다.

translation.en: The young man continued to speak.
translation.kr: 젊은 남자는 계속해서 말을 이었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘The sandals themselves will guide you on the road, for they are divine and cannot stray; and this sword itself, the Argus-slayer, will kill her, for it is divine, and needs no second stroke.  Arise, and gird them on, and go forth.’

translation.en: The divine sandals will guide you and never lose the way.
translation.kr: 신성한 샌들이 당신을 안내할 것이니 절대 길을 잃지 않을 것입니다.

translation.en: This magical sword will kill her with a single strike.
translation.kr: 이 마법의 검은 단 일격에 그녀를 베어버릴 것입니다.

translation.en: Stand up, put them on, and begin your journey.
translation.kr: 일어나서 이것들을 착용하고 여정을 떠나십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: So Perseus arose, and girded on the sandals and the sword.

translation.en: Perseus stood up and strapped on the sandals and the sword.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 일어나 샌들과 검을 착용했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: And Athené cried, ‘Now leap from the cliff and be gone.’

translation.en: Now leap from the cliff and go! Athene commanded.
translation.kr: 이제 절벽에서 뛰어내려 떠나십시오! 아테나가 명령했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: But Perseus lingered.

translation.en: But Perseus hesitated.
translation.kr: 하지만 페르세우스는 주저했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘May I not bid farewell to my mother and to Dictys?  And may I not offer burnt-offerings to you, and to Hermes the far-famed Argus-slayer, and to Father Zeus above?’

translation.en: May I not say goodbye to my mother and Dictys?
translation.kr: 어머니와 딕티스에게 작별 인사를 할 수는 없습니까?

translation.en: Shouldn't I offer sacrifices to you and to Hermes?
translation.kr: 당신과 헤르메스에게 제물을 바쳐야 하지 않겠습니까?

translation.en: And must I not make an offering to Father Zeus above?
translation.kr: 그리고 위대한 제우스 아버지께도 제물을 올려야 하지 않습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: ‘You shall not bid farewell to your mother, lest your heart relent at her weeping.  I will comfort her and Dictys until you return in peace.  Nor shall you offer burnt-offerings to the Olympians; for your offering shall be Medusa’s head.  Leap, and trust in the armour of the Immortals.’

translation.en: You must not say goodbye to your mother.
translation.kr: 당신의 어머니에게 작별 인사를 해서는 안 됩니다.

translation.en: Her tears might weaken your resolve.
translation.kr: 그녀의 눈물을 보면 당신의 결심이 흔들릴 수 있습니다.

translation.en: I will comfort her and Dictys until you return safely.
translation.kr: 당신이 무사히 돌아올 때까지 내가 그녀와 딕티스를 위로하겠습니다.

translation.en: Do not offer sacrifices to the gods right now.
translation.kr: 지금은 신들에게 제물을 바치지 마십시오.

translation.en: The head of Medusa will be your ultimate offering.
translation.kr: 메두사의 머리가 당신의 최고의 제물이 될 것입니다.

translation.en: Leap from the cliff and trust in this divine armor.
translation.kr: 절벽에서 뛰어내리고 이 신성한 무구들을 믿으십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus looked down the cliff and shuddered; but he was ashamed to show his dread.  Then he thought of Medusa and the renown before him, and he leaped into the empty air.

translation.en: Perseus looked down the steep cliff and shuddered.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 가파른 절벽 아래를 내려다보며 몸서리쳤습니다.

translation.en: He was too ashamed to show his deep fear.
translation.kr: 그는 너무 부끄러워서 자신의 깊은 두려움을 드러낼 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: He thought of Medusa and the great glory waiting for him.
translation.kr: 그는 메두사와 자신을 기다리는 위대한 영광을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: Then he leaped bravely into the empty air.
translation.kr: 그리고 그는 허공을 향해 용감하게 몸을 던졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Perseus Vowed a Rash Vow
paragraphs.raw: And behold, instead of falling he floated, and stood, and ran along the sky.  He looked back, but Athené had vanished, and Hermes; and the sandals led him on northward ever, like a crane who follows the spring toward the Ister fens.

translation.en: To his amazement, he floated instead of falling.
translation.kr: 놀랍게도 그는 떨어지지 않고 공중에 떠올랐습니다.

translation.en: He stood upright and began to run across the sky.
translation.kr: 그는 똑바로 서서 하늘을 가로질러 달리기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: He looked back, but Athene and Hermes had vanished.
translation.kr: 그가 뒤돌아보았지만, 아테나와 헤르메스는 이미 사라지고 없었습니다.

translation.en: The sandals carried him ever northward.
translation.kr: 샌들은 그를 계속해서 북쪽으로 데려갔습니다.

translation.en: He flew like a crane chasing the spring toward the marshes.
translation.kr: 그는 봄을 좇아 습지로 날아가는 두루미처럼 하늘을 날았습니다.

chapters.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: PART III HOW PERSEUS SLEW THE GORGON

translation.en: Part 3: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
translation.kr: [3부: 페르세우스가 고르고를 물리치다]

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: So Perseus started on his journey, going dry-shod over land and sea; and his heart was high and joyful, for the winged sandals bore him each day a seven days’ journey.

translation.en: Perseus began his journey, crossing land and sea without getting wet.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 바다와 육지를 건너며 발을 적시지 않고 여행을 시작했습니다.

translation.en: His heart was full of joy and courage.
translation.kr: 그의 마음은 기쁨과 용기로 가득 찼습니다.

translation.en: The winged sandals carried him a seven days' distance in a single day.
translation.kr: 날개 달린 샌들이 하루 만에 칠 일 거리를 날아갈 수 있게 해주었기 때문입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: And he went by Cythnus, and by Ceos, and the pleasant Cyclades to Attica; and past Athens and Thebes, and the Copaic lake, and up the vale of Cephissus, and past the peaks of Œta and Pindus, and over the rich Thessalian plains, till the sunny hills of Greece were behind him, and before him were the wilds of the north.  Then he passed the Thracian mountains, and many a barbarous tribe, Pæons and Dardans and Triballi, till he came to the Ister stream, and the dreary Scythian plains.  And he walked across the Ister dry-shod, and away through the moors and fens, day and night toward the bleak north-west, turning neither to the right hand nor the left, till he came to the Unshapen Land, and the place which has no name.

translation.en: He flew past numerous islands, lakes, and valleys.
translation.kr: 그는 수많은 섬과 호수, 계곡을 지나쳐 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: He crossed over rich plains and towering mountain peaks.
translation.kr: 풍요로운 평원과 높이 솟은 산봉우리들도 넘어갔습니다.

translation.en: Soon, the sunny hills of Greece were far behind him.
translation.kr: 머지않아 햇살 가득한 그리스의 언덕들은 그의 뒤편으로 멀어졌습니다.

translation.en: Before him lay the untamed wilderness of the north.
translation.kr: 이제 그의 앞에는 길들여지지 않은 북쪽의 황야가 펼쳐져 있었습니다.

translation.en: He passed rugged mountains and many fierce tribes.
translation.kr: 그는 험준한 산맥과 수많은 사나운 부족들을 지나쳤습니다.

translation.en: At last, he reached a broad river and dreary, empty plains.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 거대한 강과 쓸쓸하고 텅 빈 평원에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: He walked right over the water without sinking.
translation.kr: 그는 물에 빠지지 않고 강 위를 걸어서 건넜습니다.

translation.en: He traveled day and night through swamps and marshes.
translation.kr: 그는 밤낮으로 늪과 습지를 통과하며 이동했습니다.

translation.en: He headed strictly toward the bleak northwest.
translation.kr: 그는 황량한 북서쪽을 향해 곧장 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he arrived at the Unshapen Land, a place with no name.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 이름조차 없는 형체 없는 땅에 이르렀습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: And seven days he walked through it, on a path which few can tell; for those who have trodden it like least to speak of it, and those who go there again in dreams are glad enough when they awake; till he came to the edge of the everlasting night, where the air was full of feathers, and the soil was hard with ice; and there at last he found the three Gray Sisters, by the shore of the freezing sea, nodding upon a white log of drift-wood, beneath the cold white winter moon; and they chaunted a low song together, ‘Why the old times were better than the new.’

translation.en: He walked for seven days along a hidden, terrible path.
translation.kr: 그는 칠 일 동안 숨겨진 끔찍한 길을 따라 걸었습니다.

translation.en: Those who walk it refuse to speak of it.
translation.kr: 이 길을 걷는 자들은 그곳에 대해 말하기를 거부합니다.

translation.en: He reached the edge of everlasting night.
translation.kr: 그는 영원한 밤이 시작되는 끝자락에 다다랐습니다.

translation.en: The air was thick with falling snow, and the ground was frozen hard.
translation.kr: 공기 중에는 눈보라가 흩날렸고, 땅은 단단하게 얼어붙어 있었습니다.

translation.en: There he found the three Gray Sisters by the freezing sea.
translation.kr: 그곳 얼어붙은 바닷가에서 그는 세 명의 늙은 자매들을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: They nodded on a white log of driftwood beneath the cold moon.
translation.kr: 그들은 차가운 달빛 아래 하얀 유목 위에 앉아 꾸벅꾸벅 졸고 있었습니다.

translation.en: They softly chanted a song about how the old times were better.
translation.kr: 그들은 옛 시절이 더 좋았다는 노래를 나지막이 흥얼거렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: There was no living thing around them, not a fly, not a moss upon the rocks.  Neither seal nor sea-gull dare come near, lest the ice should clutch them in its claws.  The surge broke up in foam, but it fell again in flakes of snow; and it frosted the hair of the three Gray Sisters, and the bones in the ice-cliff above their heads.  They passed the eye from one to the other, but for all that they could not see; and they passed the tooth from one to the other, but for all that they could not eat; and they sat in the full glare of the moon, but they were none the warmer for her beams.  And Perseus pitied the three Gray Sisters; but they did not pity themselves.

translation.en: There was no living thing around them at all.
translation.kr: 그들 주위에는 살아있는 것이라곤 전혀 없었습니다.

translation.en: No flies buzzed, and no moss grew on the rocks.
translation.kr: 파리 한 마리 날아다니지 않았고 바위에 이끼조차 없었습니다.

translation.en: Seals and seagulls stayed far away to avoid the freezing ice.
translation.kr: 물개와 갈매기들도 얼어붙을까 두려워 멀리 떨어져 있었습니다.

translation.en: The waves crashed and turned into falling snow.
translation.kr: 파도는 부서지며 내리는 눈송이로 변했습니다.

translation.en: The snow covered the sisters' hair and the icy cliffs above.
translation.kr: 그 눈은 자매들의 머리카락과 머리 위 얼음 절벽을 하얗게 뒤덮었습니다.

translation.en: They passed a single eye back and forth, but they could not see.
translation.kr: 그들은 단 하나뿐인 눈을 서로 번갈아 가졌지만 앞을 보지 못했습니다.

translation.en: They passed a single tooth back and forth, but they could not eat.
translation.kr: 단 하나뿐인 치아도 번갈아 가졌지만 아무것도 먹을 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: The bright moon brought them no warmth.
translation.kr: 밝은 달빛도 그들에게는 어떤 온기도 주지 못했습니다.

translation.en: Perseus felt pity for them, though they felt none for themselves.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그들을 불쌍히 여겼지만, 정작 그들은 스스로를 연민하지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: So he said, ‘Oh, venerable mothers, wisdom is the daughter of old age. You therefore should know many things.  Tell me, if you can, the path to the Gorgon.’

translation.en: Venerable mothers, wisdom is the daughter of old age, he said.
translation.kr: 존경하는 어머니들, 지혜는 노년의 딸과 같습니다, 하고 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: You must know many things.
translation.kr: 여러분은 분명 많은 것을 알고 계실 것입니다.

translation.en: Tell me, if you can, the path to the Gorgon.
translation.kr: 고르고에게 가는 길을 알고 계시다면 제게 알려 주십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then one cried, ‘Who is this who reproaches us with old age?’  And another, ‘This is the voice of one of the children of men.’

translation.en: Who is this that insults us with old age? one cried.
translation.kr: 누가 감히 우리의 늙은 모습을 모욕하는가? 하고 한 명이 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: This is the voice of a mortal, another added.
translation.kr: 이것은 인간의 목소리입니다, 하고 다른 한 명이 덧붙였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: And he, ‘I do not reproach, but honour your old age, and I am one of the sons of men and of the heroes.  The rulers of Olympus have sent me to you to ask the way to the Gorgon.’

translation.en: I do not insult you, but honor your age, he replied.
translation.kr: 저는 모욕하는 것이 아니라 여러분의 연륜을 존중하는 것입니다, 하고 그가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: I am a mortal and a hero.
translation.kr: 저는 인간이자 영웅입니다.

translation.en: The rulers of Olympus sent me to ask you the way to the Gorgon.
translation.kr: 올림포스의 지배자들이 제게 고르고에게 가는 길을 물어보라며 이곳으로 보냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then one, ‘There are new rulers in Olympus, and all new things are bad.’ And another, ‘We hate your rulers, and the heroes, and all the children of men.  We are the kindred of the Titans, and the Giants, and the Gorgons, and the ancient monsters of the deep.’  And another, ‘Who is this rash and insolent man who pushes unbidden into our world?’  And the first, ‘There never was such a world as ours, nor will be; if we let him see it, he will spoil it all.’

translation.en: There are new rulers in Olympus, and all new things are bad, one said.
translation.kr: 올림포스에 새로운 지배자들이 생겼지만, 새로운 것은 모두 나쁩니다, 하고 한 명이 말했습니다.

translation.en: We hate your rulers, the heroes, and all mortals, another added.
translation.kr: 우리는 당신의 지배자들과 영웅들, 그리고 모든 인간을 증오합니다, 하고 다른 한 명이 덧붙였습니다.

translation.en: We are kin to the Titans, Giants, Gorgons, and ancient sea monsters.
translation.kr: 우리는 티탄, 거인족, 고르고, 그리고 고대 바다 괴물들의 친척입니다.

translation.en: Who is this rude man pushing into our world? asked another.
translation.kr: 초대받지도 않고 우리 세계에 밀고 들어온 이 무례한 자는 누구인가? 하고 다른 한 명이 물었습니다.

translation.en: If we let him see it, he will ruin it all, said the first.
translation.kr: 만약 그가 이곳을 보게 내버려 둔다면 그가 모든 것을 망칠 것입니다, 하고 첫 번째 자매가 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then one cried, ‘Give me the eye, that I may see him;’ and another, ‘Give me the tooth, that I may bite him.’  But Perseus, when he saw that they were foolish and proud, and did not love the children of men, left off pitying them, and said to himself, ‘Hungry men must needs be hasty; if I stay making many words here, I shall be starved.’  Then he stepped close to them, and watched till they passed the eye from hand to hand.  And as they groped about between themselves, he held out his own hand gently, till one of them put the eye into it, fancying that it was the hand of her sister.  Then he sprang back, and laughed, and cried—

translation.en: Give me the eye so I can see him, one cried.
translation.kr: 그자를 볼 수 있게 내게 눈을 주시오, 하고 한 명이 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Give me the tooth so I can bite him, said another.
translation.kr: 그자를 물어뜯을 수 있게 내게 이빨을 주시오, 하고 다른 한 명이 말했습니다.

translation.en: Perseus saw they were foolish, proud, and hated mortals.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그들이 어리석고 교만하며 인간을 미워한다는 것을 알았습니다.

translation.en: He stopped feeling pity for them.
translation.kr: 그는 그들에 대한 동정심을 거두었습니다.

translation.en: I will starve if I waste time talking here, he thought.
translation.kr: 여기서 계속 말을 낭비하다가는 내가 먼저 굶어 죽겠군, 하고 그는 생각했습니다.

translation.en: He stepped close and watched them pass the eye hand to hand.
translation.kr: 그는 가까이 다가가 그들이 손에서 손으로 눈을 건네는 모습을 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: As they groped around, he gently held out his own hand.
translation.kr: 그들이 더듬거릴 때, 그는 조용히 자신의 손을 내밀었습니다.

translation.en: One of them placed the eye in his hand, thinking it was her sister's.
translation.kr: 자매 중 한 명이 자기 자매의 손인 줄 알고 그의 손에 눈을 쥐여 주었습니다.

translation.en: He sprang back and laughed aloud.
translation.kr: 그는 뒤로 물러서며 크게 웃었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: ‘Cruel and proud old women, I have your eye; and I will throw it into the sea, unless you tell me the path to the Gorgon, and swear to me that you tell me right.’

translation.en: Cruel and proud old women, I have your eye, he declared.
translation.kr: 잔인하고 교만한 노파들이여, 내가 당신들의 눈을 가졌습니다, 하고 그가 선언했습니다.

translation.en: I will throw it into the sea unless you tell me the way to the Gorgon.
translation.kr: 고르고에게 가는 길을 알려주지 않으면 이것을 바다에 던져버리겠습니다.

translation.en: You must swear to tell me the truth.
translation.kr: 제게 진실만을 말하겠다고 맹세하십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then they wept, and chattered, and scolded; but in vain.  They were forced to tell the truth, though, when they told it, Perseus could hardly make out the road.

translation.en: They wept, chattered, and scolded, but it was useless.
translation.kr: 그들은 울고 떠들며 욕을 했지만 아무 소용이 없었습니다.

translation.en: They had to tell the truth.
translation.kr: 그들은 진실을 말할 수밖에 없었습니다.

translation.en: Even then, Perseus could barely understand the directions.
translation.kr: 그럼에도 페르세우스는 그들이 알려주는 길을 거의 이해할 수 없었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: ‘You must go,’ they said, ‘foolish boy, to the southward, into the ugly glare of the sun, till you come to Atlas the Giant, who holds the heaven and the earth apart.  And you must ask his daughters, the Hesperides, who are young and foolish like yourself.  And now give us back our eye, for we have forgotten all the rest.’

translation.en: You must go south into the sun's glare, foolish boy, they said.
translation.kr: 어리석은 소년아, 남쪽의 강렬한 태양 빛 속으로 향해야 한다, 하고 그들이 말했습니다.

translation.en: Keep going until you find Atlas the Giant.
translation.kr: 거인 아틀라스를 만날 때까지 계속 가거라.

translation.en: He is the one who holds the heaven and earth apart.
translation.kr: 그는 하늘과 땅을 떨어뜨려 떠받치고 있는 자란다.

translation.en: You must ask his daughters, who are young and foolish like you.
translation.kr: 너처럼 어리고 어리석은 그의 딸들에게 길을 물어보아라.

translation.en: Now give us back our eye, for we have forgotten the rest.
translation.kr: 우리는 나머지를 잊어버렸으니 이제 우리 눈을 돌려다오.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: So Perseus gave them back their eye; but instead of using it, they nodded and fell fast asleep, and were turned into blocks of ice, till the tide came up and washed them all away.  And now they float up and down like icebergs for ever, weeping whenever they meet the sunshine, and the fruitful summer and the warm south wind, which fill young hearts with joy.

translation.en: Perseus gave them back their eye.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그들에게 눈을 돌려주었습니다.

translation.en: Instead of using it, they fell fast asleep.
translation.kr: 하지만 그들은 눈을 사용하는 대신 곧장 깊은 잠에 빠졌습니다.

translation.en: They turned into blocks of ice until the tide washed them away.
translation.kr: 그들은 밀물이 들어와 휩쓸어 갈 때까지 거대한 얼음덩어리로 변해버렸습니다.

translation.en: Now they float forever like icebergs.
translation.kr: 이제 그들은 영원히 빙산처럼 떠돌아다닙니다.

translation.en: They weep whenever they meet sunshine and the warm south wind.
translation.kr: 햇빛과 따뜻한 남풍을 만날 때마다 그들은 하염없이 눈물을 흘립니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: But Perseus leaped away to the southward, leaving the snow and the ice behind: past the isle of the Hyperboreans, and the tin isles, and the long Iberian shore, while the sun rose higher day by day upon a bright blue summer sea.  And the terns and the sea-gulls swept laughing round his head, and called to him to stop and play, and the dolphins gambolled up as he passed, and offered to carry him on their backs.  And all night long the sea-nymphs sang sweetly, and the Tritons blew upon their conchs, as they played round Galatæa their queen, in her car of pearled shells. Day by day the sun rose higher, and leaped more swiftly into the sea at night, and more swiftly out of the sea at dawn; while Perseus skimmed over the billows like a sea-gull, and his feet were never wetted; and leapt on from wave to wave, and his limbs were never weary, till he saw far away a mighty mountain, all rose-red in the setting sun.  Its feet were wrapped in forests, and its head in wreaths of cloud; and Perseus knew that it was Atlas, who holds the heavens and the earth apart.

translation.en: Perseus leaped southward, leaving the snow and ice behind.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 눈과 얼음을 뒤로하고 남쪽을 향해 도약했습니다.

translation.en: He passed islands and long coastlines over a bright blue sea.
translation.kr: 그는 눈부시게 푸른 바다 위로 수많은 섬과 긴 해안선을 지나쳤습니다.

translation.en: Seagulls swept laughing around his head, calling him to play.
translation.kr: 갈매기들이 그의 머리 위를 맴돌며 웃으며 놀자고 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Dolphins gamboled as he passed, offering rides on their backs.
translation.kr: 돌고래들도 그가 지나갈 때 장난을 치며 등 위에 태워주겠다고 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: All night long, the sea-nymphs sang sweetly.
translation.kr: 밤새도록 바다의 요정들은 달콤한 노래를 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Perseus skimmed over the waves like a seagull, his feet perfectly dry.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 갈매기처럼 파도 위를 스치듯 날았고, 그의 발은 전혀 젖지 않았습니다.

translation.en: He leaped from wave to wave without ever growing weary.
translation.kr: 그는 지칠 줄 모르고 파도에서 파도로 뛰어올랐습니다.

translation.en: Far away, he finally saw a mighty mountain, red in the setting sun.
translation.kr: 마침내 멀리서 석양에 붉게 물든 거대한 산을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: Its base was wrapped in forests, and its peak was hidden in clouds.
translation.kr: 산의 밑동은 숲으로 덮여 있었고 꼭대기는 구름에 가려져 있었습니다.

translation.en: He knew it was Atlas, holding the heavens and the earth apart.
translation.kr: 그는 그것이 하늘과 땅을 떠받치고 있는 아틀라스라는 것을 알았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: He came to the mountain, and leapt on shore, and wandered upward, among pleasant valleys and waterfalls, and tall trees and strange ferns and flowers; but there was no smoke rising from any glen, nor house, nor sign of man.

translation.en: He came to the mountain and leaped ashore.
translation.kr: 그는 산에 다다라 해안으로 뛰어내렸습니다.

translation.en: He wandered upward among pleasant valleys, waterfalls, and tall trees.
translation.kr: 그는 아름다운 계곡과 폭포, 높은 나무들 사이를 걸어 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: There was no smoke, no house, and no sign of people.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 연기도, 집도, 사람의 흔적도 없었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: At last he heard sweet voices singing; and he guessed that he was come to the garden of the Nymphs, the daughters of the Evening Star.

translation.en: At last, he heard sweet voices singing.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 달콤한 노랫소리를 들었습니다.

translation.en: He guessed he had reached the garden of the Nymphs.
translation.kr: 그는 자신이 요정들의 정원에 도착했음을 직감했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: They sang like nightingales among the thickets, and Perseus stopped to hear their song; but the words which they spoke he could not understand; no, nor no man after him for many a hundred years.  So he stepped forward and saw them dancing, hand in hand around the charmed tree, which bent under its golden fruit; and round the tree-foot was coiled the dragon, old Ladon the sleepless snake, who lies there for ever, listening to the song of the maidens, blinking and watching with dry bright eyes.

translation.en: They sang like nightingales among the thickets.
translation.kr: 그들은 덤불 속에서 나이팅게일처럼 노래했습니다.

translation.en: Perseus stopped to listen, but he could not understand their words.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 멈춰 서서 들었지만 그들의 말을 이해할 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: He stepped forward and saw them dancing around a magical tree.
translation.kr: 그가 앞으로 나아가자, 마법의 나무 주위를 춤추며 도는 그들의 모습이 보였습니다.

translation.en: The tree was heavy with golden fruit.
translation.kr: 그 나무에는 황금빛 열매가 주렁주렁 매달려 있었습니다.

translation.en: A sleepless dragon was coiled around the base of the tree.
translation.kr: 잠들지 않는 용 한 마리가 나무 밑동을 칭칭 감고 있었습니다.

translation.en: It lay there forever, blinking and watching with bright, dry eyes.
translation.kr: 그 용은 영원히 그곳에 머물며 메마르고 빛나는 눈으로 주변을 감시했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus stopped, not because he feared the dragon, but because he was bashful before those fair maids; but when they saw him, they too stopped, and called to him with trembling voices—

translation.en: Perseus stopped, feeling shy before the beautiful maidens.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 아름다운 소녀들 앞에서 부끄러움을 느껴 멈춰 섰습니다.

translation.en: When they saw him, they stopped and called out with trembling voices.
translation.kr: 그들도 그를 보자 춤을 멈추고 떨리는 목소리로 외쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: ‘Who are you?  Are you Heracles the mighty, who will come to rob our garden, and carry off our golden fruit?’  And he answered—

translation.en: Who are you? they asked.
translation.kr: 당신은 누구십니까? 하고 그들이 물었습니다.

translation.en: Are you mighty Heracles, come to steal our golden fruit?
translation.kr: 우리의 황금 열매를 훔치러 온 위대한 헤라클레스입니까?

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: ‘I am not Heracles the mighty, and I want none of your golden fruit. Tell me, fair Nymphs, the way which leads to the Gorgon, that I may go on my way and slay her.’

translation.en: I am not mighty Heracles, and I do not want your fruit, he answered.
translation.kr: 저는 헤라클레스가 아니며 당신들의 열매도 원하지 않습니다, 하고 그가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Tell me the way to the Gorgon so I may slay her.
translation.kr: 제가 고르고를 물리칠 수 있도록 그곳으로 가는 길을 알려주십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: ‘Not yet, not yet, fair boy; come dance with us around the tree in the garden which knows no winter, the home of the south wind and the sun. Come hither and play with us awhile; we have danced alone here for a thousand years, and our hearts are weary with longing for a playfellow. So come, come, come!’

translation.en: Not yet, fair boy, they pleaded.
translation.kr: 아직은 안 됩니다, 아름다운 소년이여, 하고 그들이 애원했습니다.

translation.en: Come dance with us around the tree in this endless summer garden.
translation.kr: 이 영원한 여름의 정원에 있는 나무 주위에서 우리와 함께 춤을 추어요.

translation.en: We have danced alone for a thousand years.
translation.kr: 우리는 천 년 동안 홀로 춤을 추었습니다.

translation.en: Our hearts ache for a playmate.
translation.kr: 우리의 마음은 함께 놀 친구를 간절히 원하고 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: ‘I cannot dance with you, fair maidens; for I must do the errand of the Immortals.  So tell me the way to the Gorgon, lest I wander and perish in the waves.’

translation.en: I cannot dance with you, he replied.
translation.kr: 저는 당신들과 춤을 출 수 없습니다, 하고 그가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: I must complete the mission given by the gods.
translation.kr: 저는 신들이 주신 임무를 완수해야만 합니다.

translation.en: Please tell me the way to the Gorgon.
translation.kr: 부디 제게 고르고에게 가는 길을 알려주십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then they sighed and wept; and answered—‘The Gorgon! she will freeze you into stone.’

translation.en: They sighed and wept, saying, The Gorgon will freeze you into stone.
translation.kr: 그들은 한숨을 쉬며 울면서 말했습니다. 고르고는 당신을 돌로 얼려버릴 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: ‘It is better to die like a hero than to live like an ox in a stall.  The Immortals have lent me weapons, and they will give me wit to use them.’

translation.en: It is better to die like a hero than to live like an ox, he said.
translation.kr: 외양간의 황소처럼 사느니 영웅처럼 죽는 것이 낫습니다, 하고 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: The gods gave me weapons, and they will give me the wits to use them.
translation.kr: 신들께서 제게 무기를 주셨으니 그것을 사용할 지혜도 주실 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then they sighed again and answered, ‘Fair boy, if you are bent on your own ruin, be it so.  We know not the way to the Gorgon; but we will ask the giant Atlas, above upon the mountain peak, the brother of our father, the silver Evening Star.  He sits aloft and sees across the ocean, and far away into the Unshapen Land.’

translation.en: They sighed again and said, If you choose your own ruin, so be it.
translation.kr: 그들은 다시 한숨을 쉬며 말했습니다. 스스로 파멸을 선택한다면 어쩔 수 없지요.

translation.en: We do not know the way, but we will ask our uncle, Atlas.
translation.kr: 우리는 길을 모르지만 삼촌인 아틀라스에게 물어보겠습니다.

translation.en: He sits high above and sees far into the Unshapen Land.
translation.kr: 그는 높은 곳에 앉아 저 멀리 형체 없는 땅까지 내려다보고 계십니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: So they went up the mountain to Atlas their uncle, and Perseus went up with them.  And they found the giant kneeling, as he held the heavens and the earth apart.

translation.en: They went up the mountain to Atlas, and Perseus followed.
translation.kr: 그들은 산을 올라 아틀라스에게 향했고, 페르세우스도 뒤따랐습니다.

translation.en: They found the giant kneeling, holding the heavens and earth apart.
translation.kr: 그들은 하늘과 땅을 밀어내며 무릎을 꿇고 있는 거인을 발견했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: They asked him, and he answered mildly, pointing to the sea-board with his mighty hand, ‘I can see the Gorgons lying on an island far away, but this youth can never come near them, unless he has the hat of darkness, which whosoever wears cannot be seen.’

translation.en: He pointed to the sea with his massive hand.
translation.kr: 그는 거대한 손으로 바다를 가리켰습니다.

translation.en: I can see the Gorgons on a distant island, he answered mildly.
translation.kr: 저 멀리 섬에 고르고들이 있는 것이 보인다, 하고 그가 부드럽게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: But you cannot approach them without the hat of darkness.
translation.kr: 하지만 어둠의 모자가 없다면 결코 그들에게 다가갈 수 없을 것이다.

translation.en: Whoever wears it becomes completely invisible.
translation.kr: 그 모자를 쓰면 누구든 완전히 투명해지지.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then cried Perseus, ‘Where is that hat, that I may find it?’

translation.en: Where is that hat, so I may find it? Perseus cried.
translation.kr: 제가 찾을 수 있도록 그 모자가 어디 있는지 알려주십시오! 하고 페르세우스가 외쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: But the giant smiled.  ‘No living mortal can find that hat, for it lies in the depths of Hades, in the regions of the dead.  But my nieces are immortal, and they shall fetch it for you, if you will promise me one thing and keep your faith.’

translation.en: The giant smiled and said, No living mortal can find it.
translation.kr: 거인은 미소를 지으며 말했습니다. 살아있는 인간은 그것을 찾을 수 없다.

translation.en: It lies deep in Hades, in the realm of the dead.
translation.kr: 그것은 죽은 자들의 영토인 하데스의 깊은 곳에 있단다.

translation.en: But my nieces are immortal and can fetch it for you.
translation.kr: 하지만 내 조카딸들은 불멸의 존재이니 널 위해 가져올 수 있을 것이다.

translation.en: They will do so if you promise me one thing.
translation.kr: 네가 내게 한 가지 약속을 지킨다면 말이다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus promised; and the giant said, ‘When you come back with the head of Medusa, you shall show me the beautiful horror, that I may lose my feeling and my breathing, and become a stone for ever; for it is weary labour for me to hold the heavens and the earth apart.’

translation.en: When you return with Medusa's head, you must show it to me, he said.
translation.kr: 네가 메두사의 머리를 가지고 돌아오면 그것을 내게 보여주어야 한다, 하고 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: I want to become stone forever and lose all feeling.
translation.kr: 나는 감각을 잃고 영원한 돌이 되고 싶단다.

translation.en: Holding the heavens and the earth apart is a weary labor.
translation.kr: 하늘과 땅을 떠받치는 이 노동은 너무나도 고통스럽기 때문이지.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then Perseus promised, and the eldest of the Nymphs went down, and into a dark cavern among the cliffs, out of which came smoke and thunder, for it was one of the mouths of Hell.

translation.en: Perseus promised to do so.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그렇게 하겠다고 약속했습니다.

translation.en: The eldest Nymph descended into a dark cavern full of smoke.
translation.kr: 첫째 요정이 연기가 자욱한 어두운 동굴 속으로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: It was one of the mouths of Hell.
translation.kr: 그곳은 지옥으로 통하는 입구 중 하나였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: And Perseus and the Nymphs sat down seven days, and waited trembling, till the Nymph came up again; and her face was pale, and her eyes dazzled with the light, for she had been long in the dreary darkness; but in her hand was the magic hat.

translation.en: Perseus and the others waited anxiously for seven days.
translation.kr: 페르세우스와 다른 이들은 칠 일 동안 초조하게 기다렸습니다.

translation.en: Finally, she emerged, pale and dazzled by the light.
translation.kr: 마침내 그녀가 창백한 얼굴로 빛에 눈부셔하며 나타났습니다.

translation.en: In her hand, she held the magic hat.
translation.kr: 그녀의 손에는 마법의 모자가 들려 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then all the Nymphs kissed Perseus, and wept over him a long while; but he was only impatient to be gone.  And at last they put the hat upon his head, and he vanished out of their sight.

translation.en: The Nymphs kissed Perseus and wept over him.
translation.kr: 요정들은 페르세우스에게 입을 맞추고 눈물을 흘렸습니다.

translation.en: But he was eager to leave.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 서둘러 떠나고 싶어 했습니다.

translation.en: They placed the hat on his head, and he vanished from sight.
translation.kr: 그들이 모자를 그의 머리에 씌워주자, 그는 시야에서 완전히 사라졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: But Perseus went on boldly, past many an ugly sight, far away into the heart of the Unshapen Land, beyond the streams of Ocean, to the isles where no ship cruises, where is neither night nor day, where nothing is in its right place, and nothing has a name; till he heard the rustle of the Gorgons’ wings and saw the glitter of their brazen talons; and then he knew that it was time to halt, lest Medusa should freeze him into stone.

translation.en: Perseus bravely pressed on into the heart of the Unshapen Land.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 용감하게 형체 없는 땅의 중심부를 향해 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: He traveled far beyond the endless ocean streams.
translation.kr: 그는 끝없는 바다의 물결을 지나 멀리 이동했습니다.

translation.en: He reached isolated islands with no day, night, or names.
translation.kr: 그는 낮도 밤도, 심지어 이름도 없는 고립된 섬들에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: Soon, he heard the rustle of the Gorgons' wings.
translation.kr: 머지않아 그는 고르고들의 날개가 스치는 소리를 들었습니다.

translation.en: He saw the glitter of their brazen claws and stopped to hide.
translation.kr: 그들의 놋쇠 발톱이 빛나는 것을 본 그는 숨기 위해 멈춰 섰습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: He thought awhile with himself, and remembered Athené’s words.  He rose aloft into the air, and held the mirror of the shield above his head, and looked up into it that he might see all that was below him.

translation.en: He paused and remembered Athena's warnings.
translation.kr: 그는 잠시 멈춰 서서 아테나의 경고를 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: He rose high into the air and held the mirrored shield above him.
translation.kr: 그는 공중 높이 솟아올라 거울 방패를 머리 위로 들어 올렸습니다.

translation.en: He looked into it to safely see everything below.
translation.kr: 그는 아래의 모든 것을 안전하게 보기 위해 방패를 들여다보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: And he saw the three Gorgons sleeping as huge as elephants.  He knew that they could not see him, because the hat of darkness hid him; and yet he trembled as he sank down near them, so terrible were those brazen claws.

translation.en: He saw the three sleeping Gorgons, huge as elephants.
translation.kr: 그는 코끼리만큼 거대한 세 명의 고르고가 잠들어 있는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: He knew the hat of darkness kept him hidden.
translation.kr: 어둠의 모자 덕분에 자신의 모습이 보이지 않는다는 것을 알았습니다.

translation.en: Yet, he trembled at the sight of their terrifying claws.
translation.kr: 하지만 그 끔찍한 발톱을 보자 그는 두려움에 떨었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Two of the Gorgons were foul as swine, and lay sleeping heavily, as swine sleep, with their mighty wings outspread; but Medusa tossed to and fro restlessly, and as she tossed Perseus pitied her, she looked so fair and sad.  Her plumage was like the rainbow, and her face was like the face of a nymph, only her eyebrows were knit, and her lips clenched, with everlasting care and pain; and her long neck gleamed so white in the mirror that Perseus had not the heart to strike, and said, ‘Ah, that it had been either of her sisters!’

translation.en: Two of the Gorgons were foul and slept heavily like swine.
translation.kr: 두 명의 고르고는 더러웠고 돼지처럼 깊이 잠들어 있었습니다.

translation.en: But Medusa tossed restlessly, and Perseus pitied her.
translation.kr: 하지만 메두사는 불안하게 뒤척였고, 페르세우스는 그녀를 불쌍하게 여겼습니다.

translation.en: She looked incredibly fair but deeply sad.
translation.kr: 그녀는 믿을 수 없을 만큼 아름다웠지만 깊은 슬픔에 잠겨 있었습니다.

translation.en: Her face was like a nymph's, but filled with endless pain.
translation.kr: 그녀의 얼굴은 요정 같았으나 끝없는 고통으로 가득 차 있었습니다.

translation.en: Her long white neck gleamed so brightly in the mirror.
translation.kr: 그녀의 길고 하얀 목이 거울 속에서 너무나도 눈부시게 빛났습니다.

translation.en: Perseus lost his nerve and wished it had been one of her sisters.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 용기를 잃고 차라리 그녀의 자매 중 한 명이었기를 바랐습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: But as he looked, from among her tresses the vipers’ heads awoke, and peeped up with their bright dry eyes, and showed their fangs, and hissed; and Medusa, as she tossed, threw back her wings and showed her brazen claws; and Perseus saw that, for all her beauty, she was as foul and venomous as the rest.

translation.en: But as he watched, the vipers in her hair awoke and hissed.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 지켜보는 동안 그녀 머리카락의 독사들이 깨어나 쉭쉭거렸습니다.

translation.en: Medusa tossed, showing her deadly brazen claws.
translation.kr: 메두사가 뒤척이며 치명적인 놋쇠 발톱을 드러냈습니다.

translation.en: Perseus realized that beneath her beauty, she was foul and venomous.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그녀의 아름다움 아래에 사악하고 맹독을 품은 본성이 있음을 깨달았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then he came down and stepped to her boldly, and looked steadfastly on his mirror, and struck with Herpé stoutly once; and he did not need to strike again.

translation.en: He stepped down boldly, keeping his eyes fixed on the mirror.
translation.kr: 그는 방패 거울에 시선을 고정한 채 용감하게 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He struck once strongly with his sword, and needed no second strike.
translation.kr: 그는 검으로 강하게 단 한 번 내리쳤고 두 번 칠 필요는 없었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then he wrapped the head in the goat-skin, turning away his eyes, and sprang into the air aloft, faster than he ever sprang before.

translation.en: Averting his eyes, he wrapped the head in the goatskin.
translation.kr: 그는 시선을 돌린 채 염소 가죽으로 그 머리를 감쌌습니다.

translation.en: He sprang back into the air faster than ever before.
translation.kr: 그는 그 어느 때보다 빠르게 공중으로 솟아올랐습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: For Medusa’s wings and talons rattled as she sank dead upon the rocks; and her two foul sisters woke, and saw her lying dead.

translation.en: Medusa's wings and talons rattled as she fell dead on the rocks.
translation.kr: 메두사가 바위 위로 쓰러지며 날개와 발톱이 요란한 소리를 냈습니다.

translation.en: Her two foul sisters woke to find her lifeless body.
translation.kr: 두 명의 사악한 자매가 잠에서 깨어 그녀의 시신을 발견했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Into the air they sprang yelling and looked for him who had done the deed.  Thrice they swung round and round, like hawks who beat for a partridge; and thrice they snuffed round and round, like hounds who draw upon a deer.  At last they struck upon the scent of the blood, and they checked for a moment to make sure; and then on they rushed with a fearful howl, while the wind rattled hoarse in their wings.

translation.en: They sprang into the air yelling, searching for the killer.
translation.kr: 그들은 비명을 지르며 공중으로 뛰어올라 암살자를 찾았습니다.

translation.en: They swung around like hawks hunting for prey.
translation.kr: 그들은 먹이를 찾는 매처럼 주위를 빙빙 돌았습니다.

translation.en: They sniffed the air like hounds tracking a deer.
translation.kr: 그들은 사슴을 추적하는 사냥개처럼 공기 냄새를 맡았습니다.

translation.en: Soon they caught the scent of blood and paused to be sure.
translation.kr: 머지않아 피 냄새를 맡은 그들은 확신하기 위해 잠시 멈췄습니다.

translation.en: Then they rushed forward with a fearful howl, wings rattling wildly.
translation.kr: 그러고는 끔찍한 울음소리를 내며 날개를 퍼덕이며 돌진했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: On they rushed, sweeping and flapping, like eagles after a hare; and Perseus’ blood ran cold, for all his courage, as he saw them come howling on his track; and he cried, ‘Bear me well now, brave sandals, for the hounds of Death are at my heels!’

translation.en: They swept and flapped after him like eagles hunting a hare.
translation.kr: 그들은 토끼를 사냥하는 독수리처럼 날개를 퍼덕이며 그를 쫓았습니다.

translation.en: Perseus' blood ran cold as he saw them howling on his track.
translation.kr: 그들이 울부짖으며 뒤쫓아오는 것을 본 페르세우스는 피가 얼어붙는 듯했습니다.

translation.en: Bear me well, brave sandals, for death is at my heels! he cried.
translation.kr: 부탁한다, 용감한 샌들이여. 죽음이 내 발끝까지 쫓아왔다! 하고 그가 외쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: And well the brave sandals bore him, aloft through cloud and sunshine, across the shoreless sea; and fast followed the hounds of Death, as the roar of their wings came down the wind.  But the roar came down fainter and fainter, and the howl of their voices died away; for the sandals were too swift, even for Gorgons, and by nightfall they were far behind, two black specks in the southern sky, till the sun sank and he saw them no more.

translation.en: The sandals bore him swiftly through clouds and across the sea.
translation.kr: 샌들은 그를 태우고 구름을 뚫고 바다를 건너 빠르게 날았습니다.

translation.en: The roaring wings of the Gorgons followed fast behind him.
translation.kr: 고르고들의 요란한 날갯짓 소리가 그의 뒤를 바짝 쫓았습니다.

translation.en: But gradually, the roar and their howling voices faded away.
translation.kr: 하지만 점차 그들의 요란한 소리와 울부짖음은 희미해졌습니다.

translation.en: His sandals were simply too swift, even for the Gorgons.
translation.kr: 그의 샌들은 고르고들조차 따라잡을 수 없을 만큼 빨랐습니다.

translation.en: By nightfall, they were just two black specks in the sky.
translation.kr: 밤이 되자 그들은 하늘의 검은 점 두 개로 보일 뿐이었습니다.

translation.en: When the sun sank, they vanished entirely.
translation.kr: 해가 저물자 그들은 완전히 사라져 보이지 않게 되었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then he came again to Atlas, and the garden of the Nymphs; and when the giant heard him coming he groaned, and said, ‘Fulfil thy promise to me.’ Then Perseus held up to him the Gorgon’s head, and he had rest from all his toil; for he became a crag of stone, which sleeps for ever far above the clouds.

translation.en: He returned to Atlas and the garden of the Nymphs.
translation.kr: 그는 아틀라스와 요정들의 정원으로 다시 돌아왔습니다.

translation.en: When the giant heard him, he groaned, Fulfill your promise to me.
translation.kr: 거인은 그가 오는 소리를 듣고 신음하며 말했습니다. 내게 한 약속을 지켜라.

translation.en: Perseus held up the Gorgon's head, granting him rest.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 고르고의 머리를 들어 올리자 그에게 안식이 찾아왔습니다.

translation.en: Atlas became a massive stone crag, sleeping forever above the clouds.
translation.kr: 아틀라스는 거대한 돌덩이가 되어 구름 위에서 영원히 잠들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then he thanked the Nymphs, and asked them, ‘By what road shall I go homeward again, for I wandered far round in coming hither?’

translation.en: Perseus thanked the Nymphs and asked for directions home.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 요정들에게 감사 인사를 전하고 집으로 가는 길을 물었습니다.

translation.en: Which way should I go, as I wandered far to get here? he asked.
translation.kr: 이곳에 오느라 멀리 돌아왔으니 이제 어느 길로 가야 합니까? 하고 그는 물었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: And they wept and cried, ‘Go home no more, but stay and play with us, the lonely maidens, who dwell for ever far away from Gods and men.’

translation.en: Do not go home, but stay and play with us, they cried.
translation.kr: 집에 가지 말고 우리와 함께 놀아요, 하고 그들이 울며 애원했습니다.

translation.en: We are lonely maidens living far away from both gods and men.
translation.kr: 우리는 신들과 인간 모두에게서 멀리 떨어져 사는 외로운 소녀들입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: But he refused, and they told him his road, and said, ‘Take with you this magic fruit, which, if you eat once, you will not hunger for seven days. For you must go eastward and eastward ever, over the doleful Lybian shore, which Poseidon gave to Father Zeus, when he burst open the Bosphorus and the Hellespont, and drowned the fair Lectonian land.  And Zeus took that land in exchange, a fair bargain, much bad ground for a little good, and to this day it lies waste and desert with shingle, and rock, and sand.’

translation.en: But he refused, so they told him the way.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 거절하자 그들은 길을 알려주었습니다.

translation.en: Take this magic fruit; if you eat it, you won't hunger for seven days.
translation.kr: 이 마법의 열매를 가져가세요. 한 입만 먹어도 칠 일 동안 배고프지 않을 것입니다.

translation.en: You must fly far eastward over the sad Libyan shore.
translation.kr: 당신은 저 멀리 슬픈 리비아 해안을 넘어 계속 동쪽으로 날아가야 합니다.

translation.en: Poseidon gave it to Zeus after drowning the beautiful Lectonian land.
translation.kr: 그곳은 포세이돈이 아름다운 렉토니아 땅을 물에 잠기게 한 뒤 제우스에게 준 곳입니다.

translation.en: Zeus took it in exchange, trading much bad ground for a little good.
translation.kr: 제우스는 약간의 좋은 땅을 대가로 많은 나쁜 땅을 받는 교환을 수락했습니다.

translation.en: To this day, it remains a wasteland of rock and sand.
translation.kr: 그곳은 오늘날까지도 바위와 모래뿐인 황무지로 남아있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Perseus Slew the Gorgon
paragraphs.raw: Then they kissed Perseus, and wept over him, and he leapt down the mountain, and went on, lessening and lessening like a sea-gull, away and out to sea.

translation.en: The Nymphs kissed him and wept over him one last time.
translation.kr: 요정들은 마지막으로 그에게 입을 맞추고 눈물을 흘렸습니다.

translation.en: He leaped down the mountain and flew out to sea.
translation.kr: 그는 산 아래로 뛰어내려 바다를 향해 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: He grew smaller and smaller, fading away like a distant seagull.
translation.kr: 그는 점점 작아지며 멀리 날아가는 갈매기처럼 시야에서 사라졌습니다.

chapters.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
paragraphs.raw: PART IV HOW PERSEUS CAME TO THE ÆTHIOPS

translation.en: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Aethiops
translation.kr: 제4부: 페르세우스가 에티오피아에 이르다

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
paragraphs.raw: So Perseus flitted onward to the north-east, over many a league of sea, till he came to the rolling sand-hills and the dreary Lybian shore.

translation.en: Perseus flew onward to the northeast over many leagues of sea.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 끝없는 바다를 지나 북동쪽으로 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he reached the rolling sand hills and the dreary Libyan shore.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 굽이치는 모래 언덕과 황량한 리비아 해안에 이르렀습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
paragraphs.raw: And he flitted on across the desert: over rock-ledges, and banks of shingle, and level wastes of sand, and shell-drifts bleaching in the sunshine, and the skeletons of great sea-monsters, and dead bones of ancient giants, strewn up and down upon the old sea-floor.  And as he went the blood-drops fell to the earth from the Gorgon’s head, and became poisonous asps and adders, which breed in the desert to this day.

translation.en: He flew on across the desert over rocky ledges and banks of pebbles.
translation.kr: 그는 암석 지대와 자갈밭을 넘어 사막을 가로질러 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: He passed level wastes of sand and piles of shells bleaching in the sunshine.
translation.kr: 그는 평평한 모래 황무지와 햇빛에 바랜 조개껍데기 더미를 지나쳤습니다.

translation.en: The skeletons of great sea monsters and dead bones of ancient giants were strewn across the old sea floor.
translation.kr: 거대한 바다 괴물의 골격과 고대 거인들의 마른 뼈가 오래된 해저 곳곳에 흩어져 있었습니다.

translation.en: As he traveled, blood fell to the earth from the Gorgon head.
translation.kr: 그가 이동하는 동안 고르곤의 머리에서 핏방울이 땅으로 떨어졌습니다.

translation.en: These drops became the poisonous snakes that breed in the desert to this day.
translation.kr: 이 핏방울들은 오늘날까지도 사막에 서식하는 맹독성 뱀이 되었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
paragraphs.raw: Over the sands he went,—he never knew how far or how long, feeding on the fruit which the Nymphs had given him, till he saw the hills of the Psylli, and the Dwarfs who fought with cranes.  Their spears were of reeds and rushes, and their houses of the egg-shells of the cranes; and Perseus laughed, and went his way to the north-east, hoping all day long to see the blue Mediterranean sparkling, that he might fly across it to his home.

translation.en: He traveled over the sands for an unknown distance and time.
translation.kr: 그는 모래 위를 얼마나 멀리, 얼마나 오랫동안 갔는지 모른 채 여행했습니다.

translation.en: He survived by eating the fruit the nymphs had given him.
translation.kr: 그는 요정들이 준 과일을 먹으며 버텼습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, he saw the hills of the Psylli and the Dwarfs who fought with cranes.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 프실리 언덕과 두루미들과 싸우는 난쟁이들을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Their spears were made of reeds, and their houses were built from crane eggshells.
translation.kr: 그들의 창은 갈대로 만들어졌고, 집은 두루미의 알껍데기로 지어졌습니다.

translation.en: Perseus laughed and continued his way to the northeast.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 웃음을 터뜨리며 북동쪽으로 길을 재촉했습니다.

translation.en: He hoped to see the sparkling blue Mediterranean so he could fly home.
translation.kr: 그는 푸른 지중해가 반짝이는 모습을 보고 무사히 고향으로 날아가기를 온종일 바랐습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
paragraphs.raw: But now came down a mighty wind, and swept him back southward toward the desert.  All day long he strove against it; but even the winged sandals could not prevail.  So he was forced to float down the wind all night; and when the morning dawned there was nothing to be seen, save the same old hateful waste of sand.

translation.en: Suddenly, a mighty wind swept him back southward toward the desert.
translation.kr: 갑자기 강력한 바람이 불어와 그를 사막이 있는 남쪽으로 휩쓸어 갔습니다.

translation.en: He struggled against it all day, but even his winged sandals could not overcome the gale.
translation.kr: 그는 온종일 바람과 맞서 싸웠지만, 날개 달린 샌들조차 폭풍을 이겨낼 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: He was forced to float with the wind all night.
translation.kr: 그는 밤새도록 바람에 떠밀려갈 수밖에 없었습니다.

translation.en: When morning dawned, nothing was visible except the same hateful waste of sand.
translation.kr: 아침이 밝았을 때, 지긋지긋한 모래 황무지 외에는 아무것도 보이지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
paragraphs.raw: And out of the north the sandstorms rushed upon him, blood-red pillars and wreaths, blotting out the noonday sun; and Perseus fled before them, lest he should be choked by the burning dust.  At last the gale fell calm, and he tried to go northward again; but again came down the sandstorms, and swept him back into the waste, and then all was calm and cloudless as before.  Seven days he strove against the storms, and seven days he was driven back, till he was spent with thirst and hunger, and his tongue clove to the roof of his mouth.  Here and there he fancied that he saw a fair lake, and the sunbeams shining on the water; but when he came to it it vanished at his feet, and there was nought but burning sand.  And if he had not been of the race of the Immortals, he would have perished in the waste; but his life was strong within him, because it was more than man’s.

translation.en: Blood-red sandstorms rushed upon him from the north.
translation.kr: 북쪽에서 핏빛 모래폭풍이 그를 덮쳤습니다.

translation.en: They blotted out the noonday sun, and Perseus fled before them to avoid suffocating.
translation.kr: 폭풍이 한낮의 태양을 가려버렸고, 페르세우스는 숨이 막히지 않으려고 도망쳤습니다.

translation.en: When the gale finally calmed, he tried to head north again.
translation.kr: 마침내 강풍이 잦아들자 그는 다시 북쪽으로 향하려 했습니다.

translation.en: But the sandstorms returned and swept him back into the wasteland.
translation.kr: 하지만 모래폭풍이 다시 돌아와 그를 황무지로 휩쓸어 갔습니다.

translation.en: He fought the storms for seven days and was driven back for seven days.
translation.kr: 그는 칠 일 동안 폭풍과 싸웠고, 칠 일 동안 뒤로 밀려났습니다.

translation.en: He was completely exhausted by thirst and hunger.
translation.kr: 그는 갈증과 굶주림으로 완전히 지쳐버렸습니다.

translation.en: His tongue stuck to the roof of his mouth.
translation.kr: 그의 혀는 입천장에 달라붙었습니다.

translation.en: Occasionally, he imagined seeing a beautiful lake sparkling in the sun.
translation.kr: 때때로 그는 햇빛에 반짝이는 아름다운 호수를 본다고 착각했습니다.

translation.en: But when he approached, it vanished into burning sand.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 다가가면 호수는 불타는 모래 속으로 사라졌습니다.

translation.en: If he had not been immortal, he would have died in the wasteland.
translation.kr: 그가 불멸의 존재가 아니었다면 황무지에서 목숨을 잃었을 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
