paragraphs.raw: But at last he said to Pelias, ‘Why do you look so sad, my uncle?  And what did you mean just now when you said that this was a doleful kingdom, and its ruler a miserable man?’

translation.en: But at last he asked Pelias a question.
translation.kr: 하지만 마침내 그는 펠리아스에게 질문했습니다.

translation.en: Why do you look so sad, my uncle?
translation.kr: 숙부님, 왜 그렇게 슬퍼 보이십니까?

translation.en: What did you mean when you called this a doleful kingdom?
translation.kr: 아까 이 왕국을 슬픈 왕국이라 하신 건 무슨 뜻입니까?

translation.en: Why would its ruler be a miserable man?
translation.kr: 왜 이 왕국의 통치자가 비참한 사람이 된다는 것입니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: Then Pelias sighed heavily again and again and again, like a man who had to tell some dreadful story, and was afraid to begin; but at last—

translation.en: Pelias sighed heavily, again and again.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 계속해서 깊은 한숨을 내쉬었습니다.

translation.en: He acted like a man afraid to tell a dreadful story.
translation.kr: 그는 끔찍한 이야기를 꺼내기 두려워하는 사람처럼 행동했습니다.

translation.en: But at last he spoke.
translation.kr: 그러다 마침내 입을 열었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: ‘For seven long years and more have I never known a quiet night; and no more will he who comes after me, till the golden fleece be brought home.’

translation.en: For seven long years, I have never known a quiet night.
translation.kr: 무려 7년이 넘도록 나는 단 하루도 편안한 밤을 보낸 적이 없다.

translation.en: Nor will the one who rules after me.
translation.kr: 내 뒤를 이을 통치자 역시 마찬가지일 것이다.

translation.en: We will not rest until the golden fleece is brought home.
translation.kr: 황금 양털을 고향으로 가져오기 전까지는 말이다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: Then he told Jason the story of Phrixus, and of the golden fleece; and told him, too, which was a lie, that Phrixus’ spirit tormented him, calling to him day and night.  And his daughters came, and told the same tale (for their father had taught them their parts), and wept, and said, ‘Oh who will bring home the golden fleece, that our uncle’s spirit may rest; and that we may have rest also, whom he never lets sleep in peace?’

translation.en: Then he told Jason the story of Phrixus and the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 그리고 그는 이아손에게 프릭소스와 황금 양털 이야기를 들려주었습니다.

translation.en: He lied that Phrixus’ spirit tormented him day and night.
translation.kr: 그는 프릭소스의 영혼이 밤낮으로 자신을 부르며 괴롭힌다고 거짓말을 했습니다.

translation.en: His daughters came and told the same tale.
translation.kr: 그의 딸들도 와서 같은 이야기를 했습니다.

translation.en: Their father had taught them their parts well.
translation.kr: 그들의 아버지가 미리 역할을 잘 가르쳐 두었기 때문입니다.

translation.en: They wept and asked who would bring home the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 그들은 울면서 누가 황금 양털을 고향으로 가져오겠냐며 물었습니다.

translation.en: They said it would let their uncle’s spirit rest.
translation.kr: 그렇게 해야만 삼촌의 영혼이 안식을 찾을 수 있다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: And then they, too, could finally sleep in peace.
translation.kr: 그래야 자신들도 마침내 편안하게 잠들 수 있다고 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: Jason sat awhile, sad and silent; for he had often heard of that golden fleece; but he looked on it as a thing hopeless and impossible for any mortal man to win it.

translation.en: Jason sat awhile, sad and silent.
translation.kr: 이아손은 슬픔에 잠겨 한동안 말없이 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: He had often heard of that golden fleece.
translation.kr: 그도 황금 양털에 대해 종종 들은 적이 있었습니다.

translation.en: But he believed it impossible for any mortal man to win it.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 인간이 그것을 얻는 것은 불가능하다고 생각했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: But when Pelias saw him silent, he began to talk of other things, and courted Jason more and more, speaking to him as if he was certain to be his heir, and asking his advice about the kingdom; till Jason, who was young and simple, could not help saying to himself, ‘Surely he is not the dark man whom people call him.  Yet why did he drive my father out?’  And he asked Pelias boldly, ‘Men say that you are terrible, and a man of blood; but I find you a kind and hospitable man; and as you are to me, so will I be to you.  Yet why did you drive my father out?’

translation.en: When Pelias saw him silent, he began to talk of other things.
translation.kr: 이아손이 아무 말도 하지 않자, 펠리아스는 다른 이야기를 꺼냈습니다.

translation.en: He courted Jason more and more.
translation.kr: 그는 더욱 이아손의 환심을 사려 했습니다.

translation.en: He spoke as if Jason were certain to be his heir.
translation.kr: 그는 이아손이 확실한 후계자인 것처럼 말했습니다.

translation.en: He even asked Jason’s advice about the kingdom.
translation.kr: 심지어 왕국의 일에 대해 이아손에게 조언을 구하기도 했습니다.

translation.en: Jason was young and simple, and he thought to himself.
translation.kr: 젊고 순진했던 이아손은 속으로 생각했습니다.

translation.en: Surely he is not the dark man people call him.
translation.kr: 사람들이 말하는 것처럼 사악한 분은 아니구나.

translation.en: Yet why did he drive my father out?
translation.kr: 그런데 왜 아버지를 쫓아내셨을까?

translation.en: So he boldly asked Pelias a direct question.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 펠리아스에게 대담하게 직설적인 질문을 던졌습니다.

translation.en: Men say you are terrible and a man of blood.
translation.kr: 사람들은 숙부님이 무시무시하고 잔인한 분이라고 말합니다.

translation.en: But I find you a kind and hospitable man.
translation.kr: 하지만 제가 보기엔 친절하고 환대해 주시는 분입니다.

translation.en: As you are to me, so will I be to you.
translation.kr: 숙부님이 제게 하신 만큼 저도 숙부님께 할 것입니다.

translation.en: Yet why did you drive my father out?
translation.kr: 하지만 왜 제 아버지를 쫓아내셨습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: Pelias smiled, and sighed.  ‘Men have slandered me in that, as in all things.  Your father was growing old and weary, and he gave the kingdom up to me of his own will.  You shall see him to-morrow, and ask him; and he will tell you the same.’

translation.en: Pelias smiled and sighed.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 미소를 지으며 한숨을 쉬었습니다.

translation.en: Men have slandered me in that, as in all things.
translation.kr: 다른 모든 일과 마찬가지로 사람들이 나를 모함한 것이란다.

translation.en: Your father was growing old and weary.
translation.kr: 네 아버지는 늙고 지쳐가고 있었지.

translation.en: He gave the kingdom up to me of his own will.
translation.kr: 그래서 자신의 뜻으로 왕국을 내게 물려준 것이다.

translation.en: You shall see him tomorrow and ask him.
translation.kr: 내일 네 아버지를 만나 직접 물어보아라.

translation.en: He will tell you the exact same thing.
translation.kr: 그도 너에게 똑같이 말할 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: Jason’s heart leapt in him when he heard that he was to see his father; and he believed all that Pelias said, forgetting that his father might not dare to tell the truth.

translation.en: Jason’s heart leapt to hear he would see his father.
translation.kr: 아버지를 만나게 될 거라는 말에 이아손의 가슴이 뛰었습니다.

translation.en: He believed all that Pelias said.
translation.kr: 그는 펠리아스의 말을 모두 믿었습니다.

translation.en: He forgot his father might not dare tell the truth.
translation.kr: 아버지가 감히 진실을 말하지 못할 수도 있다는 사실은 잊어버렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: ‘One thing more there is,’ said Pelias, ‘on which I need your advice; for, though you are young, I see in you a wisdom beyond your years. There is one neighbour of mine, whom I dread more than all men on earth. I am stronger than he now, and can command him; but I know that if he stay among us, he will work my ruin in the end.  Can you give me a plan, Jason, by which I can rid myself of that man?’

translation.en: There is one more thing, said Pelias.
translation.kr: 한 가지 더 물어볼 게 있단다, 라고 펠리아스가 말했습니다.

translation.en: I need your advice on this matter.
translation.kr: 이 문제에 대해 네 조언이 필요하구나.

translation.en: Though young, you show wisdom beyond your years.
translation.kr: 너는 비록 어리지만 나이에 비해 뛰어난 지혜를 가졌으니까.

translation.en: I have a neighbor whom I dread more than anyone else.
translation.kr: 내 이웃 중에 내가 세상 누구보다 두려워하는 자가 있단다.

translation.en: I am stronger than him now and can command him.
translation.kr: 지금은 내가 그보다 강해서 그에게 명령을 내릴 수 있지.

translation.en: But if he stays, he will ruin me in the end.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 계속 여기 머문다면 결국 나를 파멸시킬 것이다.

translation.en: Can you give me a plan to rid myself of this man?
translation.kr: 이아손, 그 자를 쫓아낼 묘안이 없겠느냐?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: After awhile Jason answered, half laughing, ‘Were I you, I would send him to fetch that same golden fleece; for if he once set forth after it you would never be troubled with him more.’

translation.en: After a while, Jason answered half-laughing.
translation.kr: 잠시 후 이아손은 반쯤 웃으며 대답했습니다.

translation.en: If I were you, I would send him to fetch the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 제가 숙부님이라면 그에게 황금 양털을 가져오라고 보내겠습니다.

translation.en: If he sets forth after it, he will never trouble you again.
translation.kr: 그가 그것을 찾으러 떠난다면 다시는 숙부님을 괴롭히지 못할 테니까요.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: And at that a bitter smile came across Pelias’ lips, and a flash of wicked joy into his eyes; and Jason saw it, and started; and over his mind came the warning of the old man, and his own one sandal, and the oracle, and he saw that he was taken in a trap.

translation.en: A bitter smile crossed Pelias’ lips.
translation.kr: 펠리아스의 입가에 씁쓸한 미소가 번졌습니다.

translation.en: A flash of wicked joy appeared in his eyes.
translation.kr: 그의 눈에는 사악한 기쁨이 번뜩였습니다.

translation.en: Jason saw it and started in surprise.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그것을 보고 깜짝 놀랐습니다.

translation.en: He remembered the old man’s warning and his single sandal.
translation.kr: 그는 노인의 경고와 자신의 샌들 한 짝을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: He remembered the oracle and realized he was trapped.
translation.kr: 신탁을 기억해 낸 그는 자신이 덫에 빠졌음을 깨달았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: But Pelias only answered gently, ‘My son, he shall be sent forthwith.’

translation.en: But Pelias only answered gently.
translation.kr: 하지만 펠리아스는 그저 부드럽게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: My son, he shall be sent immediately.
translation.kr: 내 아들아, 당장 그를 보내야겠구나.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: ‘You mean me?’ cried Jason, starting up, ‘because I came here with one sandal?’  And he lifted his fist angrily, while Pelias stood up to him like a wolf at bay; and whether of the two was the stronger and the fiercer it would be hard to tell.

translation.en: You mean me? cried Jason, starting up.
translation.kr: 저를 말씀하시는 겁니까? 이아손이 벌떡 일어나며 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Is it because I came here with one sandal?
translation.kr: 제가 샌들을 한 짝만 신고 왔기 때문입니까?

translation.en: He lifted his fist angrily.
translation.kr: 그는 분노하며 주먹을 치켜들었습니다.

translation.en: Pelias stood up to him like a wolf at bay.
translation.kr: 펠리아스도 궁지에 몰린 늑대처럼 맞섰습니다.

translation.en: It was hard to tell who was stronger or fiercer.
translation.kr: 둘 중 누가 더 강하고 사나운지 우열을 가리기 힘들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: But after a moment Pelias spoke gently, ‘Why then so rash, my son?  You, and not I, have said what is said; why blame me for what I have not done? Had you bid me love the man of whom I spoke, and make him my son-in-law and heir, I would have obeyed you; and what if I obey you now, and send the man to win himself immortal fame?  I have not harmed you, or him. One thing at least I know, that he will go, and that gladly; for he has a hero’s heart within him, loving glory, and scorning to break the word which he has given.’

translation.en: But after a moment, Pelias spoke gently.
translation.kr: 하지만 잠시 후, 펠리아스는 부드럽게 말했습니다.

translation.en: Why so rash, my son?
translation.kr: 왜 이리 성급하게 구느냐, 아들아?

translation.en: You said the words, not I.
translation.kr: 그렇게 말한 것은 내가 아니라 너다.

translation.en: Why blame me for what I have not done?
translation.kr: 왜 내가 하지 않은 일로 나를 탓하느냐?

translation.en: Had you asked me to love that man, I would have obeyed.
translation.kr: 네가 그 사람을 아껴서 사위나 후계자로 삼으라고 했다면 난 따랐을 것이다.

translation.en: What if I obey you now and send him to win immortal fame?
translation.kr: 지금 네 말에 따라 그를 불멸의 명예를 얻을 길로 보낸다면 어떻겠느냐?

translation.en: I have harmed neither you nor him.
translation.kr: 나는 너도, 그 사람도 해치지 않았다.

translation.en: I know that he will go gladly.
translation.kr: 나는 그가 기쁜 마음으로 갈 것이란 걸 안다.

translation.en: He has a hero’s heart, loves glory, and scorns to break his word.
translation.kr: 그는 영웅의 심장을 가졌고, 영광을 사랑하며, 자신이 한 말을 어기는 것을 경멸하니까.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: Jason saw that he was entrapped; but his second promise to Cheiron came into his mind, and he thought, ‘What if the Centaur were a prophet in that also, and meant that I should win the fleece!’  Then he cried aloud—

translation.en: Jason saw that he was entrapped.
translation.kr: 이아손은 자신이 덫에 걸렸음을 알았습니다.

translation.en: But his second promise to Chiron came to his mind.
translation.kr: 하지만 케이론과 한 두 번째 약속이 떠올랐습니다.

translation.en: What if the Centaur foresaw this as well?
translation.kr: 그 켄타우로스가 이 일도 내다본 것이라면? 그는 생각했습니다.

translation.en: Did he mean for me to win the fleece?
translation.kr: 내가 그 양털을 얻기를 바랐던 것일까?

translation.en: Then he cried aloud.
translation.kr: 그리고 그는 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: ‘You have well spoken, cunning uncle of mine!  I love glory, and I dare keep to my word.  I will go and fetch this golden fleece.  Promise me but this in return, and keep your word as I keep mine.  Treat my father lovingly while I am gone, for the sake of the all-seeing Zeus; and give me up the kingdom for my own on the day that I bring back the golden fleece.’

translation.en: You have spoken well, my cunning uncle!
translation.kr: 말씀 한 번 잘하셨습니다, 교활한 숙부님!

translation.en: I love glory, and I dare keep my word.
translation.kr: 저는 영광을 사랑하고, 제 말은 반드시 지킵니다.

translation.en: I will go and fetch this golden fleece.
translation.kr: 제가 가서 이 황금 양털을 가져오겠습니다.

translation.en: Promise me this in return, and keep your word.
translation.kr: 그 대신 숙부님도 한 가지 약속을 하고 꼭 지키십시오.

translation.en: Treat my father lovingly while I am gone.
translation.kr: 모든 것을 꿰뚫어 보시는 제우스를 걸고, 제가 없는 동안 아버지를 잘 보살펴 주십시오.

translation.en: And give the kingdom to me on the day I bring the fleece.
translation.kr: 그리고 제가 황금 양털을 가져오는 날, 이 왕국을 제게 넘겨주십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: Then Pelias looked at him and almost loved him, in the midst of all his hate; and said, ‘I promise, and I will perform.  It will be no shame to give up my kingdom to the man who wins that fleece.’  Then they swore a great oath between them; and afterwards both went in, and lay down to sleep.

translation.en: Pelias looked at him and almost loved him, despite his hate.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 그를 쳐다보며, 자신의 증오 속에서도 그를 향한 애정을 느낄 뻔했습니다.

translation.en: I promise, and I will perform, he said.
translation.kr: 약속하마, 그리고 반드시 지킬 것이다, 라고 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: It is no shame to yield to the man who wins that fleece.
translation.kr: 그 양털을 얻어 온 사내에게 왕국을 물려주는 것은 전혀 부끄러운 일이 아니니까.

translation.en: Then they swore a great oath between them.
translation.kr: 그리고 그들은 굳게 맹세했습니다.

translation.en: Afterward, both went in and lay down to sleep.
translation.kr: 그 후 두 사람은 안으로 들어가 잠자리에 들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: But Jason could not sleep for thinking of his mighty oath, and how he was to fulfil it, all alone, and without wealth or friends.  So he tossed a long time upon his bed, and thought of this plan and of that; and sometimes Phrixus seemed to call him, in a thin voice, faint and low, as if it came from far across the sea, ‘Let me come home to my fathers and have rest.’  And sometimes he seemed to see the eyes of Hera, and to hear her words again—‘Call on me in the hour of need, and see if the Immortals can forget.’

translation.en: But Jason could not sleep for thinking of his mighty oath.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손은 자신의 엄청난 맹세에 대해 생각하느라 잠을 이룰 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: He wondered how to fulfill it without wealth or friends.
translation.kr: 돈도 친구도 없이 홀로 어떻게 그 맹세를 지킬지 고민했습니다.

translation.en: He tossed for a long time on his bed, thinking of many plans.
translation.kr: 그는 침대에서 오랫동안 뒤척이며 이런저런 계획을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: Sometimes Phrixus seemed to call him in a faint voice.
translation.kr: 가끔은 프릭소스가 희미하고 낮은 목소리로 그를 부르는 것 같았습니다.

translation.en: It sounded as if it came from far across the sea.
translation.kr: 마치 바다 건너 멀리서 들려오는 소리 같았습니다.

translation.en: Let me come home to my fathers and have rest.
translation.kr: 나를 조상들의 고향으로 데려가 편히 쉬게 해다오.

translation.en: Sometimes he seemed to see the eyes of Hera.
translation.kr: 때로는 헤라 여신의 눈이 보이는 듯했습니다.

translation.en: He heard her words again.
translation.kr: 그녀의 목소리가 다시 들렸습니다.

translation.en: Call on me in the hour of need.
translation.kr: 어려운 일이 생기면 나를 부르거라.

translation.en: See if the immortals can forget.
translation.kr: 신들이 은혜를 잊는지 아닌지 알게 될 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: And on the morrow he went to Pelias, and said, ‘Give me a victim, that I may sacrifice to Hera.’  So he went up, and offered his sacrifice; and as he stood by the altar Hera sent a thought into his mind; and he went back to Pelias, and said—

translation.en: On the next day, he went to Pelias.
translation.kr: 다음 날, 그는 펠리아스에게 갔습니다.

translation.en: Give me a victim to sacrifice to Hera, he said.
translation.kr: 헤라 여신께 제물로 바칠 짐승을 주십시오, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: So he went up and offered his sacrifice.
translation.kr: 그는 위로 올라가 제물을 바쳤습니다.

translation.en: As he stood by the altar, Hera sent a thought into his mind.
translation.kr: 그가 제단 옆에 서 있을 때, 헤라 여신이 그의 마음속에 한 가지 생각을 불어넣었습니다.

translation.en: He went back to Pelias and spoke.
translation.kr: 그는 다시 펠리아스에게 돌아가 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: ‘If you are indeed in earnest, give me two heralds, that they may go round to all the princes of the Minuai, who were pupils of the Centaur with me, that we may fit out a ship together, and take what shall befall.’

translation.en: If you are truly in earnest, give me two heralds.
translation.kr: 숙부님이 정말 진심이시라면 제게 두 명의 전령을 주십시오.

translation.en: They can go to all the princes of the Minyans.
translation.kr: 전령들이 저와 함께 케이론의 제자였던 미니아이족의 모든 왕자들에게 가게 해주십시오.

translation.en: We will fit out a ship together and face whatever comes.
translation.kr: 우리가 함께 배를 준비하여 어떤 운명이든 맞설 수 있도록 말입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
paragraphs.raw: At that Pelias praised his wisdom, and hastened to send the heralds out; for he said in his heart, ‘Let all the princes go with him, and, like him, never return; for so I shall be lord of all the Minuai, and the greatest king in Hellas.’

translation.en: Pelias praised his wisdom and hurried to send the heralds.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 그의 지혜를 칭찬하며 서둘러 전령들을 보냈습니다.

translation.en: For he said in his heart.
translation.kr: 그는 속으로 이렇게 생각했기 때문입니다.

translation.en: Let all the princes go with him and never return.
translation.kr: 모든 왕자들이 그와 함께 떠나 영영 돌아오지 않기를.

translation.en: Then I will be lord of all the Minyans.
translation.kr: 그러면 내가 모든 미니아이족의 주인이 될 것이다.

translation.en: I will be the greatest king in Hellas.
translation.kr: 그리고 헬라스에서 가장 위대한 왕이 될 것이다.

chapters.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: PART III HOW THEY BUILT THE SHIP ‘ARGO’ IN IOLCOS

translation.en: Part 3: How They Built the Ship Argo in Iolcos
translation.kr: [3부: 이올코스에서 아르고 호를 건조하다]

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: So the heralds went out, and cried to all the heroes of the Minuai, ‘Who dare come to the adventure of the golden fleece?’

translation.en: The heralds went out and called to all the heroes of the Minyans.
translation.kr: 전령들이 밖으로 나가 미니아이의 모든 영웅들에게 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Who dares to join the adventure for the golden fleece?
translation.kr: 누가 황금 양털을 찾는 모험에 나서겠습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: And Hera stirred the hearts of all the princes, and they came from all their valleys to the yellow sands of Pagasai.  And first came Heracles the mighty, with his lion’s skin and club, and behind him Hylas his young squire, who bore his arrows and his bow; and Tiphys, the skilful steersman; and Butes, the fairest of all men; and Castor and Polydeuces the twins, the sons of the magic swan; and Cæneus, the strongest of mortals, whom the Centaurs tried in vain to kill, and overwhelmed him with trunks of pine-trees, but even so he would not die; and thither came Zetes and Calais, the winged sons of the north wind; and Peleus, the father of Achilles, whose bride was silver-footed Thetis, the goddess of the sea.  And thither came Telamon and Oileus, the fathers of the two Aiantes, who fought upon the plains of Troy; and Mopsus, the wise soothsayer, who knew the speech of birds; and Idmon, to whom Phoebus gave a tongue to prophesy of things to come; and Ancaios, who could read the stars, and knew all the circles of the heavens; and Argus, the famed shipbuilder, and many a hero more, in helmets of brass and gold with tall dyed horse-hair crests, and embroidered shirts of linen beneath their coats of mail, and greaves of polished tin to guard their knees in fight; with each man his shield upon his shoulder, of many a fold of tough bull’s hide, and his sword of tempered bronze in his silver-studded belt; and in his right hand a pair of lances, of the heavy white ash-staves.

translation.en: Hera stirred the hearts of all the princes.
translation.kr: 헤라 여신이 모든 왕자들의 마음을 움직였습니다.

translation.en: They traveled from their valleys to the yellow sands of Pagasae.
translation.kr: 그들은 각자의 계곡을 떠나 파가사이의 노란 모래밭으로 모여들었습니다.

translation.en: First came mighty Heracles with his lion skin and club.
translation.kr: 가장 먼저 사자 가죽을 걸치고 몽둥이를 든 강력한 헤라클레스가 왔습니다.

translation.en: Behind him walked his young squire Hylas, carrying his bow and arrows.
translation.kr: 그 뒤에는 활과 화살을 든 젊은 종자 힐라스가 따랐습니다.

translation.en: Then came Tiphys, the skilled steersman, and Butes, the most handsome of men.
translation.kr: 노련한 조타수 티피스와 세상에서 가장 잘생긴 사내 부테스도 왔습니다.

translation.en: Castor and Polydeuces arrived, the twin sons of the magic swan.
translation.kr: 마법의 백조가 낳은 쌍둥이 형제 카스토르와 폴리데우케스도 도착했습니다.

translation.en: Caeneus also joined them, the strongest of all mortals.
translation.kr: 인간 중 가장 힘이 센 카이네우스도 그들과 합류했습니다.

translation.en: The Centaurs had tried to kill him by burying him under pine trees, but he survived.
translation.kr: 켄타우로스들이 그를 소나무 몸통 아래 묻어 죽이려 했지만, 그는 살아남았습니다.

translation.en: Zetes and Calais, the winged sons of the North Wind, flew in.
translation.kr: 북풍의 날개 달린 아들들인 제테스와 칼라이스도 날아왔습니다.

translation.en: Peleus came too. He was the father of Achilles and husband to the sea goddess Thetis.
translation.kr: 펠레우스도 왔습니다. 그는 아킬레스의 아버지이자 바다의 여신 테티스의 남편이었습니다.

translation.en: Telamon and Oileus arrived, fathers of the two heroes named Ajax who fought at Troy.
translation.kr: 트로이 평원에서 싸운 두 명의 아이아스의 아버지들, 텔라몬과 오일레우스도 도착했습니다.

translation.en: Mopsus, the wise soothsayer who understood the language of birds, joined them.
translation.kr: 새들의 언어를 이해하는 지혜로운 예언자 몹소스도 함께했습니다.

translation.en: Idmon also came, gifted by Phoebus with the power to see the future.
translation.kr: 포이보스로부터 미래를 내다보는 능력을 받은 이드몬도 왔습니다.

translation.en: Ancaeus, who could read the stars and map the heavens, arrived next.
translation.kr: 별을 읽고 하늘의 지도를 그릴 줄 아는 안카이오스도 다음으로 도착했습니다.

translation.en: Argus, the famous shipbuilder, came alongside many more legendary heroes.
translation.kr: 유명한 조선공 아르고스도 다른 수많은 전설적인 영웅들과 함께 왔습니다.

translation.en: They wore brass and gold helmets with tall, dyed horsehair crests.
translation.kr: 그들은 높게 염색된 말갈기 장식이 달린 황동과 황금 투구를 썼습니다.

translation.en: Embroidered linen shirts peeked out from beneath their coats of mail.
translation.kr: 쇠사슬 갑옷 아래로는 수를 놓은 린넨 셔츠가 보였습니다.

translation.en: Polished tin armor protected their knees for battle.
translation.kr: 매끄럽게 광을 낸 주석 갑옷이 전투를 위해 그들의 무릎을 보호했습니다.

translation.en: Each man carried a thick bull-hide shield on his shoulder.
translation.kr: 각자는 튼튼한 황소 가죽으로 만든 두꺼운 방패를 어깨에 멨습니다.

translation.en: Bronze swords hung from their silver-studded belts.
translation.kr: 은 장식이 박힌 허리띠에는 청동 검이 매달려 있었습니다.

translation.en: In their right hands, they grasped pairs of heavy white ash lances.
translation.kr: 오른손에는 희고 단단한 물푸레나무로 만든 무거운 창 두 자루씩을 쥐었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: So they came down to Iolcos, and all the city came out to meet them, and were never tired with looking at their height, and their beauty, and their gallant bearing and the glitter of their inlaid arms.  And some said, ‘Never was such a gathering of the heroes since the Hellens conquered the land.’  But the women sighed over them, and whispered, ‘Alas! they are all going to their death!’

translation.en: They marched down to Iolcos, and the entire city came out to greet them.
translation.kr: 그들이 이올코스로 내려가자 온 도시 사람들이 나와 그들을 맞이했습니다.

translation.en: The people could not stop staring at their impressive height and beauty.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그들의 훤칠한 키와 아름다운 모습에 눈을 떼지 못했습니다.

translation.en: They marveled at their brave postures and the glitter of their decorated weapons.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그들의 용감한 자태와 화려하게 장식된 무기의 광채에 경탄했습니다.

translation.en: Some people said, Never has there been such a gathering of heroes since the Hellenes conquered the land.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 헬렌 족이 이 땅을 정복한 이래로 이렇게 많은 영웅이 모인 적은 없었다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: But the women sighed as they watched them pass.
translation.kr: 하지만 여자들은 그들이 지나가는 것을 보며 한숨을 쉬었습니다.

translation.en: Alas! They are all marching straight to their deaths!
translation.kr: 아아! 저들은 모두 죽음을 향해 걸어가고 있구나!

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: Then they felled the pines on Pelion, and shaped them with the axe, and Argus taught them to build a galley, the first long ship which ever sailed the seas.  They pierced her for fifty oars—an oar for each hero of the crew—and pitched her with coal-black pitch, and painted her bows with vermilion; and they named her _Argo_ after Argus, and worked at her all day long.  And at night Pelias feasted them like a king, and they slept in his palace-porch.

translation.en: The heroes chopped down pine trees on Mount Pelion and shaped them with axes.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 펠리온 산의 소나무를 베어 도끼로 다듬었습니다.

translation.en: Argus taught them how to build a galley, the first long ship to ever sail the seas.
translation.kr: 아르고스는 그들에게 바다를 항해하는 최초의 긴 배인 갤리선을 짓는 법을 가르쳤습니다.

translation.en: They carved holes for fifty oars, providing one for every hero in the crew.
translation.kr: 그들은 쉰 개의 노가 들어갈 구멍을 뚫어, 선원인 모든 영웅에게 노를 하나씩 배정했습니다.

translation.en: The men sealed the hull with coal-black pitch and painted the front bright red.
translation.kr: 사내들은 선체를 칠흑 같은 타르로 밀봉하고 뱃머리를 밝은 붉은색으로 칠했습니다.

translation.en: They named the ship Argo in honor of Argus and worked on her all day long.
translation.kr: 그들은 아르고스를 기려 배의 이름을 아르고라 짓고 온종일 배를 만드는 데 매달렸습니다.

translation.en: At night, Pelias threw grand royal feasts for them.
translation.kr: 밤이 되면 펠리아스는 그들을 위해 성대한 왕실 연회를 열어주었습니다.

translation.en: Afterward, the weary heroes slept soundly on the palace porch.
translation.kr: 그 후 지친 영웅들은 궁전 현관에서 깊은 잠에 빠졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: But Jason went away to the northward, and into the land of Thrace, till he found Orpheus, the prince of minstrels, where he dwelt in his cave under Rhodope, among the savage Cicon tribes.  And he asked him, ‘Will you leave your mountains, Orpheus, my fellow-scholar in old times, and cross Strymon once more with me, to sail with the heroes of the Minuai, and bring home the golden fleece, and charm for us all men and all monsters with your magic harp and song?’

translation.en: Meanwhile, Jason traveled north into the land of Thrace.
translation.kr: 한편, 이아손은 북쪽 트라키아 땅으로 향했습니다.

translation.en: He searched until he found Orpheus, the greatest of all musicians.
translation.kr: 그는 가장 위대한 음악가인 오르페우스를 찾을 때까지 헤매었습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus was living in a cave beneath Mount Rhodope among the wild Cicon tribes.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 로도페 산 아래의 동굴에서 거친 키콘 부족과 함께 살고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Jason asked him, Will you leave your mountains, my old friend and fellow student?
translation.kr: 이아손이 그에게 물었습니다. 나의 옛 친구이자 동학이여, 이 산을 떠나 주시겠소?

translation.en: Will you cross the river Strymon with me one more time?
translation.kr: 나와 함께 스트리몬 강을 한 번 더 건너 주시겠소?

translation.en: Come sail with the Minyan heroes to bring home the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 미니아이의 영웅들과 함께 항해하여 황금 양털을 집으로 가져옵시다.

translation.en: You can charm men and monsters alike with your magic harp and beautiful songs.
translation.kr: 당신의 마법 하프와 아름다운 노래라면 인간과 괴물 모두를 매혹할 수 있을 것이오.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: Then Orpheus sighed, ‘Have I not had enough of toil and of weary wandering, far and wide since I lived in Cheiron’s cave, above Iolcos by the sea?  In vain is the skill and the voice which my goddess mother gave me; in vain have I sung and laboured; in vain I went down to the dead, and charmed all the kings of Hades, to win back Eurydice my bride.  For I won her, my beloved, and lost her again the same day, and wandered away in my madness, even to Egypt and the Libyan sands, and the isles of all the seas, driven on by the terrible gadfly, while I charmed in vain the hearts of men, and the savage forest beasts, and the trees, and the lifeless stones, with my magic harp and song, giving rest, but finding none.  But at last Calliope my mother delivered me, and brought me home in peace; and I dwell here in the cave alone, among the savage Cicon tribes, softening their wild hearts with music and the gentle laws of Zeus.  And now I must go out again, to the ends of all the earth, far away into the misty darkness, to the last wave of the Eastern Sea.  But what is doomed must be, and a friend’s demand obeyed; for prayers are the daughters of Zeus, and who honours them honours him.’

translation.en: Orpheus let out a heavy sigh and replied.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 깊은 한숨을 내쉬며 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Have I not endured enough hardship and endless wandering?
translation.kr: 나는 이미 충분한 고난과 끝없는 방황을 겪지 않았소?

translation.en: I have traveled far and wide since our days in Cheiron's cave by the sea.
translation.kr: 바닷가 이올코스의 케이론의 동굴에서 지내던 시절 이후로 나는 참으로 멀고 넓은 세상을 떠돌았소.

translation.en: The skill and voice my goddess mother gave me have brought me no joy.
translation.kr: 여신 어머니께서 내게 주신 재능과 목소리도 내게는 아무런 기쁨을 주지 못했다오.

translation.en: I have sung and labored to no purpose.
translation.kr: 나는 헛되이 노래하고 애를 썼소.

translation.en: I even traveled down to the land of the dead and charmed the rulers of Hades.
translation.kr: 심지어 죽은 자들의 땅으로 내려가 하데스의 지배자들을 매혹하기도 했소.

translation.en: I did it all just to win back my bride, Eurydice.
translation.kr: 그 모든 것은 오직 나의 신부 에우리디케를 되찾기 위함이었지.

translation.en: I saved my beloved, only to lose her again on the very same day.
translation.kr: 나는 사랑하는 이를 구했지만, 바로 그날 그녀를 다시 잃고 말았소.

translation.en: Madness drove me across Egypt, the Libyan sands, and countless islands.
translation.kr: 광기에 사로잡힌 나는 이집트와 리비아의 사막, 그리고 수많은 섬들을 떠돌았지.

translation.en: I was pushed forward relentlessly, singing in vain to men, beasts, and stones.
translation.kr: 나는 무언가에 쫓기듯 끝없이 나아가며 사람과 짐승, 돌멩이들에게조차 헛된 노래를 불렀다오.

translation.en: My magic harp gave rest to everyone else, but I found no peace for myself.
translation.kr: 내 마법 하프는 다른 모든 이에게 안식을 주었지만, 정작 나 자신은 어떤 평화도 찾지 못했소.

translation.en: Finally, my mother Calliope rescued me and brought me home in peace.
translation.kr: 마침내 나의 어머니 칼리오페께서 나를 구해주셨고, 평화롭게 집으로 데려와 주셨지.

translation.en: Now I live here alone, soothing the wild Cicon tribes with music and Zeus's gentle laws.
translation.kr: 지금 나는 이곳 동굴에 홀로 살며, 음악과 제우스의 온화한 법으로 거친 키콘 부족을 달래고 있소.

translation.en: Yet you ask me to journey again to the edges of the earth and the misty darkness.
translation.kr: 그런데도 당신은 나에게 세상의 끝, 저 안개 낀 어둠 속 동쪽 바다의 마지막 파도를 향해 다시 떠나자고 하는구려.

translation.en: But I must accept my fate and answer the call of a true friend.
translation.kr: 하지만 운명은 받아들여야 하고, 진정한 친구의 부름에는 응해야 마땅할 것이오.

translation.en: Prayers are the daughters of Zeus, and whoever honors them honors the gods.
translation.kr: 간청은 제우스의 딸들이니, 이를 존중하는 자는 곧 신을 존중하는 것이기 때문이지.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: Then Orpheus rose up sighing, and took his harp, and went over Strymon. And he led Jason to the south-west, up the banks of Haliacmon and over the spurs of Pindus, to Dodona the town of Zeus, where it stood by the side of the sacred lake, and the fountain which breathed out fire, in the darkness of the ancient oakwood, beneath the mountain of the hundred springs.  And he led him to the holy oak, where the black dove settled in old times, and was changed into the priestess of Zeus, and gave oracles to all nations round.  And he bade him cut down a bough, and sacrifice to Hera and to Zeus; and they took the bough and came to Iolcos, and nailed it to the beak-head of the ship.

translation.en: Orpheus stood up with another sigh, grabbed his harp, and crossed the river.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 다시 한번 한숨을 내쉬며 일어섰고, 하프를 챙겨 강을 건넜습니다.

translation.en: He led Jason southwest along the riverbanks and over the mountain ridges.
translation.kr: 그는 이아손을 이끌고 강둑을 따라 산등성이를 넘어 남서쪽으로 향했습니다.

translation.en: They reached Dodona, the holy town of Zeus beside the sacred lake.
translation.kr: 그들은 신성한 호숫가에 자리한 제우스의 거룩한 도시 도도나에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: A fiery fountain burned there in the darkness of the ancient oak forest.
translation.kr: 그곳의 오래된 참나무 숲의 어둠 속에는 불을 내뿜는 샘이 있었습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus brought Jason to the ancient holy oak tree.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 이아손을 아주 오래된 신성한 참나무로 데려갔습니다.

translation.en: A black dove had once rested there, transforming into the priestess of Zeus.
translation.kr: 옛날에 검은 비둘기 한 마리가 그곳에 앉았다가 제우스의 여사제로 변한 적이 있었습니다.

translation.en: She had spoken wise prophecies to all the surrounding nations.
translation.kr: 그녀는 주변의 모든 나라에 지혜로운 신탁을 전해주곤 했습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus told Jason to cut down a sturdy branch and offer sacrifices to the gods.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 이아손에게 튼튼한 나뭇가지를 꺾어 신들에게 제물을 바치라고 말했습니다.

translation.en: They took the sacred branch back to Iolcos and securely nailed it to the ship's front.
translation.kr: 그들은 그 신성한 나뭇가지를 이올코스로 가져와 배의 뱃머리에 단단히 못 박았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: And at last the ship was finished, and they tried to launch her down the beach; but she was too heavy for them to move her, and her keel sank deep into the sand.  Then all the heroes looked at each other blushing; but Jason spoke, and said, ‘Let us ask the magic bough; perhaps it can help us in our need.’

translation.en: At last, the ship was finished, and they tried to push it into the water.
translation.kr: 마침내 배가 완성되었고, 그들은 배를 물가로 밀어내려 했습니다.

translation.en: But it was incredibly heavy, and the bottom sank deep into the soft sand.
translation.kr: 하지만 배는 엄청나게 무거웠고, 바닥은 부드러운 모래 속으로 깊이 가라앉고 말았습니다.

translation.en: The mighty heroes looked at one another, blushing in embarrassment.
translation.kr: 강력한 영웅들은 당황하여 얼굴을 붉힌 채 서로를 쳐다보았습니다.

translation.en: Jason broke the silence and offered a solution.
translation.kr: 이아손이 침묵을 깨고 해결책을 제시했습니다.

translation.en: Let us ask the magic branch. Perhaps it can help us in our time of need.
translation.kr: 마법의 나뭇가지에게 물어봅시다. 어쩌면 우리가 도움이 필요할 때 힘이 되어줄지도 모릅니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: Then a voice came from the bough, and Jason heard the words it said, and bade Orpheus play upon the harp, while the heroes waited round, holding the pine-trunk rollers, to help her toward the sea.

translation.en: A voice spoke directly from the branch, and Jason listened closely.
translation.kr: 나뭇가지에서 직접 목소리가 흘러나왔고, 이아손은 귀를 기울였습니다.

translation.en: He told Orpheus to play his harp while the heroes stood by.
translation.kr: 그는 오르페우스에게 하프를 연주하라고 말하며, 영웅들에게는 대기하라고 지시했습니다.

translation.en: They held the heavy pine-trunk rollers ready to push the ship into the sea.
translation.kr: 그들은 배를 바다로 밀어넣기 위해 무거운 소나무 통나무 굴림대를 쥐고 준비했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: Then Orpheus took his harp, and began his magic song—‘How sweet it is to ride upon the surges, and to leap from wave to wave, while the wind sings cheerful in the cordage, and the oars flash fast among the foam!  How sweet it is to roam across the ocean, and see new towns and wondrous lands, and to come home laden with treasure, and to win undying fame!’

translation.en: Orpheus took up his harp and began to sing a powerful, magic song.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 하프를 집어 들고 강력한 마법의 노래를 부르기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: How sweet it is to ride the surging waves and leap across the water!
translation.kr: 요동치는 파도를 타고 물결을 뛰어넘는 것은 얼마나 달콤한가!

translation.en: The wind sings happily in the ropes while the oars flash through the bright foam.
translation.kr: 밧줄 사이로 바람이 즐겁게 노래하고, 빛나는 거품 사이로 노가 번쩍이네.

translation.en: How wonderful it is to roam the endless ocean and discover marvelous new lands!
translation.kr: 끝없는 바다를 누비며 경이롭고 새로운 땅을 발견하는 것은 얼마나 놀라운 일인가!

translation.en: We will return home burdened with treasure and win eternal glory!
translation.kr: 우리는 보물을 가득 안고 고향으로 돌아가 영원한 영광을 얻으리라!

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: And the good ship _Argo_ heard him, and longed to be away and out at sea; till she stirred in every timber, and heaved from stem to stern, and leapt up from the sand upon the rollers, and plunged onward like a gallant horse; and the heroes fed her path with pine-trunks, till she rushed into the whispering sea.

translation.en: The brave ship Argo heard his music and deeply longed to sail the open sea.
translation.kr: 용감한 배 아르고가 그의 음악을 듣고는 넓은 바다를 항해하고픈 깊은 열망에 사로잡혔습니다.

translation.en: Every timber in her body stirred, heaving violently from front to back.
translation.kr: 배를 이루는 모든 목재가 요동치며 앞뒤로 격렬하게 흔들렸습니다.

translation.en: She leaped off the sand onto the rollers, charging forward like a brave warhorse.
translation.kr: 배는 모래를 박차고 굴림대 위로 뛰어올라, 마치 용감한 군마처럼 앞으로 돌진했습니다.

translation.en: The heroes quickly laid pine trunks in her path as she rushed toward the whispering ocean.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 배가 속삭이는 바다를 향해 돌진할 때, 그 길을 따라 서둘러 소나무 통나무들을 깔아주었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How They Built the Ship 'Argo' in Iolcos
paragraphs.raw: Then they stored her well with food and water, and pulled the ladder up on board, and settled themselves each man to his oar, and kept time to Orpheus’ harp; and away across the bay they rowed southward, while the people lined the cliffs; and the women wept, while the men shouted, at the starting of that gallant crew.

translation.en: The crew loaded the ship with plenty of food and fresh water.
translation.kr: 선원들은 배에 식량과 신선한 물을 넉넉히 실었습니다.

translation.en: They pulled the boarding ladder up and sat down at their heavy oars.
translation.kr: 그들은 승선용 사다리를 끌어 올리고 무거운 노 앞에 자리를 잡았습니다.

translation.en: The men rowed in perfect time to the steady rhythm of Orpheus's harp.
translation.kr: 사내들은 오르페우스의 하프가 만들어내는 일정한 리듬에 맞춰 완벽하게 노를 저었습니다.

translation.en: They headed south across the wide bay as the city's people lined the tall cliffs.
translation.kr: 도시 사람들이 높은 절벽에 늘어선 가운데, 그들은 넓은 만을 가로질러 남쪽으로 향했습니다.

translation.en: Women wept and men shouted in awe as the brave crew began their great journey.
translation.kr: 용감한 선원들이 위대한 여정을 시작하자 여자들은 눈물을 흘렸고 남자들은 경외심에 차 환호했습니다.

chapters.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: PART IV HOW THE ARGONAUTS SAILED TO COLCHIS

translation.en: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
translation.kr: 4부: 아르고 호 원정대가 콜키스로 향하다

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And what happened next, my children, whether it be true or not, stands written in ancient songs, which you shall read for yourselves some day. And grand old songs they are, written in grand old rolling verse; and they call them the Songs of Orpheus, or the Orphics, to this day.  And they tell how the heroes came to Aphetai, across the bay, and waited for the south-west wind, and chose themselves a captain from their crew: and how all called for Heracles, because he was the strongest and most huge; but Heracles refused, and called for Jason, because he was the wisest of them all.  So Jason was chosen captain; and Orpheus heaped a pile of wood, and slew a bull, and offered it to Hera, and called all the heroes to stand round, each man’s head crowned with olive, and to strike their swords into the bull.  Then he filled a golden goblet with the bull’s blood, and with wheaten flour, and honey, and wine, and the bitter salt-sea water, and bade the heroes taste.  So each tasted the goblet, and passed it round, and vowed an awful vow: and they vowed before the sun, and the night, and the blue-haired sea who shakes the land, to stand by Jason faithfully in the adventure of the golden fleece; and whosoever shrank back, or disobeyed, or turned traitor to his vow, then justice should minister against him, and the Erinnues who track guilty men.

translation.en: My children, what happened next stands written in ancient songs that you may read for yourselves someday.
translation.kr: 아이들아, 다음으로 무슨 일이 일어났는지는 훗날 여러분이 직접 읽게 될 오래된 노래에 기록되어 있답니다.

translation.en: These magnificent old songs are written in grand, rolling verses.
translation.kr: 이 장엄하고 오래된 노래들은 아주 크고 웅장한 운율로 쓰였지요.

translation.en: To this day, they are called the Songs of Orpheus, or the Orphics.
translation.kr: 오늘날까지도 사람들은 이를 오르페우스의 노래라고 부른답니다.

translation.en: They tell how the heroes crossed the bay to Aphetai and waited for the southwest wind.
translation.kr: 노래는 영웅들이 만을 건너 아페타이에 도착해 남서풍을 기다린 이야기를 들려줍니다.

translation.en: There, they needed to choose a captain from among their crew.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 그들은 일행을 이끌 선장을 뽑아야 했습니다.

translation.en: Everyone called for Heracles because he was the strongest and most massive of them all.
translation.kr: 모두가 헤라클레스를 외쳤는데, 그가 가장 힘이 세고 체격이 컸기 때문이지요.

translation.en: But Heracles refused and instead nominated Jason, for he was the wisest among them.
translation.kr: 하지만 헤라클레스는 거절하며, 그들 중 가장 지혜로운 이아손을 추천했습니다.

translation.en: So Jason was chosen as their captain.
translation.kr: 그리하여 이아손이 선장으로 뽑혔습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus then gathered a pile of wood, sacrificed a bull, and offered it to Hera.
translation.kr: 그러자 오르페우스가 장작을 쌓고 황소를 제물로 바쳐 헤라 여신에게 바쳤습니다.

translation.en: He called all the heroes, wearing olive crowns, to strike their swords into the bull.
translation.kr: 그는 올리브 관을 쓴 영웅들을 모두 불러 모아 황소에 칼을 꽂게 했습니다.

translation.en: He filled a golden goblet with the bull's blood, flour, honey, wine, and salty seawater.
translation.kr: 그는 황금 잔에 황소의 피와 밀가루, 꿀, 포도주, 그리고 짠 바닷물을 채웠습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus then asked the heroes to taste the mixture.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 영웅들에게 그 잔을 맛보라고 했습니다.

translation.en: Each man tasted the goblet, passed it around, and swore a solemn oath.
translation.kr: 각자 잔을 맛보고 돌려 마시며 엄숙한 맹세를 맺었습니다.

translation.en: They vowed before the sun, the night, and the mighty sea god to stand faithfully by Jason.
translation.kr: 그들은 태양과 밤, 그리고 강력한 바다의 신 앞에서 이아손을 충실히 따르겠다고 맹세했습니다.

translation.en: Whoever backed down, disobeyed, or betrayed the vow would face justice.
translation.kr: 누구든 물러서거나 명령을 어기고 맹세를 배반하는 자는 심판을 받을 것이라 다짐했지요.

translation.en: The Furies, who relentlessly track guilty men, would hunt down any traitor.
translation.kr: 죄지은 자를 끝까지 추적하는 복수의 여신들이 배신자를 사냥할 것이었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Jason lighted the pile, and burnt the carcase of the bull; and they went to their ship and sailed eastward, like men who have a work to do; and the place from which they went was called Aphetai, the sailing-place, from that day forth.  Three thousand years and more they sailed away, into the unknown Eastern seas; and great nations have come and gone since then, and many a storm has swept the earth; and many a mighty armament, to which _Argo_ would be but one small boat; English and French, Turkish and Russian, have sailed those waters since; yet the fame of that small _Argo_ lives for ever, and her name is become a proverb among men.

translation.en: Then Jason lit the pyre and burned the carcass of the bull.
translation.kr: 그 후 이아손이 장작더미에 불을 붙여 황소의 몸을 태웠습니다.

translation.en: They boarded their ship and sailed eastward, determined to complete their task.
translation.kr: 그들은 배에 올라타 임무를 완수하겠다는 결의를 다지며 동쪽으로 항해했습니다.

translation.en: From that day on, the place they departed from was called Aphetai, the sailing-place.
translation.kr: 그날 이후로 그들이 떠난 곳은 출발지라는 뜻의 아페타이로 불렸습니다.

translation.en: They sailed into the unknown Eastern seas over three thousand years ago.
translation.kr: 그들은 3천 년도 더 전에 미지의 동쪽 바다로 항해를 떠났습니다.

translation.en: Since then, great nations have risen and fallen, and many storms have swept the earth.
translation.kr: 그 이래로 위대한 국가들이 일어섰다 쓰러졌고, 수많은 폭풍이 세상을 휩쓸었습니다.

translation.en: Mighty fleets, compared to which the Argo would be but a small boat, have sailed those waters.
translation.kr: 아르고 호가 그저 작은 조각배로 보일 만큼 거대한 함대들이 그 바다를 항해했지요.

translation.en: English, French, Turkish, and Russian ships have all passed through since.
translation.kr: 영국, 프랑스, 튀르키예, 러시아의 배들이 모두 그곳을 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: Yet the fame of that small Argo lives forever, and its name remains a legend among men.
translation.kr: 하지만 작디작은 아르고 호의 명성은 영원히 살아남아, 그 이름은 사람들 사이에서 전설이 되었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So they sailed past the Isle of Sciathos, with the Cape of Sepius on their left, and turned to the northward toward Pelion, up the long Magnesian shore.  On their right hand was the open sea, and on their left old Pelion rose, while the clouds crawled round his dark pine-forests, and his caps of summer snow.  And their hearts yearned for the dear old mountain, as they thought of pleasant days gone by, and of the sports of their boyhood, and their hunting, and their schooling in the cave beneath the cliff.  And at last Peleus spoke, ‘Let us land here, friends, and climb the dear old hill once more.  We are going on a fearful journey; who knows if we shall see Pelion again?  Let us go up to Cheiron our master, and ask his blessing ere we start.  And I have a boy, too, with him, whom he trains as he trained me once—the son whom Thetis brought me, the silver-footed lady of the sea, whom I caught in the cave, and tamed her, though she changed her shape seven times.  For she changed, as I held her, into water, and to vapour, and to burning flame, and to a rock, and to a black-maned lion, and to a tall and stately tree.  But I held her and held her ever, till she took her own shape again, and led her to my father’s house, and won her for my bride.  And all the rulers of Olympus came to our wedding, and the heavens and the earth rejoiced together, when an Immortal wedded mortal man.  And now let me see my son; for it is not often I shall see him upon earth: famous he will be, but short-lived, and die in the flower of youth.’

translation.en: They sailed past the Isle of Sciathos, leaving the Cape of Sepias on their left.
translation.kr: 그들은 세피아스 곶을 왼쪽에 두고 스키아토스 섬을 지나 항해했습니다.

translation.en: Then they turned northward toward Pelion, sailing up the long Magnesian shore.
translation.kr: 그러고는 마그네시아의 긴 해안을 따라 펠리온 산을 향해 북쪽으로 방향을 틀었습니다.

translation.en: On their right was the open sea, and on their left rose old Mount Pelion.
translation.kr: 오른쪽에는 탁 트인 바다가 있었고, 왼쪽에는 오래된 펠리온 산이 솟아 있었습니다.

translation.en: Clouds crawled around its dark pine forests and its peaks of summer snow.
translation.kr: 어두운 소나무 숲과 여름에도 눈이 덮인 산봉우리 주위로 구름이 천천히 흘러갔습니다.

translation.en: Their hearts yearned for the dear old mountain as they recalled their pleasant past.
translation.kr: 그들은 즐거웠던 과거를 떠올리며 그리운 옛 산을 향해 마음이 끌렸습니다.

translation.en: They remembered their boyhood games, their hunting, and their schooling in the cliffside cave.
translation.kr: 어린 시절의 놀이와 사냥, 절벽 아래 동굴에서 가르침을 받던 때를 기억했지요.

translation.en: At last Peleus spoke, Let us land here, friends, and climb the dear old hill once more.
translation.kr: 마침내 펠레우스가 말했습니다. 친구들, 여기서 상륙해 그리운 옛 산을 다시 한번 올라갑시다.

translation.en: We are going on a fearful journey, and who knows if we shall ever see Pelion again?
translation.kr: 우리는 두려운 여정을 떠나는데, 펠리온 산을 다시 볼 수 있을지 누가 알겠습니까?

translation.en: Let us go up to our master Chiron and ask for his blessing before we depart.
translation.kr: 우리의 스승이신 키론 님께 올라가 출발하기 전에 축복을 청합시다.

translation.en: I also have a boy with him, whom he trains just as he once trained me.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 스승님이 예전의 나처럼 가르치고 있는 내 아들도 있소.

translation.en: He is the son given to me by Thetis, the silver-footed lady of the sea.
translation.kr: 은빛 발을 가진 바다의 여인 테티스가 내게 낳아준 아들이지요.

translation.en: I caught her in the cave and tamed her, even though she changed her shape seven times.
translation.kr: 동굴에서 그녀를 붙잡아 길들였는데, 그녀는 무려 일곱 번이나 모습을 바꾸었소.

translation.en: As I held her, she turned into water, vapor, burning flame, and a rock.
translation.kr: 내가 붙들고 있는 동안 그녀는 물, 수증기, 타오르는 불꽃, 그리고 바위로 변했습니다.

translation.en: She even became a black-maned lion and a tall, stately tree.
translation.kr: 심지어 검은 갈기의 사자와 키가 크고 위풍당당한 나무로도 변했지요.

translation.en: But I held on tightly until she returned to her true shape.
translation.kr: 하지만 그녀가 원래의 모습을 되찾을 때까지 나는 단단히 붙잡고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Then I led her to my father's house and won her as my bride.
translation.kr: 그러고는 그녀를 내 아버지의 집으로 이끌어 신부로 맞이했소.

translation.en: All the rulers of Olympus attended our wedding.
translation.kr: 올림포스의 모든 지배자들이 우리 결혼식에 참석했습니다.

translation.en: Heaven and earth rejoiced together when an immortal wedded a mortal man.
translation.kr: 불멸의 존재가 필멸의 인간과 결혼하자 하늘과 땅이 함께 기뻐했지요.

translation.en: Now let me see my son, for I shall not often see him on earth.
translation.kr: 이제 내 아들을 보게 해주시오, 이 땅에서 그 아이를 자주 볼 수 없을 테니까요.

translation.en: He will be famous, but his life will be short, and he will die in the flower of youth.
translation.kr: 그는 유명해질 테지만, 수명이 짧아 꽃다운 젊은 나이에 죽고 말 것이오.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So Tiphys the helmsman steered them to the shore under the crags of Pelion; and they went up through the dark pine-forests towards the Centaur’s cave.

translation.en: So Tiphys the helmsman steered them to the shore under the crags of Pelion.
translation.kr: 그리하여 조타수 티피스는 펠리온 산의 암벽 아래 해안으로 배를 몰았습니다.

translation.en: They walked up through the dark pine forests toward the Centaur's cave.
translation.kr: 그들은 어두운 소나무 숲을 지나 켄타우로스의 동굴을 향해 걸어 올라갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And they came into the misty hall, beneath the snow-crowned crag; and saw the great Centaur lying, with his huge limbs spread upon the rock; and beside him stood Achilles, the child whom no steel could wound, and played upon his harp right sweetly, while Cheiron watched and smiled.

translation.en: They entered the misty hall beneath the snow-crowned cliff.
translation.kr: 그들은 눈 덮인 절벽 아래 안개 낀 회랑으로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: The great Centaur lay there, resting his massive limbs on the rock.
translation.kr: 거대한 켄타우로스는 바위 위에 크고 튼튼한 팔다리를 뻗고 누워 있었습니다.

translation.en: Beside him stood Achilles, the child whom no blade could wound.
translation.kr: 어떤 칼날로도 상처 입힐 수 없는 소년 아킬레우스가 그의 곁에 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: The boy played his harp beautifully while Chiron watched and smiled.
translation.kr: 소년이 아름답게 하프를 연주하는 동안 키론은 미소를 지으며 지켜보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Cheiron leapt up and welcomed them, and kissed them every one, and set a feast before them of swine’s flesh, and venison, and good wine; and young Achilles served them, and carried the golden goblet round.  And after supper all the heroes clapped their hands, and called on Orpheus to sing; but he refused, and said, ‘How can I, who am the younger, sing before our ancient host?’  So they called on Cheiron to sing, and Achilles brought him his harp; and he began a wondrous song; a famous story of old time, of the fight between the Centaurs and the Lapithai, which you may still see carved in stone. {96}  He sang how his brothers came to ruin by their folly, when they were mad with wine; and how they and the heroes fought, with fists, and teeth, and the goblets from which they drank; and how they tore up the pine-trees in their fury, and hurled great crags of stone, while the mountains thundered with the battle, and the land was wasted far and wide; till the Lapithai drove them from their home in the rich Thessalian plains to the lonely glens of Pindus, leaving Cheiron all alone.  And the heroes praised his song right heartily; for some of them had helped in that great fight.

translation.en: Chiron leaped up to welcome them with a kiss for each hero.
translation.kr: 키론은 벌떡 일어나 영웅들 하나하나에게 입을 맞추며 환영했습니다.

translation.en: He prepared a feast of pork, venison, and fine wine.
translation.kr: 그는 돼지고기와 사슴고기, 그리고 훌륭한 포도주로 연회를 베풀었습니다.

translation.en: Young Achilles served the guests and carried the golden goblet around.
translation.kr: 어린 아킬레우스가 손님들을 시중들며 황금 잔을 돌렸습니다.

translation.en: After supper, the heroes clapped and asked Orpheus to sing.
translation.kr: 저녁 식사가 끝난 후, 영웅들은 박수를 치며 오르페우스에게 노래를 청했습니다.

translation.en: He refused, asking how someone so young could sing before their ancient host.
translation.kr: 그는 어린 자신이 어찌 연로한 주인 앞에서 노래할 수 있겠냐며 거절했습니다.

translation.en: So they asked Chiron to sing, and Achilles brought him his harp.
translation.kr: 그래서 그들은 키론에게 노래를 부탁했고, 아킬레우스는 그에게 하프를 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: He began a wondrous ancient song about the battle between the Centaurs and the Lapiths.
translation.kr: 그는 켄타우로스와 라피테스 족 사이의 전투를 다룬 놀라운 옛 노래를 시작했습니다.

translation.en: You can still see this famous story carved into stone today.
translation.kr: 오늘날에도 돌에 새겨진 이 유명한 이야기를 볼 수 있습니다.

translation.en: He sang of how his brothers were ruined by their own foolishness when maddened by wine.
translation.kr: 그는 포도주에 취해 이성을 잃은 형제들이 자신들의 어리석음으로 어떻게 파멸했는지 노래했습니다.

translation.en: They fought the heroes using fists, teeth, and their drinking goblets.
translation.kr: 그들은 주먹과 이빨, 그리고 마시던 술잔을 휘두르며 영웅들과 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: In their fury, they tore up pine trees and hurled massive rocks.
translation.kr: 분노한 그들은 소나무를 뿌리째 뽑고 거대한 바위를 던졌습니다.

translation.en: The mountains thundered with the battle, and the land was laid waste.
translation.kr: 전투의 굉음이 산을 울렸고 온 땅이 폐허로 변했습니다.

translation.en: Finally, the Lapiths drove them from the rich Thessalian plains to the lonely glens of Pindus.
translation.kr: 마침내 라피테스 족은 그들을 비옥한 테살리아 평원에서 핀두스의 외딴 골짜기로 몰아냈습니다.

translation.en: This left Chiron all alone.
translation.kr: 그렇게 키론은 완전히 혼자가 되었습니다.

translation.en: The heroes heartily praised his song, as some of them had fought in that great battle.
translation.kr: 영웅들 중 일부는 그 위대한 전투에 참전했었기에 진심으로 그의 노래를 칭찬했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Orpheus took the lyre, and sang of Chaos, and the making of the wondrous World, and how all things sprang from Love, who could not live alone in the Abyss.  And as he sang, his voice rose from the cave, above the crags, and through the tree-tops, and the glens of oak and pine.  And the trees bowed their heads when they heard it, and the gray rocks cracked and rang, and the forest beasts crept near to listen, and the birds forsook their nests and hovered round.  And old Cheiron claps his hands together, and beat his hoofs upon the ground, for wonder at that magic song.

translation.en: Then Orpheus took the lyre and sang of Chaos and the creation of the wondrous world.
translation.kr: 그러자 오르페우스가 수금을 들고 혼돈과 경이로운 세상의 창조에 대해 노래했습니다.

translation.en: He sang of how everything sprang from Love, who could not endure the lonely abyss.
translation.kr: 그는 고독한 심연을 견디지 못한 사랑으로부터 어떻게 모든 것이 생겨났는지 불렀습니다.

translation.en: His voice soared from the cave, rising over the cliffs and through the treetops.
translation.kr: 그의 목소리는 동굴에서 솟아올라 절벽을 넘고 나무 꼭대기를 가로질렀습니다.

translation.en: The melody echoed across the glens filled with oak and pine.
translation.kr: 그 선율은 참나무와 소나무로 가득한 골짜기에 울려 퍼졌습니다.

translation.en: Hearing his voice, the trees bowed down, and the gray rocks cracked and rang.
translation.kr: 그의 목소리를 듣고 나무들은 고개를 숙였고, 잿빛 바위는 갈라지며 공명했습니다.

translation.en: Forest beasts crept closer to listen, and birds left their nests to hover nearby.
translation.kr: 숲의 짐승들은 노래를 듣기 위해 다가왔고, 새들은 둥지를 떠나 주위를 맴돌았습니다.

translation.en: Old Chiron clapped his hands and beat his hooves on the ground, amazed by the magic song.
translation.kr: 늙은 키론은 그 마법 같은 노래에 감탄하여 박수를 치고 발굽으로 땅을 굴렀습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Peleus kissed his boy, and wept over him, and they went down to the ship; and Cheiron came down with them, weeping, and kissed them one by one, and blest them, and promised to them great renown.  And the heroes wept when they left him, till their great hearts could weep no more; for he was kind and just and pious, and wiser than all beasts and men.  Then he went up to a cliff, and prayed for them, that they might come home safe and well; while the heroes rowed away, and watched him standing on his cliff above the sea, with his great hands raised toward heaven, and his white locks waving in the wind; and they strained their eyes to watch him to the last, for they felt that they should look on him no more.

translation.en: Peleus kissed his son and wept over him before going down to the ship.
translation.kr: 펠레우스는 배로 내려가기 전 아들에게 입을 맞추고 눈물을 흘렸습니다.

translation.en: Chiron wept as he accompanied them, kissing and blessing each hero.
translation.kr: 키론도 눈물을 흘리며 그들과 동행했고, 영웅들 하나하나에게 입을 맞추고 축복을 내렸습니다.

translation.en: He promised them that they would achieve great renown.
translation.kr: 그는 영웅들이 엄청난 명성을 얻게 될 것이라고 약속했습니다.

translation.en: The heroes wept until their great hearts could shed no more tears.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 거대한 심장이 더 이상 눈물을 흘리지 못할 때까지 울었습니다.

translation.en: Chiron was kind, just, and wiser than all other beasts and men.
translation.kr: 키론은 친절하고 정의로우며 다른 어떤 짐승이나 사람보다 지혜로웠기 때문입니다.

translation.en: He climbed a cliff and prayed for their safe and healthy return.
translation.kr: 그는 절벽에 올라 그들이 무사히 건강하게 돌아오기를 기도했습니다.

translation.en: The heroes rowed away, watching him stand on the cliff above the sea.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 노를 저어 멀어지며 바다 위 절벽에 선 그를 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: His great hands were raised toward heaven, and his white hair waved in the wind.
translation.kr: 그의 커다란 두 손은 하늘을 향해 들려 있었고, 하얀 머리카락이 바람에 흩날렸습니다.

translation.en: They strained their eyes to watch him until he faded from sight.
translation.kr: 그들은 그의 모습이 시야에서 사라질 때까지 눈을 떼지 못했습니다.

translation.en: They knew in their hearts that they would never see him again.
translation.kr: 그들은 그를 다시는 볼 수 없으리라는 것을 마음속으로 알고 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So they rowed on over the long swell of the sea, past Olympus, the seat of the Immortals, and past the wooded bays of Athos, and Samothrace the sacred isle; and they came past Lemnos to the Hellespont, and through the narrow strait of Abydos, and so on into the Propontis, which we call Marmora now.  And there they met with Cyzicus, ruling in Asia over the Dolions, who, the songs say, was the son of Æneas, of whom you will hear many a tale some day.  For Homer tells us how he fought at Troy, and Virgil how he sailed away and founded Rome; and men believed until late years that from him sprang our old British kings.  Now Cyzicus, the songs say, welcomed the heroes, for his father had been one of Cheiron’s scholars; so he welcomed them, and feasted them, and stored their ship with corn and wine, and cloaks and rugs, the songs say, and shirts, of which no doubt they stood in need.

translation.en: They rowed over the long ocean swells, passing Mount Olympus, home of the gods.
translation.kr: 그들은 긴 바다의 파도를 타고 신들의 거처인 올림포스 산을 지나 노를 저었습니다.

translation.en: They sailed past the wooded bays of Athos and the sacred island of Samothrace.
translation.kr: 그들은 아토스의 숲이 우거진 만과 신성한 섬 사모트라케를 지났습니다.

translation.en: Passing Lemnos, they entered the Hellespont and the narrow strait of Abydos.
translation.kr: 렘노스를 지난 그들은 헬레스폰트와 아비도스의 좁은 해협으로 들어섰습니다.

translation.en: From there, they sailed into the Propontis, which we now call the Sea of Marmara.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 그들은 오늘날 마르마라해라고 불리는 프로폰티스로 항해했습니다.

translation.en: There they met Cyzicus, who ruled over the Dolionians in Asia.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 그들은 아시아의 돌리오니아인들을 다스리는 키지코스를 만났습니다.

translation.en: The old songs say he was the son of Aeneas, a famous hero with many legends.
translation.kr: 옛 노래에 따르면 그는 수많은 전설을 남긴 유명한 영웅 아이네이아스의 아들이었다고 합니다.

translation.en: Homer tells of his battles at Troy, and Virgil describes how he founded Rome.
translation.kr: 호메로스는 그가 트로이에서 치른 전투를 이야기하고, 베르길리우스는 그가 어떻게 로마를 세웠는지 묘사합니다.

translation.en: For many years, people believed that early British kings descended from him.
translation.kr: 오랜 세월 동안 사람들은 초기 영국의 왕들이 그의 후손이라고 믿었습니다.

translation.en: Legends say Cyzicus welcomed the heroes because his father had studied under Chiron.
translation.kr: 전설에 따르면 키지코스의 아버지가 키론에게서 배웠기 때문에 그가 영웅들을 환영했다고 합니다.

translation.en: He hosted a grand feast and generously supplied their ship.
translation.kr: 그는 성대한 연회를 열고 그들의 배에 물자를 아낌없이 채워주었습니다.

translation.en: He gave them much-needed grain, wine, cloaks, rugs, and fresh shirts.
translation.kr: 그는 그들에게 꼭 필요했던 곡물, 포도주, 망토, 깔개, 그리고 새 셔츠를 주었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But at night, while they lay sleeping, came down on them terrible men, who lived with the bears in the mountains, like Titans or giants in shape; for each of them had six arms, and they fought with young firs and pines.  But Heracles killed them all before morn with his deadly poisoned arrows; but among them, in the darkness, he slew Cyzicus the kindly prince.

translation.en: But at night, while they lay sleeping, terrible men came down on them from the mountains.
translation.kr: 하지만 밤이 되어 그들이 잠든 사이, 산에서 끔찍한 사내들이 습격해 왔습니다.

translation.en: These men lived with the bears and looked like Titans or giants.
translation.kr: 이들은 곰들과 함께 살았으며 마치 타이탄이나 거인 같은 모습이었습니다.

translation.en: Each of them had six arms, and they fought using young fir and pine trees as weapons.
translation.kr: 모두 여섯 개의 팔을 가졌고, 어린 전나무와 소나무를 무기 삼아 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: Before morning, Heracles killed them all with his deadly poisoned arrows.
translation.kr: 날이 밝기 전, 헤라클레스는 치명적인 독화살로 그들을 모두 쓰러뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: Tragically, in the darkness, he also slew the kindly prince Cyzicus.
translation.kr: 하지만 비극적이게도 어둠 속에서 그만 친절한 왕자 키지코스까지 죽이고 말았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then they got to their ship and to their oars, and Tiphys bade them cast off the hawsers and go to sea.  But as he spoke a whirlwind came, and spun the _Argo_ round, and twisted the hawsers together, so that no man could loose them.  Then Tiphys dropped the rudder from his hand, and cried, ‘This comes from the Gods above.’  But Jason went forward, and asked counsel of the magic bough.

translation.en: Then they returned to their ship and took to their oars.
translation.kr: 그 후 일행은 배로 돌아가 노를 잡았습니다.

translation.en: Tiphys ordered them to cast off the ropes and head out to sea.
translation.kr: 티피스는 밧줄을 풀고 바다로 나가라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: But as he spoke, a whirlwind spun the Argo around and twisted the ropes tightly together.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 말하는 순간 회오리바람이 불어와 아르고호를 회전시켰고, 밧줄을 단단히 꼬아버렸습니다.

translation.en: No man could loosen them.
translation.kr: 아무도 그 밧줄을 풀 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: Tiphys dropped the rudder from his hand and cried, This comes from the Gods above.
translation.kr: 티피스는 손에서 방향타를 놓으며, 이것은 하늘의 신들이 내린 일이라고 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Jason went forward and asked the magic bough for guidance.
translation.kr: 이아손은 앞으로 나아가 마법의 나뭇가지에게 조언을 구했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then the magic bough spoke, and answered, ‘This is because you have slain Cyzicus your friend.  You must appease his soul, or you will never leave this shore.’

translation.en: The magic bough answered, This is because you have slain your friend Cyzicus.
translation.kr: 마법의 나뭇가지가 대답하기를, 이것은 당신들이 친구인 키지코스를 죽였기 때문이라고 했습니다.

translation.en: You must appease his soul, or you will never leave this shore.
translation.kr: 그의 영혼을 달래주지 않으면 결코 이 해안을 떠날 수 없을 것이라고도 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Jason went back sadly, and told the heroes what he had heard.  And they leapt on shore, and searched till dawn; and at dawn they found the body, all rolled in dust and blood, among the corpses of those monstrous beasts.  And they wept over their kind host, and laid him on a fair bed, and heaped a huge mound over him, and offered black sheep at his tomb, and Orpheus sang a magic song to him, that his spirit might have rest. And then they held games at the tomb, after the custom of those times, and Jason gave prizes to each winner.  To Ancæus he gave a golden cup, for he wrestled best of all; and to Heracles a silver one, for he was the strongest of all; and to Castor, who rode best, a golden crest; and Polydeuces the boxer had a rich carpet, and to Orpheus for his song a sandal with golden wings.  But Jason himself was the best of all the archers, and the Minuai crowned him with an olive crown; and so, the songs say, the soul of good Cyzicus was appeased and the heroes went on their way in peace.

translation.en: Jason went back sadly and told the heroes what he had heard.
translation.kr: 이아손은 슬픈 얼굴로 돌아와 영웅들에게 자신이 들은 이야기를 전했습니다.

translation.en: They leapt onto the shore and searched until dawn.
translation.kr: 그들은 해안으로 뛰어내려 동이 틀 때까지 찾아 헤매었습니다.

translation.en: At dawn they found the body, covered in dust and blood, among the corpses of the monstrous beasts.
translation.kr: 새벽녘에 그들은 괴물 같은 짐승들의 시체 사이에서 먼지와 피투성이가 된 시신을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: They wept over their kind host and laid him on a beautiful bed.
translation.kr: 그들은 친절했던 주인을 위해 눈물을 흘리며 그를 아름다운 침상에 뉘었습니다.

translation.en: They heaped a huge mound over him and offered black sheep at his tomb.
translation.kr: 그 위로 거대한 흙무덤을 쌓아 올리고, 무덤 앞에서 검은 양을 제물로 바쳤습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus sang a magic song to him, so that his spirit might find rest.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 그의 영혼이 안식을 찾을 수 있도록 마법의 노래를 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Then they held funeral games at the tomb, following the custom of those times.
translation.kr: 그리고 그 시절의 관습에 따라 무덤 곁에서 장례 경기를 열었습니다.

translation.en: Jason gave prizes to each winner.
translation.kr: 이아손은 각 경기의 우승자에게 상을 주었습니다.

translation.en: He gave a golden cup to Ancaeus, who wrestled the best.
translation.kr: 씨름을 가장 잘한 안카이오스에게는 황금 잔을 주었습니다.

translation.en: Heracles received a silver cup, as he was the strongest of all.
translation.kr: 가장 힘이 셌던 헤라클레스는 은 잔을 받았습니다.

translation.en: Castor, who rode best, won a golden crest.
translation.kr: 승마 솜씨가 제일 뛰어났던 카스토르는 황금 장식을 받았습니다.

translation.en: Polydeuces the boxer received a rich carpet.
translation.kr: 권투 선수인 폴리데우케스는 화려한 양탄자를 차지했습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus was rewarded with a golden-winged sandal for his song.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 노래에 대한 보답으로 황금 날개가 달린 샌들을 받았습니다.

translation.en: But Jason himself was the best of all the archers.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손 자신이 모든 궁수 중 가장 뛰어났습니다.

translation.en: The Minyans crowned him with an olive wreath.
translation.kr: 미니아스인들은 그에게 올리브 화관을 씌워 주었습니다.

translation.en: Thus, the songs say, the soul of good Cyzicus was appeased.
translation.kr: 전해지는 노래에 따르면, 이리하여 선량한 키지코스의 영혼이 달래졌다고 합니다.

translation.en: The heroes then went on their way in peace.
translation.kr: 그 후 영웅들은 평온하게 길을 떠났습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But when Cyzicus’ wife heard that he was dead she died likewise of grief; and her tears became a fountain of clear water, which flows the whole year round.

translation.en: When Cyzicus's wife heard that he was dead, she died of grief as well.
translation.kr: 남편이 죽었다는 소식을 들은 키지코스의 아내 역시 슬픔을 이기지 못하고 세상을 떠났습니다.

translation.en: Her tears became a fountain of clear water, which flows year-round.
translation.kr: 그녀의 눈물은 맑은 샘물이 되어 일 년 내내 흐르고 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then they rowed away, the songs say, along the Mysian shore, and past the mouth of Rhindacus, till they found a pleasant bay, sheltered by the long ridges of Arganthus, and by high walls of basalt rock.  And there they ran the ship ashore upon the yellow sand, and furled the sail, and took the mast down, and lashed it in its crutch.  And next they let down the ladder, and went ashore to sport and rest.

translation.en: The songs say they rowed along the Mysian shore and past the mouth of the Rhindacus.
translation.kr: 전설에 따르면, 그들은 미시아 해안을 따라 린다코스 강어귀를 지나 노를 저어갔습니다.

translation.en: They eventually found a pleasant bay sheltered by the long ridges of Arganthus and high walls of basalt rock.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 아르간토스의 긴 능선과 높은 현무암 절벽으로 둘러싸인 아늑한 만을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: They ran the ship ashore onto the yellow sand, furled the sail, and took down the mast to lash it in its crutch.
translation.kr: 그들은 노란 모래사장에 배를 대고 돛을 접은 뒤, 돛대를 내려 받침대에 단단히 묶었습니다.

translation.en: Next, they let down the ladder and went ashore to rest and play.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 사다리를 내리고 뭍으로 올라가 휴식을 취하며 즐거운 시간을 보냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And there Heracles went away into the woods, bow in hand, to hunt wild deer; and Hylas the fair boy slipt away after him, and followed him by stealth, until he lost himself among the glens, and sat down weary to rest himself by the side of a lake; and there the water nymphs came up to look at him, and loved him, and carried him down under the lake to be their playfellow, for ever happy and young.  And Heracles sought for him in vain, shouting his name till all the mountains rang; but Hylas never heard him, far down under the sparkling lake.  So while Heracles wandered searching for him, a fair breeze sprang up, and Heracles was nowhere to be found; and the _Argo_ sailed away, and Heracles was left behind, and never saw the noble Phasian stream.

translation.en: Heracles went into the woods with his bow to hunt wild deer.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 야생 사슴을 사냥하기 위해 활을 들고 숲으로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: The beautiful boy Hylas slipped away and stealthily followed him.
translation.kr: 아름다운 소년 힐라스가 남몰래 빠져나와 그의 뒤를 쫓았습니다.

translation.en: Hylas soon lost his way among the glens and sat down wearily by a lake to rest.
translation.kr: 곧 골짜기에서 길을 잃은 힐라스는 지친 몸을 이끌고 호숫가에 주저앉아 쉬었습니다.

translation.en: The water nymphs came up to look at him and instantly fell in love.
translation.kr: 물의 요정들이 그를 보러 수면 위로 올라왔다가 첫눈에 반하고 말았습니다.

translation.en: They carried him down beneath the lake to be their playmate, forever happy and young.
translation.kr: 그들은 영원히 젊고 행복하게 함께 놀기 위해 소년을 호수 밑바닥으로 데려갔습니다.

translation.en: Heracles searched for him in vain, shouting his name until the mountains rang.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 산이 쩌렁쩌렁 울리도록 소년의 이름을 부르며 찾아 헤매었으나 헛수고였습니다.

translation.en: Far down under the sparkling lake, Hylas never heard his calls.
translation.kr: 반짝이는 호수 저 깊은 곳에 있는 힐라스에게는 그 목소리가 닿지 않았습니다.

translation.en: While Heracles wandered in search of the boy, a fair breeze sprang up.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스가 소년을 찾아 헤매는 동안 순조로운 바람이 불기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: When Heracles could not be found, the Argo sailed away without him.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스가 끝내 돌아오지 않자, 아르고 호는 그를 남겨둔 채 출항해 버렸습니다.

translation.en: Thus, Heracles was left behind and never saw the noble Phasis River.
translation.kr: 결국 홀로 남겨진 헤라클레스는 그 장엄한 파시스 강을 영영 보지 못했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then the Minuai came to a doleful land, where Amycus the giant ruled, and cared nothing for the laws of Zeus, but challenged all strangers to box with him, and those whom he conquered he slew.  But Polydeuces the boxer struck him a harder blow than he ever felt before, and slew him; and the Minuai went on up the Bosphorus, till they came to the city of Phineus, the fierce Bithynian king; for Zetes and Calais bade Jason land there, because they had a work to do.

translation.en: The Minyans then arrived at a mournful land ruled by the giant Amycus.
translation.kr: 그 후 미니아이 사람들은 거인 아미코스가 지배하는 음울한 땅에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: He cared nothing for the laws of Zeus and challenged all strangers to a boxing match, slaying those he defeated.
translation.kr: 그는 제우스의 법칙을 무시한 채 낯선 이들에게 권투 시합을 걸어 패자들을 모조리 죽여버렸습니다.

translation.en: However, the expert boxer Polydeuces struck the giant with a crushing blow and killed him.
translation.kr: 하지만 뛰어난 권투 선수 폴리데우케스가 뼈가 부서질 듯한 강력한 일격을 날려 거인을 쓰러뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: The Argonauts continued up the Bosphorus until they reached the city of Phineus, the fierce Bithynian king.
translation.kr: 아르고 호 원정대는 보스포루스 해협을 거슬러 올라가 맹렬한 비티니아의 왕 피네우스의 도시에 닿았습니다.

translation.en: Zetes and Calais had urged Jason to land there because they had a task to fulfill.
translation.kr: 제테스와 칼라이스는 자신들이 완수해야 할 임무가 있다며 이아손에게 그곳에 상륙하자고 재촉했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And they went up from the shore toward the city, through forests white with snow; and Phineus came out to meet them with a lean and woful face, and said, ‘Welcome, gallant heroes, to the land of bitter blasts, the land of cold and misery; yet I will feast you as best I can.’  And he led them in, and set meat before them; but before they could put their hands to their mouths, down came two fearful monsters, the like of whom man never saw; for they had the faces and the hair of fair maidens, but the wings and claws of hawks; and they snatched the meat from off the table, and flew shrieking out above the roofs.

translation.en: They walked from the shore toward the city through forests white with snow.
translation.kr: 그들은 해안에서 출발해 눈 덮인 하얀 숲을 지나 도시를 향해 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: Phineus came out to meet them with a gaunt and sorrowful face.
translation.kr: 피네우스가 수척하고 슬픈 얼굴로 나와 그들을 맞이했습니다.

translation.en: Welcome, gallant heroes, to the land of bitter blasts, cold, and misery, he said.
translation.kr: 용감한 영웅들이여, 살을 에는 듯한 칼바람과 추위, 그리고 고통의 땅에 오신 것을 환영합니다, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: Yet I will feast you as best as I can.
translation.kr: 하지만 최선을 다해 여러분을 대접하겠습니다.

translation.en: He led them inside and set meat before them on the table.
translation.kr: 왕은 그들을 안으로 안내하여 고기를 식탁에 차려주었습니다.

translation.en: But before they could take a single bite, two fearful monsters swooped down.
translation.kr: 그러나 그들이 한 입 베어 물기도 전에 끔찍한 두 괴물이 쏜살같이 내려왔습니다.

translation.en: These creatures had the faces and hair of fair maidens, but the wings and claws of hawks.
translation.kr: 그 생물들은 아름다운 처녀의 얼굴과 머리카락을 가졌지만, 매의 날개와 발톱을 하고 있었습니다.

translation.en: They snatched the meat from the table and flew shrieking away above the roofs.
translation.kr: 괴물들은 식탁에서 고기를 낚아채더니 날카로운 비명을 지르며 지붕 위로 날아가 버렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Phineus beat his breast and cried, ‘These are the Harpies, whose names are the Whirlwind and the Swift, the daughters of Wonder and of the Amber-nymph, and they rob us night and day.  They carried off the daughters of Pandareus, whom all the Gods had blest; for Aphrodite fed them on Olympus with honey and milk and wine; and Hera gave them beauty and wisdom, and Athené skill in all the arts; but when they came to their wedding, the Harpies snatched them both away, and gave them to be slaves to the Erinnues, and live in horror all their days.  And now they haunt me, and my people, and the Bosphorus, with fearful storms; and sweep away our food from off our tables, so that we starve in spite of all our wealth.’

translation.en: Phineus beat his chest in despair and cried out.
translation.kr: 피네우스는 절망에 빠져 가슴을 치며 울부짖었습니다.

translation.en: These are the Harpies, the daughters of Wonder and the Amber-nymph.
translation.kr: 이들은 경이로움의 신과 호박의 요정 사이에서 태어난 딸들, 바로 하르피이아이입니다.

translation.en: Their names are Whirlwind and Swift, and they rob us night and day.
translation.kr: 돌풍과 발빠름이라는 이름을 가진 이 괴물들은 밤낮을 가리지 않고 우리를 약탈합니다.

translation.en: They once carried off the blessed daughters of Pandareus.
translation.kr: 그들은 과거에 신들의 축복을 받은 판다레오스의 딸들도 납치해 갔습니다.

translation.en: Aphrodite had fed those girls on Olympus with honey, milk, and wine.
translation.kr: 아프로디테는 올림포스에서 그 소녀들에게 꿀과 우유, 포도주를 먹여 키웠습니다.

translation.en: Hera gave them beauty and wisdom, while Athena taught them skill in all the arts.
translation.kr: 헤라는 아름다움과 지혜를, 아테나는 모든 예술의 재능을 주었습니다.

translation.en: But on their wedding day, the Harpies snatched them away to be slaves to the Furies.
translation.kr: 그러나 결혼식 날, 하르피이아이가 신부들을 낚아채 복수의 여신들의 노예로 만들어 버렸습니다.

translation.en: The poor girls were forced to live in horror for the rest of their days.
translation.kr: 가엾은 소녀들은 평생을 끔찍한 공포 속에서 살아야만 했습니다.

translation.en: Now they haunt me, my people, and the Bosphorus with fearful storms.
translation.kr: 이제 그 괴물들은 무서운 폭풍우를 몰고 와 저와 제 백성, 그리고 보스포루스 해협을 끈질기게 괴롭힙니다.

translation.en: They sweep the food from our tables, leaving us to starve despite all our wealth.
translation.kr: 그들은 우리 식탁의 음식마저 모조리 휩쓸어 가버려서, 우리는 아무리 부유해도 굶주려야만 합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then up rose Zetes and Calais, the winged sons of the North-wind, and said, ‘Do you not know us, Phineus, and these wings which grow upon our backs?’  And Phineus hid his face in terror; but he answered not a word.

translation.en: Then Zetes and Calais, the winged sons of the North Wind, stood up.
translation.kr: 그러자 북풍의 날개 달린 아들들인 제테스와 칼라이스가 일어났습니다.

translation.en: They asked, Do you not know us, Phineus, and these wings on our backs?
translation.kr: 그들이 물었습니다. 피네우스, 우리와 우리 등에서 자라난 이 날개들을 알아보지 못하시겠습니까?

translation.en: Phineus hid his face in terror, but he did not answer a word.
translation.kr: 피네우스는 공포에 질려 얼굴을 숨겼지만, 한마디도 대답하지 못했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘Because you have been a traitor, Phineus, the Harpies haunt you night and day.  Where is Cleopatra our sister, your wife, whom you keep in prison? and where are her two children, whom you blinded in your rage, at the bidding of an evil woman, and cast them out upon the rocks?  Swear to us that you will right our sister, and cast out that wicked woman; and then we will free you from your plague, and drive the whirlwind maidens to the south; but if not, we will put out your eyes, as you put out the eyes of your own sons.’

translation.en: Because you have been a traitor, Phineus, the Harpies haunt you night and day.
translation.kr: 당신이 배신자였기 때문에 하피들이 밤낮으로 당신을 괴롭히는 것입니다, 피네우스.

translation.en: Where is our sister Cleopatra, your wife, whom you keep in prison?
translation.kr: 당신이 감옥에 가둬둔 당신의 아내이자 우리 누이인 클레오파트라는 어디 있습니까?

translation.en: Where are her two children, whom you blinded in rage and cast upon the rocks?
translation.kr: 사악한 여자의 꼬임에 넘어가 분노로 눈을 멀게 하고 바위 위에 내다 버린 두 아이는 어디 있습니까?

translation.en: Swear that you will restore our sister and banish that wicked woman.
translation.kr: 우리 누이의 권리를 되찾아 주고 그 사악한 여자를 내쫓겠다고 맹세하십시오.
