translation.en: Then we will free you from your plague and drive the winged maidens south.
translation.kr: 그러면 우리가 당신을 그 재앙에서 구해주고 날개 달린 처녀들을 남쪽으로 쫓아내겠습니다.

translation.en: If not, we will put out your eyes just as you blinded your own sons.
translation.kr: 만약 그렇지 않으면, 당신이 친아들들의 눈을 멀게 한 것처럼 우리도 당신의 눈을 멀게 할 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Phineus swore an oath to them, and drove out the wicked woman; and Jason took those two poor children, and cured their eyes with magic herbs.

translation.en: Phineus swore an oath to them and drove out the wicked woman.
translation.kr: 피네우스는 그들에게 맹세하고 사악한 여자를 쫓아냈습니다.

translation.en: Jason took those two poor children and cured their eyes with magic herbs.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그 두 불쌍한 아이들을 데려와 마법의 약초로 눈을 치료해주었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But Zetes and Calais rose up sadly and said, ‘Farewell now, heroes all; farewell, our dear companions, with whom we played on Pelion in old times; for a fate is laid upon us, and our day is come at last, in which we must hunt the whirlwinds over land and sea for ever; and if we catch them they die, and if not, we die ourselves.’

translation.en: Zetes and Calais stood up sadly.
translation.kr: 제테스와 칼라이스는 슬프게 일어났습니다.

translation.en: Farewell now, all you heroes.
translation.kr: 이제 안녕히 계십시오, 모든 영웅들이여.

translation.en: Farewell, our dear companions, with whom we played on Mount Pelion in the old days.
translation.kr: 우리가 옛날 펠리온 산에서 함께 놀았던 사랑하는 동료들이여, 안녕히 계십시오.

translation.en: A tragic fate is laid upon us, and our time has finally come.
translation.kr: 우리에게 비극적인 운명이 주어졌고, 마침내 우리의 때가 왔습니다.

translation.en: We must hunt the whirlwinds over land and sea forever.
translation.kr: 우리는 영원히 육지와 바다를 넘어 회오리바람을 쫓아야만 합니다.

translation.en: If we catch them, they die, but if we fail, we die ourselves.
translation.kr: 우리가 그들을 잡으면 그들이 죽지만, 우리가 실패하면 우리 스스로가 죽게 됩니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: At that all the heroes wept; but the two young men sprang up, and aloft into the air after the Harpies, and the battle of the winds began.

translation.en: At that, all the heroes wept.
translation.kr: 그 말에 모든 영웅들이 눈물을 흘렸습니다.

translation.en: The two young men sprang high into the air to chase the Harpies.
translation.kr: 두 청년은 하피들을 쫓기 위해 공중으로 높이 뛰어올랐습니다.

translation.en: Thus, the great battle of the winds began.
translation.kr: 이렇게 하여 바람들의 거대한 전투가 시작되었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: The heroes trembled in silence as they heard the shrieking of the blasts; while the palace rocked and all the city, and great stones were torn from the crags, and the forest pines were hurled earthward, north and south and east and west, and the Bosphorus boiled white with foam, and the clouds were dashed against the cliffs.

translation.en: The heroes trembled in silence as they heard the shrieking of the blasts.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 비명을 지르는 듯한 강풍 소리를 들으며 말없이 떨었습니다.

translation.en: The palace and the whole city rocked from the fierce wind.
translation.kr: 사나운 바람에 궁전과 도시 전체가 흔들렸습니다.

translation.en: Great stones were torn from the crags, and forest pines were hurled to the ground in every direction.
translation.kr: 커다란 돌들이 절벽에서 떨어져 나갔고, 숲의 소나무들은 사방으로 내동댕이쳐졌습니다.

translation.en: The Bosphorus boiled white with foam, and clouds crashed against the cliffs.
translation.kr: 보스포루스 해협은 하얀 거품을 일으키며 끓어올랐고, 구름은 절벽에 부딪혔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But at last the battle ended, and the Harpies fled screaming toward the south, and the sons of the North-wind rushed after them, and brought clear sunshine where they passed.  For many a league they followed them, over all the isles of the Cyclades, and away to the south-west across Hellas, till they came to the Ionian Sea, and there they fell upon the Echinades, at the mouth of the Achelous; and those isles were called the Whirlwind Isles for many a hundred years.  But what became of Zetes and Calais I know not, for the heroes never saw them again: and some say that Heracles met them, and quarrelled with them, and slew them with his arrows; and some say that they fell down from weariness and the heat of the summer sun, and that the Sun-god buried them among the Cyclades, in the pleasant Isle of Tenos; and for many hundred years their grave was shown there, and over it a pillar, which turned to every wind.  But those dark storms and whirlwinds haunt the Bosphorus until this day.

translation.en: At last the battle ended.
translation.kr: 마침내 전투가 끝났습니다.

translation.en: The Harpies fled screaming toward the south.
translation.kr: 하피들은 비명을 지르며 남쪽으로 도망쳤습니다.

translation.en: The sons of the North Wind rushed after them, bringing clear sunshine wherever they passed.
translation.kr: 북풍의 아들들이 그들을 바짝 뒤쫓았고, 그들이 지나간 자리에는 맑은 햇살이 비쳤습니다.

translation.en: They chased the monsters for many miles over the Cyclades islands.
translation.kr: 그들은 키클라데스 제도 너머로 수 마일 동안 괴물들을 추격했습니다.

translation.en: They crossed Greece to the southwest until they reached the Ionian Sea.
translation.kr: 그들은 그리스를 가로질러 남서쪽으로 날아가 마침내 이오니아 해에 이르렀습니다.

translation.en: There they finally caught them at the Echinades islands, near the mouth of the Achelous river.
translation.kr: 그들은 아켈로오스 강 어귀에 있는 에키나데스 제도에서 마침내 그들을 붙잡았습니다.

translation.en: Those islands were called the Whirlwind Isles for many centuries.
translation.kr: 그 섬들은 수백 년 동안 회오리바람 섬이라고 불렸습니다.

translation.en: I do not know what became of Zetes and Calais, for the heroes never saw them again.
translation.kr: 영웅들이 그들을 다시는 보지 못했기 때문에, 저는 제테스와 칼라이스에게 무슨 일이 일어났는지 모릅니다.

translation.en: Some say that Heracles met them, argued with them, and killed them with his arrows.
translation.kr: 어떤 사람들은 헤라클레스가 그들을 만나 다투다가 자신의 화살로 죽였다고 말합니다.

translation.en: Others say they collapsed from weariness and the heat of the summer sun.
translation.kr: 또 다른 사람들은 그들이 피로와 여름 햇빛의 열기에 지쳐 쓰러졌다고 말합니다.

translation.en: They believe the Sun God buried them among the Cyclades in the pleasant island of Tenos.
translation.kr: 태양신이 그들을 키클라데스 제도의 아름다운 테노스 섬에 묻어주었다고 믿습니다.

translation.en: For many centuries, their grave was shown there with a pillar that turned to face every wind.
translation.kr: 수백 년 동안 그곳에는 그들의 무덤이 있었고, 그 위에는 모든 바람을 향해 도는 기둥이 세워져 있었습니다.

translation.en: But those dark storms and whirlwinds still haunt the Bosphorus to this day.
translation.kr: 하지만 그 어두운 폭풍과 회오리바람은 오늘날까지도 보스포루스 해협에 출몰합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But the Argonauts went eastward, and out into the open sea, which we now call the Black Sea, but it was called the Euxine then.  No Hellen had ever crossed it, and all feared that dreadful sea, and its rocks, and shoals, and fogs, and bitter freezing storms; and they told strange stories of it, some false and some half-true, how it stretched northward to the ends of the earth, and the sluggish Putrid Sea, and the everlasting night, and the regions of the dead.  So the heroes trembled, for all their courage, as they came into that wild Black Sea, and saw it stretching out before them, without a shore, as far as eye could see.

translation.en: The Argonauts sailed eastward into the open sea.
translation.kr: 아르고 호 원정대는 동쪽으로 항해하여 탁 트인 바다로 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: We now call it the Black Sea, but back then it was known as the Euxine.
translation.kr: 우리는 지금 그곳을 흑해라고 부르지만, 당시에는 에욱시노스라고 알려져 있었습니다.

translation.en: No Greek had ever crossed it before.
translation.kr: 이전에 그곳을 건넌 그리스인은 아무도 없었습니다.

translation.en: Everyone feared that dreadful sea with its jagged rocks, hidden shoals, thick fogs, and freezing storms.
translation.kr: 모두가 뾰족한 바위, 숨겨진 얕은 여울, 짙은 안개, 얼어붙을 듯한 폭풍이 있는 그 무서운 바다를 두려워했습니다.

translation.en: They told strange stories about it, some false and some half-true.
translation.kr: 그들은 그것에 대해 거짓도 있고 반쯤 진실인 이상한 이야기들을 나누었습니다.

translation.en: They claimed it stretched northward to the ends of the earth and the sluggish Putrid Sea.
translation.kr: 그들은 그 바다가 북쪽으로 지구 끝과 고여 있는 썩은 바다까지 뻗어 있다고 주장했습니다.

translation.en: They believed it led to everlasting night and the realm of the dead.
translation.kr: 그들은 그곳이 영원한 밤과 죽은 자들의 왕국으로 이어진다고 믿었습니다.

translation.en: So despite all their courage, the heroes trembled as they entered that wild Black Sea.
translation.kr: 그래서 그들의 모든 용기에도 불구하고, 영웅들은 그 거친 흑해에 들어서며 몸을 떨었습니다.

translation.en: They saw it stretching out endlessly before them, without a single shore in sight.
translation.kr: 그들은 해안 하나 보이지 않고 눈앞에 끝없이 펼쳐진 바다를 보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And first Orpheus spoke, and warned them, ‘We shall come now to the wandering blue rocks; my mother warned me of them, Calliope, the immortal muse.’

translation.en: Orpheus spoke first to warn them.
translation.kr: 오르페우스가 먼저 나서서 그들에게 경고했습니다.

translation.en: We will soon reach the wandering blue rocks.
translation.kr: 우리는 곧 떠돌아다니는 푸른 바위들에 도착할 것입니다.

translation.en: My mother, the immortal muse Calliope, warned me about them.
translation.kr: 불멸의 무사이 여신인 제 어머니 칼리오페께서 그것들에 대해 제게 경고하셨습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And soon they saw the blue rocks shining like spires and castles of gray glass, while an ice-cold wind blew from them and chilled all the heroes’ hearts.  And as they neared they could see them heaving, as they rolled upon the long sea-waves, crashing and grinding together, till the roar went up to heaven.  The sea sprang up in spouts between them, and swept round them in white sheets of foam; but their heads swung nodding high in air, while the wind whistled shrill among the crags.

translation.en: Soon they saw the blue rocks shining like tall spires and castles made of gray glass.
translation.kr: 곧 그들은 회색 유리로 만들어진 높은 첨탑과 성처럼 빛나는 푸른 바위들을 보았습니다.

translation.en: An ice-cold wind blew from the rocks and chilled the hearts of all the heroes.
translation.kr: 얼음처럼 차가운 바람이 바위에서 불어와 모든 영웅들의 가슴을 서늘하게 했습니다.

translation.en: As they drew nearer, they could see the massive rocks heaving on the long ocean waves.
translation.kr: 그들이 더 가까이 다가가자, 거대한 바위들이 긴 바다 물결 위에서 들썩이는 것을 볼 수 있었습니다.

translation.en: The rocks rolled and crashed together with a deafening roar that reached the heavens.
translation.kr: 바위들은 구르며 부딪혔고, 하늘까지 닿을 듯한 귀를 찢는 굉음을 냈습니다.

translation.en: The sea sprayed high into the air between them and swept around them in white sheets of foam.
translation.kr: 바다 물결은 바위들 사이로 높이 솟구쳤고, 하얀 거품을 일으키며 주변을 휩쓸었습니다.

translation.en: The towering peaks of the rocks swung violently in the air.
translation.kr: 바위의 우뚝 솟은 봉우리들이 공중에서 격렬하게 흔들렸습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, the fierce wind whistled shrilly through the jagged crags.
translation.kr: 그동안 사나운 바람은 뾰족한 절벽 사이로 날카로운 소리를 내며 불었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: The heroes’ hearts sank within them, and they lay upon their oars in fear; but Orpheus called to Tiphys the helmsman, ‘Between them we must pass; so look ahead for an opening, and be brave, for Hera is with us.’ But Tiphys the cunning helmsman stood silent, clenching his teeth, till he saw a heron come flying mast-high toward the rocks, and hover awhile before them, as if looking for a passage through.  Then he cried, ‘Hera has sent us a pilot; let us follow the cunning bird.’

translation.en: The heroes' hearts sank, and they rested on their oars in fear.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 가슴이 철렁 내려앉아 두려움에 노에 기대어 가만히 있었습니다.

translation.en: But Orpheus called to Tiphys the helmsman.
translation.kr: 하지만 오르페우스가 조타수 티피스에게 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: We must pass between them, so look ahead for an opening.
translation.kr: 우리는 저 사이를 지나가야 하니 뚫고 나갈 길을 찾아보십시오.

translation.en: Be brave, for Hera is with us.
translation.kr: 헤라 여신께서 우리와 함께하시니 용기를 내십시오.

translation.en: The clever helmsman stood silent, clenching his teeth.
translation.kr: 영리한 조타수 티피스는 이를 악문 채 침묵을 지키며 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: Soon he saw a heron flying toward the rocks at mast-height.
translation.kr: 이내 그는 왜가리 한 마리가 바위를 향해 돛대 높이로 날아오는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: It hovered before them as if looking for a passage through.
translation.kr: 새는 마치 빠져나갈 길을 찾는 것처럼 그들 앞에서 잠시 맴돌았습니다.

translation.en: Then he cried, Hera has sent us a pilot!
translation.kr: 그러자 그가 소리쳤습니다. 헤라 여신께서 우리에게 길잡이를 보내주셨소!

translation.en: Let us follow the cunning bird.
translation.kr: 저 영리한 새를 따라갑시다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then the heron flapped to and fro a moment, till he saw a hidden gap, and into it he rushed like an arrow, while the heroes watched what would befall.

translation.en: The heron flapped back and forth for a moment.
translation.kr: 왜가리는 잠시 이리저리 날갯짓을 했습니다.

translation.en: It soon saw a hidden gap and rushed into it like an arrow.
translation.kr: 이내 숨겨진 틈을 발견한 새는 화살처럼 그곳으로 돌진했습니다.

translation.en: The heroes watched closely to see what would happen.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 무슨 일이 벌어질지 유심히 지켜보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And the blue rocks clashed together as the bird fled swiftly through; but they struck but a feather from his tail, and then rebounded apart at the shock.

translation.en: The blue rocks clashed together as the bird fled swiftly through.
translation.kr: 새가 날쌔게 빠져나갈 때 푸른 바위들이 쿵 하고 맞부딪혔습니다.

translation.en: They only struck a single feather from its tail.
translation.kr: 하지만 바위들은 꼬리 깃털 하나만을 스치고 지나갔을 뿐이었습니다.

translation.en: The rocks then rebounded apart from the powerful shock.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 바위들은 그 엄청난 충격에 다시 튕겨 나갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Tiphys cheered the heroes, and they shouted; and the oars bent like withes beneath their strokes as they rushed between those toppling ice-crags and the cold blue lips of death.  And ere the rocks could meet again they had passed them, and were safe out in the open sea.

translation.en: Tiphys cheered the heroes on, and they shouted in return.
translation.kr: 티피스가 영웅들을 격려하자 그들도 함성을 질렀습니다.

translation.en: The oars bent like willow branches beneath their powerful strokes.
translation.kr: 그들의 힘찬 노젓기에 노가 버드나무 가지처럼 휘어졌습니다.

translation.en: They rushed between the toppling ice-crags and the cold blue lips of death.
translation.kr: 그들은 무너져 내리는 얼음 절벽과 차갑고 푸른 죽음의 입술 사이로 돌진했습니다.

translation.en: Before the rocks could meet again, they had passed safely through.
translation.kr: 바위가 다시 만나기 전에 그들은 무사히 그곳을 통과했습니다.

translation.en: Finally, they were completely safe out in the open sea.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 탁 트인 바다로 나와 완전히 안전해졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And after that they sailed on wearily along the Asian coast, by the Black Cape and Thyneis, where the hot stream of Thymbris falls into the sea, and Sangarius, whose waters float on the Euxine, till they came to Wolf the river, and to Wolf the kindly king.  And there died two brave heroes, Idmon and Tiphys the wise helmsman: one died of an evil sickness, and one a wild boar slew.  So the heroes heaped a mound above them, and set upon it an oar on high, and left them there to sleep together, on the far-off Lycian shore.  But Idas killed the boar, and avenged Tiphys; and Ancaios took the rudder and was helmsman, and steered them on toward the east.

translation.en: After that, they sailed wearily along the Asian coast.
translation.kr: 그 후 그들은 아시아 해안을 따라 지친 몸을 이끌고 항해했습니다.

translation.en: They passed the Black Cape and Thyneis, where the hot stream of Thymbris falls into the sea.
translation.kr: 그들은 팀브리스의 뜨거운 물줄기가 바다로 떨어지는 검은 곶과 티네이스를 지났습니다.

translation.en: They also passed the Sangarius River, whose waters float on the Euxine Sea.
translation.kr: 또한 흑해 위를 떠다니는 상가리우스 강도 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: At last, they reached the Wolf River and met Wolf, the kindly king.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 늑대 강에 도착하여 친절한 늑대 왕을 만났습니다.

translation.en: There, two brave heroes, Idmon and Tiphys the wise helmsman, tragically died.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 두 명의 용감한 영웅인 이드몬과 지혜로운 조타수 티피스가 비극적인 죽음을 맞이했습니다.

translation.en: One died of a terrible sickness, and a wild boar slew the other.
translation.kr: 한 명은 끔찍한 병으로 죽었고, 다른 한 명은 멧돼지에게 목숨을 잃었습니다.

translation.en: The heroes heaped a burial mound above them and set a tall oar upon it.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 그들 위에 무덤을 쌓아 올리고 그 위에 높은 노를 세웠습니다.

translation.en: They left them there to sleep together on the distant Lycian shore.
translation.kr: 그리고 머나먼 리키아 해안에서 두 사람이 함께 잠들도록 남겨두었습니다.

translation.en: But Idas killed the boar and avenged Tiphys.
translation.kr: 하지만 이다스는 멧돼지를 죽여 티피스의 복수를 했습니다.

translation.en: Ancaeus then took the rudder, becoming the new helmsman.
translation.kr: 안카이오스가 키를 잡아 새로운 조타수가 되었습니다.

translation.en: He steered the ship onward toward the east.
translation.kr: 그는 동쪽을 향해 배를 몰았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And they went on past Sinope, and many a mighty river’s mouth, and past many a barbarous tribe, and the cities of the Amazons, the warlike women of the East, till all night they heard the clank of anvils and the roar of furnace-blasts, and the forge-fires shone like sparks through the darkness in the mountain glens aloft; for they were come to the shores of the Chalybes, the smiths who never tire, but serve Ares the cruel War-god, forging weapons day and night.

translation.en: They sailed past Sinope, numerous mighty river mouths, and many foreign tribes.
translation.kr: 그들은 시노페와 수많은 거대한 강어귀, 그리고 많은 이국적인 부족들을 지나쳐 항해했습니다.

translation.en: They passed the cities of the Amazons, the fierce warrior women of the East.
translation.kr: 그리고 동방의 사나운 여전사들인 아마존족의 도시들을 지나쳤습니다.

translation.en: All night they heard the clank of anvils and the roar of furnace blasts.
translation.kr: 밤새도록 모루를 두드리는 소리와 용광로가 뿜어내는 굉음이 들려왔습니다.

translation.en: Forge fires shone like sparks through the darkness in the mountain glens above.
translation.kr: 저 위쪽 산골짜기에서는 대장간의 불빛이 어둠 속에서 불꽃처럼 빛났습니다.

translation.en: They had reached the shores of the Chalybes, the tireless smiths.
translation.kr: 그들은 지칠 줄 모르는 대장장이들인 칼리베스족의 해안에 도착한 것이었습니다.

translation.en: These smiths forged weapons day and night to serve Ares, the cruel god of war.
translation.kr: 이 대장장이들은 잔혹한 전쟁의 신 아레스를 모시며 밤낮으로 무기를 만들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And at day-dawn they looked eastward, and midway between the sea and the sky they saw white snow-peaks hanging, glittering sharp and bright above the clouds.  And they knew that they were come to Caucasus, at the end of all the earth: Caucasus the highest of all mountains, the father of the rivers of the East.  On his peak lies chained the Titan, while a vulture tears his heart; and at his feet are piled dark forests round the magic Colchian land.

translation.en: At dawn they looked eastward and saw white snow peaks hanging between sea and sky.
translation.kr: 동이 트자 그들은 동쪽을 바라보았고, 바다와 하늘 사이에 새하얀 설봉들이 떠 있는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: The peaks glittered sharply and brightly above the clouds.
translation.kr: 그 봉우리들은 구름 위에서 날카롭고 눈부시게 반짝였습니다.

translation.en: They knew they had reached the Caucasus mountains at the very end of the earth.
translation.kr: 그들은 세상의 끝에 있는 코카서스산맥에 도착했다는 것을 깨달았습니다.

translation.en: The Caucasus was the highest of all mountains and the father of Eastern rivers.
translation.kr: 코카서스는 모든 산 중에서 가장 높았으며 동방으로 흐르는 강들의 아버지였습니다.

translation.en: A Titan lay chained on its peak while a vulture tore at his heart.
translation.kr: 그 산 정상에는 티탄족 하나가 사슬에 묶인 채 독수리에게 심장을 뜯기고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Below its feet, dark forests surrounded the magical land of Colchis.
translation.kr: 그 산기슭 아래로는 마법의 땅 콜키스를 둘러싼 울창하고 어두운 숲이 펼쳐져 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And they rowed three days to the eastward, while Caucasus rose higher hour by hour, till they saw the dark stream of Phasis rushing headlong to the sea, and, shining above the tree-tops, the golden roofs of King Aietes, the child of the Sun.

translation.en: They rowed eastward for three days as the Caucasus rose higher every hour.
translation.kr: 그들은 사흘 동안 동쪽으로 노를 저었고, 코카서스산맥은 시간마다 더 높이 솟아올랐습니다.

translation.en: Finally, they saw the dark stream of the Phasis river rushing wildly into the sea.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 바다로 거세게 흘러드는 파시스강의 어두운 물줄기를 보았습니다.

translation.en: Above the treetops shone the golden roofs of King Aeetes, child of the Sun.
translation.kr: 그리고 나무 꼭대기 위로는 태양의 아들 아이에테스 왕의 황금빛 지붕들이 빛나고 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then out spoke Ancaios the helmsman, ‘We are come to our goal at last, for there are the roofs of Aietes, and the woods where all poisons grow; but who can tell us where among them is hid the golden fleece?  Many a toil must we bear ere we find it, and bring it home to Greece.’

translation.en: Then Ancaeus the helmsman spoke up to the crew.
translation.kr: 그때 조타수 안카이오스가 선원들에게 말했습니다.

translation.en: We have finally reached our goal, for there are the roofs of Aeetes.
translation.kr: 우리는 마침내 목적지에 도달했소. 저기에 아이에테스의 지붕들이 보이기 때문이오.

translation.en: There are the woods where all deadly poisons grow.
translation.kr: 모든 치명적인 독초들이 자라는 숲도 저기에 있소.

translation.en: But who can tell us where the Golden Fleece is hidden among them?
translation.kr: 하지만 그 숲 어디에 황금 양모가 숨겨져 있는지 누가 우리에게 말해줄 수 있겠소?

translation.en: We must endure many hardships before we find it and bring it home to Greece.
translation.kr: 그것을 찾아 그리스의 고향으로 가져가기 전까지 우리는 많은 고난을 견뎌내야만 할 것이오.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But Jason cheered the heroes, for his heart was high and bold; and he said, ‘I will go alone up to Aietes, though he be the child of the Sun, and win him with soft words.  Better so than to go altogether, and to come to blows at once.’  But the Minuai would not stay behind, so they rowed boldly up the stream.

translation.en: But Jason cheered the heroes, for his heart was courageous and bold.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손은 용감하고 대담한 마음씨를 지녔기에 영웅들을 격려했습니다.

translation.en: I will go up to Aeetes alone, even though he is the child of the Sun.
translation.kr: 그가 비록 태양의 아들이라 할지라도, 나 홀로 아이에테스에게 올라가겠소.

translation.en: I will try to win him over with gentle words.
translation.kr: 부드러운 말로 그를 설득해 보도록 하겠소.

translation.en: This is better than going all together and starting a fight immediately.
translation.kr: 다 함께 몰려가 단번에 싸움을 벌이는 것보다 이 편이 나을 것이오.

translation.en: But the Minyans refused to stay behind, so they rowed boldly up the stream.
translation.kr: 그러나 미니아이 사람들은 뒤에 남기를 거부했고, 이내 대담하게 강을 거슬러 노를 저어갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And a dream came to Aietes, and filled his heart with fear.  He thought he saw a shining star, which fell into his daughter’s lap; and that Medeia his daughter took it gladly, and carried it to the river-side, and cast it in, and there the whirling river bore it down, and out into the Euxine Sea.

translation.en: A dream came to Aietes and filled his heart with fear.
translation.kr: 아이이에테스에게 꿈이 찾아와 그의 마음을 두려움으로 가득 채웠습니다.

translation.en: He dreamed a shining star fell into his daughter's lap.
translation.kr: 그는 빛나는 별이 딸의 무릎 위로 떨어지는 꿈을 꾸었습니다.

translation.en: His daughter Medea gladly carried it to the river and threw it in.
translation.kr: 그의 딸 메데이아는 기뻐하며 그것을 강으로 가져가 던졌습니다.

translation.en: The whirling river carried it down and out into the Euxine Sea.
translation.kr: 소용돌이치는 강물은 그것을 흑해로 실어 보냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then he leapt up in fear, and bade his servants bring his chariot, that he might go down to the river-side and appease the nymphs, and the heroes whose spirits haunt the bank.  So he went down in his golden chariot, and his daughters by his side, Medeia the fair witch-maiden, and Chalciope, who had been Phrixus’ wife, and behind him a crowd of servants and soldiers, for he was a rich and mighty prince.

translation.en: He leaped up in fear and ordered his servants to bring his chariot.
translation.kr: 그는 두려움에 벌떡 일어나 하인들에게 전차를 가져오라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: He wanted to go to the river to appease the nymphs and spirits of the bank.
translation.kr: 그는 강으로 가서 님프들과 강둑에 머무는 영혼들을 달래고 싶었습니다.

translation.en: He rode down in his golden chariot with his daughters beside him.
translation.kr: 그는 딸들을 곁에 태우고 황금 전차를 타고 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: These were the fair witch Medea and Chalciope, the widow of Phrixus.
translation.kr: 딸들은 아름다운 마녀 메데이아와 프릭소스의 미망인인 칼키오페였습니다.

translation.en: A crowd of servants and soldiers followed the rich and mighty prince.
translation.kr: 수많은 하인과 군인들이 이 부유하고 강력한 왕자의 뒤를 따랐습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And as he drove down by the reedy river he saw _Argo_ sliding up beneath the bank, and many a hero in her, like Immortals for beauty and for strength, as their weapons glittered round them in the level morning sunlight, through the white mist of the stream.  But Jason was the noblest of all; for Hera, who loved him, gave him beauty and tallness and terrible manhood.

translation.en: As he drove by the river, he saw the Argo gliding near the bank.
translation.kr: 강가를 달리던 중 그는 아르고 호가 강둑 근처로 미끄러지듯 다가오는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Many heroes were inside, looking like immortals in beauty and strength.
translation.kr: 그 안에는 아름다움과 힘에서 불멸의 신들과 같은 많은 영웅들이 있었습니다.

translation.en: Their weapons glittered in the morning sunlight through the white mist.
translation.kr: 그들의 무기는 하얀 안개 너머 아침 햇살을 받아 반짝였습니다.

translation.en: Jason was the noblest of all.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그중에서도 가장 고귀해 보였습니다.

translation.en: Hera loved him and gave him great beauty, height, and fierce manhood.
translation.kr: 헤라가 그를 사랑하여 뛰어난 아름다움과 큰 키, 그리고 늠름한 남성미를 주었기 때문입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And when they came near together and looked into each other’s eyes the heroes were awed before Aietes as he shone in his chariot, like his father the glorious Sun; for his robes were of rich gold tissue, and the rays of his diadem flashed fire; and in his hand he bore a jewelled sceptre, which glittered like the stars; and sternly he looked at them under his brows, and sternly he spoke and loud—

translation.en: When they came near, the heroes were awed by Aietes.
translation.kr: 가까이 다가갔을 때, 영웅들은 아이이에테스를 보고 경외감에 사로잡혔습니다.

translation.en: He shone in his chariot like his father, the glorious Sun.
translation.kr: 그는 자신의 아버지인 영광스러운 태양처럼 전차 안에서 빛나고 있었습니다.

translation.en: His robes were made of rich gold tissue.
translation.kr: 그의 옷은 화려한 금실로 짜여 있었습니다.

translation.en: The rays of his crown flashed with fire.
translation.kr: 그가 쓴 왕관의 빛은 불꽃처럼 번쩍였습니다.

translation.en: He held a jewelled scepter that glittered like the stars.
translation.kr: 그는 별처럼 반짝이는 보석 장식의 홀을 들고 있었습니다.

translation.en: He looked at them sternly and spoke in a loud voice.
translation.kr: 그는 엄격한 눈빛으로 그들을 바라보며 큰 소리로 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘Who are you, and what want you here, that you come to the shore of Cutaia?  Do you take no account of my rule, nor of my people the Colchians who serve me, who never tired yet in the battle, and know well how to face an invader?’

translation.en: Who are you, and what do you want on the shores of Cutaia?
translation.kr: 너희는 누구이며, 쿠타이아 해안에 와서 무엇을 바라는 것이냐?

translation.en: Do you have no respect for my rule or my Colchian people?
translation.kr: 너희는 나의 통치와 나를 섬기는 콜키스 백성들이 두렵지도 않단 말이냐?

translation.en: We never tire in battle and know how to face an invader.
translation.kr: 우리는 전투에서 결코 지치지 않으며 침략자에 맞서는 법을 잘 알고 있다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And the heroes sat silent awhile before the face of that ancient king. But Hera the awful goddess put courage into Jason’s heart, and he rose and shouted loudly in answer, ‘We are no pirates nor lawless men.  We come not to plunder and to ravage, or carry away slaves from your land; but my uncle, the son of Poseidon, Pelias the Minuan king, he it is who has set me on a quest to bring home the golden fleece.  And these too, my bold comrades, they are no nameless men; for some are the sons of Immortals, and some of heroes far renowned.  And we too never tire in battle, and know well how to give blows and to take: yet we wish to be guests at your table: it will be better so for both.’

translation.en: The heroes sat silently for a moment before the ancient king.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 그 늙은 왕 앞에서 잠시 말없이 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: But the awe-inspiring goddess Hera put courage into Jason's heart.
translation.kr: 하지만 경외감을 자아내는 여신 헤라가 이아손의 마음에 용기를 불어넣었습니다.

translation.en: He stood up and shouted his answer boldly.
translation.kr: 그는 자리에서 일어나 담대하게 소리쳐 대답했습니다.

translation.en: We are neither pirates nor lawless men.
translation.kr: 우리는 해적도 무법자도 아닙니다.

translation.en: We have not come to plunder, destroy, or take slaves from your land.
translation.kr: 우리는 당신의 땅을 약탈하거나 파괴하거나 노예를 잡아가려고 온 것이 아닙니다.

translation.en: My uncle Pelias, the Minyan king and son of Poseidon, sent me on a quest.
translation.kr: 포세이돈의 아들이자 미니아스의 왕인 제 삼촌 펠리아스가 저에게 임무를 맡겼습니다.

translation.en: He commanded me to bring the golden fleece back home.
translation.kr: 그는 제게 황금 양모를 고향으로 가져오라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: My brave comrades here are not nameless men, either.
translation.kr: 여기 있는 제 용감한 동료들도 이름 없는 자들이 아닙니다.

translation.en: Some are sons of immortals, and others are famous heroes.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 불멸의 신들의 아들이고, 또 어떤 이들은 널리 알려진 영웅들입니다.

translation.en: We never tire in battle and know exactly how to fight.
translation.kr: 우리는 전투에서 결코 지치지 않으며 싸우는 법을 아주 잘 알고 있습니다.

translation.en: Yet we wish to be peaceful guests at your table.
translation.kr: 하지만 우리는 당신의 식탁에서 평화로운 손님이 되고 싶습니다.

translation.en: This will be much better for both of us.
translation.kr: 그것이 우리 양측 모두에게 훨씬 나을 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Aietes’ race rushed up like a whirlwind, and his eyes flashed fire as he heard; but he crushed his anger down in his breast, and spoke mildly a cunning speech—

translation.en: King Aeetes's anger flared like a whirlwind.
translation.kr: 아이에테스 왕의 분노가 회오리바람처럼 치솟았습니다.

translation.en: His eyes flashed with fire as he listened.
translation.kr: 그의 눈은 이야기를 듣는 내내 불꽃처럼 번쩍였습니다.

translation.en: But he forced his rage down and spoke a cunning response mildly.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 분노를 억누르고 온화한 태도로 교활한 대답을 꺼냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘If you will fight for the fleece with my Colchians, then many a man must die.  But do you indeed expect to win from me the fleece in fight?  So few you are that if you be worsted I can load your ship with your corpses.  But if you will be ruled by me, you will find it better far to choose the best man among you, and let him fulfil the labours which I demand.  Then I will give him the golden fleece for a prize and a glory to you all.’

translation.en: If you fight my Colchian warriors for the fleece, many men will die.
translation.kr: 당신들이 황금 양모를 두고 콜키스 전사들과 싸운다면 많은 사람이 죽을 것이오.

translation.en: Do you truly expect to win the fleece from me in battle?
translation.kr: 당신들은 정말 전투를 통해 내게서 양모를 얻을 수 있다고 생각하시오?

translation.en: You have so few men that I could fill your ship with your corpses.
translation.kr: 당신들은 수가 너무 적어서 패배하면 당신들의 시체로 배를 채울 수도 있소.

translation.en: But if you listen to me, you will find a much better way.
translation.kr: 하지만 내 제안을 따른다면 훨씬 더 나은 방법을 찾을 수 있을 것이오.

translation.en: Choose the best man among you.
translation.kr: 당신들 중에서 가장 훌륭한 자를 고르시오.

translation.en: Let him complete the tasks that I demand.
translation.kr: 그리고 그가 내가 요구하는 과업들을 완수하게 하시오.

translation.en: If he succeeds, I will give him the golden fleece as a prize.
translation.kr: 성공한다면 그에게 황금 양모를 상으로 주겠소.

translation.en: It will be a great glory to all of you.
translation.kr: 그것은 당신들 모두에게도 큰 영광이 될 것이오.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So saying, he turned his horses and drove back in silence to the town. And the Minuai sat silent with sorrow, and longed for Heracles and his strength; for there was no facing the thousands of the Colchians and the fearful chance of war.

translation.en: After speaking, the king turned his horses and drove back to the city in silence.
translation.kr: 그렇게 말한 뒤, 왕은 말머리를 돌려 아무 말 없이 도시로 돌아갔습니다.

translation.en: The Minyans sat in silent sorrow.
translation.kr: 미니아스인들은 슬픔에 잠겨 말없이 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: They deeply missed Heracles and his immense strength.
translation.kr: 그들은 헤라클레스와 그의 엄청난 힘을 몹시 그리워했습니다.

translation.en: They could not possibly face thousands of Colchian warriors in a terrifying war.
translation.kr: 수천 명의 콜키스 전사들과 맞서 끔찍한 전쟁을 치를 수는 없었기 때문입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But Chalciope, Phrixus’ widow, went weeping to the town; for she remembered her Minuan husband, and all the pleasures of her youth, while she watched the fair faces of his kinsmen, and their long locks of golden hair.  And she whispered to Medeia her sister, ‘Why should all these brave men die? why does not my father give them up the fleece, that my husband’s spirit may have rest?’

translation.en: But Phrixus's widow, Chalciope, went back to the city in tears.
translation.kr: 하지만 프리크소스의 미망인인 칼키오페는 눈물을 흘리며 도시로 돌아갔습니다.

translation.en: She remembered her Minyan husband and the joys of her youth.
translation.kr: 그녀는 미니아스인이었던 남편과 젊은 시절의 기쁨을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: She felt this as she watched his kinsmen with their fair faces and long golden hair.
translation.kr: 아름다운 얼굴에 긴 금발을 가진 남편의 동족들을 보았기 때문입니다.

translation.en: She whispered softly to her sister, Medea.
translation.kr: 그녀는 여동생 메데이아에게 작게 속삭였습니다.

translation.en: Why should all these brave men have to die?
translation.kr: 왜 이 용감한 남자들이 모두 죽어야만 하는 걸까?

translation.en: Why does our father not simply give them the fleece?
translation.kr: 왜 아버지는 그냥 그들에게 양모를 내주지 않으시는 걸까?

translation.en: Then my husband's spirit could finally find rest.
translation.kr: 그러면 내 남편의 영혼도 마침내 안식을 찾을 수 있을 텐데.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And Medeia’s heart pitied the heroes, and Jason most of all; and she answered, ‘Our father is stern and terrible, and who can win the golden fleece?’  But Chalciope said, ‘These men are not like our men; there is nothing which they cannot dare nor do.’

translation.en: Medeia felt deep pity for the heroes, and especially for Jason.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 영웅들, 특히 이아손에게 깊은 연민을 느꼈습니다.

translation.en: Our father is stern and terrifying, so who could possibly win the golden fleece? she answered.
translation.kr: 우리 아버지는 엄격하고 무서운 분이신데 누가 감히 황금 양모를 얻을 수 있겠어? 그녀가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: But Chalciope said these men were unlike their own.
translation.kr: 하지만 칼키오페는 이 사람들이 이곳의 남자들과는 다르다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: There is nothing they cannot dare or do.
translation.kr: 그들은 두려워하거나 해내지 못할 일이 전혀 없어.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And Medeia thought of Jason and his brave countenance, and said, ‘If there was one among them who knew no fear, I could show him how to win the fleece.’

translation.en: Medeia thought of Jason and his courageous face.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 이아손과 그의 용맹한 얼굴을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: If there is a man among them who knows no fear, I can show him how to win the fleece, she said.
translation.kr: 그들 중 두려움을 모르는 자가 있다면, 내가 그에게 황금 양모를 얻는 방법을 알려줄 수 있어, 그녀가 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So in the dusk of evening they went down to the river-side, Chalciope and Medeia the witch-maiden, and Argus, Phrixus’ son.  And Argus the boy crept forward, among the beds of reeds, till he came where the heroes were sleeping, on the thwarts of the ship, beneath the bank, while Jason kept ward on shore, and leant upon his lance full of thought.  And the boy came to Jason, and said—

translation.en: In the evening dusk, Chalciope, the witch-maiden Medeia, and Phrixus's son Argus went down to the riverbank.
translation.kr: 해 질 녘 어스름 속에 칼키오페와 마녀 소녀 메데이아, 그리고 프릭소스의 아들 아르고스가 강가로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: The boy Argus crept forward through the reed beds.
translation.kr: 소년 아르고스는 갈대밭 사이로 살금살금 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: He reached the place beneath the bank where the heroes were sleeping on the ship's benches.
translation.kr: 그는 강둑 아래 배의 의자 위에서 영웅들이 잠들어 있는 곳에 다다랐습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, Jason kept watch on shore, leaning on his spear lost in thought.
translation.kr: 그동안 이아손은 창에 기대어 깊은 생각에 잠긴 채 해변에서 망을 보고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The boy approached Jason and spoke.
translation.kr: 소년이 이아손에게 다가가 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘I am the son of Phrixus, your Cousin; and Chalciope my mother waits for you, to talk about the golden fleece.’

translation.en: I am the son of your cousin Phrixus.
translation.kr: 저는 당신의 사촌인 프릭소스의 아들입니다.

translation.en: My mother Chalciope is waiting to talk to you about the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 어머니 칼키오페께서 황금 양모에 대해 의논하려고 당신을 기다리고 계십니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Jason went boldly with the boy, and found the two princesses standing; and when Chalciope saw him she wept, and took his hands, and cried—‘O cousin of my beloved, go home before you die!’

translation.en: Jason boldly followed the boy and found the two princesses standing there.
translation.kr: 이아손은 용감하게 소년을 따라갔고, 그곳에 서 있는 두 공주를 발견했습니다.

translation.en: When Chalciope saw him, she wept and took his hands.
translation.kr: 칼키오페는 그를 보자마자 눈물을 흘리며 두 손을 붙잡았습니다.

translation.en: O cousin of my beloved, go home before you die! she cried.
translation.kr: 내 사랑하는 이의 사촌이여, 목숨을 잃기 전에 어서 고향으로 돌아가시오! 그녀가 외쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘It would be base to go home now, fair princess, and to have sailed all these seas in vain.’  Then both the princesses besought him; but Jason said, ‘It is too late.’

translation.en: It would be shameful to return home now, fair princess.
translation.kr: 공주님, 지금 고향으로 돌아가는 것은 수치스러운 일입니다.

translation.en: I will not have sailed all these seas in vain.
translation.kr: 이 모든 바다를 헛되이 항해한 채로 남을 수는 없습니다.

translation.en: Both princesses begged him to reconsider.
translation.kr: 두 공주가 마음을 돌려달라고 간청했습니다.

translation.en: But Jason insisted it was too late.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손은 이미 늦었다고 고집했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘But you know not,’ said Medeia, ‘what he must do who would win the fleece.  He must tame the two brazen-footed bulls, who breathe devouring flame; and with them he must plough ere nightfall four acres in the field of Ares; and he must sow them with serpents’ teeth, of which each tooth springs up into an armed man.  Then he must fight with all those warriors; and little will it profit him to conquer them, for the fleece is guarded by a serpent, more huge than any mountain pine; and over his body you must step if you would reach the golden fleece.’

translation.en: Medeia spoke out.
translation.kr: 메데이아가 말했습니다.

translation.en: You do not know what the one who seeks the fleece must face.
translation.kr: 황금 양털을 얻으려는 자가 무엇을 해야 하는지 당신은 모릅니다.

translation.en: He must tame two brazen-footed bulls that breathe devouring flames.
translation.kr: 탐욕스러운 불꽃을 내뿜는 청동 발의 두 황소를 길들여야 합니다.

translation.en: With them, he must plough four acres in the field of Ares before nightfall.
translation.kr: 해가 지기 전에 그 황소들로 아레스의 들판 4에이커를 갈아야 합니다.

translation.en: He must then sow the teeth of serpents, which will spring up into armed men.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 독사의 이빨을 뿌려야 하는데, 이빨마다 무장한 전사가 솟아납니다.

translation.en: You must fight all those warriors.
translation.kr: 그러면 당신은 그 모든 전사들과 싸워야 합니다.

translation.en: But defeating them brings little profit.
translation.kr: 그들을 물리쳐도 큰 소용이 없습니다.

translation.en: The fleece is guarded by a serpent larger than any mountain pine.
translation.kr: 황금 양털은 산속의 소나무보다 더 거대한 뱀이 지키고 있기 때문입니다.

translation.en: You must step over its body to reach the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 황금 양털에 닿으려면 그 뱀의 몸을 밟고 지나가야 합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Jason laughed bitterly.  ‘Unjustly is that fleece kept here, and by an unjust and lawless king; and unjustly shall I die in my youth, for I will attempt it ere another sun be set.’

translation.en: Jason laughed bitterly.
translation.kr: 이아손은 씁쓸하게 웃었습니다.

translation.en: This fleece is kept unjustly by a lawless king.
translation.kr: 이 양털은 부당하고 무법적인 왕에 의해 이곳에 부당하게 보관되어 있습니다.

translation.en: I shall attempt it before another sun sets, even if it means dying unjustly in my youth.
translation.kr: 저는 또 다른 해가 지기 전에 그것을 시도할 것이고 부당하게 젊은 나이에 죽게 될 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Medeia trembled, and said, ‘No mortal man can reach that fleece unless I guide him through.  For round it, beyond the river, is a wall full nine ells high, with lofty towers and buttresses, and mighty gates of threefold brass; and over the gates the wall is arched, with golden battlements above.  And over the gateway sits Brimo, the wild witch-huntress of the woods, brandishing a pine-torch in her hands, while her mad hounds howl around.  No man dare meet her or look on her, but only I her priestess, and she watches far and wide lest any stranger should come near.’

translation.en: Medeia trembled as she spoke.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 떨면서 말했습니다.

translation.en: No mortal can reach the fleece without my guidance.
translation.kr: 제가 안내하지 않으면 어떤 필멸자도 그 양털에 다가갈 수 없습니다.

translation.en: Beyond the river, a wall nine ells high surrounds it.
translation.kr: 강 너머 양털 주변에는 9엘 높이의 성벽이 있습니다.

translation.en: It has lofty towers, strong buttresses, and mighty gates of threefold brass.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 높이 솟은 탑과 튼튼한 버팀벽, 삼중 놋쇠로 된 거대한 문이 있습니다.

translation.en: The wall arches over the gates, topped with golden battlements.
translation.kr: 문 위로는 성벽이 아치형을 이루고 황금빛 흉벽이 솟아 있습니다.

translation.en: Over the gateway sits Brimo, the wild witch-huntress of the woods, brandishing a pine torch.
translation.kr: 숲의 거친 마녀 사냥꾼 브리모가 문 위에 앉아 손에 소나무 횃불을 휘두릅니다.

translation.en: Her mad hounds howl around her.
translation.kr: 그녀의 주변에서는 미친 사냥개들이 울부짖습니다.

translation.en: No man dares to face her or look upon her.
translation.kr: 어떤 남자도 감히 그녀를 마주하거나 쳐다볼 수 없습니다.

translation.en: Only I, her priestess, may do so.
translation.kr: 오직 그녀의 여사제인 저만이 가능합니다.

translation.en: She watches tirelessly so no stranger can approach.
translation.kr: 그녀는 낯선 이가 접근하지 못하도록 사방을 샅샅이 감시합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘No wall so high but it may be climbed at last, and no wood so thick but it may be crawled through; no serpent so wary but he may be charmed, or witch-queen so fierce but spells may soothe her; and I may yet win the golden fleece, if a wise maiden help bold men.’

translation.en: No wall is too high to be climbed, and no wood is too thick to crawl through.
translation.kr: 아무리 높은 벽이라도 결국 오를 수 있고, 아무리 빽빽한 숲이라도 기어갈 수 있습니다.

translation.en: No serpent is so wary it cannot be charmed, and no witch-queen is too fierce to be soothed by spells.
translation.kr: 아무리 조심성 많은 뱀이라도 마법에 걸릴 수 있고, 아무리 사나운 마녀 여왕이라도 마법으로 진정시킬 수 있습니다.

translation.en: If a wise maiden helps bold men, I may still win the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 지혜로운 처녀가 용감한 남자를 돕는다면 저는 여전히 황금 양털을 얻을 수 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And he looked at Medeia cunningly, and held her with his glittering eye, till she blushed and trembled, and said—

translation.en: Jason looked at Medeia cunningly.
translation.kr: 이아손은 메데이아를 교활하게 바라보았습니다.

translation.en: He captivated her with his glittering eyes, until she blushed and trembled, saying—
translation.kr: 그는 번쩍이는 눈빛으로 그녀를 사로잡았고, 그녀는 얼굴을 붉히며 떨리는 목소리로 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘Who can face the fire of the bulls’ breath, and fight ten thousand armed men?’

translation.en: Who can face the bulls' fiery breath and fight ten thousand armed men?
translation.kr: 누가 황소 입김의 불꽃을 마주하고 만 명의 무장한 남자와 싸울 수 있겠습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘He whom you help,’ said Jason, flattering her, ‘for your fame is spread over all the earth.  Are you not the queen of all enchantresses, wiser even than your sister Circe, in her fairy island in the West?’

translation.en: Jason flattered her with his response.
translation.kr: 이아손이 그녀에게 아부하며 말했습니다.

translation.en: The one you choose to help.
translation.kr: 당신이 돕는 사람입니다.

translation.en: Are you not the queen of all enchantresses, wiser even than your sister Circe on her fairy island in the West?
translation.kr: 서쪽 요정의 섬에 있는 당신의 언니 키르케보다 더 지혜로운 모든 마법사의 여왕이 아니십니까?

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘Would that I were with my sister Circe in her fairy island in the West, far away from sore temptation and thoughts which tear the heart!  But if it must be so—for why should you die?—I have an ointment here; I made it from the magic ice-flower which sprang from Prometheus’ wound, above the clouds on Caucasus, in the dreary fields of snow.  Anoint yourself with that, and you shall have in you seven men’s strength; and anoint your shield with it, and neither fire nor sword can harm you.  But what you begin you must end before sunset, for its virtue lasts only one day.  And anoint your helmet with it before you sow the serpents’ teeth; and when the sons of earth spring up, cast your helmet among their ranks, and the deadly crop of the War-god’s field will mow itself, and perish.’

translation.en: I wish I were with my sister Circe on her fairy island in the West, far from sore temptations and heartbreaking thoughts!
translation.kr: 뼈아픈 유혹과 가슴을 찢는 생각들로부터 멀리 떨어져 서쪽 요정의 섬에 있는 언니 키르케와 함께 있다면 얼마나 좋을까요!

translation.en: But if it must be so, why should you die?
translation.kr: 하지만 꼭 그래야 한다면 왜 당신이 죽어야 합니까?

translation.en: I have an ointment here.
translation.kr: 여기에 연고가 있습니다.

translation.en: I made it from the magic ice-flower that sprang from Prometheus' wound, high on the snowy fields of the Caucasus.
translation.kr: 저는 카프카스의 구름 위 삭막한 눈밭에서 프로메테우스의 상처에서 피어난 마법의 얼음꽃으로 이것을 만들었습니다.

translation.en: Anoint yourself with it, and you shall gain the strength of seven men.
translation.kr: 이 연고를 몸에 바르면 일곱 남자의 힘을 얻게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: Anoint your shield, and neither fire nor sword will harm you.
translation.kr: 방패에 바르면 불도 칼도 당신을 해칠 수 없습니다.

translation.en: But you must finish before sunset, as its power lasts only one day.
translation.kr: 효력은 하루만 지속되니 시작한 일은 해지기 전에 끝내야 합니다.

translation.en: Anoint your helmet before you sow the serpents' teeth.
translation.kr: 독사의 이빨을 뿌리기 전에 투구에도 이것을 바르십시오.

translation.en: When the sons of earth spring up, cast your helmet among them.
translation.kr: 대지의 아들들이 솟아날 때 무리 가운데로 투구를 던지십시오.

translation.en: Then the deadly crop of the War-god's field will turn on itself and perish.
translation.kr: 그러면 전쟁의 신이 다스리는 들판의 치명적인 작물들이 스스로를 베고 파멸할 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Jason fell on his knees before her, and thanked her and kissed her hands; and she gave him the vase of ointment, and fled trembling through the reeds.  And Jason told his comrades what had happened, and showed them the box of ointment; and all rejoiced but Idas, and he grew mad with envy.

translation.en: Jason fell to his knees, thanking her and kissing her hands.
translation.kr: 그러자 이아손은 그녀 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 감사하며 그녀의 손에 입을 맞추었습니다.

translation.en: She handed him the vase of ointment and fled trembling through the reeds.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 그에게 연고병을 주고 갈대 사이로 떨며 달아났습니다.

translation.en: Jason told his comrades what had happened and showed them the ointment.
translation.kr: 이아손은 동료들에게 일어난 일을 말하고 연고 상자를 보여주었습니다.

translation.en: Everyone rejoiced except Idas, who grew mad with envy.
translation.kr: 이다스를 제외한 모두가 기뻐했지만, 이다스는 질투심에 미쳐버렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And at sunrise Jason went and bathed, and anointed himself from head to foot, and his shield, and his helmet, and his weapons, and bade his comrades try the spell.  So they tried to bend his lance, but it stood like an iron bar; and Idas in spite hewed at it with his sword, but the blade flew to splinters in his face.  Then they hurled their lances at his shield, but the spear-points turned like lead; and Caineus tried to throw him, but he never stirred a foot; and Polydeuces struck him with his fist a blow which would have killed an ox, but Jason only smiled, and the heroes danced about him with delight; and he leapt, and ran, and shouted in the joy of that enormous strength, till the sun rose, and it was time to go and to claim Aietes’ promise.

translation.en: At sunrise, Jason bathed and anointed himself from head to foot.
translation.kr: 해가 뜨자 이아손은 목욕을 하고 머리부터 발끝까지 연고를 발랐습니다.

translation.en: He also anointed his shield, helmet, and weapons, then asked his comrades to test the spell.
translation.kr: 방패와 투구와 무기에도 바르고 동료들에게 마법을 시험해 보라고 했습니다.

translation.en: They tried to bend his lance, but it remained as rigid as an iron bar.
translation.kr: 그들이 창을 구부리려 했지만 창은 쇠막대기처럼 굳건했습니다.

translation.en: Idas spitefully struck it with his sword, but the blade shattered into his face.
translation.kr: 이다스가 악의를 품고 칼로 내리쳤지만 칼날은 산산조각 나서 그의 얼굴로 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: They hurled their lances at his shield, but the spearheads bent like lead.
translation.kr: 방패에 창을 던졌지만 창끝은 납처럼 휘어졌습니다.

translation.en: Caineus tried to throw him, but Jason did not budge an inch.
translation.kr: 카이네우스가 그를 던지려 했지만 이아손은 한 발짝도 움직이지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Polydeuces struck him with a blow that could kill an ox, but Jason only smiled.
translation.kr: 폴리데우케스가 황소라도 죽일 만한 주먹으로 그를 쳤지만 이아손은 미소만 지었습니다.

translation.en: The heroes danced around him in delight.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 기뻐하며 그의 주위를 돌며 춤을 추었습니다.

translation.en: Jason leapt, ran, and shouted in the joy of his enormous strength until the sun fully rose.
translation.kr: 이아손은 해가 뜰 때까지 엄청난 힘의 기쁨에 겨워 뛰고 달리고 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: It was finally time to claim Aietes' promise.
translation.kr: 마침내 아이에테스의 약속을 요구하러 갈 시간이 되었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So he sent up Telamon and Aithalides to tell Aietes that he was ready for the fight; and they went up among the marble walls, and beneath the roofs of gold, and stood in Aietes’ hall, while he grew pale with rage.

translation.en: He sent Telamon and Aithalides to tell Aietes he was ready for the fight.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 텔라몬과 아이탈리데스를 보내 아이에테스에게 싸울 준비가 되었다고 전했습니다.

translation.en: They walked among marble walls and golden roofs into Aietes' hall, where the king turned pale with rage.
translation.kr: 그들은 대리석 성벽 사이와 황금 지붕 아래로 올라가 아이에테스의 홀에 섰고, 왕은 분노로 창백해졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘Fulfil your promise to us, child of the blazing Sun.  Give us the serpents’ teeth, and let loose the fiery bulls; for we have found a champion among us who can win the golden fleece.’

translation.en: Fulfill your promise to us, child of the blazing Sun.
translation.kr: 불타는 태양의 자손이여, 우리에게 한 약속을 지키십시오.

translation.en: Give us the serpents' teeth and unleash the fiery bulls.
translation.kr: 우리에게 독사의 이빨을 주고 불타는 황소를 풀어주십시오.

translation.en: We have found a champion among us who can claim the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 황금 양털을 차지할 챔피언을 우리 사이에서 찾았기 때문입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And Aietes bit his lips, for he fancied that they had fled away by night: but he could not go back from his promise; so he gave them the serpents’ teeth.

translation.en: Aietes bit his lip, having hoped they had fled in the night.
translation.kr: 아이에테스는 그들이 밤에 도망쳤다고 상상했기 때문에 입술을 깨물었습니다.

translation.en: He could not break his promise, so he handed over the serpents' teeth.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 약속을 물릴 수 없었고, 그래서 그들에게 독사의 이빨을 주었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then he called for his chariot and his horses, and sent heralds through all the town; and all the people went out with him to the dreadful War-god’s field.

translation.en: He then called for his chariot and sent heralds throughout the town.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 그는 전차와 말을 부르고 온 도시에 전령을 보냈습니다.

translation.en: All the people followed him to the dreadful field of the War-god.
translation.kr: 그리고 모든 사람들이 그와 함께 전쟁의 신이 다스리는 무서운 들판으로 나갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And there Aietes sat upon his throne, with his warriors on each hand, thousands and tens of thousands, clothed from head to foot in steel chain-mail.  And the people and the women crowded to every window and bank and wall; while the Minuai stood together, a mere handful in the midst of that great host.

translation.en: Aietes sat on his throne, flanked by tens of thousands of warriors in full chain-mail.
translation.kr: 아이에테스는 양옆에 머리부터 발끝까지 강철 사슬 갑옷을 입은 수만 명의 전사들을 거느리고 왕좌에 앉았습니다.

translation.en: The townspeople crowded every window, bank, and wall.
translation.kr: 사람들과 여자들은 모든 창문과 언덕과 성벽으로 몰려들었습니다.

translation.en: The Minuai stood together, a small handful amidst the vast host.
translation.kr: 그 엄청난 군중 한가운데에 미니아스인들은 소수만이 뭉쳐 서 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And Chalciope was there and Argus, trembling, and Medeia, wrapped closely in her veil; but Aietes did not know that she was muttering cunning spells between her lips.

translation.en: Chalciope and Argus stood there trembling.
translation.kr: 칼키오페와 아르고스도 두려움에 떨며 그곳에 있었습니다.

translation.en: Medeia was closely wrapped in her veil.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 베일로 얼굴을 꽁꽁 싸맨 채 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: Aietes did not realize she was muttering cunning spells under her breath.
translation.kr: 아이에테스는 그녀가 입술 사이로 교활한 주문을 중얼거리고 있다는 것을 알지 못했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Jason cried, ‘Fulfil your promise, and let your fiery bulls come forth.’

translation.en: Jason cried out.
translation.kr: 그러자 이아손이 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Fulfill your promise and bring forth your fiery bulls.
translation.kr: 약속을 이행하고 불타는 황소가 나오게 하십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Aietes bade open the gates, and the magic bulls leapt out.  Their brazen hoofs rang upon the ground, and their nostrils sent out sheets of flame, as they rushed with lowered heads upon Jason; but he never flinched a step.  The flame of their breath swept round him, but it singed not a hair of his head; and the bulls stopped short and trembled when Medeia began her spell.

translation.en: Aietes ordered the gates opened, and the magic bulls charged out.
translation.kr: 그러자 아이에테스가 문을 열라고 명령했고, 마법의 황소들이 뛰쳐나왔습니다.

translation.en: Their brazen hooves rang, and their nostrils blasted sheets of flame.
translation.kr: 놋쇠 발굽이 땅에 부딪히며 울렸고, 콧구멍에서는 화염이 뿜어져 나왔습니다.

translation.en: They rushed at Jason with lowered heads, but he never flinched.
translation.kr: 그들은 고개를 숙이고 이아손을 향해 돌진했지만 그는 한 발짝도 움찔하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: The fiery breath swept around him without singeing a single hair.
translation.kr: 황소의 입김에서 뿜어져 나온 불꽃이 그를 휩쓸었지만 머리카락 하나 그을리지 않았습니다.

translation.en: As Medeia began her spell, the bulls stopped and trembled.
translation.kr: 메데이아가 주문을 시작하자 황소들은 걸음을 멈추고 몸을 떨었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Jason sprang upon the nearest and seized him by the horn; and up and down they wrestled, till the bull fell grovelling on his knees; for the heart of the brute died within him, and his mighty limbs were loosed, beneath the steadfast eye of that dark witch-maiden and the magic whisper of her lips.

translation.en: Jason leapt upon the nearest bull and seized it by the horns.
translation.kr: 이아손은 가장 가까운 황소에게 달려들어 뿔을 잡았습니다.

translation.en: They wrestled until the bull was forced to its knees.
translation.kr: 황소가 무릎을 꿇고 엎드릴 때까지 그들은 엎치락뒤치락 씨름을 벌였습니다.

translation.en: The beast's spirit broke under the steadfast gaze of the dark witch-maiden.
translation.kr: 어둠의 마녀 처녀의 확고한 눈빛과 마법의 속삭임에 짐승의 기세가 꺾이고 말았습니다.

translation.en: Its mighty limbs weakened at the magical whisper of her lips.
translation.kr: 그리고 그 강력한 사지의 힘이 풀렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So both the bulls were tamed and yoked; and Jason bound them to the plough, and goaded them onward with his lance till he had ploughed the sacred field.

translation.en: Both bulls were tamed and yoked.
translation.kr: 그래서 두 마리의 황소는 길들여져 멍에를 메게 되었습니다.

translation.en: Jason bound them to the plough, goading them with his lance to plough the sacred field.
translation.kr: 이아손은 황소들을 쟁기에 묶고 창으로 찌르며 몰아서 신성한 들판을 갈았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And all the Minuai shouted; but Aietes bit his lips with rage, for the half of Jason’s work was over, and the sun was yet high in heaven.

translation.en: All the Minuai shouted in triumph.
translation.kr: 모든 미니아스인들이 환호했습니다.

translation.en: Aietes bit his lip in rage, for Jason had finished half his task while the sun was still high.
translation.kr: 이아손의 일이 절반이나 끝났고 해는 아직 하늘 높이 떠 있었기에, 아이에테스는 분노로 입술을 깨물었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then he took the serpents’ teeth and sowed them, and waited what would befall.  But Medeia looked at him and at his helmet, lest he should forget the lesson she had taught.

translation.en: Jason then sowed the serpents' teeth and waited to see what would happen.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 이아손은 독사의 이빨을 가져다가 뿌리고 무슨 일이 일어날지 기다렸습니다.

translation.en: Medeia watched him carefully, ensuring he did not forget her instructions.
translation.kr: 하지만 메데이아는 그가 가르쳐 준 교훈을 잊을까 봐 그와 그의 투구를 번갈아 바라보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And every furrow heaved and bubbled, and out of every clod arose a man. Out of the earth they rose by thousands, each clad from head to foot in steel, and drew their swords and rushed on Jason, where he stood in the midst alone.

translation.en: Every furrow heaved and bubbled, and a man rose from every clod.
translation.kr: 밭고랑마다 들썩이고 거품이 일더니 흙덩이마다 사람이 솟아올랐습니다.

translation.en: Thousands of men clad in steel sprang from the earth.
translation.kr: 머리부터 발끝까지 강철로 무장한 수천 명의 남자들이 땅에서 솟아났습니다.

translation.en: They drew their swords and rushed at Jason, who stood alone in their midst.
translation.kr: 그들은 칼을 뽑고 한가운데 홀로 서 있는 이아손에게 달려들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then the Minuai grew pale with fear for him; but Aietes laughed a bitter laugh.  ‘See! if I had not warriors enough already round me, I could call them out of the bosom of the earth.’

translation.en: The Minuai grew pale with fear, but Aietes let out a bitter laugh.
translation.kr: 미니아스인들은 그를 걱정하며 두려움에 창백해졌지만, 아이에테스는 씁쓸한 웃음을 지었습니다.

translation.en: If I lacked warriors around me, I could always summon them from the earth's bosom.
translation.kr: 보라! 내 주위에 이미 전사들이 충분하지 않다면, 대지의 품에서 그들을 불러낼 수 있을 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But Jason snatched off his helmet, and hurled it into the thickest of the throng.  And blind madness came upon them, suspicion, hate, and fear; and one cried to his fellow, ‘Thou didst strike me!’ and another, ‘Thou art Jason; thou shalt die!’  So fury seized those earth-born phantoms, and each turned his hand against the rest; and they fought and were never weary, till they all lay dead upon the ground.  Then the magic furrows opened, and the kind earth took them home into her breast and the grass grew up all green again above them, and Jason’s work was done.

translation.en: Jason snatched off his helmet and hurled it into the thickest part of the crowd.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손은 투구를 벗어 군중이 가장 빽빽한 곳으로 던졌습니다.

translation.en: Blind madness, suspicion, hate, and fear overcame them.
translation.kr: 그러자 그들에게 의심과 증오, 두려움이라는 맹목적인 광기가 찾아왔습니다.

translation.en: They accused each other, crying out in confusion and anger.
translation.kr: 한 명이 동료에게 "네가 나를 쳤다!"라고 외쳤고, 다른 한 명은 "네가 이아손이구나. 죽어라!"라고 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Fury seized the earth-born phantoms, turning them against one another.
translation.kr: 흙에서 태어난 유령들은 분노에 사로잡혀 각자 서로에게 칼을 겨누었습니다.

translation.en: They fought tirelessly until every single one lay dead on the ground.
translation.kr: 그들은 지치지도 않고 싸워 마침내 모두 땅에 쓰러져 죽었습니다.

translation.en: The magic furrows opened, and the kind earth took them back into her breast.
translation.kr: 마법의 밭고랑이 열리고 자비로운 대지가 그들을 가슴으로 거두어들였습니다.

translation.en: Green grass grew over them again, and Jason's work was complete.
translation.kr: 그들 위로 다시 푸른 풀이 자라났고 이아손의 임무는 끝이 났습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then the Minuai rose and shouted, till Prometheus heard them from his crag.  And Jason cried, ‘Lead me to the fleece this moment, before the sun goes down.’

translation.en: The Minuai rose and shouted loud enough for Prometheus to hear from his crag.
translation.kr: 그러자 미니아스인들이 일어나 소리를 질렀고, 바위산에 있던 프로메테우스까지 그 소리를 들었습니다.

translation.en: Jason demanded to be led to the fleece before the sun set.
translation.kr: 이아손이 외쳤습니다. 해가 지기 전에 지금 당장 나를 황금 양털로 안내하시오.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But Aietes thought, ‘He has conquered the bulls, and sown and reaped the deadly crop.  Who is this who is proof against all magic?  He may kill the serpent yet.’  So he delayed, and sat taking counsel with his princes till the sun went down and all was dark.  Then he bade a herald cry, ‘Every man to his home for to-night.  To-morrow we will meet these heroes, and speak about the golden fleece.’

translation.en: Aietes pondered the situation.
translation.kr: 하지만 아이에테스는 생각했습니다.

translation.en: He conquered the bulls and harvested the deadly crop.
translation.kr: 그는 황소를 정복하고 치명적인 작물을 뿌려 거두었다.

translation.en: Who is this man immune to all magic? He might even slay the serpent.
translation.kr: 이 모든 마법을 견뎌낸 자는 대체 누구란 말인가? 그는 뱀마저 죽일지도 모른다.

translation.en: He delayed, taking counsel with his princes until darkness fell.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 지체하며 해가 지고 사방이 어두워질 때까지 왕자들과 앉아 상의했습니다.

translation.en: Then he ordered a herald to dismiss everyone for the night.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 전령에게 외치게 했습니다. 오늘 밤은 모두 집으로 돌아가라.

translation.en: We will meet these heroes tomorrow to discuss the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 내일 우리는 이 영웅들을 만나 황금 양털에 대해 이야기할 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then he turned and looked at Medeia.  ‘This is your doing, false witch-maid!  You have helped these yellow-haired strangers, and brought shame upon your father and yourself!’

translation.en: He turned and glared at Medeia.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 그는 돌아서서 메데이아를 바라보았습니다.

translation.en: This is your doing, you false witch!
translation.kr: 거짓된 마녀 계집, 이 모든 것이 네 짓이구나!

translation.en: You helped these strangers and shamed both your father and yourself!
translation.kr: 너는 이 노란 머리의 이방인들을 도와 아버지와 네 자신에게 수치를 안겨주었다!

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Medeia shrank and trembled, and her face grew pale with fear; and Aietes knew that she was guilty, and whispered, ‘If they win the fleece, you die!’

translation.en: Medeia shrank back in pale terror.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 움츠러들며 떨었고 두려움에 얼굴이 창백해졌습니다.

translation.en: Aietes knew she was guilty and whispered a threat.
translation.kr: 아이에테스는 그녀가 유죄임을 직감하고 속삭였습니다.

translation.en: If they take the fleece, you will die!
translation.kr: 만약 그들이 황금 양털을 얻는다면 너는 죽을 것이다!

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But the Minuai marched toward their ship, growling like lions cheated of their prey; for they saw that Aietes meant to mock them, and to cheat them out of all their toil.  And Oileus said, ‘Let us go to the grove together, and take the fleece by force.’

translation.en: The Minuai marched back to their ship, growling like lions denied their prey.
translation.kr: 미니아스인들은 사냥감을 빼앗긴 사자처럼 으르렁거리며 배를 향해 행진했습니다.

translation.en: They realized Aietes meant to mock them and cheat them out of their reward.
translation.kr: 그들은 아이에테스가 자신들을 조롱하고 모든 수고를 헛되게 하려 한다는 것을 알았습니다.

translation.en: Oileus urged them to head to the grove and seize the fleece by force.
translation.kr: 오일레우스가 말했습니다. 다 같이 숲으로 가서 무력으로 양털을 빼앗자.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And Idas the rash cried, ‘Let us draw lots who shall go in first; for, while the dragon is devouring one, the rest can slay him and carry off the fleece in peace.’  But Jason held them back, though he praised them; for he hoped for Medeia’s help.

translation.en: Rash Idas suggested they draw lots to see who would go first.
translation.kr: 성급한 이다스가 외쳤습니다. 누가 먼저 들어갈지 제비뽑기를 합시다.

translation.en: While the dragon devours the first, the rest can slay it and take the fleece.
translation.kr: 용이 한 명을 잡아먹는 동안 나머지는 용을 죽이고 무사히 양털을 가져갈 수 있을 것입니다.

translation.en: Jason praised their courage but held them back, still hoping for Medeia's help.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그들을 칭찬하면서도 만류했습니다. 그는 메데이아의 도움을 바랐기 때문입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And after awhile Medeia came trembling, and wept a long while before she spoke.  And at last—

translation.en: After a while, Medeia approached them, trembling and weeping.
translation.kr: 잠시 후 메데이아가 떨면서 다가왔고, 한참을 운 뒤에야 입을 열었습니다.

translation.en: At last, she spoke.
translation.kr: 그리고 마침내 그녀는 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘My end is come, and I must die; for my father has found out that I have helped you.  You he would kill if he dared; but he will not harm you, because you have been his guests.  Go then, go, and remember poor Medeia when you are far away across the sea.’  But all the heroes cried—

translation.en: My end has come, and I must die.
translation.kr: 제 마지막이 왔습니다. 저는 죽어야 합니다.

translation.en: My father knows I helped you.
translation.kr: 아버지는 제가 당신을 도왔다는 것을 알아차렸습니다.

translation.en: He would kill you if he dared.
translation.kr: 할 수만 있다면 아버지는 당신을 죽이려 할 것입니다.

translation.en: But he won't harm you since you have been his guests.
translation.kr: 하지만 당신은 그의 손님이었기에 해치지는 않을 것입니다.

translation.en: Go now, and remember poor Medeia when you are far across the sea.
translation.kr: 그러니 가십시오. 어서 가서 바다 건너 멀리 있을 때 불쌍한 메데이아를 기억해 주십시오.

translation.en: But all the heroes cried out in response.
translation.kr: 그러나 모든 영웅들이 외쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘If you die, we die with you; for without you we cannot win the fleece, and home we will not go without it, but fall here fighting to the last man.’

translation.en: If you die, we will die with you.
translation.kr: 당신이 죽는다면 우리도 당신과 함께 죽겠습니다.

translation.en: We cannot win the fleece without you, and we will not go home empty-handed.
translation.kr: 당신 없이는 황금 양털을 얻을 수 없고, 그것 없이는 고향에 돌아가지 않겠습니다.

translation.en: We will fight here to the last man.
translation.kr: 우리는 마지막 한 사람까지 이곳에서 싸우다 쓰러질 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘You need not die,’ said Jason.  ‘Flee home with us across the sea.  Show us first how to win the fleece; for you can do it.  Why else are you the priestess of the grove?  Show us but how to win the fleece, and come with us, and you shall be my queen, and rule over the rich princes of the Minuai, in Iolcos by the sea.’

translation.en: Jason assured her she did not need to die.
translation.kr: 이아손이 말했습니다. 당신은 죽을 필요가 없습니다.

translation.en: Flee across the sea with us.
translation.kr: 우리와 함께 바다를 건너 제 고향으로 피신합시다.

translation.en: First, show us how to win the fleece.
translation.kr: 먼저 양털을 얻는 방법을 알려주십시오. 당신은 할 수 있습니다.

translation.en: Why else would you be the priestess of the grove?
translation.kr: 그렇지 않다면 왜 당신이 숲의 여사제이겠습니까?

translation.en: Show us the way and come with us.
translation.kr: 황금 양털을 얻는 방법을 알려주고 우리와 함께 가십시오.

translation.en: You shall be my queen in Iolcos by the sea.
translation.kr: 그러면 바닷가 이올코스에서 미니아스의 부유한 왕자들을 다스리는 나의 여왕이 될 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And all the heroes pressed round, and vowed to her that she should be their queen.

translation.en: The heroes gathered around her, vowing she would be their queen.
translation.kr: 모든 영웅들이 그녀를 에워싸고 그녀가 자신들의 여왕이 될 것이라고 맹세했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Medeia wept, and shuddered, and hid her face in her hands; for her heart yearned after her sisters and her playfellows, and the home where she was brought up as a child.  But at last she looked up at Jason, and spoke between her sobs—

translation.en: Medeia wept, shuddered, and hid her face in her hands.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 울면서 몸을 떨며 두 손으로 얼굴을 감쌌습니다.

translation.en: Her heart longed for her sisters, playmates, and her childhood home.
translation.kr: 언니들과 친구들, 어릴 적 자란 고향에 대한 그리움에 마음이 아팠기 때문입니다.

translation.en: At last, she looked up at Jason and spoke through her sobs.
translation.kr: 하지만 마침내 그녀는 이아손을 올려다보며 흐느낌 속에 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: ‘Must I leave my home and my people, to wander with strangers across the sea?  The lot is cast, and I must endure it.  I will show you how to win the golden fleece.  Bring up your ship to the wood-side, and moor her there against the bank; and let Jason come up at midnight, and one brave comrade with him, and meet me beneath the wall.’

translation.en: Must I leave my home and people to wander with strangers across the sea?
translation.kr: 낯선 사람들과 바다를 건너 방황하기 위해 제 고향과 가족을 떠나야 합니까?

translation.en: The lot is cast, and I must endure it.
translation.kr: 주사위는 던져졌고, 저는 그것을 견뎌야 합니다.

translation.en: I will show you how to win the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 황금 양털을 얻는 방법을 알려드리겠습니다.

translation.en: Bring your ship to the edge of the woods and moor it against the bank.
translation.kr: 배를 숲 쪽으로 끌고 와 둑에 대고 정박시키십시오.

translation.en: Jason must come at midnight with one brave comrade and meet me beneath the wall.
translation.kr: 이아손은 자정에 용감한 동료 한 명과 함께 성벽 아래에서 저를 만나러 오십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then all the heroes cried together, ‘I will go!’ ‘and I!’ ‘and I!’  And Idas the rash grew mad with envy; for he longed to be foremost in all things.  But Medeia calmed them, and said, ‘Orpheus shall go with Jason, and bring his magic harp; for I hear of him that he is the king of all minstrels, and can charm all things on earth.’

translation.en: All the heroes eagerly volunteered to go.
translation.kr: 그러자 모든 영웅들이 "내가 가겠다!" "나도!" "나도!" 하며 함께 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Rash Idas went mad with envy, always wanting to be first.
translation.kr: 성급한 이다스는 모든 일에서 앞장서기를 갈망했기에 질투심에 미쳐버렸습니다.

translation.en: Medeia calmed them and chose Orpheus to accompany Jason.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 그들을 진정시키며 오르페우스가 이아손과 함께 가야 한다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: He must bring his magic harp.
translation.kr: 그의 마법의 하프를 가져와야 합니다.

translation.en: I hear he is the king of minstrels, able to charm all things on earth.
translation.kr: 그가 모든 음유시인의 왕이며 지구상의 모든 것을 매혹시킬 수 있다고 들었기 때문입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And Orpheus laughed for joy, and clapped his hands, because the choice had fallen on him; for in those days poets and singers were as bold warriors as the best.

translation.en: Orpheus laughed for joy and clapped his hands at being chosen.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 기뻐서 웃으며 박수를 쳤습니다. 자신이 선택되었기 때문입니다.

translation.en: In those days, poets and singers were as bold as the finest warriors.
translation.kr: 그 당시 시인과 가수들은 최고의 전사들만큼이나 용감했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: So at midnight they went up the bank, and found Medeia; and beside came Absyrtus her young brother, leading a yearling lamb.

translation.en: At midnight, they went up the bank and found Medeia.
translation.kr: 자정에 그들은 언덕으로 올라가 메데이아를 만났습니다.

translation.en: Beside her was her young brother Absyrtus, leading a yearling lamb.
translation.kr: 그녀 옆에는 어린 동생 압시르토스가 한 살짜리 양을 이끌고 와 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then Medeia brought them to a thicket beside the War-god’s gate; and there she bade Jason dig a ditch, and kill the lamb, and leave it there, and strew on it magic herbs and honey from the honeycomb.

translation.en: Medeia brought them to a thicket beside the War-god's gate.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 전쟁의 신의 문 옆에 있는 덤불로 그들을 데려갔습니다.

translation.en: She bade Jason dig a ditch, kill the lamb, and leave it there.
translation.kr: 그녀는 이아손에게 도랑을 파서 양을 죽이고 그곳에 두라고 지시했습니다.

translation.en: He was to scatter magic herbs and fresh honey over it.
translation.kr: 그리고 마법의 허브와 벌집에서 나온 꿀을 그 위에 뿌리라고 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: Then sprang up through the earth, with the red fire flashing before her, Brimo the wild witch-huntress, while her mad hounds howled around.  She had one head like a horse’s, and another like a ravening hound’s, and another like a hissing snake’s, and a sword in either hand.  And she leapt into the ditch with her hounds, and they ate and drank their fill, while Jason and Orpheus trembled, and Medeia hid her eyes.  And at last the witch-queen vanished, and fled with her hounds into the woods; and the bars of the gates fell down, and the brazen doors flew wide, and Medeia and the heroes ran forward and hurried through the poison wood, among the dark stems of the mighty beeches, guided by the gleam of the golden fleece, until they saw it hanging on one vast tree in the midst. And Jason would have sprung to seize it; but Medeia held him back, and pointed, shuddering, to the tree-foot, where the mighty serpent lay, coiled in and out among the roots, with a body like a mountain pine.  His coils stretched many a fathom, spangled with bronze and gold; and half of him they could see, but no more, for the rest lay in the darkness far beyond.

translation.en: Red fire flashed as Brimo, the wild witch-huntress, sprang from the earth.
translation.kr: 붉은 불꽃이 번쩍이는 가운데 거친 마녀 사냥꾼 브리모가 땅에서 솟아났습니다.

translation.en: Her mad hounds howled around her.
translation.kr: 그녀의 주변에서는 미친 사냥개들이 울부짖었습니다.

translation.en: She had three heads: one like a horse, one like a ravenous hound, and one like a hissing snake.
translation.kr: 그녀는 말 같은 머리, 굶주린 사냥개 같은 머리, 쉿쉿거리는 뱀 같은 머리를 가졌습니다.

translation.en: She held a sword in each hand.
translation.kr: 그리고 양손에는 칼을 들고 있었습니다.

translation.en: She leapt into the ditch with her hounds, and they feasted.
translation.kr: 그녀는 사냥개들과 함께 도랑으로 뛰어들어 배불리 먹고 마셨습니다.

translation.en: Jason and Orpheus trembled, and Medeia covered her eyes.
translation.kr: 이아손과 오르페우스는 떨었고 메데이아는 눈을 가렸습니다.

translation.en: Finally, the witch-queen and her hounds vanished into the woods.
translation.kr: 마침내 마녀 여왕은 사냥개들과 함께 숲 속으로 도망쳐 사라졌습니다.

translation.en: The gate bars dropped, and the brazen doors flew open.
translation.kr: 성문의 빗장이 떨어지고 놋쇠 문이 활짝 열렸습니다.

translation.en: Guided by the gleam of the golden fleece, they hurried through the dark poison wood.
translation.kr: 메데이아와 영웅들은 황금 양털의 빛을 따라 거대한 너도밤나무의 어두운 줄기들 사이로 독이 있는 숲을 가로질러 달렸습니다.

translation.en: They saw it hanging on a vast tree in the center.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 한가운데 있는 거대한 나무에 황금 양털이 걸려 있는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Jason was about to spring for it.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그것을 잡으려고 뛰어올랐을 것입니다.

translation.en: But Medeia held him back and pointed shuddering at the tree's base.
translation.kr: 그러나 메데이아는 그를 만류하고 몸을 떨며 나무 밑동을 가리켰습니다.

translation.en: A mighty serpent as huge as a mountain pine lay coiled among the roots.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 산소나무 같은 몸집의 거대한 뱀이 뿌리 사이로 똬리를 틀고 누워 있었습니다.

translation.en: Its coils, spangled with bronze and gold, stretched for many fathoms.
translation.kr: 청동과 황금으로 반짝이는 뱀의 똬리는 몇 패덤이나 뻗어 있었습니다.

translation.en: They could only see half of it; the rest lay hidden in the deep darkness.
translation.kr: 그들은 뱀의 절반만 볼 수 있었고, 나머지는 저 너머 어둠 속에 누워 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And when he saw them coming he lifted up his head, and watched them with his small bright eyes, and flashed his forked tongue, and roared like the fire among the woodlands, till the forest tossed and groaned.  For his cries shook the trees from leaf to root, and swept over the long reaches of the river, and over Aietes’ hall, and woke the sleepers in the city, till mothers clasped their children in their fear.

translation.en: Seeing them approach, the serpent lifted its head and watched them with bright little eyes.
translation.kr: 뱀은 그들이 오는 것을 보고 고개를 들어 작고 밝은 눈으로 그들을 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: It flashed its forked tongue and roared like a woodland fire, shaking the forest.
translation.kr: 갈라진 혀를 널름거리며 숲의 불길처럼 포효하자 숲이 흔들리며 신음했습니다.

translation.en: The cries shook the trees from leaf to root.
translation.kr: 그 울음소리는 나뭇잎부터 뿌리까지 나무를 뒤흔들었습니다.

translation.en: The sound swept over the river, past Aietes' hall, and woke the sleepers in the city.
translation.kr: 길게 뻗은 강을 지나 아이에테스의 홀을 넘어 도시에서 잠든 사람들을 깨웠습니다.

translation.en: Mothers tightly clutched their children in fear.
translation.kr: 두려움에 휩싸인 어머니들은 아이들을 꼭 껴안았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: But Medeia called gently to him, and he stretched out his long spotted neck, and licked her hand, and looked up in her face, as if to ask for food.  Then she made a sign to Orpheus, and he began his magic song.

translation.en: Medeia called gently to it, and the serpent stretched its long, spotted neck.
translation.kr: 메데이아가 그를 부드럽게 부르자 뱀은 길고 점박이인 목을 뻗어 그녀의 손을 핥았습니다.

translation.en: It looked up into her face, seemingly asking for food.
translation.kr: 마치 먹이를 달라는 듯 그녀의 얼굴을 올려다보았습니다.

translation.en: She signaled Orpheus, and he began his magic song.
translation.kr: 그녀가 오르페우스에게 신호를 보내자 그가 마법의 노래를 부르기 시작했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: And as he sung, the forest grew calm again, and the leaves on every tree hung still; and the serpent’s head sank down, and his brazen coils grew limp, and his glittering eyes closed lazily, till he breathed as gently as a child, while Orpheus called to pleasant Slumber, who gives peace to men, and beasts, and waves.

translation.en: As he sang, the forest calmed, and the leaves hung perfectly still.
translation.kr: 그가 노래를 부르자 숲은 다시 고요해졌고 모든 나무의 잎사귀는 미동도 하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: The serpent's head sank, and its brazen coils went limp.
translation.kr: 뱀의 머리가 가라앉고 놋쇠 같은 똬리가 늘어졌습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus called to the soothing slumber that brings peace to men, beasts, and waves.
translation.kr: 사람과 짐승, 파도에 평화를 주는 즐거운 잠의 신을 오르페우스가 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Its glittering eyes slowly closed, and it breathed as gently as a sleeping child.
translation.kr: 뱀의 반짝이는 눈이 나른하게 감겼고, 마침내 어린아이처럼 부드럽게 숨을 쉬게 되었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
paragraphs.raw: [Picture: Jason takes the fleece]

translation.en: [Picture: Jason takes the fleece]
translation.kr: [그림: 이아손이 양털을 가져가다]

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
