translation.kr: 모든 사람들은 영웅들의 명성이 헛되지 않았다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: They stand like giants or immortals descended from Olympus.
translation.kr: 그들은 마치 거인이나 올림포스에서 내려온 불사신들처럼 서 있습니다.

translation.en: They look magnificent despite the harsh winters and fearful storms.
translation.kr: 혹독한 겨울과 무서운 폭풍우에도 불구하고 그들은 훌륭해 보입니다.

translation.en: Imagine how they looked when they first sailed from Iolcus.
translation.kr: 그들이 오래 전 이올코스에서 처음 출항했을 때의 모습은 어땠을지 상상해 보십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then they went out to the garden; and the merchant princes said, ‘Heroes, run races with us.  Let us see whose feet are nimblest.’

translation.en: They went out to the garden.
translation.kr: 그들은 정원으로 나갔습니다.

translation.en: The merchant princes challenged the heroes to run races.
translation.kr: 상인 왕자들은 영웅들에게 달리기 경주를 하자고 제안했습니다.

translation.en: Let us see whose feet are the fastest.
translation.kr: 누구의 발이 가장 빠른지 봅시다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘We cannot race against you, for our limbs are stiff from sea; and we have lost our two swift comrades, the sons of the north wind.  But do not think us cowards: if you wish to try our strength, we will shoot, and box, and wrestle, against any men on earth.’

translation.en: We cannot race against you because our limbs are stiff.
translation.kr: 우리는 팔다리가 뻣뻣해서 당신들과 경주를 할 수 없습니다.

translation.en: We have also lost our two swiftest comrades, the sons of the North Wind.
translation.kr: 우리는 또한 북풍의 아들들인 가장 빠른 두 동료를 잃었습니다.

translation.en: But please do not think of us as cowards.
translation.kr: 하지만 우리를 겁쟁이라고 생각하지는 마십시오.

translation.en: We will gladly shoot, box, or wrestle against any man on earth.
translation.kr: 우리는 세상 그 누구를 상대로도 기꺼이 활쏘기, 권투, 레슬링을 할 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And Alcinous smiled, and answered, ‘I believe you, gallant guests; with your long limbs and broad shoulders, we could never match you here.  For we care nothing here for boxing, or for shooting with the bow; but for feasts, and songs, and harping, and dancing, and running races, to stretch our limbs on shore.’

translation.en: Alcinous smiled and assured the gallant guests that he believed them.
translation.kr: 알키노우스는 미소를 지으며 용감한 손님들을 믿는다고 안심시켰습니다.

translation.en: With your long limbs and broad shoulders, we could never match you.
translation.kr: 당신들의 긴 팔다리와 넓은 어깨를 우리는 결코 당해낼 수 없을 것입니다.

translation.en: We do not care for boxing or archery here.
translation.kr: 우리는 이곳에서 권투나 양궁에는 관심이 없습니다.

translation.en: We prefer feasts, songs, harp playing, and dancing.
translation.kr: 우리는 연회, 노래, 하프 연주, 그리고 춤을 더 좋아합니다.

translation.en: We only run races to stretch our legs on the shore.
translation.kr: 우리는 그저 해변에서 다리를 풀기 위해 달리기 경주를 할 뿐입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: So they danced there and ran races, the jolly merchant kings, till the night fell, and all went in.

translation.en: The jolly merchant kings danced and ran races until night fell.
translation.kr: 유쾌한 상인 왕들은 밤이 될 때까지 춤을 추고 달리기 경주를 했습니다.

translation.en: Then everyone went back inside.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 모두 다시 안으로 들어갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And then they ate and drank, and comforted their weary souls, till Alcinous called a herald, and bade him go and fetch the harper.

translation.en: They ate, drank, and comforted their weary souls.
translation.kr: 그들은 먹고 마시며 지친 영혼을 위로했습니다.

translation.en: Alcinous called a herald and ordered him to fetch the harper.
translation.kr: 알키노우스는 전령을 불러 하프 연주자를 데려오라고 명령했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: The herald went out, and fetched the harper, and led him in by the hand; and Alcinous cut him a piece of meat, from the fattest of the haunch, and sent it to him, and said, ‘Sing to us, noble harper, and rejoice the heroes’ hearts.’

translation.en: The herald went out, brought the harper, and led him inside.
translation.kr: 전령은 밖으로 나가 하프 연주자를 데리고 안으로 들어왔습니다.

translation.en: Alcinous cut a prime piece of meat for the harper.
translation.kr: 알키노우스는 하프 연주자를 위해 최고급 고기를 잘랐습니다.

translation.en: Sing to us, noble harper, and bring joy to the heroes' hearts.
translation.kr: 우리를 위해 노래해 주시오, 고귀한 연주자여. 그리고 영웅들의 마음에 기쁨을 주시오.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: So the harper played and sang, while the dancers danced strange figures; and after that the tumblers showed their tricks, till the heroes laughed again.

translation.en: The harper played and sang while the dancers performed strange figures.
translation.kr: 하프 연주자가 노래를 부르는 동안 무용수들은 신기한 춤을 추었습니다.

translation.en: Afterward, the acrobats showed their tricks until the heroes laughed.
translation.kr: 그 후 곡예사들이 재주를 부리자 영웅들은 웃음을 터뜨렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then, ‘Tell me, heroes,’ asked Alcinous, ‘you who have sailed the ocean round, and seen the manners of all nations, have you seen such dancers as ours here, or heard such music and such singing?  We hold ours to be the best on earth.’

translation.en: Alcinous asked the heroes if they had ever seen such dancers.
translation.kr: 알키노우스는 영웅들에게 이처럼 훌륭한 무용수들을 본 적이 있는지 물었습니다.

translation.en: You have sailed the oceans and seen the customs of many nations.
translation.kr: 당신들은 바다를 항해하며 많은 나라의 풍습을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Have you heard such incredible music and singing anywhere else?
translation.kr: 다른 어느 곳에서 이렇게 훌륭한 음악과 노래를 들어본 적이 있습니까?

translation.en: We believe our performers are the best on earth.
translation.kr: 우리는 우리 공연자들이 세상에서 최고라고 믿습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘Such dancing we have never seen,’ said Orpheus; ‘and your singer is a happy man, for Phoebus himself must have taught him, or else he is the son of a Muse, as I am also, and have sung once or twice, though not so well as he.’

translation.en: We have never seen such spectacular dancing, Orpheus replied.
translation.kr: 이토록 멋진 춤은 본 적이 없습니다, 라고 오르페우스가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Your singer is a truly fortunate man.
translation.kr: 당신의 가수는 참으로 운이 좋은 사람입니다.

translation.en: Apollo himself must have taught him his craft.
translation.kr: 아폴론 신이 직접 그에게 노래를 가르쳤음이 틀림없습니다.

translation.en: Perhaps he is the son of a Muse, just like me.
translation.kr: 어쩌면 그도 저처럼 무사이 여신의 아들일지도 모릅니다.

translation.en: I have sung once or twice, but never as well as he does.
translation.kr: 저도 노래를 불러본 적이 있지만, 그 사람만큼 잘하지는 못합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘Sing to us, then, noble stranger,’ said Alcinous; ‘and we will give you precious gifts.’

translation.en: Sing to us, noble stranger, Alcinous requested.
translation.kr: 우리를 위해 노래해 주시오, 고귀한 이방인이여, 라고 알키노우스가 부탁했습니다.

translation.en: We will reward you with precious gifts.
translation.kr: 우리가 값진 선물로 보답하겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: So Orpheus took his magic harp, and sang to them a stirring song of their voyage from Iolcos, and their dangers, and how they won the golden fleece; and of Medeia’s love, and how she helped them, and went with them over land and sea; and of all their fearful dangers, from monsters, and rocks, and storms, till the heart of Arete was softened, and all the women wept.  And the merchant kings rose up, each man from off his golden throne, and clapped their hands, and shouted, ‘Hail to the noble Argonauts, who sailed the unknown sea!’

translation.en: Orpheus took his magic harp and sang a stirring song.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 마법의 하프를 들고 감동적인 노래를 불렀습니다.

translation.en: He sang of their voyage from Iolcus and the dangers they faced.
translation.kr: 그는 이올코스에서 출발한 항해와 그들이 직면했던 위험에 대해 노래했습니다.

translation.en: He recounted how they successfully captured the Golden Fleece.
translation.kr: 그는 그들이 어떻게 황금 양털을 차지했는지 이야기했습니다.

translation.en: He sang of Medea's love and how she helped them across land and sea.
translation.kr: 그는 메데이아의 사랑과 그녀가 육지와 바다에서 그들을 어떻게 도왔는지 노래했습니다.

translation.en: He described their fearful encounters with monsters, rocks, and storms.
translation.kr: 그는 괴물, 암초, 폭풍우와의 두려운 만남을 묘사했습니다.

translation.en: Arete's heart was softened, and all the women began to weep.
translation.kr: 아레테의 마음은 부드러워졌고, 모든 여인들이 눈물을 흘리기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: The merchant kings rose from their golden thrones.
translation.kr: 상인 왕들은 황금 왕좌에서 일어났습니다.

translation.en: They clapped their hands and shouted their praises.
translation.kr: 그들은 손뼉을 치며 찬사를 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Hail to the noble Argonauts who sailed the unknown sea!
translation.kr: 미지의 바다를 항해한 고귀한 아르고나우타이 만세!

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then he went on, and told their journey over the sluggish northern main, and through the shoreless outer ocean, to the fairy island of the west; and of the Sirens, and Scylla, and Charybdis, and all the wonders they had seen, till midnight passed and the day dawned; but the kings never thought of sleep.  Each man sat still and listened, with his chin upon his hand.

translation.en: Orpheus continued, detailing their journey over the sluggish northern main.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 느릿한 북쪽 바다를 가로지른 그들의 여정을 계속해서 설명했습니다.

translation.en: He sang of the shoreless outer ocean and the fairy island of the west.
translation.kr: 그는 끝없는 외곽의 대양과 서쪽의 요정 섬에 대해 노래했습니다.

translation.en: He told them about the Sirens, Scylla, and Charybdis.
translation.kr: 그는 세이렌, 스킬라, 카리브디스에 대해 이야기했습니다.

translation.en: He described all the wonders they had seen until the day dawned.
translation.kr: 그는 날이 밝을 때까지 그들이 본 모든 경이로움을 묘사했습니다.

translation.en: The kings never even considered going to sleep.
translation.kr: 왕들은 잠자리에 들 생각조차 하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Each man sat perfectly still, listening with his chin resting on his hand.
translation.kr: 모든 남자들은 턱을 괸 채 꼼짝 않고 앉아 귀를 기울였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And at last, when Orpheus had ended, they all went thoughtful out, and the heroes lay down to sleep, beneath the sounding porch outside, where Arete had strewn them rugs and carpets, in the sweet still summer night.

translation.en: When Orpheus finally finished, they all walked out deep in thought.
translation.kr: 오르페우스가 마침내 노래를 마쳤을 때, 그들은 모두 깊은 생각에 잠겨 밖으로 나갔습니다.

translation.en: The heroes lay down to sleep beneath the echoing porch outside.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 밖의 울리는 현관 아래에 누워 잠을 청했습니다.

translation.en: Arete had prepared rugs and carpets for them in the sweet summer night.
translation.kr: 아레테는 달콤한 여름밤을 위해 그들에게 양탄자와 융단을 깔아주었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: But Arete pleaded hard with her husband for Medeia, for her heart was softened.  And she said, ‘The Gods will punish her, not we.  After all, she is our guest and my suppliant, and prayers are the daughters of Zeus. And who, too, dare part man and wife, after all they have endured together?’

translation.en: Arete pleaded earnestly with her husband on behalf of Medea.
translation.kr: 아레테는 메데이아를 위해 남편에게 간곡히 부탁했습니다.

translation.en: Her heart had been thoroughly softened by the story.
translation.kr: 그녀의 마음은 그 이야기로 인해 완전히 부드러워졌습니다.

translation.en: The gods will punish her, not us.
translation.kr: 신들이 그녀를 벌할 것이지, 우리가 할 일이 아닙니다.

translation.en: After all, she is our guest and has sought my protection.
translation.kr: 어쨌든 그녀는 우리의 손님이며 나의 보호를 구했습니다.

translation.en: Prayers are considered the daughters of Zeus.
translation.kr: 기도는 제우스의 딸들로 여겨집니다.

translation.en: Who would dare separate a husband and wife after all they have endured?
translation.kr: 그들이 겪은 모든 고난 이후에 누가 감히 남편과 아내를 갈라놓을 수 있겠습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And Alcinous smiled.  ‘The minstrel’s song has charmed you: but I must remember what is right, for songs cannot alter justice; and I must be faithful to my name.  Alcinous I am called, the man of sturdy sense; and Alcinous I will be.’  But for all that Arete besought him, until she won him round.

translation.en: Alcinous smiled at his wife's earnest plea.
translation.kr: 알키노우스는 아내의 간절한 부탁에 미소를 지었습니다.

translation.en: The minstrel's song has clearly charmed you.
translation.kr: 음유시인의 노래가 당신을 완전히 매혹시켰군요.

translation.en: However, I must remember what is truly right.
translation.kr: 하지만 나는 진정으로 옳은 것이 무엇인지 기억해야 합니다.

translation.en: Songs cannot alter the course of justice.
translation.kr: 노래가 정의의 방향을 바꿀 수는 없습니다.

translation.en: I must remain faithful to my name, Alcinous, the man of sturdy sense.
translation.kr: 나는 확고한 분별력을 가진 사람이라는 알키노우스라는 내 이름에 충실해야 합니다.

translation.en: Despite his words, Arete continued to beg until she finally won him over.
translation.kr: 그의 말에도 불구하고 아레테는 계속해서 애원했고, 마침내 그의 마음을 돌렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: So next morning he sent a herald, and called the kings into the square, and said, ‘This is a puzzling matter: remember but one thing.  These Minuai live close by us, and we may meet them often on the seas; but Aietes lives afar off, and we have only heard his name.  Which, then, of the two is it safer to offend—the men near us, or the men far off?’

translation.en: The next morning, he sent a herald to call the kings to the square.
translation.kr: 다음 날 아침, 그는 전령을 보내 왕들을 광장으로 불렀습니다.

translation.en: This is a very puzzling matter, but remember one crucial thing.
translation.kr: 이것은 매우 당혹스러운 문제이지만 한 가지 중요한 사실을 기억하십시오.

translation.en: These Minyans live close to us.
translation.kr: 이 미니아인들은 우리와 가까이 살고 있습니다.

translation.en: We will likely encounter them often on the seas.
translation.kr: 우리는 바다에서 그들을 자주 마주칠 가능성이 높습니다.

translation.en: Aeetes, however, lives far away, and we have only heard his name.
translation.kr: 하지만 아이에테스는 멀리 살고 있으며, 우리는 단지 그의 이름만 들었을 뿐입니다.

translation.en: Is it safer to offend the men near us, or the men far off?
translation.kr: 우리와 가까운 사람들의 분노를 사는 것과 멀리 있는 사람들의 분노를 사는 것 중 어느 쪽이 더 안전하겠습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: The princes laughed, and praised his wisdom; and Alcinous called the heroes to the square, and the Colchi also; and they came and stood opposite each other, but Medeia stayed in the palace.  Then Alcinous spoke, ‘Heroes of the Colchi, what is your errand about this lady?’

translation.en: The princes laughed and praised his wisdom.
translation.kr: 왕자들은 웃으며 그의 지혜를 칭찬했습니다.

translation.en: Alcinous summoned the heroes and the Colchians to the square.
translation.kr: 알키노우스는 영웅들과 콜키스인들을 광장으로 불렀습니다.

translation.en: They stood facing each other, but Medea remained in the palace.
translation.kr: 그들은 서로 마주 보고 섰지만, 메데이아는 궁전에 남았습니다.

translation.en: Heroes of the Colchians, what is your purpose regarding this lady?
translation.kr: 콜키스의 영웅들이여, 이 부인에 대한 당신들의 목적은 무엇입니까?

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘To carry her home with us, that she may die a shameful death; but if we return without her, we must die the death she should have died.’

translation.en: We intend to carry her home so she may die a shameful death.
translation.kr: 우리는 그녀를 고향으로 데려가 수치스러운 죽음을 맞게 할 작정입니다.

translation.en: If we return without her, we must face the death she deserves.
translation.kr: 만약 그녀 없이 돌아간다면, 우리가 그 죽음을 대신 맞아야 합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘What say you to this, Jason the Æolid?’ said Alcinous, turning to the Minuai.

translation.en: What do you have to say to this, Jason?
translation.kr: 이 일에 대해 할 말이 있소, 이아손?

translation.en: Alcinous turned to address the Minyans.
translation.kr: 알키노우스가 미니아인들을 향해 몸을 돌렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘I say,’ said the cunning Jason, ‘that they are come here on a bootless errand.  Do you think that you can make her follow you, heroes of the Colchi—her, who knows all spells and charms?  She will cast away your ships on quicksands, or call down on you Brimo the wild huntress; or the chains will fall from off her wrists, and she will escape in her dragon-car; or if not thus, some other way, for she has a thousand plans and wiles.  And why return home at all, brave heroes, and face the long seas again, and the Bosphorus, and the stormy Euxine, and double all your toil?  There is many a fair land round these coasts, which waits for gallant men like you.  Better to settle there, and build a city, and let Aietes and Colchis help themselves.’

translation.en: I say they have come here on a pointless errand, the cunning Jason replied.
translation.kr: 나는 그들이 쓸데없는 심부름을 하러 이곳에 왔다고 생각합니다, 라고 교활한 이아손이 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Do you really think you can force her to follow you, heroes of Colchis?
translation.kr: 콜키스의 영웅들이여, 당신들은 진정 그녀가 당신들을 따라가게 만들 수 있다고 생각합니까?

translation.en: She knows every spell and magic charm.
translation.kr: 그녀는 모든 주문과 마법을 알고 있습니다.

translation.en: She will cast your ships onto the quicksands.
translation.kr: 그녀는 당신들의 배를 유사 속으로 던져버릴 것입니다.

translation.en: Or she might call down the wrath of Brimo the wild huntress upon you.
translation.kr: 아니면 야생의 사냥꾼 브리모의 분노를 당신들에게 내릴지도 모릅니다.

translation.en: The chains will easily fall from her wrists, and she will escape in her dragon chariot.
translation.kr: 그녀의 손목에서 사슬이 쉽게 풀릴 것이고, 그녀는 용 전차를 타고 달아날 것입니다.

translation.en: If not that way, she will find another, for she has a thousand schemes.
translation.kr: 그 방법이 아니더라도 그녀는 수천 가지의 계략을 가지고 있으니 다른 길을 찾을 것입니다.

translation.en: Why return home at all to face the long seas again?
translation.kr: 왜 먼 바다를 다시 마주하며 굳이 고향으로 돌아가려 하십니까?

translation.en: Why brave the Bosphorus and the stormy Black Sea to double your hardship?
translation.kr: 왜 보스포루스 해협과 폭풍우 치는 흑해를 무릅쓰고 고통을 두 배로 늘리려 하십니까?

translation.en: There is many a fair land around these coasts waiting for gallant men like you.
translation.kr: 이 해안 주변에는 당신들처럼 용감한 사람들을 기다리는 아름다운 땅이 많이 있습니다.

translation.en: It is better to settle there and build a city.
translation.kr: 그곳에 정착하여 도시를 세우는 편이 낫습니다.

translation.en: Let Aeetes and Colchis fend for themselves.
translation.kr: 아이에테스와 콜키스는 스스로 알아서 하게 내버려 두십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then a murmur rose among the Colchi, and some cried ‘He has spoken well;’ and some, ‘We have had enough of roving, we will sail the seas no more!’ And the chief said at last, ‘Be it so, then; a plague she has been to us, and a plague to the house of her father, and a plague she will be to you. Take her, since you are no wiser; and we will sail away toward the north.’

translation.en: A murmur rose among the Colchians.
translation.kr: 콜키스인들 사이에서 웅성거림이 일었습니다.

translation.en: Some agreed that he had spoken well.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 그의 말이 옳다고 동의했습니다.

translation.en: Others declared they had enough of roaming and would sail no more.
translation.kr: 다른 이들은 방랑에 지쳐 더 이상 항해하지 않겠다고 선언했습니다.

translation.en: Finally, the chief announced his decision.
translation.kr: 마침내 우두머리가 결정을 내렸습니다.

translation.en: Let it be so, then.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 그렇게 합시다.

translation.en: She has been a plague to us and to her father's house.
translation.kr: 그녀는 우리와 그녀 아버지의 가문에 재앙이었습니다.

translation.en: She will surely be a plague to you as well.
translation.kr: 그녀는 틀림없이 당신들에게도 재앙이 될 것입니다.

translation.en: Take her, since you are no wiser.
translation.kr: 당신들이 어리석으니 그녀를 데려가십시오.

translation.en: We will sail away toward the north.
translation.kr: 우리는 북쪽을 향해 항해할 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then Alcinous gave them food, and water, and garments, and rich presents of all sorts; and he gave the same to the Minuai, and sent them all away in peace.

translation.en: Alcinous provided them with food, water, and fresh garments.
translation.kr: 알키노우스는 그들에게 식량, 물, 그리고 새 옷을 제공했습니다.

translation.en: He also gave them rich presents of all sorts.
translation.kr: 그는 또한 그들에게 온갖 종류의 값진 선물을 주었습니다.

translation.en: He gave the same to the Minyans and sent everyone away in peace.
translation.kr: 그는 미니아인들에게도 똑같이 베풀었고 모두 평화롭게 떠나보냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: So Jason kept the dark witch-maiden to breed him woe and shame; and the Colchi went northward into the Adriatic, and settled, and built towns along the shore.

translation.en: Jason kept the dark witch-maiden, which would later bring him sorrow and shame.
translation.kr: 이아손은 어둠의 마녀 소녀를 곁에 두었고, 이는 훗날 그에게 슬픔과 수치를 안겨주게 됩니다.

translation.en: The Colchians traveled north into the Adriatic Sea.
translation.kr: 콜키스인들은 북쪽으로 이동하여 아드리아 해로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: They settled there and built thriving towns along the shore.
translation.kr: 그들은 그곳에 정착하여 해안을 따라 번성하는 마을들을 세웠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then the heroes rowed away to the eastward, to reach Hellas, their beloved land; but a storm came down upon them, and swept them far away toward the south.  And they rowed till they were spent with struggling, through the darkness and the blinding rain; but where they were they could not tell, and they gave up all hope of life.  And at last touched the ground, and when daylight came waded to the shore; and saw nothing round but sand and desolate salt pools, for they had come to the quicksands of the Syrtis, and the dreary treeless flats which lie between Numidia and Cyrene, on the burning shore of Africa.  And there they wandered starving for many a weary day, ere they could launch their ship again, and gain the open sea.  And there Canthus was killed, while he was trying to drive off sheep, by a stone which a herdsman threw.

translation.en: The heroes rowed eastward to reach Hellas, their beloved homeland.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 사랑하는 고향 헬라스를 향해 동쪽으로 노를 저었습니다.

translation.en: However, a terrible storm swept them far away to the south.
translation.kr: 하지만 끔찍한 폭풍우가 그들을 남쪽으로 멀리 휩쓸어 버렸습니다.

translation.en: They rowed through the darkness and blinding rain until they were completely exhausted.
translation.kr: 그들은 어둠과 눈을 뜰 수 없는 비를 뚫고 완전히 지칠 때까지 노를 저었습니다.

translation.en: They could not tell where they were and gave up all hope of survival.
translation.kr: 그들은 자신들이 어디에 있는지 알 수 없었고 생존에 대한 모든 희망을 포기했습니다.

translation.en: Finally, the ship touched the ground.
translation.kr: 마침내 배가 땅에 닿았습니다.

translation.en: When daylight came, they waded onto the desolate shore.
translation.kr: 날이 밝자 그들은 황량한 해안으로 걸어 나갔습니다.

translation.en: They saw nothing but sand and barren salt pools.
translation.kr: 그들은 모래와 메마른 소금 웅덩이 외에는 아무것도 보지 못했습니다.

translation.en: They had reached the quicksands of the Syrtis.
translation.kr: 그들은 시르티스의 유사 지대에 도착했던 것입니다.

translation.en: These were the dreary, treeless flats between Numidia and Cyrene on the burning African coast.
translation.kr: 그곳은 불타는 아프리카 해안의 누미디아와 키레네 사이에 있는 나무 한 그루 없는 쓸쓸한 평원이었습니다.

translation.en: They wandered there starving for many weary days.
translation.kr: 그들은 며칠 동안이나 굶주린 채 그곳을 헤매었습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, they managed to launch their ship again and reach the open sea.
translation.kr: 결국 그들은 간신히 배를 다시 띄워 넓은 바다로 나갈 수 있었습니다.

translation.en: During this time, Canthus was killed by a stone thrown by a herdsman.
translation.kr: 이 기간 동안 칸투스는 양을 훔치려다 목동이 던진 돌에 맞아 목숨을 잃었습니다.

translation.en: He died while trying to drive off some local sheep.
translation.kr: 그는 그곳의 양 떼를 몰아내려다 죽고 말았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And there too Mopsus died, the seer who knew the voices of all birds; but he could not foretell his own end, for he was bitten in the foot by a snake, one of those which sprang from the Gorgon’s head when Perseus carried it across the sands.

translation.en: Mopsus, the seer who understood the voices of birds, also died there.
translation.kr: 새들의 목소리를 이해하는 예언자 몹소스도 그곳에서 죽었습니다.

translation.en: He could not foresee his own tragic end.
translation.kr: 그는 자신의 비극적인 최후를 예견하지 못했습니다.

translation.en: He was bitten on the foot by a deadly snake.
translation.kr: 그는 치명적인 독사에게 발을 물렸습니다.

translation.en: The snake had sprung from the Gorgon's head when Perseus carried it across the sands.
translation.kr: 그 뱀은 페르세우스가 모래사장을 가로질러 들고 가던 고르곤의 머리에서 태어난 것이었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: At last they rowed away toward the northward, for many a weary day, till their water was spent, and their food eaten; and they were worn out with hunger and thirst.  But at last they saw a long steep island, and a blue peak high among the clouds; and they knew it for the peak of Ida, and the famous land of Crete.  And they said, ‘We will land in Crete, and see Minos the just king, and all his glory and his wealth; at least he will treat us hospitably, and let us fill our water-casks upon the shore.’

translation.en: They rowed northward for many exhausting days.
translation.kr: 그들은 지칠 대로 지친 채 며칠 동안 북쪽으로 노를 저었습니다.

translation.en: Their water was entirely spent, and their food was gone.
translation.kr: 그들의 물은 완전히 바닥났고 식량도 떨어졌습니다.

translation.en: They were completely worn out with hunger and severe thirst.
translation.kr: 그들은 굶주림과 극심한 갈증으로 완전히 지쳐 있었습니다.

translation.en: At last, they spotted a long, steep island with a high blue peak in the clouds.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 구름 속에 높이 솟은 푸른 봉우리가 있는 길고 가파른 섬을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: They recognized it as the peak of Ida in the famous land of Crete.
translation.kr: 그들은 그것이 유명한 크레타 땅의 이다산 봉우리라는 것을 알아차렸습니다.

translation.en: We will land in Crete and seek out Minos, the just king.
translation.kr: 우리는 크레타에 상륙하여 공정한 왕 미노스를 찾을 것이다.

translation.en: We want to see his glory and immense wealth.
translation.kr: 우리는 그의 영광과 엄청난 부를 보고 싶다.

translation.en: Surely he will treat us with hospitality.
translation.kr: 틀림없이 그는 우리를 환대할 것이다.

translation.en: At the very least, he will let us fill our water casks upon the shore.
translation.kr: 적어도 해변에서 물통을 채울 수는 있게 해줄 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: But when they came nearer to the island they saw a wondrous sight upon the cliffs.  For on a cape to the westward stood a giant, taller than any mountain pine, who glittered aloft against the sky like a tower of burnished brass.  He turned and looked on all sides round him, till he saw the _Argo_ and her crew; and when he saw them he came toward them, more swiftly than the swiftest horse, leaping across the glens at a bound, and striding at one step from down to down.  And when he came abreast of them he brandished his arms up and down, as a ship hoists and lowers her yards, and shouted with his brazen throat like a trumpet from off the hills, ‘You are pirates, you are robbers!  If you dare land here, you die.’

translation.en: As they drew closer to the island, they witnessed a wondrous sight.
translation.kr: 섬에 가까워지면서 그들은 놀라운 광경을 목격했습니다.

translation.en: A giant stood on a western cape, taller than any mountain pine.
translation.kr: 어떤 산 소나무보다 키가 큰 거인이 서쪽 곶에 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: He gleamed against the sky like a tower of polished brass.
translation.kr: 그는 닦아놓은 놋쇠 탑처럼 하늘을 배경으로 번쩍였습니다.

translation.en: He turned and surveyed his surroundings until he spotted the Argo.
translation.kr: 그는 몸을 돌려 주변을 살피다가 아르고호를 발견했습니다.

translation.en: When he saw them, he rushed forward faster than the swiftest horse.
translation.kr: 그들을 보자 그는 가장 빠른 말보다도 더 빠르게 달려왔습니다.

translation.en: He leaped across deep glens in a single bound.
translation.kr: 그는 한 번의 도약으로 깊은 골짜기들을 가로질렀습니다.

translation.en: He strode from hill to hill with massive steps.
translation.kr: 그는 거대한 보폭으로 언덕에서 언덕으로 성큼성큼 걸었습니다.

translation.en: When he drew level with them, he brandished his massive arms.
translation.kr: 그들과 나란히 섰을 때, 그는 거대한 팔을 휘둘렀습니다.

translation.en: He swung them like a ship hoisting and lowering its yards.
translation.kr: 그는 마치 배가 돛대를 올리고 내리는 것처럼 팔을 휘둘렀습니다.

translation.en: He shouted with a brazen throat that echoed like a trumpet.
translation.kr: 그는 나팔처럼 울려 퍼지는 쇳소리 나는 목청으로 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: You are pirates and robbers!
translation.kr: 너희들은 해적이고 도둑들이다!

translation.en: If you dare to land here, you will die.
translation.kr: 감히 이곳에 상륙한다면 너희는 죽을 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then the heroes cried, ‘We are no pirates.  We are all good men and true, and all we ask is food and water;’ but the giant cried the more—

translation.en: The heroes shouted back that they were not pirates.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 자신들이 해적이 아니라고 소리쳐 대답했습니다.

translation.en: We are all good and honest men.
translation.kr: 우리는 모두 선량하고 정직한 사람들입니다.

translation.en: All we ask for is food and water.
translation.kr: 우리가 원하는 것은 식량과 물뿐입니다.

translation.en: But the giant only bellowed louder.
translation.kr: 하지만 거인은 더욱 큰 소리로 고함을 질렀습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘You are robbers, you are pirates all; I know you; and if you land, you shall die the death.’

translation.en: You are all robbers and pirates!
translation.kr: 너희들은 모두 도둑이고 해적들이다!

translation.en: I know exactly who you are.
translation.kr: 나는 너희들이 누구인지 정확히 알고 있다.

translation.en: If you land on this shore, you shall surely die.
translation.kr: 이 해안에 상륙한다면 너희는 반드시 죽을 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then he waved his arms again as a signal, and they saw the people flying inland, driving their flocks before them, while a great flame arose among the hills.  Then the giant ran up a valley and vanished, and the heroes lay on their oars in fear.

translation.en: He waved his arms again as a terrifying signal.
translation.kr: 그는 무시무시한 신호로 다시 팔을 휘둘렀습니다.

translation.en: They watched the local people flee inland with their flocks.
translation.kr: 그들은 현지인들이 양 떼를 이끌고 내륙으로 달아나는 것을 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: A massive flame erupted among the distant hills.
translation.kr: 멀리 떨어진 언덕 사이에서 거대한 불길이 솟아올랐습니다.

translation.en: The giant ran up a valley and completely vanished.
translation.kr: 거인은 계곡 위로 달려가 완전히 사라졌습니다.

translation.en: The terrified heroes rested on their oars in fear.
translation.kr: 겁에 질린 영웅들은 두려움 속에 노를 내려놓고 쉬었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: But Medeia stood watching all from under her steep black brows, with a cunning smile upon her lips, and a cunning plot within her heart.  At last she spoke, ‘I know this giant.  I heard of him in the East. Hephaistos the Fire King made him in his forge in Ætna beneath the earth, and called him Talus, and gave him to Minos for a servant, to guard the coast of Crete.  Thrice a day he walks round the island, and never stops to sleep; and if strangers land he leaps into his furnace, which flames there among the hills; and when he is red-hot he rushes on them, and burns them in his brazen hands.’

translation.en: Medea watched everything intently from under her dark brows.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 짙은 눈썹 아래로 모든 것을 주의 깊게 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: A cunning smile played upon her lips.
translation.kr: 그녀의 입술에는 교활한 미소가 번졌습니다.

translation.en: A brilliant plot formed quickly in her mind.
translation.kr: 그녀의 마음속에 재빠르게 뛰어난 계획이 세워졌습니다.

translation.en: Finally, she revealed that she knew this giant.
translation.kr: 마침내 그녀는 이 거인을 알고 있다고 밝혔습니다.

translation.en: I heard tales of him when I was in the East.
translation.kr: 동방에 있을 때 그에 대한 이야기를 들었습니다.

translation.en: Hephaestus, the Fire King, forged him deep beneath Mount Etna.
translation.kr: 불의 왕 헤파이스토스가 에트나산 지하 깊은 곳에서 그를 만들었습니다.

translation.en: He called him Talos and gave him to Minos as a loyal servant.
translation.kr: 그는 그를 탈로스라 부르며 충실한 하인으로 미노스에게 주었습니다.

translation.en: His duty is to guard the coast of Crete.
translation.kr: 그의 임무는 크레타 해안을 지키는 것입니다.

translation.en: He patrols the island three times a day without ever sleeping.
translation.kr: 그는 잠도 자지 않고 하루 세 번씩 섬을 순찰합니다.

translation.en: If strangers land, he leaps straight into his blazing furnace.
translation.kr: 낯선 사람들이 상륙하면 그는 불타는 용광로 속으로 뛰어듭니다.

translation.en: When he is glowing red-hot, he rushes at the intruders.
translation.kr: 벌겋게 달아오르면 그는 침입자들에게 달려듭니다.

translation.en: He crushes and burns them in his massive brazen hands.
translation.kr: 그는 거대한 놋쇠 손으로 그들을 으스러뜨리고 태워버립니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then all the heroes cried, ‘What shall we do, wise Medeia?  We must have water, or we die of thirst.  Flesh and blood we can face fairly; but who can face this red-hot brass?’

translation.en: The desperate heroes asked the wise Medea what they should do.
translation.kr: 절망에 빠진 영웅들은 지혜로운 메데이아에게 어떻게 해야 할지 물었습니다.

translation.en: We must have water immediately, or we will die of thirst.
translation.kr: 당장 물을 구하지 못하면 우리는 갈증으로 죽고 말 것입니다.

translation.en: We can fight any opponent made of flesh and blood.
translation.kr: 피와 살로 이루어진 상대라면 누구와도 싸울 수 있습니다.

translation.en: But no mortal can stand against red-hot brass.
translation.kr: 하지만 붉게 달아오른 놋쇠에 맞설 수 있는 사람은 없습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘I can face red-hot brass, if the tale I hear be true.  For they say that he has but one vein in all his body, filled with liquid fire; and that this vein is closed with a nail: but I know not where that nail is placed.  But if I can get it once into these hands, you shall water your ship here in peace.’

translation.en: I can face red-hot brass if the rumors are true.
translation.kr: 소문이 사실이라면 내가 붉게 달아오른 놋쇠와 맞설 수 있습니다.

translation.en: They say he has only one vein running through his entire body.
translation.kr: 사람들 말로는 그의 온몸을 흐르는 혈관이 단 하나뿐이라고 합니다.

translation.en: This single vein is filled entirely with liquid fire.
translation.kr: 이 단 하나의 혈관은 액체 불로 가득 차 있습니다.

translation.en: It is sealed securely with a bronze nail.
translation.kr: 그것은 청동 못으로 단단히 밀봉되어 있습니다.

translation.en: I do not know exactly where this nail is located.
translation.kr: 나는 이 못이 정확히 어디에 있는지 모릅니다.

translation.en: But if I can get him into my hands, you shall water your ship in peace.
translation.kr: 하지만 내가 그를 손에 넣을 수 있다면 당신들은 평화롭게 배에 물을 채울 수 있을 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then she bade them put her on shore, and row off again, and wait what would befall.

translation.en: She told them to drop her off on the shore.
translation.kr: 그녀는 자신을 해안에 내려달라고 말했습니다.

translation.en: Then they were to row away and wait to see what happened.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 멀리 노를 저어가서 무슨 일이 일어나는지 지켜보라고 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And the heroes obeyed her unwillingly, for they were ashamed to leave her so alone; but Jason said, ‘She is dearer to me than to any of you, yet I will trust her freely on shore; she has more plots than we can dream of in the windings of that fair and cunning head.’

translation.en: The heroes obeyed her reluctantly, ashamed to leave her alone.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 그녀를 홀로 남겨두는 것을 부끄러워하며 마지못해 복종했습니다.

translation.en: Jason assured them she was dearer to him than anyone.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그녀가 그 누구보다도 자신에게 소중한 사람이라고 확신시켰습니다.

translation.en: Yet I will trust her completely on that shore.
translation.kr: 그럼에도 나는 저 해안에서 그녀를 완전히 믿을 것입니다.

translation.en: Her beautiful and cunning mind holds more plots than we could ever imagine.
translation.kr: 그녀의 아름답고 교활한 마음속에는 우리가 상상할 수 있는 것보다 더 많은 계획이 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: So they left the witch-maiden on the shore; and she stood there in her beauty all alone, till the giant strode back red-hot from head to heel, while the grass hissed and smoked beneath his tread.

translation.en: They left the witch-maiden standing alone on the shore.
translation.kr: 그들은 마녀 소녀를 해안에 홀로 남겨두었습니다.

translation.en: She stood there in her striking beauty.
translation.kr: 그녀는 눈부신 아름다움을 뽐내며 그곳에 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: Soon the giant strode back, glowing red-hot from head to toe.
translation.kr: 곧 거인이 머리부터 발끝까지 붉게 달아오른 채 성큼성큼 걸어왔습니다.

translation.en: The grass hissed and smoked violently beneath his heavy tread.
translation.kr: 그의 무거운 발걸음 아래에서 풀이 쉿쉿 소리를 내며 격렬하게 연기를 뿜어냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And when he saw the maiden alone, he stopped; and she looked boldly up into his face without moving, and began her magic song:—

translation.en: When he saw the maiden standing completely alone, he stopped.
translation.kr: 완전히 홀로 서 있는 소녀를 보자 그는 걸음을 멈추었습니다.

translation.en: She looked boldly up into his face without flinching.
translation.kr: 그녀는 움츠러들지 않고 대담하게 그의 얼굴을 올려다보았습니다.

translation.en: Then she began to sing her powerful magic song.
translation.kr: 그리고 그녀는 강력한 마법의 노래를 부르기 시작했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘Life is short, though life is sweet; and even men of brass and fire must die.  The brass must rust, the fire must cool, for time gnaws all things in their turn.  Life is short, though life is sweet: but sweeter to live for ever; sweeter to live ever youthful like the Gods, who have ichor in their veins—ichor which gives life, and youth, and joy, and a bounding heart.’

translation.en: Life is short, though life is incredibly sweet.
translation.kr: 인생은 비록 믿을 수 없을 만큼 달콤하지만 짧습니다.

translation.en: Even beings forged of brass and fire must eventually die.
translation.kr: 놋쇠와 불로 만들어진 존재조차도 언젠가는 죽어야 합니다.

translation.en: The brass must rust, and the fire must cool.
translation.kr: 놋쇠는 녹슬고 불은 식어야만 합니다.

translation.en: Time relentlessly gnaws away at all things in their turn.
translation.kr: 시간은 차례대로 모든 것을 무자비하게 갉아먹습니다.

translation.en: Life is short, though life is sweet.
translation.kr: 인생은 달콤하지만 짧습니다.

translation.en: But it is far sweeter to live forever.
translation.kr: 하지만 영원히 사는 것은 훨씬 더 달콤합니다.

translation.en: It is sweeter to remain forever youthful like the Gods.
translation.kr: 신들처럼 영원히 젊음을 유지하는 것은 더 달콤합니다.

translation.en: They possess immortal ichor flowing through their veins.
translation.kr: 그들의 혈관에는 불멸의 이코르가 흐르고 있습니다.

translation.en: This ichor grants eternal life, youth, joy, and a bounding heart.
translation.kr: 이 이코르는 영원한 생명, 젊음, 기쁨, 그리고 활기찬 심장을 부여합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then Talus said, ‘Who are you, strange maiden, and where is this ichor of youth?’

translation.en: Talos asked her who she was.
translation.kr: 탈로스는 그녀가 누구인지 물었습니다.

translation.en: He wanted to know where he could find this ichor of youth.
translation.kr: 그는 이 젊음의 이코르를 어디서 찾을 수 있는지 알고 싶어 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then Medeia held up a flask of crystal, and said, ‘Here is the ichor of youth.  I am Medeia the enchantress; my sister Circe gave me this, and said, “Go and reward Talus, the faithful servant, for his fame is gone out into all lands.”  So come, and I will pour this into your veins, that you may live for ever young.’

translation.en: Medea held up a sparkling crystal flask.
translation.kr: 메데이아가 반짝이는 수정 플라스크를 들어 올렸습니다.

translation.en: She told him that the flask contained the ichor of youth.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그 플라스크 안에 젊음의 이코르가 들어 있다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: I am Medea, the great enchantress.
translation.kr: 나는 위대한 마법사 메데이아입니다.

translation.en: My sister Circe gave this precious gift to me.
translation.kr: 나의 자매 키르케가 이 귀중한 선물을 내게 주었습니다.

translation.en: She told me to find and reward Talos, the faithful servant.
translation.kr: 그녀는 내게 충실한 하인 탈로스를 찾아 보상하라고 말했습니다.

translation.en: His glorious fame has spread throughout all lands.
translation.kr: 그의 영광스러운 명성은 모든 땅에 퍼졌습니다.

translation.en: Come here, and I will pour this into your veins.
translation.kr: 이리 오세요, 그러면 당신의 혈관에 이것을 부어드리겠습니다.

translation.en: Then you may live forever young and strong.
translation.kr: 그러면 당신은 영원히 젊고 강하게 살 수 있을 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And he listened to her false words, that simple Talus, and came near; and Medeia said, ‘Dip yourself in the sea first, and cool yourself, lest you burn my tender hands; then show me where the nail in your vein is, that I may pour the ichor in.’

translation.en: The simple Talos eagerly listened to her false words.
translation.kr: 단순한 탈로스는 그녀의 거짓말을 열심히 귀담아들었습니다.

translation.en: He stepped closer to the cunning enchantress.
translation.kr: 그는 교활한 마법사에게 더 가까이 다가갔습니다.

translation.en: Medea warned him to dip himself in the sea first to cool down.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 먼저 바다에 몸을 담가 열을 식히라고 경고했습니다.

translation.en: Otherwise, you might burn my tender hands.
translation.kr: 그렇지 않으면 내 연약한 손에 화상을 입힐 수도 있습니다.

translation.en: Then you can show me where the nail in your vein is hidden.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 당신 혈관의 못이 어디에 숨겨져 있는지 내게 보여주세요.

translation.en: Once I find it, I will pour the immortal ichor inside.
translation.kr: 그것을 찾으면 그 안에 불멸의 이코르를 부어 넣겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then that simple Talus dipped himself in the sea, till it hissed, and roared, and smoked; and came and knelt before Medeia, and showed her the secret nail.

translation.en: The simple-minded Talos plunged himself into the sea.
translation.kr: 단순한 탈로스는 바다로 뛰어들었습니다.

translation.en: The water hissed, roared, and sent up massive clouds of smoke.
translation.kr: 물이 쉿쉿 소리를 내며 굉음을 냈고, 거대한 연기 구름을 피워 올렸습니다.

translation.en: He returned and knelt obediently before Medea.
translation.kr: 그는 돌아와 메데이아 앞에 순순히 무릎을 꿇었습니다.

translation.en: He revealed the location of his secret nail.
translation.kr: 그는 비밀 못이 있는 위치를 드러냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And she drew the nail out gently, but she poured no ichor in; and instead the liquid fire spouted forth, like a stream of red-hot iron.  And Talus tried to leap up, crying, ‘You have betrayed me, false witch-maiden!’ But she lifted up her hands before him, and sang, till he sank beneath her spell.  And as he sank, his brazen limbs clanked heavily, and the earth groaned beneath his weight; and the liquid fire ran from his heel, like a stream of lava, to the sea; and Medeia laughed, and called to the heroes, ‘Come ashore, and water your ship in peace.’

translation.en: She gently drew the nail out, but poured no ichor in.
translation.kr: 그녀는 부드럽게 못을 뽑았지만 이코르는 붓지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Instead, the liquid fire violently spouted forth.
translation.kr: 대신 액체 불이 맹렬하게 뿜어져 나왔습니다.

translation.en: It gushed like a blazing stream of red-hot iron.
translation.kr: 그것은 붉게 달아오른 철이 타오르는 시냇물처럼 쏟아졌습니다.

translation.en: Talos tried desperately to leap up.
translation.kr: 탈로스는 필사적으로 위로 뛰어오르려 했습니다.

translation.en: You have betrayed me, you false witch!
translation.kr: 네가 나를 배신했구나, 이 거짓말쟁이 마녀야!

translation.en: She lifted her hands before him and continued her song.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그를 향해 손을 들어 올리고 노래를 계속했습니다.

translation.en: He sank completely beneath the power of her spell.
translation.kr: 그는 그녀의 주문의 힘 아래 완전히 무너져 내렸습니다.

translation.en: As he fell, his massive brazen limbs clanked heavily.
translation.kr: 그가 쓰러지자 거대한 놋쇠 팔다리가 둔탁한 소리를 냈습니다.

translation.en: The earth groaned loudly beneath his immense weight.
translation.kr: 지구는 그의 엄청난 무게 아래에서 큰 소리로 신음했습니다.

translation.en: The liquid fire drained from his heel and ran to the sea like lava.
translation.kr: 액체 불이 그의 발뒤꿈치에서 빠져나와 용암처럼 바다로 흘러갔습니다.

translation.en: Medea laughed triumphantly and called out to the heroes.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 승리감에 차 웃으며 영웅들을 향해 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Come ashore and water your ship in peace.
translation.kr: 해안으로 와서 평화롭게 배에 물을 채우시오.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: So they came, and found the giant lying dead; and they fell down, and kissed Medeia’s feet; and watered their ship, and took sheep and oxen, and so left that inhospitable shore.

translation.en: They arrived and found the giant lying completely dead.
translation.kr: 그들이 도착해 보니 거인은 완전히 죽어 누워 있었습니다.

translation.en: They fell down and gratefully kissed Medea's feet.
translation.kr: 그들은 엎드려 감사한 마음으로 메데이아의 발에 입을 맞췄습니다.

translation.en: They watered their ship and gathered sheep and oxen.
translation.kr: 그들은 배에 물을 채우고 양과 소를 모았습니다.

translation.en: Then they swiftly departed from that inhospitable shore.
translation.kr: 그리고 나서 그들은 그 불친절한 해안을 서둘러 떠났습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: At last, after many more adventures, they came to the Cape of Malea, at the south-west point of the Peloponnese.  And there they offered sacrifices, and Orpheus purged them from their guilt.  Then they rode away again to the northward, past the Laconian shore, and came all worn and tired by Sunium, and up the long Euboean Strait, until they saw once more Pelion, and Aphetai, and Iolcos by the sea.

translation.en: After surviving many more adventures, they reached the Cape of Malea.
translation.kr: 수많은 모험을 더 이겨낸 후 그들은 말레아 곶에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: It was located at the southwest point of the Peloponnese.
translation.kr: 그곳은 펠로폰네소스 반도의 남서쪽 끝에 있었습니다.

translation.en: There they offered solemn sacrifices to the gods.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 그들은 신들에게 엄숙한 제사를 올렸습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus completely purged them from their lingering guilt.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 그들에게 남아 있던 죄책감을 완전히 씻어주었습니다.

translation.en: They rowed northward once again, passing the Laconian shore.
translation.kr: 그들은 다시 북쪽으로 노를 저어 라코니아 해안을 지났습니다.

translation.en: Worn and tired, they sailed past Sunium and up the Euboean Strait.
translation.kr: 지치고 피곤한 몸으로 수니온을 지나 에우보이아 해협을 거슬러 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: Finally, they saw Pelion, Aphetae, and Iolcus by the sea once more.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 펠리온, 아페타이, 그리고 바닷가의 이올코스를 다시 보게 되었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And they ran the ship ashore; but they had no strength left to haul her up the beach; and they crawled out on the pebbles, and sat down, and wept till they could weep no more.  For the houses and the trees were all altered; and all the faces which they saw were strange; and their joy was swallowed up in sorrow, while they thought of their youth, and all their labour, and the gallant comrades they had lost.

translation.en: They ran the ship securely onto the shore.
translation.kr: 그들은 배를 해안에 안전하게 댔습니다.

translation.en: But they had no strength left to haul her up the beach.
translation.kr: 하지만 배를 해변으로 끌어올릴 힘이 남아있지 않았습니다.

translation.en: They crawled out onto the pebbles and sat down heavily.
translation.kr: 그들은 조약돌 위로 기어 나와 무겁게 주저앉았습니다.

translation.en: They wept until they could shed no more tears.
translation.kr: 그들은 더 이상 눈물이 나오지 않을 때까지 울었습니다.

translation.en: The houses and trees had completely changed.
translation.kr: 집과 나무들은 완전히 변해 있었습니다.

translation.en: Every face they looked upon was strange and unfamiliar.
translation.kr: 그들이 바라본 모든 얼굴은 낯설고 생소했습니다.

translation.en: Their joy was entirely swallowed up in deep sorrow.
translation.kr: 그들의 기쁨은 깊은 슬픔 속에 완전히 삼켜졌습니다.

translation.en: They thought of their lost youth and all their grueling labor.
translation.kr: 그들은 잃어버린 젊음과 자신들의 모든 고된 노동을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: They mourned the gallant comrades they had lost along the way.
translation.kr: 그들은 그 과정에서 잃은 용감한 동료들을 애도했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And the people crowded round, and asked them ‘Who are you, that you sit weeping here?’

translation.en: The local people crowded around them with great curiosity.
translation.kr: 현지 사람들이 큰 호기심을 가지고 그들 주위로 모여들었습니다.

translation.en: Who are you, and why do you sit weeping here?
translation.kr: 당신들은 누구이며, 왜 여기서 울고 있습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘We are the sons of your princes, who sailed out many a year ago.  We went to fetch the golden fleece, and we have brought it, and grief therewith.  Give us news of our fathers and our mothers, if any of them be left alive on earth.’

translation.en: We are the sons of your princes who sailed away many years ago.
translation.kr: 우리는 수년 전 항해를 떠났던 여러분의 왕자들의 아들들입니다.

translation.en: We went to fetch the Golden Fleece.
translation.kr: 우리는 황금 양털을 가져오기 위해 떠났습니다.

translation.en: We have brought it back, along with immense grief.
translation.kr: 우리는 엄청난 슬픔과 함께 그것을 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: Please give us news of our fathers and mothers.
translation.kr: 우리 아버지와 어머니의 소식을 전해주십시오.

translation.en: Tell us if any of them are still left alive on this earth.
translation.kr: 그분들 중 한 분이라도 이 세상에 살아 계신지 알려주십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then there was shouting, and laughing, and weeping; and all the kings came to the shore, and they led away the heroes to their homes, and bewailed the valiant dead.

translation.en: Suddenly, there was a great deal of shouting, laughing, and weeping.
translation.kr: 갑자기 엄청난 환호와 웃음, 그리고 울음소리가 터져 나왔습니다.

translation.en: All the local kings rushed down to the shore.
translation.kr: 지역의 모든 왕들이 해안으로 달려왔습니다.

translation.en: They proudly led the heroes away to their homes.
translation.kr: 그들은 자랑스럽게 영웅들을 자신들의 집으로 이끌었습니다.

translation.en: Together, they bitterly bewailed the valiant dead.
translation.kr: 그들은 함께 용감하게 죽은 자들을 몹시 슬퍼했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then Jason went up with Medeia to the palace of his uncle Pelias.  And when he came in Pelias sat by the hearth, crippled and blind with age; while opposite him sat Æson, Jason’s father, crippled and blind likewise; and the two old men’s heads shook together as they tried to warm themselves before the fire.

translation.en: Jason went up with Medea to the palace of his uncle Pelias.
translation.kr: 이아손은 메데이아와 함께 삼촌 펠리아스의 궁전으로 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: When he entered, he saw Pelias sitting by the hearth.
translation.kr: 안으로 들어갔을 때, 그는 화로 곁에 앉아 있는 펠리아스를 보았습니다.

translation.en: The old king was severely crippled and blind with age.
translation.kr: 늙은 왕은 노환으로 심하게 다리를 절고 눈이 멀어 있었습니다.

translation.en: Opposite him sat Aeson, Jason's own father.
translation.kr: 그의 맞은편에는 이아손의 아버지인 아이손이 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: Aeson was also crippled and completely blind.
translation.kr: 아이손 역시 다리를 절고 완전히 눈이 멀어 있었습니다.

translation.en: The two old men's heads shook uncontrollably together.
translation.kr: 두 노인의 머리가 주체할 수 없이 함께 떨렸습니다.

translation.en: They were desperately trying to warm themselves before the fading fire.
translation.kr: 그들은 사그라지는 불 앞에서 필사적으로 몸을 녹이려 하고 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: And Jason fell down at his father’s knees, and wept, and called him by his name.  And the old man stretched his hands out, and felt him, and said, ‘Do not mock me, young hero.  My son Jason is dead long ago at sea.’

translation.en: Jason fell heavily down at his father's knees.
translation.kr: 이아손은 아버지의 무릎 아래에 무겁게 엎드렸습니다.

translation.en: He wept bitterly and called his father by his name.
translation.kr: 그는 몹시 울며 아버지의 이름을 불렀습니다.

translation.en: The old man stretched out his frail hands and touched him.
translation.kr: 노인은 연약한 손을 뻗어 그를 만졌습니다.

translation.en: Do not mock a broken old man, young hero.
translation.kr: 부서진 노인을 조롱하지 마시오, 젊은 영웅이여.

translation.en: My son Jason died at sea a very long time ago.
translation.kr: 내 아들 이아손은 아주 오래전 바다에서 죽었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: ‘I am your own son Jason, whom you trusted to the Centaur upon Pelion; and I have brought home the golden fleece, and a princess of the Sun’s race for my bride.  So now give me up the kingdom, Pelias my uncle, and fulfil your promise as I have fulfilled mine.’

translation.en: I am your own son Jason, whom you trusted to the Centaur upon Pelion.
translation.kr: 저는 아버지가 펠리온산의 켄타우로스에게 맡기셨던 당신의 아들 이아손입니다.

translation.en: I have brought home the Golden Fleece.
translation.kr: 저는 황금 양털을 집으로 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: I have also brought a princess of the Sun's race as my bride.
translation.kr: 저는 또한 태양의 혈통을 이은 공주를 제 신부로 데려왔습니다.

translation.en: Now give up the kingdom to me, Pelias my uncle.
translation.kr: 그러니 이제 왕국을 제게 넘겨주십시오, 삼촌 펠리아스.

translation.en: Fulfill your promise just as I have faithfully fulfilled mine.
translation.kr: 제가 제 약속을 충실히 지켰듯 당신의 약속을 이행하십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part V: How the Argonauts Were Driven into the Unknown Sea
paragraphs.raw: Then his father clung to him like a child, and wept, and would not let him go; and cried, ‘Now I shall not go down lonely to my grave.  Promise me never to leave me till I die.’

translation.en: His father clung to him tightly like a frightened child.
translation.kr: 그의 아버지는 겁먹은 어린아이처럼 그에게 꽉 매달렸습니다.

translation.en: He wept tears of joy and refused to let him go.
translation.kr: 그는 기쁨의 눈물을 흘리며 그를 놓아주려 하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Now I shall not go down lonely to my grave.
translation.kr: 이제 나는 외롭게 무덤으로 내려가지 않을 것이다.

translation.en: Promise me that you will never leave me until I die.
translation.kr: 내가 죽을 때까지 내 곁을 떠나지 않겠다고 약속해 다오.

chapters.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: PART VI WHAT WAS THE END OF THE HEROES

translation.en: Part 6: What Was the End of the Heroes
translation.kr: [6부: 영웅들의 최후는 어떠했는가]

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: And now I wish that I could end my story pleasantly; but it is no fault of mine that I cannot.  The old songs end it sadly, and I believe that they are right and wise; for though the heroes were purified at Malea, yet sacrifices cannot make bad hearts good, and Jason had taken a wicked wife, and he had to bear his burden to the last.

translation.en: I wish I could end my story on a happy note.
translation.kr: 이제 제 이야기를 즐겁게 마무리하고 싶습니다.

translation.en: But it is not my fault that I cannot.
translation.kr: 하지만 그럴 수 없는 것은 제 잘못이 아닙니다.

translation.en: The ancient songs end sadly, and I believe they are wise to do so.
translation.kr: 오래된 노래들은 이 이야기를 슬프게 끝맺고 있으며, 저는 그것이 옳고 지혜롭다고 믿습니다.

translation.en: The heroes were purified at Malea, but sacrifices cannot make a bad heart good.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 말레아에서 정화 의식을 치렀지만, 제물이 악한 마음을 선하게 만들 수는 없습니다.

translation.en: Jason had chosen a wicked wife, and he had to bear his heavy burden to the very end.
translation.kr: 이아손은 사악한 아내를 맞이했고, 그는 마지막 순간까지 그 무거운 짐을 견뎌야만 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: And first she laid a cunning plot to punish that poor old Pelias, instead of letting him die in peace.

translation.en: First, Medea devised a cunning plot to punish old Pelias.
translation.kr: 먼저 메데이아는 늙은 펠리아스를 벌하기 위해 교활한 음모를 꾸몄습니다.

translation.en: She refused to let him die in peace.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그가 평화롭게 죽도록 내버려 두지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: For she told his daughters, ‘I can make old things young again; I will show you how easy it is to do.’  So she took an old ram and killed him, and put him in a cauldron with magic herbs; and whispered her spells over him, and he leapt out again a young lamb.  So that ‘Medeia’s cauldron’ is a proverb still, by which we mean times of war and change, when the world has become old and feeble, and grows young again through bitter pains.

translation.en: She told his daughters, I can make old things young again.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그의 딸들에게 말했습니다. 나는 늙은 것을 다시 젊게 만들 수 있어요.

translation.en: I will show you how easily it can be done.
translation.kr: 그것이 얼마나 쉬운 일인지 여러분에게 보여주겠어요.

translation.en: She took an old ram, killed it, and placed it in a cauldron with magic herbs.
translation.kr: 그녀는 늙은 숫양을 잡아 죽인 뒤, 마법의 약초와 함께 가마솥에 넣었습니다.

translation.en: She whispered her spells over it, and a young lamb leaped out.
translation.kr: 그녀가 그 위로 주문을 속삭이자, 어린 양 한 마리가 펄쩍 뛰어올랐습니다.

translation.en: Medeas cauldron is still a proverb today.
translation.kr: 메데이아의 가마솥은 오늘날에도 여전히 속담으로 남아 있습니다.

translation.en: It describes times of war and change.
translation.kr: 그것은 전쟁과 변화의 시대를 묘사합니다.

translation.en: It means the world has grown old and weak, but becomes young again through bitter pain.
translation.kr: 이는 세상이 늙고 쇠약해졌다가 극심한 고통을 겪고 다시 젊어지는 것을 의미합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: Then she said to Pelias’ daughters, ‘Do to your father as I did to this ram, and he will grow young and strong again.’  But she only told them half the spell; so they failed, while Medeia mocked them; and poor old Pelias died, and his daughters came to misery.  But the songs say she cured Æson, Jason’s father, and he became young, and strong again.

translation.en: Then she told the daughters to do the same to their father.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 그녀는 딸들에게 아버지에게도 똑같이 하라고 말했습니다.

translation.en: She promised he would grow young and strong again.
translation.kr: 그녀는 아버지가 다시 젊고 강해질 것이라고 약속했습니다.

translation.en: But she only taught them half of the spell.
translation.kr: 하지만 그녀는 주문의 절반만 가르쳐 주었습니다.

translation.en: They failed, and Medea mocked them.
translation.kr: 그들은 실패했고 메데이아는 그들을 조롱했습니다.

translation.en: Poor old Pelias died, and his daughters were left in misery.
translation.kr: 불쌍하고 늙은 펠리아스는 죽었고 그의 딸들은 비참한 처지에 놓였습니다.

translation.en: But the ancient songs say she cured Jasons father, Aeson.
translation.kr: 하지만 오래된 노래들에 따르면 그녀는 이아손의 아버지인 아이손을 치료했다고 합니다.

translation.en: Aeson became young and strong once more.
translation.kr: 아이손은 다시 젊고 강해졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: But Jason could not love her, after all her cruel deeds.  So he was ungrateful to her, and wronged her; and she revenged herself on him.  And a terrible revenge she took—too terrible to speak of here.  But you will hear of it yourselves when you grow up, for it has been sung in noble poetry and music; and whether it be true or not, it stands for ever as a warning to us not to seek for help from evil persons, or to gain good ends by evil means.  For if we use an adder even against our enemies, it will turn again and sting us.

translation.en: But Jason could not love her after all her cruel deeds.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손은 그녀의 잔인한 행동들 때문에 그녀를 사랑할 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: He was ungrateful and treated her terribly.
translation.kr: 그는 은혜를 모르고 그녀를 끔찍하게 대했습니다.

translation.en: Medea took a terrible revenge on him.
translation.kr: 메데이아는 그에게 끔찍한 복수를 했습니다.

translation.en: Her revenge was too awful to speak of here.
translation.kr: 그녀의 복수는 여기서 말하기에는 너무나 끔찍했습니다.

translation.en: You will hear about it yourselves when you grow older.
translation.kr: 여러분이 어른이 되면 그에 대해 직접 듣게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: It has been sung in noble poetry and beautiful music.
translation.kr: 그 이야기는 훌륭한 시와 아름다운 음악으로 불려져 왔습니다.

translation.en: Whether the story is true or not, it stands as an eternal warning.
translation.kr: 그 이야기가 사실이든 아니든, 그것은 영원한 경고로 남아 있습니다.

translation.en: We must never seek help from evil people.
translation.kr: 우리는 결코 악한 사람들에게 도움을 구해서는 안 됩니다.

translation.en: We must never try to achieve good goals through evil methods.
translation.kr: 우리는 악한 방법을 통해 선한 목표를 이루려고 해서도 안 됩니다.

translation.en: If we use a poisonous snake against our enemies, it will turn and strike us.
translation.kr: 만약 우리가 적에게 독사를 사용한다면, 그 뱀은 돌아서서 우리를 물 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: But of all the other heroes there is many a brave tale left, which I have no space to tell you, so you must read them for yourselves;—of the hunting of the boar in Calydon, which Meleager killed; and of Heracles’ twelve famous labours; and of the seven who fought at Thebes; and of the noble love of Castor and Polydeuces, the twin Dioscouroi—how when one died the other would not live without him, so they shared their immortality between them; and Zeus changed them into the two twin stars which never rise both at once.

translation.en: There are many brave tales left about the other heroes.
translation.kr: 다른 영웅들에 대해서도 용감한 이야기들이 많이 남아 있습니다.

translation.en: I have no space to tell them all, so you must read them yourselves.
translation.kr: 모두 이야기할 지면이 부족하니 여러분이 직접 읽어보셔야 합니다.

translation.en: You can read about the hunting of the Calydonian boar, which Meleager killed.
translation.kr: 멜레아그로스가 죽인 칼리돈의 멧돼지 사냥에 대해 읽어보실 수 있습니다.

translation.en: You can read about the twelve famous labors of Heracles.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스의 유명한 열두 가지 과업에 대해서도 읽어볼 수 있습니다.

translation.en: There is the story of the seven heroes who fought at Thebes.
translation.kr: 테베에서 싸웠던 일곱 영웅의 이야기도 있습니다.

translation.en: There is the noble love of the twins, Castor and Polydeuces.
translation.kr: 쌍둥이인 카스토르와 폴리데우케스의 고귀한 사랑 이야기도 빼놓을 수 없습니다.

translation.en: When one died, the other refused to live without him.
translation.kr: 한 명이 죽자 다른 한 명은 그 없이 살기를 거부했습니다.

translation.en: So they shared their immortality with each other.
translation.kr: 그래서 그들은 서로의 불멸성을 나누어 가졌습니다.

translation.en: Zeus changed them into twin stars that never rise at the same time.
translation.kr: 제우스는 그들을 결코 동시에 떠오르지 않는 쌍둥이 별로 만들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: And what became of Cheiron, the good immortal beast?  That, too, is a sad story; for the heroes never saw him more.  He was wounded by a poisoned arrow, at Pholoe among the hills, when Heracles opened the fatal wine-jar, which Cheiron had warned him not to touch.  And the Centaurs smelt the wine, and flocked to it, and fought for it with Heracles; but he killed them all with his poisoned arrows, and Cheiron was left alone. Then Cheiron took up one of the arrows, and dropped it by chance upon his foot; and the poison ran like fire along his veins, and he lay down and longed to die; and cried, ‘Through wine I perish, the bane of all my race.  Why should I live for ever in this agony?  Who will take my immortality, that I may die?’

translation.en: And what happened to Chiron, the good immortal beast?
translation.kr: 그리고 선하고 불멸하는 야수인 케이론에게는 무슨 일이 일어났을까요?

translation.en: That is also a sad story, for the heroes never saw him again.
translation.kr: 그 또한 슬픈 이야기입니다. 영웅들은 그를 다시는 보지 못했기 때문입니다.

translation.en: He was wounded by a poisoned arrow in the hills of Pholoe.
translation.kr: 그는 폴로에의 언덕에서 독화살에 상처를 입었습니다.

translation.en: Heracles had opened the fatal wine jar that Chiron warned him not to touch.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 케이론이 만지지 말라고 경고했던 치명적인 항아리를 열고 말았습니다.

translation.en: The Centaurs smelled the wine, flocked to it, and fought Heracles for it.
translation.kr: 켄타우로스들은 포도주 냄새를 맡고 몰려들어 헤라클레스와 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: But Heracles killed them all with his poisoned arrows.
translation.kr: 하지만 헤라클레스는 독화살로 그들을 모두 죽였습니다.

translation.en: Chiron was left completely alone.
translation.kr: 케이론은 완전히 홀로 남겨졌습니다.

translation.en: Chiron picked up one of the arrows and accidentally dropped it on his foot.
translation.kr: 케이론은 화살 하나를 집어 들었다가 실수로 자신의 발에 떨어뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: The poison burned like fire through his veins.
translation.kr: 독이 불처럼 그의 혈관을 타고 퍼졌습니다.

translation.en: He lay down, wishing to die, and cried out in pain.
translation.kr: 그는 자리에 누워 죽기를 바라며 고통 속에 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: I am dying because of wine, the ruin of all my people.
translation.kr: 내 동족 모두를 파멸시킨 포도주 때문에 내가 죽는구나.

translation.en: Why must I live forever in this terrible agony?
translation.kr: 내가 왜 이 끔찍한 고통 속에서 영원히 살아야 한단 말인가?

translation.en: Who will take my immortality so that I can finally die?
translation.kr: 내가 마침내 죽을 수 있도록 누가 나의 불멸성을 가져갈 것인가?

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: Then Prometheus answered, the good Titan, whom Heracles had set free from Caucasus, ‘I will take your immortality and live for ever, that I may help poor mortal men.’  So Cheiron gave him his immortality, and died, and had rest from pain.  And Heracles and Prometheus wept over him, and went to bury him on Pelion; but Zeus took him up among the stars, to live for ever, grand and mild, low down in the far southern sky.

translation.en: Then the good Titan Prometheus answered him.
translation.kr: 그러자 선한 티탄인 프로메테우스가 그에게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Heracles had recently freed Prometheus from the Caucasus mountains.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 최근에 코카서스 산맥에서 프로메테우스를 풀어준 참이었습니다.

translation.en: Prometheus said, I will take your immortality and live forever so that I may help poor mortal men.
translation.kr: 프로메테우스가 말했습니다. 가엾은 인간들을 도울 수 있도록, 내가 당신의 불멸성을 가져가 영원히 살겠습니다.

translation.en: Chiron gave up his immortality, died, and finally found rest from his pain.
translation.kr: 케이론은 불멸성을 포기하고 숨을 거두었으며 마침내 고통에서 벗어나 안식을 찾았습니다.

translation.en: Heracles and Prometheus wept over him.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스와 프로메테우스는 그를 위해 눈물을 흘렸습니다.

translation.en: They went to bury him on Mount Pelion.
translation.kr: 그들은 펠리온 산에 그를 묻어주러 갔습니다.

translation.en: But Zeus took Chiron up among the stars to live forever.
translation.kr: 하지만 제우스는 케이론을 별들 사이로 데려가 영원히 살게 했습니다.

translation.en: He shines grand and gentle, low in the far southern sky.
translation.kr: 그는 머나먼 남쪽 하늘 아래에서 웅장하고 온화하게 빛나고 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part VI: What Was the End of the Heroes
paragraphs.raw: And in time the heroes died, all but Nestor, the silver-tongued old man; and left behind them valiant sons, but not so great as they had been. Yet their fame, too, lives till this day, for they fought at the ten years’ siege of Troy: and their story is in the book which we call Homer, in two of the noblest songs on earth—the ‘Iliad,’ which tells us of the siege of Troy, and Achilles’ quarrel with the kings; and the ‘Odyssey,’ which tells the wanderings of Odysseus, through many lands for many years, and how Alcinous sent him home at last, safe to Ithaca his beloved island, and to Penelope his faithful wife, and Telemachus his son, and Euphorbus the noble swineherd, and the old dog who licked his hand and died.  We will read that sweet story, children, by the fire some winter night.  And now I will end my tale, and begin another and a more cheerful one, of a hero who became a worthy king, and won his people’s love.

translation.en: In time, all the heroes died except Nestor, the silver-tongued old man.
translation.kr: 시간이 흘러 은빛 혀를 가진 노인 네스토르를 제외하고 모든 영웅들이 세상을 떠났습니다.

translation.en: They left behind brave sons, though not as great as their fathers.
translation.kr: 그들은 용감한 아들들을 남겼지만, 아버지들만큼 위대하지는 않았습니다.

translation.en: Yet their fame lives on to this day.
translation.kr: 그러나 그들의 명성 또한 오늘날까지 살아 숨 쉬고 있습니다.

translation.en: Their sons fought in the ten-year siege of Troy.
translation.kr: 그들의 아들들은 10년에 걸친 트로이 포위전에서 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: Their story is found in the book we call Homer.
translation.kr: 그들의 이야기는 우리가 호메로스라고 부르는 책에 담겨 있습니다.

translation.en: It contains two of the noblest songs on earth.
translation.kr: 그 책에는 세상에서 가장 고귀한 두 곡의 노래가 들어 있습니다.

translation.en: The Iliad tells of the siege of Troy and Achilles quarrel with the kings.
translation.kr: 일리아스는 트로이 포위전과 아킬레우스가 왕들과 벌인 다툼을 들려줍니다.

translation.en: The Odyssey tells of the long wanderings of Odysseus.
translation.kr: 오디세이아는 오디세우스의 기나긴 방랑을 이야기합니다.

translation.en: He traveled through many lands for many years.
translation.kr: 그는 오랜 세월 동안 많은 나라들을 떠돌았습니다.

translation.en: King Alcinous finally sent him safely home to his beloved island of Ithaca.
translation.kr: 마침내 알키노오스 왕은 그를 사랑하는 섬 이타카로 무사히 돌려보냈습니다.

translation.en: Odysseus returned to his faithful wife Penelope and his son Telemachus.
translation.kr: 오디세우스는 충실한 아내 페넬로페와 아들 텔레마코스에게 돌아갔습니다.

translation.en: He saw the noble swineherd Euphorbus and his old dog.
translation.kr: 그는 고귀한 돼지치기 에우포르보스와 자신의 늙은 개를 만났습니다.

translation.en: The old dog licked his hand and died.
translation.kr: 그 늙은 개는 그의 손을 핥고 죽었습니다.

translation.en: Children, we will read that sweet story by the fire some winter night.
translation.kr: 얘들아, 어느 겨울밤 난롯가에 앉아 그 아름다운 이야기를 읽어보자꾸나.

translation.en: And now I will end my tale.
translation.kr: 이제 제 이야기를 마치려 합니다.

translation.en: I will begin a more cheerful story about a hero who became a worthy king.
translation.kr: 대신 훌륭한 왕이 되어 백성들의 사랑을 받은 영웅의 더 밝은 이야기를 시작하겠습니다.

chapters.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: PART I HOW THESEUS LIFTED THE STONE

translation.en: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
translation.kr: [1부: 테세우스가 바위를 들어 올리다]

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: Once upon a time there was a princess in Trœzene, Aithra, the daughter of Pittheus the king.  She had one fair son, named Theseus, the bravest lad in all the land; and Aithra never smiled but when she looked at him, for her husband had forgotten her, and lived far away.  And she used to go up to the mountain above Troezene, to the temple of Poseidon and sit there all day looking out across the bay, over Methana, to the purple peaks of Ægina and the Attic shore beyond.  And when Theseus was full fifteen years old she took him up with her to the temple, and into the thickets of the grove which grew in the temple-yard.  And she led him to a tall plane-tree, beneath whose shade grew arbutus, and lentisk, and purple heather-bushes.  And there she sighed, and said, ‘Theseus, my son, go into that thicket and you will find at the plane-tree foot a great flat stone; lift it, and bring me what lies underneath.’

translation.en: Once, Princess Aithra lived in Troezen.
translation.kr: 옛날 트로이젠에 아이트라라는 공주가 살았습니다.

translation.en: She was the daughter of King Pittheus.
translation.kr: 그녀는 피테우스 왕의 딸이었습니다.

translation.en: She had a brave son named Theseus.
translation.kr: 그녀에게는 온 나라에서 가장 용감한 테세우스라는 아들이 있었습니다.

translation.en: Aithra only smiled when she looked at him.
translation.kr: 아이트라는 아들을 볼 때만 미소를 지었습니다.

translation.en: Her husband had left her to live far away.
translation.kr: 그녀의 남편이 그녀를 잊은 채 멀리 떠나 살았기 때문입니다.

translation.en: She often went up the mountain to the temple of Poseidon.
translation.kr: 그녀는 종종 트로이젠 위의 산에 있는 포세이돈 신전에 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: She would sit there all day.
translation.kr: 그녀는 하루 종일 그곳에 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: She looked across the bay past Methana.
translation.kr: 그녀는 바다를 지나 메타나 너머를 바라보았습니다.

translation.en: She watched the purple peaks of Aegina and the distant Attic shore.
translation.kr: 그녀는 아이기나의 자줏빛 봉우리와 저 멀리 아티카 해안을 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: When Theseus turned fifteen, she took him to the temple.
translation.kr: 테세우스가 열다섯 살이 되자, 그녀는 아들을 신전으로 데려갔습니다.

translation.en: They walked into the thick grove in the temple yard.
translation.kr: 그들은 신전 뜰에 있는 울창한 숲으로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: She led him to a tall plane tree.
translation.kr: 그녀는 아들을 키가 큰 플라타너스 나무로 이끌었습니다.

translation.en: Bushes and purple heather grew in its shade.
translation.kr: 그 그늘 아래에는 덤불과 자줏빛 히스가 자라고 있었습니다.

translation.en: She sighed and spoke to him.
translation.kr: 그녀는 한숨을 쉬며 아들에게 말했습니다.

translation.en: Theseus, my son, go into that thicket.
translation.kr: 테세우스야, 저 덤불 속으로 들어가거라.

translation.en: You will find a great flat stone at the base of the tree.
translation.kr: 나무 밑동에서 크고 평평한 바위를 하나 찾을 수 있을 것이다.

translation.en: Lift it up and bring me what lies underneath.
translation.kr: 그것을 들어 올려서 그 아래에 있는 것을 내게 가져오너라.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus pushed his way in through the thick bushes, and saw that they had not been moved for many a year.  And searching among their roots he found a great flat stone, all overgrown with ivy, and acanthus, and moss.  He tried to lift it, but he could not.  And he tried till the sweat ran down his brow from heat, and the tears from his eyes for shame; but all was of no avail.  And at last he came back to his mother, and said, ‘I have found the stone, but I cannot lift it; nor do I think that any man could in all Troezene.’

translation.en: Theseus pushed his way through the thick bushes.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 빽빽한 덤불을 헤치고 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: He saw they had not been touched for years.
translation.kr: 그는 그곳이 수년 동안 사람의 손길이 닿지 않았다는 것을 알았습니다.

translation.en: Among the roots, he found a great flat stone.
translation.kr: 뿌리들 사이에서 그는 크고 평평한 바위를 하나 발견했습니다.

translation.en: It was covered in ivy, moss, and leafy vines.
translation.kr: 그것은 담쟁이덩굴과 이끼, 그리고 잎이 무성한 덩굴로 덮여 있었습니다.

translation.en: He tried to lift the stone, but he failed.
translation.kr: 그는 바위를 들어 올리려 했지만 실패했습니다.

translation.en: He struggled until sweat ran down his face.
translation.kr: 그는 땀이 얼굴을 타고 흘러내릴 때까지 애를 썼습니다.

translation.en: Tears of shame filled his eyes, but it was useless.
translation.kr: 부끄러움에 눈물이 고였지만 아무 소용이 없었습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he went back to his mother.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 어머니에게 돌아갔습니다.

translation.en: I found the stone, but I cannot lift it.
translation.kr: 바위를 찾았지만 들어 올릴 수가 없어요.

translation.en: I do not think anyone in Troezen could lift it.
translation.kr: 트로이젠의 그 누구도 그 바위를 들 수 없을 거예요.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: Then she sighed, and said, ‘The Gods wait long; but they are just at last.  Let it be for another year.  The day may come when you will be a stronger man than lives in all Troezene.’

translation.en: She sighed and spoke to him gently.
translation.kr: 그녀는 한숨을 내쉬며 다정하게 말했습니다.

translation.en: The gods wait a long time, but they are just.
translation.kr: 신들은 오래 기다리시지만 결국에는 공정하시단다.

translation.en: Let it rest for another year.
translation.kr: 일 년만 더 기다려 보자꾸나.

translation.en: You may yet become the strongest man in Troezen.
translation.kr: 네가 트로이젠에서 가장 힘센 남자가 되는 날이 올지도 모르지.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: Then she took him by the hand, and went into the temple and prayed, and came down again with Theseus to her home.

translation.en: She took him by the hand.
translation.kr: 그녀는 아들의 손을 잡았습니다.

translation.en: They went into the temple and prayed.
translation.kr: 그들은 신전으로 들어가 기도를 올렸습니다.

translation.en: Then they returned together to their home.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 두 사람은 함께 집으로 돌아왔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: And when a full year was past she led Theseus up again to the temple, and bade him lift the stone; but he could not.

translation.en: A full year passed.
translation.kr: 일 년이라는 시간이 흘렀습니다.

translation.en: She led Theseus back up to the temple.
translation.kr: 그녀는 테세우스를 다시 신전으로 데려갔습니다.

translation.en: She told him to lift the stone, but he could not.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그에게 바위를 들어 올리라고 했지만, 그는 여전히 들 수 없었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: Then she sighed, and said the same words again, and went down, and came again the next year; but Theseus could not lift the stone then, nor the year after; and he longed to ask his mother the meaning of that stone, and what might lie underneath it; but her face was so sad that he had not the heart to ask.

translation.en: She sighed and repeated her words.
translation.kr: 그녀는 한숨을 쉬며 똑같은 말을 반복했습니다.

translation.en: They went home and returned the next year.
translation.kr: 그들은 집으로 돌아갔고 이듬해에 다시 찾아왔습니다.

translation.en: Theseus could not lift the stone that year, either.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그해에도 바위를 들어 올리지 못했습니다.

translation.en: He failed the year after that as well.
translation.kr: 그다음 해에도 마찬가지였습니다.

translation.en: He wanted to ask his mother about the stone.
translation.kr: 그는 어머니에게 그 바위에 대해 묻고 싶었습니다.

translation.en: He wondered what lay hidden beneath it.
translation.kr: 그는 바위 아래에 무엇이 숨겨져 있는지 궁금했습니다.

translation.en: But her face looked so sad that he could not ask.
translation.kr: 하지만 어머니의 표정이 너무 슬퍼 보여서 차마 물어볼 수가 없었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: So he said to himself, ‘The day shall surely come when I will lift that stone, though no man in Troezene can.’  And in order to grow strong he spent all his days in wrestling, and boxing, and hurling, and taming horses, and hunting the boar and the bull, and coursing goats and deer among the rocks; till upon all the mountains there was no hunter so swift as Theseus; and he killed Phaia the wild sow of Crommyon, which wasted all the land; till all the people said, ‘Surely the Gods are with the lad.’

translation.en: He made a promise to himself.
translation.kr: 그는 스스로에게 다짐했습니다.

translation.en: The day will come when I lift that stone.
translation.kr: 언젠가는 내가 저 바위를 들어 올릴 날이 올 것이다.

translation.en: I will do it even if no one else can.
translation.kr: 다른 사람은 못 하더라도 나는 해낼 것이다.

translation.en: He spent his days training to grow strong.
translation.kr: 그는 힘을 기르기 위해 매일같이 훈련했습니다.

translation.en: He wrestled, boxed, and practiced throwing.
translation.kr: 그는 레슬링과 권투를 하고 던지기를 연습했습니다.

translation.en: He tamed wild horses.
translation.kr: 그는 야생마를 길들였습니다.

translation.en: He hunted boars and bulls.
translation.kr: 그는 멧돼지와 황소를 사냥했습니다.

translation.en: He chased goats and deer across the rocky hills.
translation.kr: 그는 바위투성이 언덕을 가로지르며 염소와 사슴을 뒤쫓았습니다.

translation.en: Soon, he became the swiftest hunter on the mountains.
translation.kr: 머지않아 그는 산에서 가장 날랜 사냥꾼이 되었습니다.

translation.en: He even killed a giant wild sow that ruined the land.
translation.kr: 그는 땅을 황폐하게 만든 거대한 야생 암퇘지도 죽였습니다.

translation.en: The people marveled at his strength.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그의 힘에 경탄했습니다.

translation.en: They said the gods were truly with the boy.
translation.kr: 그들은 신들께서 진정으로 저 소년과 함께하신다고 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: And when his eighteenth year was past, Aithra led him up again to the temple, and said, ‘Theseus, lift the stone this day, or never know who you are.’  And Theseus went into the thicket, and stood over the stone, and tugged at it; and it moved.  Then his spirit swelled within him, and he said, ‘If I break my heart in my body, it shall up.’  And he tugged at it once more, and lifted it, and rolled it over with a shout.

translation.en: When he turned eighteen, Aithra brought him back.
translation.kr: 그가 열여덟 살이 되자, 아이트라는 다시 아들을 데려왔습니다.

translation.en: She told him to lift the stone today.
translation.kr: 그녀는 오늘 그 바위를 들어 올리라고 말했습니다.

translation.en: If you fail, you will never know who you truly are.
translation.kr: 실패한다면, 네가 진정 누구인지 영원히 알 수 없을 것이다.

translation.en: Theseus went into the thicket and stood over the stone.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 덤불 속으로 들어가 바위 위로 섰습니다.

translation.en: He pulled at it, and the rock finally moved.
translation.kr: 그가 끌어당기자 마침내 바위가 움직였습니다.

translation.en: His spirit swelled with fierce pride.
translation.kr: 그의 마음속에 강렬한 자부심이 차올랐습니다.

translation.en: I will lift it even if my heart bursts.
translation.kr: 내 심장이 터지는 한이 있더라도 반드시 들어 올릴 것이다.

translation.en: He pulled once more with all his might.
translation.kr: 그는 온 힘을 다해 다시 한번 끌어당겼습니다.

translation.en: He shouted as he lifted the stone and rolled it away.
translation.kr: 그는 고함을 지르며 바위를 들어 올려 굴려 버렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part I: How Theseus Lifted the Stone
paragraphs.raw: And when he looked beneath it, on the ground lay a sword of bronze, with a hilt of glittering gold, and by it a pair of golden sandals; and he caught them up, and burst through the bushes like a wild boar, and leapt to his mother, holding them high above his head.

translation.en: He looked beneath the heavy stone.
translation.kr: 그는 무거운 바위 아래를 내려다보았습니다.
