It is well for you that I met you, for my whole joy is to find strangers, and to feast them at my castle, and hear tales from them of foreign lands.  Come up with me, and eat the best of venison, and drink the rich red wine, and sleep upon my famous bed, of which all travellers say that they never saw the like.  For whatsoever the stature of my guest, however tall or short, that bed fits him to a hair, and he sleeps on it as he never slept before.’  And he laid hold on Theseus’ hands, and would not let him go.

translation.en: Alas! You have wandered far from the right path.
translation.kr: 이런! 길을 단단히 잘못 드셨구려.

translation.en: You cannot reach Aphidnai tonight, for miles of steep passes and dangerous cliffs lie ahead.
translation.kr: 가파른 고갯길과 위험한 절벽이 까마득히 이어져 있어 오늘 밤엔 아피드나이에 절대 닿지 못할 거요.

translation.en: It is a good thing I found you, for my greatest joy is feasting strangers in my castle and hearing their tales.
translation.kr: 나를 만난 게 참으로 다행이지 않소. 낯선 사람들을 성으로 데려가 잔치를 베풀고 그들의 모험담을 듣는 것이 내 유일한 낙이라오.

translation.en: Come with me to eat the best venison and drink rich red wine.
translation.kr: 나와 함께 가서 최고급 사슴고기를 맛보고 향긋한 붉은 포도주도 마시도록 합시다.

translation.en: You can sleep upon my famous bed, which travelers say is unlike any other.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 여행자들 사이에서 칭송이 자자한 내 특별한 침대에 누워 푹 쉬시구려.

translation.en: Whether a guest is tall or short, the bed fits him perfectly, giving him the best sleep of his life.
translation.kr: 키가 크든 작든 손님의 체격에 머리카락 하나 안 틀리고 딱 맞춘 듯해서 평생 처음 겪는 달콤한 잠을 선사한다오.

translation.en: The man grabbed Theseus by the hands and would not let him go.
translation.kr: 남자는 테세우스의 손을 부여잡고는 결코 놓아주려 하지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Theseus wished to go forwards: but he was ashamed to seem churlish to so hospitable a man; and he was curious to see that wondrous bed; and beside, he was hungry and weary: yet he shrank from the man, he knew not why; for, though his voice was gentle and fawning, it was dry and husky like a toad’s; and though his eyes were gentle, they were dull and cold like stones.  But he consented, and went with the man up a glen which led from the road toward the peaks of Parnes, under the dark shadow of the cliffs.

translation.en: Theseus wanted to keep moving, but he felt bad refusing such a welcoming host.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 계속 길을 재촉하고 싶었지만 이렇게 환대해 주는 사람에게 무례하게 굴기가 미안했습니다.

translation.en: He was also hungry, tired, and curious to see this wondrous bed.
translation.kr: 게다가 배도 고프고 몹시 지쳐 있던 터라 그 신기한 침대를 한번 보고 싶은 호기심도 생겼습니다.

translation.en: Still, something about the man made him hesitate.
translation.kr: 그럼에도 웬일인지 그 남자에게서 묘한 거부감이 느껴졌습니다.

translation.en: His voice was gentle but dry and husky like a toad, and his eyes were dull and cold as stone.
translation.kr: 그의 목소리는 부드럽고 상냥했지만 두꺼비처럼 건조하고 쇳소리가 났으며, 눈빛 또한 친절해 보이면서도 돌멩이처럼 탁하고 차가웠기 때문입니다.

translation.en: Finally, Theseus agreed and followed the man up a narrow valley toward the dark cliffs of Mount Parnes.
translation.kr: 결국 테세우스는 그를 따라 굽이진 길을 지나 파르네스의 산봉우리를 향해 드리워진 짙은 절벽 그림자 아래 좁은 골짜기로 들어섰습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And as they went up, the glen grew narrower, and the cliffs higher and darker, and beneath them a torrent roared, half seen between bare limestone crags.  And around there was neither tree nor bush, while from the white peaks of Parnes the snow-blasts swept down the glen, cutting and chilling till a horror fell on Theseus as he looked round at that doleful place.  And he asked at last, ‘Your castle stands, it seems, in a dreary region.’

translation.en: As they climbed, the valley grew narrower, and the cliffs loomed higher and darker.
translation.kr: 위로 올라갈수록 골짜기는 더욱 좁아지고 절벽은 한층 더 높고 어두컴컴해졌습니다.

translation.en: A roaring torrent flowed far below them through the bare limestone rocks.
translation.kr: 저 아래 앙상한 석회암 바위들 틈새로는 세찬 급류가 소리치며 흐르고 있었습니다.

translation.en: There were no trees or bushes, and freezing wind swept down from the snowy peaks.
translation.kr: 주변엔 나무 한 그루, 덤불 하나 찾아볼 수 없었고 하얗게 눈 덮인 산봉우리에서 불어온 매서운 눈보라가 골짜기를 할퀴듯 몰아쳤습니다.

translation.en: A sense of dread fell upon Theseus as he looked around the gloomy place.
translation.kr: 그 을씨년스러운 풍경을 둘러보던 테세우스의 마음에 왠지 모를 두려움이 엄습했습니다.

translation.en: He finally said, It seems your castle stands in a rather dreary region.
translation.kr: 결국 그가 입을 열어 댁의 성은 다소 음산한 곳에 자리 잡고 있군요 하고 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Yes; but once within it, hospitality makes all things cheerful.  But who are these?’ and he looked back, and Theseus also; and far below, along the road which they had left, came a string of laden asses, and merchants walking by them, watching their ware.

translation.en: Yes, but once inside, my hospitality makes everything cheerful.
translation.kr: 그렇긴 하지만 일단 성에 들어서서 대접을 받다 보면 모든 게 즐거워질 거요.

translation.en: But who are these people? the man asked, looking back.
translation.kr: 아니, 저 사람들은 누굴까? 하고 남자가 뒤를 돌아보며 물었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus looked down and saw merchants leading loaded donkeys along the road below.
translation.kr: 테세우스도 뒤를 돌아 저 멀리 아래쪽 길을 내려다보니 상인들이 물건을 잔뜩 짊어진 당나귀들을 줄지어 몰고 오고 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Ah, poor souls!’ said the stranger.  ‘Well for them that I looked back and saw them!  And well for me too, for I shall have the more guests at my feast.  Wait awhile till I go down and call them, and we will eat and drink together the livelong night.  Happy am I, to whom Heaven sends so many guests at once!’

translation.en: Ah, the poor souls! said the stranger.
translation.kr: 아, 가엾은 사람들! 하고 남자가 말했습니다.

translation.en: It is a good thing I looked back and saw them!
translation.kr: 내가 뒤를 돌아봐서 저들을 발견했으니 참으로 다행이오!

translation.en: It is good for me too, for I will have more guests at my feast.
translation.kr: 내 잔치에 손님이 더 늘게 되었으니 나에게도 좋은 일이지요.

translation.en: Wait here while I go down and call them, so we can all eat and drink together tonight.
translation.kr: 내가 내려가 저들을 데려올 테니 여기서 잠시만 기다리시오, 그러면 밤새도록 다 함께 먹고 마실 수 있을 거요.

translation.en: I am so lucky that heaven has sent me all these guests at once!
translation.kr: 하늘이 이렇게 한꺼번에 많은 손님을 보내 주시다니 나는 정말 운이 좋은 사람이오!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And he ran back down the hill, waving his hand and shouting, to the merchants, while Theseus went slowly up the steep pass.

translation.en: He ran back down the hill, waving his hand and shouting to the merchants.
translation.kr: 그는 언덕 아래로 달려 내려가 상인들을 향해 손을 흔들며 크게 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, Theseus continued slowly up the steep mountain pass.
translation.kr: 그사이 테세우스는 가파른 산길을 따라 천천히 걸어 올라갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: But as he went up he met an aged man, who had been gathering drift-wood in the torrent-bed.  He had laid down his faggot in the road, and was trying to lift it again to his shoulder.  And when he saw Theseus, he called to him, and said—

translation.en: As he climbed, he met an old man who had been gathering firewood from the riverbed.
translation.kr: 계속 걸어 올라가던 그는 강바닥에서 땔감을 줍고 있던 한 노인과 마주쳤습니다.

translation.en: The man had set his bundle down and was struggling to lift it back onto his shoulder.
translation.kr: 노인은 장작단을 길바닥에 내려놓고 다시 어깨에 짊어지려고 몹시 쩔쩔매고 있었습니다.

translation.en: When he saw Theseus, he called out to him.
translation.kr: 테세우스를 본 그가 소리쳐 불렀습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘O fair youth, help me up with my burden, for my limbs are stiff and weak with years.’

translation.en: Young man, please help me lift my burden.
translation.kr: 젊은이, 이 짐을 올리는 것 좀 도와주구려.

translation.en: My limbs are stiff and weak with age.
translation.kr: 나이가 들어 팔다리가 뻣뻣하고 기운이 하나도 없어서 그렇소.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus lifted the burden on his back.  And the old man blest him, and then looked earnestly upon him, and said—

translation.en: Theseus lifted the burden onto his back.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 짐을 등 위로 들어 올렸습니다.

translation.en: The old man blessed him, looked earnestly at him, and spoke.
translation.kr: 노인은 그를 축복하고 진지하게 바라보며 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Who are you, fair youth, and wherefore travel you this doleful road?’

translation.en: Who are you, fair youth, and why do you travel this sorrowful road?
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 누구이며 왜 이 슬픈 길을 여행하고 있습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Who I am my parents know; but I travel this doleful road because I have been invited by a hospitable man, who promises to feast me, and to make me sleep upon I know not what wondrous bed.’

translation.en: My parents know who I am.
translation.kr: 제 부모님은 제가 누구인지 알고 계십니다.

translation.en: But I travel this sad road because a hospitable man invited me.
translation.kr: 하지만 어떤 친절한 남자가 저를 초대했기 때문에 이 슬픈 길을 여행하고 있습니다.

translation.en: He promised to feast me and let me sleep on some wondrous bed.
translation.kr: 그는 저를 대접하고 어떤 놀라운 침대에서 재워주겠다고 약속했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then the old man clapped his hands together and cried—

translation.en: The old man clapped his hands together and cried out.
translation.kr: 그러자 노인은 두 손을 마주치며 소리쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘O house of Hades, man-devouring! will thy maw never be full?  Know, fair youth, that you are going to torment and to death, for he who met you (I will requite your kindness by another) is a robber and a murderer of men. Whatsoever stranger he meets he entices him hither to death; and as for this bed of which he speaks, truly it fits all comers, yet none ever rose alive off it save me.’

translation.en: Oh, man-devouring house of Hades!
translation.kr: 아, 사람을 집어삼키는 하데스의 집이여!

translation.en: Will your stomach never be full?
translation.kr: 당신의 배는 영원히 채워지지 않을 것입니까?

translation.en: Know this, fair youth, you are heading to torment and death.
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 고통과 죽음을 향해 가고 있다는 것을 아십시오.

translation.en: I will return your kindness by warning you.
translation.kr: 당신의 친절에 보답하기 위해 경고하겠습니다.

translation.en: The man who met you is a robber and a murderer.
translation.kr: 당신이 만난 남자는 강도이자 살인마입니다.

translation.en: He entices every stranger he meets here to their death.
translation.kr: 그는 만나는 모든 낯선 사람들을 이곳으로 유인하여 죽입니다.

translation.en: As for that bed he speaks of, it truly fits all comers.
translation.kr: 그가 말하는 그 침대는 모든 방문객에게 딱 맞습니다.

translation.en: Yet no one has ever risen alive from it except me.
translation.kr: 하지만 나를 제외하고는 아무도 그곳에서 살아서 일어난 적이 없습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Why?’ asked Theseus, astonished.

translation.en: Why? asked Theseus, astonished.
translation.kr: 왜입니까? 테세우스가 깜짝 놀라 물었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Because, if a man be too tall for it, he lops his limbs till they be short enough, and if he be too short, he stretches his limbs till they be long enough: but me only he spared, seven weary years agone; for I alone of all fitted his bed exactly, so he spared me, and made me his slave. And once I was a wealthy merchant, and dwelt in brazen-gated Thebes; but now I hew wood and draw water for him, the torment of all mortal men.’

translation.en: If a man is too tall for it, he chops off his limbs until they are short enough.
translation.kr: 만약 사람이 너무 크면 그는 다리가 짧아질 때까지 잘라냅니다.

translation.en: If he is too short, he stretches his limbs until they are long enough.
translation.kr: 만약 너무 작으면 다리가 길어질 때까지 늘립니다.

translation.en: He only spared me seven weary years ago.
translation.kr: 그는 7년 전 힘들었던 때에 나만을 살려주었습니다.

translation.en: I alone perfectly fitted his bed, so he made me his slave.
translation.kr: 나만이 유일하게 그의 침대에 딱 맞았고 그래서 그는 나를 노예로 삼았습니다.

translation.en: I was once a wealthy merchant living in brazen-gated Thebes.
translation.kr: 저는 한때 청동 문이 있는 테베에 살던 부유한 상인이었습니다.

translation.en: But now I chop wood and draw water for this tormentor of all mortal men.
translation.kr: 하지만 지금은 모든 인간을 괴롭히는 그를 위해 장작을 패고 물을 긷고 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus said nothing; but he ground his teeth together.

translation.en: Theseus said nothing, but he ground his teeth together.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 아무 말도 하지 않았지만 이를 갈았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Escape, then,’ said the old man, ‘for he will have no pity on thy youth. But yesterday he brought up hither a young man and a maiden, and fitted them upon his bed; and the young man’s hands and feet he cut off, but the maiden’s limbs he stretched until she died, and so both perished miserably—but I am tired of weeping over the slain.  And therefore he is called Procrustes the stretcher, though his father called him Damastes. Flee from him: yet whither will you flee?  The cliffs are steep, and who can climb them? and there is no other road.’

translation.en: Escape, then, said the old man.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 도망치십시오, 노인이 말했습니다.

translation.en: He will have no pity on your youth.
translation.kr: 그는 당신의 젊음을 불쌍히 여기지 않을 것입니다.

translation.en: Just yesterday he brought a young man and a maiden here.
translation.kr: 바로 어제 그는 젊은 남자와 처녀를 이곳으로 데려왔습니다.

translation.en: He fitted them upon his bed.
translation.kr: 그는 그들을 침대에 맞추었습니다.

translation.en: He cut off the young man's hands and feet.
translation.kr: 그는 젊은 남자의 손과 발을 잘랐습니다.

translation.en: He stretched the maiden's limbs until she died.
translation.kr: 그는 처녀가 죽을 때까지 팔다리를 늘렸습니다.

translation.en: So both perished miserably.
translation.kr: 그래서 두 사람 모두 비참하게 죽고 말았습니다.

translation.en: I am so tired of weeping over the slain.
translation.kr: 살해당한 사람들을 위해 우는 것도 이제 지쳤습니다.

translation.en: That is why he is called Procrustes the stretcher.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 늘리는 자 프로크루스테스라고 불립니다.

translation.en: His father originally named him Damastes.
translation.kr: 그의 아버지는 원래 그를 다마스테스라고 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Flee from him, yet where will you go?
translation.kr: 그에게서 도망치십시오, 하지만 어디로 가시겠습니까?

translation.en: The cliffs are steep, and no one can climb them.
translation.kr: 절벽은 가파르고 아무도 오를 수 없습니다.

translation.en: There is no other road.
translation.kr: 다른 길은 없습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: But Theseus laid his hand upon the old man’s month, and said, ‘There is no need to flee;’ and he turned to go down the pass.

translation.en: But Theseus covered the old man's mouth with his hand.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 노인의 입을 손으로 막았습니다.

translation.en: There is no need to flee, he said.
translation.kr: 도망칠 필요가 없습니다, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: He then turned to head down the pass.
translation.kr: 그러고는 고개를 돌려 길을 따라 내려갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Do not tell him that I have warned you, or he will kill me by some evil death;’ and the old man screamed after him down the glen; but Theseus strode on in his wrath.

translation.en: Do not tell him that I have warned you, or he will kill me brutally!
translation.kr: 제가 경고했다고 그에게 말하지 마십시오, 아니면 저를 잔인하게 죽일 것입니다!

translation.en: The old man screamed after him down the glen.
translation.kr: 노인은 계곡 아래로 가는 그를 향해 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus strode on in his wrath.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 분노에 차 성큼성큼 걸어갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And he said to himself, ‘This is an ill-ruled land; when shall I have done ridding it of monsters?’  And as he spoke, Procrustes came up the hill, and all the merchants with him, smiling and talking gaily.  And when he saw Theseus, he cried, ‘Ah, fair young guest, have I kept you too long waiting?’

translation.en: He said to himself, this is a poorly ruled land.
translation.kr: 그는 속으로 이 땅은 통치가 엉망이라고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: When will I finish ridding it of monsters?
translation.kr: 언제쯤 이 괴물들을 다 없앨 수 있을까?

translation.en: As he spoke, Procrustes came up the hill.
translation.kr: 그가 말할 때 프로크루스테스가 언덕을 올라왔습니다.

translation.en: He had merchants with him, all smiling and chatting happily.
translation.kr: 그는 상인들과 함께 모두 웃으며 즐겁게 이야기하고 있었습니다.

translation.en: When he saw Theseus, he cried out.
translation.kr: 그는 테세우스를 보자마자 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Ah, fair young guest, have I kept you waiting too long?
translation.kr: 아, 아름다운 젊은 손님이여, 제가 너무 오래 기다리게 했습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: But Theseus answered, ‘The man who stretches his guests upon a bed and hews off their hands and feet, what shall be done to him, when right is done throughout the land?’

translation.en: But Theseus answered him directly.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그에게 단도직입적으로 대답했습니다.

translation.en: When justice rules the land, what should be done to a man like you?
translation.kr: 정의가 온 땅을 지배할 때 당신 같은 사람은 어떻게 되어야 합니까?

translation.en: You stretch your guests on a bed and chop off their limbs.
translation.kr: 손님들을 침대에 눕혀 팔다리를 잘라버리는 자 말입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Procrustes’ countenance changed, and his cheeks grew as green as a lizard, and he felt for his sword in haste; but Theseus leapt on him, and cried—

translation.en: Procrustes' expression immediately changed.
translation.kr: 프로크루스테스의 표정이 즉시 바뀌었습니다.

translation.en: His cheeks turned as green as a lizard.
translation.kr: 그의 뺨은 도마뱀처럼 초록색으로 변했습니다.

translation.en: He hastily reached for his sword.
translation.kr: 그는 서둘러 칼을 찾았습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus leaped onto him and shouted.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그에게 달려들며 소리쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Is this true, my host, or is it false?’ and he clasped Procrustes round waist and elbow, so that he could not draw his sword.

translation.en: Is this true, my host, or is it false?
translation.kr: 이것이 사실입니까, 나의 주인이여, 아니면 거짓입니까?

translation.en: He grabbed Procrustes tightly by the waist and elbow.
translation.kr: 그는 프로크루스테스의 허리와 팔꿈치를 단단히 붙잡았습니다.

translation.en: This trapped him so he could not draw his sword.
translation.kr: 그렇게 그를 묶어두어 칼을 뽑을 수 없게 만들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Is this true, my host, or is it false?’  But Procrustes answered never a word.

translation.en: Is this true, my host, or is it false?
translation.kr: 이것이 사실입니까, 나의 주인이여, 아니면 거짓입니까?

translation.en: But Procrustes did not answer a single word.
translation.kr: 하지만 프로크루스테스는 단 한마디도 대답하지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus flung him from him, and lifted up his dreadful club; and before Procrustes could strike him he had struck, and felled him to the ground.

translation.en: Theseus flung him away and raised his dreadful club.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그를 내동댕이치고 무시무시한 곤봉을 치켜들었습니다.

translation.en: Before Procrustes could strike, Theseus swung first.
translation.kr: 프로크루스테스가 공격하기도 전에 테세우스가 먼저 휘둘렀습니다.

translation.en: The blow sent him crashing to the ground.
translation.kr: 그 일격에 그는 땅에 쓰러졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And once again he struck him; and his evil soul fled forth, and went down to Hades squeaking, like a bat into the darkness of a cave.

translation.en: He struck him once more.
translation.kr: 그는 그를 한 번 더 때렸습니다.

translation.en: His evil soul fled from his body.
translation.kr: 그의 사악한 영혼이 몸에서 빠져나갔습니다.

translation.en: It squeaked like a bat disappearing into a dark cave.
translation.kr: 마치 어두운 동굴로 사라지는 박쥐처럼 찍찍거리며 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: Then it descended into the realm of Hades.
translation.kr: 그러고는 하데스의 영역으로 내려갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus stript him of his gold ornaments, and went up to his house, and found there great wealth and treasure, which he had stolen from the passers-by.  And he called the people of the country, whom Procrustes had spoiled a long time, and parted the spoil among them, and went down the mountains, and away.

translation.en: Theseus stripped him of his gold ornaments.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그의 금 장신구를 벗겨냈습니다.

translation.en: He went up to his house and found vast wealth and treasure.
translation.kr: 그는 그의 집으로 올라가 엄청난 부와 보물을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: It had all been stolen from passing travelers.
translation.kr: 그것들은 모두 지나가는 여행객들에게서 훔친 것이었습니다.

translation.en: He summoned the local people whom Procrustes had long oppressed.
translation.kr: 그는 오랫동안 프로크루스테스에게 억압받던 지역 사람들을 불렀습니다.

translation.en: He divided the spoils among them.
translation.kr: 그는 그들에게 전리품을 나누어 주었습니다.

translation.en: Then he traveled down the mountains and moved on.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 그는 산을 내려가 길을 떠났습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And he went down the glens of Parnes, through mist, and cloud, and rain, down the slopes of oak, and lentisk, and arbutus, and fragrant bay, till he came to the Vale of Cephisus, and the pleasant town of Aphidnai, and the home of the Phytalid heroes, where they dwelt beneath a mighty elm.

translation.en: He hiked down the glens of Mount Parnes.
translation.kr: 그는 파르네스 산의 계곡을 따라 걸어 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He passed through mist, cloud, and heavy rain.
translation.kr: 그는 안개와 구름, 그리고 쏟아지는 비를 뚫고 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: He descended slopes covered in oak, mastic, and fragrant bay trees.
translation.kr: 그는 참나무와 매스틱, 향기로운 월계수가 덮인 비탈을 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he reached the Vale of Cephisus.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 케피소스 계곡에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: He found the pleasant town of Aphidnai.
translation.kr: 그는 아름다운 마을 아피드나이를 발견했습니다.

translation.en: There stood the home of the Phytalid heroes.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 피탈리드 영웅들의 집이 있었습니다.

translation.en: They lived peacefully beneath a massive elm tree.
translation.kr: 그들은 거대한 느릅나무 아래에서 평화롭게 살고 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And there they built an altar, and bade him bathe in Cephisus, and offer a yearling ram, and purified him from the blood of Sinis, and sent him away in peace.

translation.en: The heroes built an altar for him.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 그를 위해 제단을 쌓았습니다.

translation.en: They told him to bathe in the Cephisus river.
translation.kr: 그들은 그에게 케피소스 강에서 목욕하라고 말했습니다.

translation.en: He offered a yearling ram as a sacrifice.
translation.kr: 그는 1년 된 숫양을 제물로 바쳤습니다.

translation.en: They purified him from the bloodshed of Sinis.
translation.kr: 그들은 시니스를 죽인 피에서 그를 정화해주었습니다.

translation.en: Then they sent him on his way in peace.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 그를 평화롭게 떠나보냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And he went down the valley by Acharnai, and by the silver-swirling stream, while all the people blessed him, for the fame of his prowess had spread wide, till he saw the plain of Athens, and the hill where Athené dwells.

translation.en: He traveled down the valley near Acharnai.
translation.kr: 그는 아카르나이 근처의 계곡을 따라 여행했습니다.

translation.en: He walked alongside the silver-swirling stream.
translation.kr: 그는 은빛으로 소용돌이치는 냇물을 따라 걸었습니다.

translation.en: All the people blessed him along the way.
translation.kr: 모든 사람들이 길을 지나는 그를 축복했습니다.

translation.en: The fame of his incredible prowess had already spread far.
translation.kr: 그의 놀라운 용맹함에 대한 명성이 이미 멀리 퍼져 있었습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, he saw the great plain of Athens.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 거대한 아테네 평원을 보았습니다.

translation.en: He gazed upon the holy hill where Athena dwells.
translation.kr: 그는 아테나 여신이 머무는 신성한 언덕을 바라보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: So Theseus went up through Athens, and all the people ran out to see him; for his fame had gone before him and every one knew of his mighty deeds. And all cried, ‘Here comes the hero who slew Sinis, and Phaia the wild sow of Crommyon, and conquered Kerkuon in wrestling, and slew Procrustes the pitiless.’  But Theseus went on sadly and steadfastly, for his heart yearned after his father; and he said, ‘How shall I deliver him from these leeches who suck his blood?’

translation.en: Theseus made his way up through Athens.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 아테네를 향해 걸어 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: The people ran out to see him, as his fame preceded him.
translation.kr: 그의 명성이 먼저 퍼져 사람들은 그를 보려고 달려나왔습니다.

translation.en: Everyone knew of his mighty deeds.
translation.kr: 모두가 그의 위대한 업적을 알고 있었습니다.

translation.en: They cried out, here comes the great hero!
translation.kr: 그들은 위대한 영웅이 오셨다며 소리쳤습니다!

translation.en: He slew Sinis and the wild sow of Crommyon.
translation.kr: 그는 시니스와 크로미온의 야생 암돼지를 죽였습니다.

translation.en: He defeated Kerkuon in wrestling and struck down pitiless Procrustes.
translation.kr: 그는 레슬링에서 케르키온을 물리쳤고 무자비한 프로크루스테스를 쓰러뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus kept walking sadly and steadfastly.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 슬프고도 확고하게 계속 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: His heart deeply yearned for his father.
translation.kr: 그의 마음은 아버지를 간절히 그리워했습니다.

translation.en: How will I save him from these leeches sucking his blood?
translation.kr: 그의 피를 빠는 거머리 같은 자들로부터 어떻게 그를 구할 수 있을까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: So he went up the holy stairs, and into the Acropolis, where Ægeus’ palace stood; and he went straight into Ægeus’ hall, and stood upon the threshold, and looked round.

translation.en: He climbed the holy stairs into the Acropolis.
translation.kr: 그는 신성한 계단을 올라 아크로폴리스로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: This was where the palace of King Aegeus stood.
translation.kr: 그곳은 아이게우스 왕의 궁전이 있는 곳이었습니다.

translation.en: He walked straight into the main hall.
translation.kr: 그는 대연회장으로 곧장 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: He stood upon the threshold and looked around.
translation.kr: 그는 문지방에 서서 주위를 둘러보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And there he saw his cousins sitting about the table at the wine: many a son of Pallas, but no Ægeus among them.  There they sat and feasted, and laughed, and passed the wine-cup round; while harpers harped, and slave-girls sang, and the tumblers showed their tricks.

translation.en: He saw his cousins sitting around the table drinking wine.
translation.kr: 그는 사촌들이 탁자에 둘러앉아 포도주를 마시는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Many sons of Pallas were present, but Aegeus was nowhere to be found.
translation.kr: 팔라스의 아들들은 많았지만 아이게우스는 어디에도 없었습니다.

translation.en: They feasted, laughed, and passed the wine cup around.
translation.kr: 그들은 포식을 하고 웃으며 포도주 잔을 돌렸습니다.

translation.en: Musicians played their harps while slave girls sang.
translation.kr: 노예 소녀들이 노래하는 동안 악사들은 하프를 연주했습니다.

translation.en: Acrobats showed off their tumbling tricks for the crowd.
translation.kr: 곡예사들은 무리를 위해 구르기 묘기를 선보였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Loud laughed the sons of Pallas, and fast went the wine-cup round; but Theseus frowned, and said under his breath, ‘No wonder that the land is full of robbers, while such as these bear rule.’

translation.en: The sons of Pallas laughed loudly.
translation.kr: 팔라스의 아들들은 크게 웃었습니다.

translation.en: The wine cup passed quickly from hand to hand.
translation.kr: 포도주 잔이 빠르게 이 손에서 저 손으로 넘어갔습니다.

translation.en: Theseus frowned and muttered under his breath.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 얼굴을 찌푸리며 낮은 목소리로 중얼거렸습니다.

translation.en: No wonder the land is full of robbers when fools like these rule.
translation.kr: 이런 바보들이 통치하니 나라에 도둑이 넘쳐나는 것도 당연하지.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then the Pallantids saw him, and called to him, half-drunk with wine, ‘Holla, tall stranger at the door, what is your will to-day?’

translation.en: The sons of Pallas noticed him standing there.
translation.kr: 팔라스의 아들들은 그곳에 서 있는 그를 알아차렸습니다.

translation.en: Half-drunk with wine, they called out to him.
translation.kr: 포도주에 반쯤 취한 그들이 그에게 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Hey, tall stranger at the door, what do you want today?
translation.kr: 이봐, 문에 서 있는 키 큰 이방인, 오늘은 무슨 일로 왔나?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘I come hither to ask for hospitality.’

translation.en: I have come here to ask for hospitality.
translation.kr: 저는 환대를 청하러 이곳에 왔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Then take it, and welcome.  You look like a hero and a bold warrior; and we like such to drink with us.’

translation.en: Then take it, and welcome.
translation.kr: 그럼 어서 오십시오.

translation.en: You look like a hero and a bold warrior.
translation.kr: 당신은 영웅이자 용감한 전사처럼 보입니다.

translation.en: We like such men to drink with us.
translation.kr: 우리는 그런 분들과 함께 술을 마시는 것을 좋아합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘I ask no hospitality of you; I ask it of Ægeus the king, the master of this house.’

translation.en: I ask no hospitality of you.
translation.kr: 저는 당신들에게 환대를 청하는 것이 아닙니다.

translation.en: I ask it of King Aegeus, the master of this house.
translation.kr: 저는 이 집의 주인이신 아이게우스 왕께 청하는 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: At that some growled, and some laughed, and shouted, ‘Heyday! we are all masters here.’

translation.en: At that, some men growled while others laughed.
translation.kr: 그 말에 어떤 남자들은 으르렁거렸고 다른 남자들은 웃음을 터뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: Hey, we are all masters here!
translation.kr: 이보시오, 우리는 모두 이곳의 주인입니다!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Then I am master as much as the rest of you,’ said Theseus, and he strode past the table up the hall, and looked around for Ægeus; but he was nowhere to be seen.

translation.en: Then I am as much a master as the rest of you.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 저 역시 여러분 못지않은 주인입니다.

translation.en: Theseus strode past the table up the hall.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 탁자를 지나 홀 위쪽으로 성큼성큼 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: He looked around for Aegeus, but the king was nowhere to be seen.
translation.kr: 그는 아이게우스를 찾기 위해 주변을 둘러보았지만 왕은 어디에도 보이지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: The Pallantids looked at him, and then at each other, and each whispered to the man next him, ‘This is a forward fellow; he ought to be thrust out at the door.’  But each man’s neighbour whispered in return, ‘His shoulders are broad; will you rise and put him out?’  So they all sat still where they were.

translation.en: The Pallantids looked at him and then at each other.
translation.kr: 팔란티드 무리는 그를 쳐다보더니 이내 서로를 마주 보았습니다.

translation.en: Each whispered to the man next to him.
translation.kr: 각자 옆에 앉은 사람에게 속삭였습니다.

translation.en: This is a forward fellow.
translation.kr: 정말 건방진 녀석입니다.

translation.en: He ought to be thrust out the door.
translation.kr: 당장 문밖으로 쫓아내야 합니다.

translation.en: But each man's neighbor whispered in return.
translation.kr: 하지만 옆에 앉은 사람들은 각자 이렇게 속삭이며 대답했습니다.

translation.en: His shoulders are very broad.
translation.kr: 저 자의 어깨는 매우 넓습니다.

translation.en: Will you rise and put him out?
translation.kr: 당신이 일어나서 그를 내쫓으시겠습니까?

translation.en: So they all sat still exactly where they were.
translation.kr: 그래서 그들은 모두 있던 자리에 가만히 앉아 있었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus called to the servants, and said, ‘Go tell King Ægeus, your master, that Theseus of Troezene is here, and asks to be his guest awhile.’

translation.en: Theseus then called to the servants.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 테세우스는 하인들을 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Go tell King Aegeus, your master, that Theseus of Troezen is here.
translation.kr: 여러분의 주인이신 아이게우스 왕께 트로이젠의 테세우스가 왔다고 전하십시오.

translation.en: Tell him I ask to be his guest for a while.
translation.kr: 제가 잠시 그의 손님이 되기를 청한다고 말씀해 주십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: A servant ran and told Ægeus, where he sat in his chamber within, by Medeia the dark witch-woman, watching her eye and hand.  And when Ægeus heard of Troezene he turned pale and red again, and rose from his seat trembling, while Medeia watched him like a snake.

translation.en: A servant ran and told Aegeus.
translation.kr: 한 하인이 달려가 아이게우스에게 알렸습니다.

translation.en: The king sat in his inner chamber beside Medea, the dark witch.
translation.kr: 왕은 어둠의 마녀 메데아 옆 내실에 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: He was carefully watching her eyes and hands.
translation.kr: 그는 그녀의 눈과 손을 유심히 지켜보고 있었습니다.

translation.en: When Aegeus heard of Troezen, he turned pale and then red again.
translation.kr: 트로이젠에 대해 듣자 아이게우스는 창백해졌다가 이내 다시 붉어졌습니다.

translation.en: He rose from his seat trembling, while Medea watched him like a snake.
translation.kr: 그가 떨면서 자리에서 일어나자, 메데아는 뱀처럼 그를 쳐다보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘What is Troezene to you?’ she asked.  But he said hastily, ‘Do you not know who this Theseus is?  The hero who has cleared the country from all monsters; but that he came from Troezene, I never heard before.  I must go out and welcome him.’

translation.en: What is Troezen to you?
translation.kr: 트로이젠이 당신과 무슨 상관이 있습니까?

translation.en: He replied hastily.
translation.kr: 그는 서둘러 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Do you not know who this Theseus is?
translation.kr: 이 테세우스가 누구인지 모른단 말입니까?

translation.en: He is the hero who has cleared the country of all monsters.
translation.kr: 그는 이 나라의 모든 괴물을 물리친 영웅입니다.

translation.en: But I never heard before that he came from Troezen.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 트로이젠 출신이라는 것은 전에 들어본 적이 없습니다.

translation.en: I must go out and welcome him.
translation.kr: 나는 나가서 그를 맞이해야 합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: So Ægeus came out into the hall; and when Theseus saw him, his heart leapt into his mouth, and he longed to fall on his neck and welcome him; but he controlled himself, and said, ‘My father may not wish for me, after all.  I will try him before I discover myself;’ and he bowed low before Ægeus, and said, ‘I have delivered the king’s realm from many monsters; therefore I am come to ask a reward of the king.’

translation.en: So Aegeus came out into the hall.
translation.kr: 그래서 아이게우스는 홀로 나왔습니다.

translation.en: When Theseus saw him, his heart leaped into his throat.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그를 보자 가슴이 철렁 내려앉았습니다.

translation.en: He longed to fall on his neck and welcome him.
translation.kr: 그는 아버지의 목을 끌어안고 환영하고 싶었습니다.

translation.en: But he controlled himself with a sudden thought.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 문득 든 생각에 스스로를 통제했습니다.

translation.en: My father may not wish for me after all.
translation.kr: 아버지는 결국 나를 원하지 않으실지도 모릅니다.

translation.en: I will test him before I reveal myself.
translation.kr: 정체를 밝히기 전에 아버지를 시험해 보겠습니다.

translation.en: He bowed low before Aegeus.
translation.kr: 그는 아이게우스 앞에서 허리를 깊이 숙여 인사했습니다.

translation.en: I have delivered the king's realm from many monsters.
translation.kr: 저는 왕의 영토를 많은 괴물들로부터 구했습니다.

translation.en: Therefore I have come to ask a reward from the king.
translation.kr: 그러므로 저는 왕께 보상을 청하러 왔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And old Ægeus looked on him, and loved him, as what fond heart would not have done?  But he only sighed, and said—

translation.en: Old Aegeus looked at him and instantly loved him.
translation.kr: 늙은 아이게우스는 그를 바라보았고 단번에 그를 사랑하게 되었습니다.

translation.en: What fond heart would not have done the same?
translation.kr: 어떤 다정한 마음이라도 그렇게 하지 않을 수 있었겠습니까?

translation.en: But he only sighed and spoke.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 단지 한숨을 쉬며 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘It is little that I can give you, noble lad, and nothing that is worthy of you; for surely you are no mortal man, or at least no mortal’s son.’

translation.en: It is very little that I can give you, noble lad.
translation.kr: 고귀한 젊은이여, 내가 당신에게 줄 수 있는 것은 아주 적습니다.

translation.en: I have nothing that is truly worthy of you.
translation.kr: 진정으로 당신에게 어울리는 것은 아무것도 없습니다.

translation.en: Surely you are no mortal man, or at least no mortal's son.
translation.kr: 당신은 분명 평범한 인간이 아니거나 적어도 필멸자의 아들이 아닐 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘All I ask,’ said Theseus, ‘is to eat and drink at your table.’

translation.en: All I ask is to eat and drink at your table.
translation.kr: 제가 바라는 것은 오직 당신의 식탁에서 먹고 마시는 것뿐입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘That I can give you,’ said Ægeus, ‘if at least I am master in my own hall.’

translation.en: That I can give you.
translation.kr: 그것이라면 내어줄 수 있습니다.

translation.en: I can do so if at least I am still master in my own hall.
translation.kr: 적어도 내 식탁에서 내가 여전히 주인이라면 그렇게 할 수 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then he bade them put a seat for Theseus, and set before him the best of the feast; and Theseus sat and ate so much, that all the company wondered at him: but always he kept his club by his side.

translation.en: Then he ordered his servants to prepare a seat for Theseus.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 그는 하인들에게 테세우스의 자리를 마련하라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: He set the best of the feast before the young hero.
translation.kr: 그는 젊은 영웅 앞에 최고의 잔칫상을 차렸습니다.

translation.en: Theseus sat and ate a massive amount of food.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 자리에 앉아 엄청난 양의 음식을 먹었습니다.

translation.en: All the company wondered at his great appetite.
translation.kr: 모든 일행이 그의 엄청난 식욕에 놀랐습니다.

translation.en: But he always kept his club close by his side.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 항상 곤봉을 자기 곁에 바싹 붙여 두었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: But Medeia the dark witch-woman had been watching him all the while.  She saw how Ægeus turned red and pale when the lad said that he came from Troezene.  She saw, too, how his heart was opened toward Theseus; and how Theseus bore himself before all the sons of Pallas, like a lion among a pack of curs.  And she said to herself, ‘This youth will be master here; perhaps he is nearer to Ægeus already than mere fancy.  At least the Pallantilds will have no chance by the side of such as he.’

translation.en: But Medea the dark witch had been watching him all the while.
translation.kr: 하지만 어둠의 마녀 메데아는 그동안 내내 그를 지켜보고 있었습니다.

translation.en: She saw how Aegeus turned red and pale at the mention of Troezen.
translation.kr: 그녀는 트로이젠이라는 말에 아이게우스가 붉어지고 창백해지는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: She also saw how his heart was opened toward Theseus.
translation.kr: 그녀는 또한 그의 마음이 테세우스를 향해 어떻게 열렸는지도 보았습니다.

translation.en: Theseus bore himself like a lion among a pack of curs.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 들개 무리 속의 사자처럼 처신했습니다.

translation.en: She spoke silently to herself.
translation.kr: 그녀는 속으로 조용히 혼잣말을 했습니다.

translation.en: This youth will soon be the master here.
translation.kr: 이 젊은이가 곧 이곳의 주인이 될 것이다.

translation.en: Perhaps he is already closer to Aegeus than mere imagination suggests.
translation.kr: 어쩌면 그는 단순한 상상 이상으로 아이게우스와 가까운 사이일지도 모른다.

translation.en: The Pallantids will have no chance against such a man.
translation.kr: 팔란티드 무리는 이런 남자 앞에서는 가망이 없을 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then she went back into her chamber modestly, while Theseus ate and drank; and all the servants whispered, ‘This, then, is the man who killed the monsters!  How noble are his looks, and how huge his size!  Ah, would that he were our master’s son!’

translation.en: Then she went back into her chamber modestly.
translation.kr: 그런 다음 그녀는 조신하게 자신의 방으로 돌아갔습니다.

translation.en: Theseus continued to eat and drink.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 계속해서 먹고 마셨습니다.

translation.en: All the servants whispered among themselves.
translation.kr: 모든 하인들이 그들끼리 속삭였습니다.

translation.en: This is the man who killed the monsters!
translation.kr: 이 사람이 바로 그 괴물들을 죽인 사람입니다!

translation.en: How noble are his looks, and how huge his size!
translation.kr: 그의 외모는 얼마나 고귀하고, 체구는 얼마나 거대한지!

translation.en: I wish he were our master's son!
translation.kr: 그가 우리 주인의 아들이었으면 좋겠습니다!

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: But presently Medeia came forth, decked in all her jewels, and her rich Eastern robes, and looking more beautiful than the day, so that all the guests could look at nothing else.  And in her right hand she held a golden cup, and in her left a flask of gold; and she came up to Theseus, and spoke in a sweet, soft, winning voice—

translation.en: Presently Medea came forth, decked in all her jewels.
translation.kr: 이윽고 메데아가 온갖 보석으로 치장하고 나왔습니다.

translation.en: She wore her rich Eastern robes and looked more beautiful than the day.
translation.kr: 그녀는 화려한 동방의 예복을 입었고 대낮보다 더 아름다워 보였습니다.

translation.en: All the guests could look at nothing else.
translation.kr: 모든 손님들은 다른 것은 전혀 쳐다볼 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: She held a golden cup in her right hand and a golden flask in her left.
translation.kr: 그녀는 오른손에는 황금 잔을, 왼손에는 황금 물병을 들고 있었습니다.

translation.en: She came up to Theseus and spoke in a sweet, winning voice.
translation.kr: 그녀는 테세우스에게 다가가 달콤하고 매혹적인 목소리로 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Hail to the hero, the conqueror, the unconquered, the destroyer of all evil things!  Drink, hero, of my charmed cup, which gives rest after every toil, which heals all wounds, and pours new life into the veins. Drink of my cup, for in it sparkles the wine of the East, and Nepenthe, the comfort of the Immortals.’

translation.en: Hail to the hero, the conqueror, and the unconquered!
translation.kr: 영웅이자 정복자이며 결코 굴복하지 않는 자에게 경배를 표합니다!

translation.en: Hail to the destroyer of all evil things!
translation.kr: 모든 사악한 것들의 파괴자에게 경배를 표합니다!

translation.en: Drink, hero, of my charmed cup.
translation.kr: 영웅이여, 나의 매혹적인 잔을 마시십시오.

translation.en: It gives rest after every toil and heals all wounds.
translation.kr: 이것은 모든 수고 뒤에 안식을 주고 모든 상처를 치유해 줍니다.

translation.en: It pours new life into the veins.
translation.kr: 그것은 핏줄 속에 새로운 생명을 불어넣어 줍니다.

translation.en: Drink of my cup, for in it sparkles the wine of the East.
translation.kr: 내 잔을 마시십시오, 그 안에는 동방의 포도주가 반짝이고 있으니까요.

translation.en: It contains Nepenthe, the comfort of the Immortals.
translation.kr: 그 안에는 불사신들의 위안인 네펜테가 들어 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And as she spoke, she poured the flask into the cup; and the fragrance of the wine spread through the hall, like the scent of thyme and roses.

translation.en: As she spoke, she poured the flask into the cup.
translation.kr: 그녀는 말과 함께 물병을 잔에 부었습니다.

translation.en: The fragrance of the wine spread through the hall.
translation.kr: 포도주의 향기가 홀 전체로 퍼졌습니다.

translation.en: It smelled like the scent of thyme and roses.
translation.kr: 그것은 백리향과 장미 냄새 같았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Theseus looked up in her fair face and into her deep dark eyes.  And as he looked, he shrank and shuddered; for they were dry like the eyes of a snake.  And he rose, and said, ‘The wine is rich and fragrant, and the wine-bearer as fair as the Immortals; but let her pledge me first herself in the cup, that the wine may be the sweeter from her lips.’

translation.en: Theseus looked up at her fair face and into her deep dark eyes.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 고개를 들어 그녀의 아름다운 얼굴과 깊고 어두운 눈을 쳐다보았습니다.

translation.en: As he looked, he shrank back and shuddered.
translation.kr: 쳐다보는 순간 그는 움츠러들며 몸서리를 쳤습니다.

translation.en: Her eyes were completely dry like the eyes of a snake.
translation.kr: 그녀의 눈은 뱀의 눈처럼 완전히 메말라 있었습니다.

translation.en: He rose from his seat and spoke.
translation.kr: 그는 자리에서 일어나 말했습니다.

translation.en: The wine is rich and fragrant.
translation.kr: 포도주는 진하고 향기롭습니다.

translation.en: The wine-bearer is as fair as the Immortals.
translation.kr: 포도주를 나르는 여인은 불사신들만큼 아름답습니다.

translation.en: But let her pledge me first by drinking from the cup herself.
translation.kr: 하지만 그녀가 먼저 잔을 마셔 저에게 잔을 권하도록 하십시오.

translation.en: The wine will be much sweeter from her lips.
translation.kr: 그녀의 입술에 닿은 포도주는 훨씬 더 달콤할 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Medeia turned pale, and stammered, ‘Forgive me, fair hero; but I am ill, and dare drink no wine.’

translation.en: Medea turned pale and stammered.
translation.kr: 메데아는 창백해져서 더듬거렸습니다.

translation.en: Forgive me, fair hero.
translation.kr: 용서하십시오, 아름다운 영웅이여.

translation.en: I am ill, and dare not drink any wine.
translation.kr: 저는 몸이 아파서 감히 포도주를 마실 수 없습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Theseus looked again into her eyes, and cried, ‘Thou shalt pledge me in that cup, or die.’  And he lifted up his brazen club, while all the guests looked on aghast.

translation.en: Theseus looked again into her eyes and shouted.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 다시 그녀의 눈을 쳐다보며 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: You shall pledge me in that cup, or die.
translation.kr: 그 잔으로 내게 건배하지 않으면 죽게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: He lifted up his massive bronze club.
translation.kr: 그는 자신의 거대한 청동 곤봉을 들어 올렸습니다.

translation.en: All the guests looked on in absolute horror.
translation.kr: 모든 손님들이 완전한 공포에 질려 바라보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Medeia shrieked a fearful shriek, and dashed the cup to the ground, and fled; and where the wine flowed over the marble pavement, the stone bubbled, and crumbled, and hissed, under the fierce venom of the draught.

translation.en: Medea let out a fearful shriek.
translation.kr: 메데아는 끔찍한 비명을 질렀습니다.

translation.en: She dashed the cup to the ground and fled.
translation.kr: 그녀는 잔을 바닥에 내동댕이치고 도망쳤습니다.

translation.en: The wine flowed over the marble pavement.
translation.kr: 포도주가 대리석 바닥 위로 흘렀습니다.

translation.en: The stone bubbled, crumbled, and hissed under the fierce venom.
translation.kr: 무서운 맹독이 닿은 돌은 거품이 일고 부서지며 쉬익 소리를 냈습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: But Medeia called her dragon chariot, and sprang into it and fled aloft, away over land and sea, and no man saw her more.

translation.en: Medea quickly called her dragon chariot.
translation.kr: 메데아는 서둘러 그녀의 용 전차를 불렀습니다.

translation.en: She sprang into it and fled high into the air.
translation.kr: 그녀는 전차에 뛰어올라 공중 높이 달아났습니다.

translation.en: She flew away over land and sea, and no man saw her again.
translation.kr: 그녀는 육지와 바다 너머로 날아갔고 다시는 아무도 그녀를 보지 못했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Ægeus cried, ‘What hast thou done?’  But Theseus pointed to the stone, ‘I have rid the land of an enchantment: now I will rid it of one more.’

translation.en: Aegeus cried out in shock.
translation.kr: 아이게우스는 충격에 빠져 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: What have you done?
translation.kr: 무슨 짓을 한 겁니까?

translation.en: Theseus pointed directly to the crumbling stone.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 부서지는 돌을 똑바로 가리켰습니다.

translation.en: I have rid the land of a wicked enchantment.
translation.kr: 제가 사악한 마법으로부터 이 땅을 구했습니다.

translation.en: Now I will rid it of one more thing.
translation.kr: 이제 한 가지를 더 없애겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And he came close to Ægeus, and drew from his bosom the sword and the sandals, and said the words which his mother bade him.

translation.en: He came close to Aegeus.
translation.kr: 그는 아이게우스에게 가까이 다가갔습니다.

translation.en: He drew the sword and the sandals from his tunic.
translation.kr: 그는 옷 속에서 칼과 샌들을 꺼냈습니다.

translation.en: He spoke the exact words which his mother had bidden him to say.
translation.kr: 그는 어머니가 하라고 당부하셨던 바로 그 말을 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Ægeus stepped back a pace, and looked at the lad till his eyes grew dim; and then he cast himself on his neck and wept, and Theseus wept on his neck, till they had no strength left to weep more.

translation.en: Aegeus stepped back a pace and looked at the lad.
translation.kr: 아이게우스는 한 걸음 물러서서 그 젊은이를 바라보았습니다.

translation.en: He stared until his eyes grew dim with tears.
translation.kr: 그는 눈물이 고여 앞이 흐려질 때까지 쳐다보았습니다.

translation.en: He cast himself on his son's neck and wept.
translation.kr: 그는 아들의 목을 끌어안고 울었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus also wept on his father's neck.
translation.kr: 테세우스 역시 아버지의 목에 기댄 채 울었습니다.

translation.en: They cried until they had no strength left to weep anymore.
translation.kr: 그들은 더 이상 울 힘이 남지 않을 때까지 울었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Ægeus turned to all the people, and cried, ‘Behold my son, children of Cecrops, a better man than his father was before him.’

translation.en: Then Aegeus turned to all the people and cried out.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 아이게우스는 모든 사람들을 향해 돌아보며 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Behold my son, children of Cecrops!
translation.kr: 케크롭스의 자손들이여, 내 아들을 보시오!

translation.en: He is a much better man than his father ever was.
translation.kr: 그는 그의 아버지였던 나보다 훨씬 더 훌륭한 사람입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Who, then, were mad but the Pallantids, though they had been mad enough before?  And one shouted, ‘Shall we make room for an upstart, a pretender, who comes from we know not where?’  And another, ‘If he be one, we are more than one; and the stronger can hold his own.’  And one shouted one thing, and one another; for they were hot and wild with wine: but all caught swords and lances off the wall, where the weapons hung around, and sprang forward to Theseus, and Theseus sprang forward to them.

translation.en: Who was truly furious then but the Pallantids?
translation.kr: 그때 팔란티드 무리 말고 누가 그토록 격노했겠습니까?

translation.en: They had been angry enough before this revelation.
translation.kr: 그들은 이 사실이 밝혀지기 전에도 이미 충분히 분노해 있었습니다.

translation.en: One of them shouted loudly.
translation.kr: 그들 중 한 명이 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Shall we make room for an upstart pretender from nowhere?
translation.kr: 어디서 왔는지도 모르는 벼락출세한 사기꾼에게 자리를 내어주란 말입니까?

translation.en: Another yelled out in response.
translation.kr: 다른 사람이 이에 대답하며 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: He is only one, but we are many!
translation.kr: 그는 혼자지만 우리는 많습니다!

translation.en: The strongest will hold his own.
translation.kr: 가장 강한 자만이 자신의 것을 지킬 수 있습니다.

translation.en: They shouted many different threats, hot and wild with wine.
translation.kr: 그들은 포도주에 취해 달아오르고 흥분하여 여러 가지 위협적인 말들을 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: They snatched swords and lances from the walls where weapons hung.
translation.kr: 그들은 무기가 걸려 있던 벽에서 칼과 창을 낚아챘습니다.

translation.en: They sprang forward to attack Theseus.
translation.kr: 그들은 테세우스를 공격하기 위해 앞으로 뛰어들었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus fiercely sprang forward to meet them.
translation.kr: 테세우스도 그들에 맞서 맹렬하게 앞으로 뛰어들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And he cried, ‘Go in peace, if you will, my cousins; but if not, your blood be on your own heads.’  But they rushed at him; and then stopped short and railed him, as curs stop and bark when they rouse a lion from his lair.

translation.en: He cried out to them firmly.
translation.kr: 그는 그들에게 단호하게 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Go in peace if you will, my cousins.
translation.kr: 원한다면 평화롭게 물러가십시오, 나의 사촌들이여.

translation.en: But if not, your blood will be on your own heads.
translation.kr: 그렇지 않다면 여러분이 피를 흘린 대가는 스스로 치러야 할 것입니다.

translation.en: They furiously rushed at him.
translation.kr: 그들은 격렬하게 그에게 달려들었습니다.

translation.en: Then they suddenly stopped short and insulted him.
translation.kr: 그러더니 그들은 갑자기 멈춰 서서 그를 모욕했습니다.

translation.en: They acted like wild dogs that stop and bark at a roused lion.
translation.kr: 그들은 잠자던 사자가 깨어나면 멈춰 서서 짖어대는 들개들처럼 행동했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: But one hurled a lance from the rear rank, which past close by Theseus’ head; and at that Theseus rushed forward, and the fight began indeed. Twenty against one they fought, and yet Theseus beat them all; and those who were left fled down into the town, where the people set on them, and drove them out, till Theseus was left alone in the palace, with Ægeus his new-found father.  But before nightfall all the town came up, with victims, and dances, and songs; and they offered sacrifices to Athené, and rejoiced all the night long, because their king had found a noble son, and an heir to his royal house.

translation.en: One man hurled a lance from the rear rank.
translation.kr: 뒷줄에 있던 한 남자가 창을 던졌습니다.

translation.en: It passed very close by Theseus's head.
translation.kr: 그것은 테세우스의 머리 바로 옆을 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: At that moment, Theseus rushed forward, and the fight truly began.
translation.kr: 그 순간 테세우스가 앞으로 돌진했고 진정한 싸움이 시작되었습니다.

translation.en: They fought twenty against one, yet Theseus beat them all.
translation.kr: 그들은 이십 대 일로 싸웠지만 테세우스는 그들 모두를 물리쳤습니다.

translation.en: The survivors fled down into the town.
translation.kr: 살아남은 자들은 마을로 도망쳤습니다.

translation.en: The people set upon them and drove them completely out.
translation.kr: 사람들이 그들을 습격하여 완전히 몰아냈습니다.

translation.en: Theseus was finally left alone in the palace with his new-found father.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 마침내 새로 찾은 아버지와 함께 궁전에 단둘이 남게 되었습니다.

translation.en: Before nightfall, the whole town came up with offerings, dances, and songs.
translation.kr: 해가 지기 전, 온 마을 사람들이 제물과 춤과 노래를 가지고 올라왔습니다.

translation.en: They offered sacrifices to Athena and rejoiced all night long.
translation.kr: 그들은 아테나에게 제물을 바치고 밤새도록 기뻐했습니다.

translation.en: Their king had finally found a noble son and heir.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들의 왕이 고귀한 아들이자 후계자를 찾았기 때문입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: So Theseus stayed with his father all the winter: and when the spring equinox drew near, all the Athenians grew sad and silent, and Theseus saw it, and asked the reason; but no one would answer him a word.

translation.en: Theseus stayed with his father all through the winter.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 겨울 내내 아버지와 함께 지냈습니다.

translation.en: When the spring equinox drew near, all the Athenians grew sad and silent.
translation.kr: 춘분이 다가오자 모든 아테네 사람들은 슬픔에 잠겨 침묵했습니다.

translation.en: Theseus saw this and asked the reason.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 이를 보고 이유를 물었습니다.

translation.en: But no one would answer him a single word.
translation.kr: 하지만 아무도 그에게 단 한마디도 대답하려 하지 않았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then he went to his father, and asked him: but Ægeus turned away his face and wept.

translation.en: Then he went to his father and asked him.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 아버지에게 가서 물었습니다.

translation.en: But Aegeus turned his face away and wept.
translation.kr: 하지만 아이게우스는 고개를 돌린 채 울기만 했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Do not ask, my son, beforehand, about evils which must happen: it is enough to have to face them when they come.’

translation.en: Do not ask beforehand about evils which must happen, my son.
translation.kr: 아들아, 반드시 일어날 끔찍한 일에 대해 미리 묻지 마십시오.

translation.en: It is painful enough to face them when they finally come.
translation.kr: 마침내 그 일들이 닥쳤을 때 마주하는 것만으로도 충분히 고통스럽습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And when the spring equinox came, a herald came to Athens, and stood in the market, and cried, ‘O people and King of Athens, where is your yearly tribute?’  Then a great lamentation arose throughout the city.  But Theseus stood up to the herald, and cried—

translation.en: When the spring equinox arrived, a herald came to Athens.
translation.kr: 춘분이 되자 한 전령이 아테네로 왔습니다.

translation.en: He stood in the market and cried out loudly.
translation.kr: 그는 시장에 서서 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: O people and King of Athens, where is your yearly tribute?
translation.kr: 오 아테네의 백성들과 왕이여, 당신들의 연례 공물은 어디 있습니까?

translation.en: A great lamentation arose throughout the city.
translation.kr: 도시 전체에서 큰 통곡 소리가 일어났습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus stood up to the herald and shouted.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 전령 앞에 서서 소리쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘And who are you, dog-faced, who dare demand tribute here?  If I did not reverence your herald’s staff, I would brain you with this club.’

translation.en: Who are you, dog-faced scoundrel, to dare demand tribute here?
translation.kr: 감히 여기서 공물을 요구하다니, 개 같은 얼굴을 한 너는 대체 누구냐?

translation.en: If I did not respect your herald's staff, I would smash your skull.
translation.kr: 내가 전령의 지팡이를 존중하지 않았다면 이 곤봉으로 네 머리를 박살 냈을 것이다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And the herald answered proudly, for he was a grave and ancient man—

translation.en: The herald answered proudly.
translation.kr: 전령은 자랑스럽게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: He was a grave and ancient man.
translation.kr: 그는 엄숙하고 나이 많은 노인이었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Fair youth, I am not dog-faced or shameless; but I do my master’s bidding, Minos, the King of hundred-citied Crete, the wisest of all kings on earth.  And you must be surely a stranger here, or you would know why I come, and that I come by right.’

translation.en: Fair youth, I am not dog-faced or shameless.
translation.kr: 잘생긴 젊은이여, 나는 개 같은 얼굴을 하거나 파렴치한 사람이 아닙니다.

translation.en: I merely do the bidding of my master, Minos.
translation.kr: 나는 단지 내 주인이신 미노스 왕의 명령을 따를 뿐입니다.

translation.en: He is the King of hundred-citied Crete and the wisest king on earth.
translation.kr: 그는 백 개의 도시를 가진 크레타의 왕이자 세상에서 가장 지혜로운 왕이십니다.

translation.en: You must surely be a stranger here.
translation.kr: 당신은 틀림없이 이곳에 온 이방인일 것입니다.

translation.en: Otherwise, you would know why I come and that I come by right.
translation.kr: 그렇지 않다면 내가 왜 왔는지, 그리고 내가 정당한 권리로 왔다는 것을 알 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘I am a stranger here.  Tell me, then, why you come.’

translation.en: I am a stranger here.
translation.kr: 나는 이곳의 이방인입니다.

translation.en: Tell me, then, exactly why you come.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 당신이 온 정확한 이유를 말해 보십시오.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘To fetch the tribute which King Ægeus promised to Minos, and confirmed his promise with an oath.  For Minos conquered all this land, and Megara which lies to the east, when he came hither with a great fleet of ships, enraged about the murder of his son.  For his son Androgeos came hither to the Panathenaic games, and overcame all the Greeks in the sports, so that the people honoured him as a hero.  But when Ægeus saw his valour, he envied him, and feared lest he should join the sons of Pallas, and take away the sceptre from him.  So he plotted against his life, and slew him basely, no man knows how or where.  Some say that he waylaid him by Oinoe, on the road which goes to Thebes; and some that he sent him against the bull of Marathon, that the beast might kill him.  But Ægeus says that the young men killed him from envy, because he had conquered them in the games.  So Minos came hither and avenged him, and would not depart till this land had promised him tribute—seven youths and seven maidens every year, who go with me in a black-sailed ship, till they come to hundred-citied Crete.’

translation.en: I have come to fetch the tribute King Aegeus promised to Minos.
translation.kr: 저는 아이게우스 왕이 미노스 왕에게 약속한 공물을 가지러 왔습니다.

translation.en: He confirmed his promise with a solemn oath.
translation.kr: 그는 엄숙한 맹세로 자신의 약속을 확증했습니다.

translation.en: Minos conquered all this land and Megara to the east.
translation.kr: 미노스 왕은 이 땅과 동쪽의 메가라를 모두 정복했습니다.

translation.en: He came here with a great fleet, enraged by the murder of his son.
translation.kr: 그는 아들의 죽음에 분노하여 대함대를 이끌고 이곳에 왔습니다.

translation.en: His son Androgeos came here to the Panathenaic games.
translation.kr: 그의 아들 안드로게오스는 판아테나이아 경기에 참가하러 이곳에 왔습니다.

translation.en: He overcame all the Greeks in the sports.
translation.kr: 그는 스포츠에서 모든 그리스인들을 이겼습니다.

translation.en: The people greatly honored him as a hero.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그를 영웅으로 크게 존경했습니다.

translation.en: But when Aegeus saw his valor, he envied him.
translation.kr: 하지만 아이게우스는 그의 용맹을 보고 그를 질투했습니다.

translation.en: He feared the young man might join the sons of Pallas.
translation.kr: 그는 그 젊은이가 팔라스의 아들들과 결탁할까 봐 두려워했습니다.

translation.en: He thought they would take the royal scepter away from him.
translation.kr: 그는 그들이 자신에게서 왕의 홀을 빼앗아 갈 것이라고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: So he plotted against his life and basely killed him.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 그의 목숨을 노리고 비열하게 그를 죽였습니다.

translation.en: No man knows exactly how or where it happened.
translation.kr: 어떻게, 어디서 그런 일이 일어났는지는 아무도 정확히 모릅니다.

translation.en: Some say he waylaid him by Oenoe, on the road to Thebes.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 그가 테베로 가는 길인 오이노에 근처에서 그를 습격했다고 말합니다.

translation.en: Others say he sent him against the fierce bull of Marathon.
translation.kr: 다른 이들은 그가 짐승에게 죽게 하려고 마라톤의 사나운 황소에게 그를 보냈다고 말합니다.

translation.en: But Aegeus claims the young men killed him out of bitter envy.
translation.kr: 하지만 아이게우스는 젊은이들이 깊은 질투심에 그를 죽였다고 주장합니다.

translation.en: They were angry because he had conquered them in the games.
translation.kr: 경기에서 그에게 패배했기 때문에 그들이 분노했다는 것입니다.

translation.en: So Minos came here and thoroughly avenged his son.
translation.kr: 그래서 미노스 왕은 이곳에 와서 철저히 아들의 복수를 했습니다.

translation.en: He refused to depart until this land promised him a yearly tribute.
translation.kr: 그는 이 땅이 그에게 매년 공물을 바치겠다고 약속할 때까지 떠나기를 거부했습니다.

translation.en: We demand seven youths and seven maidens every year.
translation.kr: 우리는 매년 일곱 명의 청년과 일곱 명의 처녀를 요구합니다.

translation.en: They go with me in a black-sailed ship to hundred-citied Crete.
translation.kr: 그들은 검은 돛을 단 배를 타고 백 개의 도시를 가진 크레타로 저와 함께 갈 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Theseus ground his teeth together, and said, ‘Wert thou not a herald I would kill thee for saying such things of my father; but I will go to him, and know the truth.’  So he went to his father, and asked him; but he turned away his head and wept, and said, ‘Blood was shed in the land unjustly, and by blood it is avenged.  Break not my heart by questions; it is enough to endure in silence.’

translation.en: Theseus ground his teeth together in anger.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 분노로 이를 갈았습니다.

translation.en: If you were not a herald, I would kill you for saying such things.
translation.kr: 당신이 전령이 아니었다면 내 아버지에 대해 그런 말을 한 죄로 당신을 죽였을 것입니다.

translation.en: I will go to him and know the truth.
translation.kr: 나는 아버지께 가서 진실을 알아볼 것입니다.

translation.en: So he went to his father and asked him directly.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 아버지에게 가서 직접 물었습니다.

translation.en: But Aegeus turned his head away and wept.
translation.kr: 하지만 아이게우스는 고개를 돌린 채 울었습니다.

translation.en: Blood was unjustly shed in this land.
translation.kr: 이 땅에서 부당하게 피가 흘려졌습니다.

translation.en: By blood it must be avenged.
translation.kr: 피는 피로써 갚아야만 합니다.

translation.en: Do not break my heart with endless questions.
translation.kr: 끝없는 질문으로 내 마음을 아프게 하지 마십시오.

translation.en: It is hard enough to endure this pain in silence.
translation.kr: 이 고통을 침묵 속에서 견디는 것만으로도 충분히 힘듭니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus groaned inwardly, and said, ‘I will go myself with these youths and maidens, and kill Minos upon his royal throne.’

translation.en: Theseus groaned inwardly and spoke with determination.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 속으로 신음하며 단호하게 말했습니다.

translation.en: I will go myself with these youths and maidens.
translation.kr: 제가 직접 이 청년과 처녀들과 함께 가겠습니다.

translation.en: I will kill Minos right upon his royal throne.
translation.kr: 미노스 왕의 옥좌 위에서 그를 죽이겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Ægeus shrieked, and cried, ‘You shall not go, my son, the light of my old age, to whom alone I look to rule this people after I am dead and gone.  You shall not go, to die horribly, as those youths and maidens die; for Minos thrusts them into a labyrinth, which Daidalos made for him among the rocks,—Daidalos the renegade, the accursed, the pest of this his native land.  From that labyrinth no one can escape, entangled in its winding ways, before they meet the Minotaur, the monster who feeds upon the flesh of men.  There he devours them horribly, and they never see this land again.’

translation.en: Aegeus shrieked and cried out in terror.
translation.kr: 아이게우스는 비명을 지르며 공포에 질려 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: You shall not go, my son, the only light of my old age.
translation.kr: 내 노년의 유일한 빛인 내 아들아, 절대 가서는 안 됩니다.

translation.en: I look to you alone to rule this people after I am gone.
translation.kr: 내가 떠난 뒤 이 백성을 다스릴 사람은 오직 당신뿐입니다.

translation.en: You shall not go to die horribly like those youths and maidens.
translation.kr: 당신이 그 청년들과 처녀들처럼 끔찍하게 죽으러 가서는 안 됩니다.

translation.en: Minos thrusts them into a deadly labyrinth among the rocks.
translation.kr: 미노스는 바위 사이에 있는 치명적인 미궁으로 그들을 밀어 넣습니다.

translation.en: Daedalus made it for him.
translation.kr: 다이달로스가 그를 위해 그것을 만들었습니다.

translation.en: Daedalus is a renegade, accursed, and a pest to his native land.
translation.kr: 다이달로스는 배신자이고, 저주받은 자이며, 자기 조국의 골칫거리입니다.

translation.en: No one can ever escape from that labyrinth.
translation.kr: 누구도 그 미궁에서 빠져나올 수 없습니다.

translation.en: They become entangled in its winding ways.
translation.kr: 그들은 구불구불한 길에 얽히게 됩니다.

translation.en: Soon they meet the Minotaur, the monster who eats human flesh.
translation.kr: 곧 그들은 인간의 고기를 먹는 괴물인 미노타우로스를 만나게 됩니다.

translation.en: There he horribly devours them.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 그는 그들을 끔찍하게 집어삼킵니다.

translation.en: They never see this land again.
translation.kr: 그들은 다시는 이 땅을 보지 못합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus grew red, and his ears tingled, and his heart beat loud in his bosom.  And he stood awhile like a tall stone pillar on the cliffs above some hero’s grave; and at last he spoke—

translation.en: Theseus grew red, and his ears tingled hotly.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 얼굴이 붉어졌고 귀가 뜨겁게 달아올랐습니다.

translation.en: His heart beat loudly in his broad chest.
translation.kr: 그의 넓은 가슴에서 심장이 크게 뛰었습니다.

translation.en: He stood awhile like a tall stone pillar.
translation.kr: 그는 한동안 커다란 돌기둥처럼 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: He looked like a monument on the cliffs above some hero's grave.
translation.kr: 그는 영웅의 무덤 위 절벽에 세워진 기념비 같았습니다.

translation.en: At last, he broke the silence and spoke.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 침묵을 깨고 입을 열었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Therefore all the more I will go with them, and slay the accursed beast. Have I not slain all evil-doers and monsters, that I might free this land?  Where are Periphetes, and Sinis, and Kerkuon, and Phaia the wild sow?  Where are the fifty sons of Pallas?  And this Minotaur shall go the road which they have gone, and Minos himself, if he dare stay me.’

translation.en: Therefore, I have even more reason to go with them.
translation.kr: 그러므로 제가 그들과 함께 가야 할 이유가 더욱 분명해졌습니다.

translation.en: I will slay that accursed beast.
translation.kr: 저는 그 저주받은 괴물을 죽이겠습니다.

translation.en: Have I not slain all evil-doers to free this land?
translation.kr: 이 땅을 해방시키기 위해 모든 악당들을 물리치지 않았습니까?

translation.en: Where are Periphetes, Sinis, Cercyon, and Phaia the wild sow?
translation.kr: 페리페테스, 시니스, 케르키온, 그리고 야생 암돼지 파이아는 지금 어디에 있습니까?

translation.en: Where are the fifty treacherous sons of Pallas?
translation.kr: 팔라스의 교활한 쉰 명의 아들들은 어디에 있습니까?

translation.en: This Minotaur shall travel the exact same road they went.
translation.kr: 이 미노타우로스 역시 그들이 갔던 길을 똑같이 걷게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: Minos himself will join them if he dares to stop me.
translation.kr: 감히 저를 막으려 든다면 미노스 자신도 그들과 함께하게 될 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘But how will you slay him, my son?  For you must leave your club and your armour behind, and be cast to the monster, defenceless and naked like the rest.’

translation.en: But how will you slay him, my brave son?
translation.kr: 하지만 어떻게 그를 죽이겠습니까, 나의 용감한 아들아?

translation.en: You must leave your club and your armor entirely behind.
translation.kr: 당신의 곤봉과 갑옷은 모두 뒤에 두고 가야 합니다.

translation.en: You will be cast to the monster, defenseless and bare.
translation.kr: 당신은 무방비 상태로 벌거벗겨진 채 그 괴물에게 던져질 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Theseus said, ‘Are there no stones in that labyrinth; and have I not fists and teeth?  Did I need my club to kill Kerkuon, the terror of all mortal men?’

translation.en: Theseus calmly replied to his father.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 아버지에게 침착하게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Are there no stones at all in that labyrinth?
translation.kr: 그 미궁 안에는 돌멩이 하나 없단 말입니까?

translation.en: Do I not still have my own fists and teeth?
translation.kr: 제게는 아직 두 주먹과 이빨이 남아 있지 않습니까?

translation.en: Did I need my club to kill Cercyon, the terror of all men?
translation.kr: 모든 사람들의 공포의 대상이었던 케르키온을 죽일 때 제가 곤봉을 썼습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: Then Ægeus clung to his knees; but he would not hear; and at last he let him go, weeping bitterly, and said only this one word—

translation.en: Aegeus desperately clung to his son's knees.
translation.kr: 아이게우스는 절망적으로 아들의 무릎에 매달렸습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus refused to change his mind.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 마음을 바꾸기를 거부했습니다.

translation.en: At last, the king let him go, weeping bitterly.
translation.kr: 마침내 왕은 비통하게 울며 그를 보내주었습니다.

translation.en: He spoke only this one final request.
translation.kr: 그는 오직 이 마지막 부탁만을 말했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: ‘Promise me but this, if you return in peace, though that may hardly be: take down the black sail of the ship (for I shall watch for it all day upon the cliffs), and hoist instead a white sail, that I may know afar off that you are safe.’

translation.en: Promise me just this one thing, if you return in peace.
translation.kr: 무사히 돌아온다면 부디 이 한 가지만은 약속해 주십시오.

translation.en: I know such a thing is nearly impossible.
translation.kr: 나도 그런 일이 거의 불가능하다는 것을 압니다.

translation.en: Take down the black sail of the returning ship.
translation.kr: 돌아오는 배의 검은 돛을 내리십시오.

translation.en: I shall watch for it all day upon the high cliffs.
translation.kr: 나는 높은 절벽 위에서 하루 종일 그 배를 기다릴 것입니다.

translation.en: Hoist a white sail instead.
translation.kr: 대신 하얀 돛을 올리십시오.

translation.en: Then I will know from afar that you are completely safe.
translation.kr: 그러면 당신이 완전히 무사하다는 것을 멀리서도 알 수 있을 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Theseus promised, and went out, and to the market-place where the herald stood, while they drew lots for the youths and maidens, who were to sail in that doleful crew.  And the people stood wailing and weeping, as the lot fell on this one and on that; but Theseus strode into the midst, and cried—‘Here is a youth who needs no lot.  I myself will be one of the seven.’

translation.en: Theseus gave his solemn promise and went out.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 굳게 약속하고 밖으로 나갔습니다.

translation.en: He headed to the marketplace where the herald stood.
translation.kr: 그는 전령이 서 있는 시장으로 향했습니다.

translation.en: They were drawing lots for the youths and maidens.
translation.kr: 그들은 젊은이들과 처녀들을 제비뽑기로 뽑고 있었습니다.

translation.en: These victims would sail in that doleful crew.
translation.kr: 이 희생자들은 그 비통한 무리에 섞여 항해하게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: The people stood wailing and weeping endlessly.
translation.kr: 사람들은 끝없이 통곡하며 울었습니다.

translation.en: The fatal lot fell on various families.
translation.kr: 운명의 제비뽑기는 여러 가족들에게 떨어졌습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus strode boldly into the very center.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 아주 한가운데로 당당하게 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: He loudly addressed the crowd.
translation.kr: 그는 군중을 향해 큰 소리로 말했습니다.

translation.en: Here is a youth who needs no lot.
translation.kr: 여기 제비뽑기가 필요 없는 청년이 있습니다.

translation.en: I myself will gladly be one of the seven.
translation.kr: 저 자신이 기꺼이 그 일곱 명 중 하나가 되겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And the herald asked in wonder, ‘Fair youth, know you whither you are going?’

translation.en: The herald asked him in total astonishment.
translation.kr: 전령은 완전히 놀라서 그에게 물었습니다.

translation.en: Fair youth, do you truly know where you are going?
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 정말로 어디로 가는지 알고 있습니까?

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: And Theseus said, ‘I know.  Let us go down to the black-sailed ship.’

translation.en: Theseus answered him calmly.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그에게 침착하게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: I know exactly where I am going.
translation.kr: 내가 어디로 가는지 정확히 알고 있습니다.

translation.en: Let us go down to the black-sailed ship.
translation.kr: 자, 검은 돛을 단 배로 내려갑시다.

paragraphs.part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
paragraphs.raw: So they went down to the black-sailed ship, seven maidens, and seven youths, and Theseus before them all, and the people following them lamenting.  But Theseus whispered to his companions, ‘Have hope, for the monster is not immortal.  Where are Periphetes, and Sinis, and Sciron, and all whom I have slain?’  Then their hearts were comforted a little; but they wept as they went on board, and the cliffs of Sunium rang, and all the isles of the Ægean Sea, with the voice of their lamentation, as they sailed on toward their deaths in Crete.

translation.en: They went down to the black-sailed ship.
translation.kr: 그들은 검은 돛을 단 배로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: There were seven maidens and seven youths.
translation.kr: 일곱 명의 처녀와 일곱 명의 청년이 있었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus walked proudly before them all.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그들 모두의 앞에서 당당하게 걸었습니다.

translation.en: The people followed behind them, loudly lamenting.
translation.kr: 사람들은 큰 소리로 통곡하며 그들 뒤를 따랐습니다.

translation.en: Theseus whispered quietly to his companions.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 동료들에게 조용히 속삭였습니다.

translation.en: Have hope, for the monster is not immortal.
translation.kr: 희망을 가지십시오, 그 괴물은 불사신이 아닙니다.

translation.en: Remember all the wicked monsters I have already slain.
translation.kr: 제가 이미 베어버린 모든 사악한 괴물들을 기억하십시오.

translation.en: Their hearts were comforted just a little.
translation.kr: 그들의 마음은 아주 조금 위로를 받았습니다.

translation.en: But they still wept as they finally went on board.
translation.kr: 하지만 그들은 마침내 배에 오를 때 여전히 눈물을 흘렸습니다.

translation.en: The cliffs of Sunion rang with their loud sorrow.
translation.kr: 수니온의 절벽이 그들의 커다란 슬픔으로 울려 퍼졌습니다.

translation.en: All the isles of the Aegean Sea echoed their lamentations.
translation.kr: 에게 해의 모든 섬들이 그들의 통곡을 메아리쳤습니다.

translation.en: They sailed on toward their expected deaths in Crete.
translation.kr: 그들은 크레타에서의 예정된 죽음을 향해 항해를 계속했습니다.

chapters.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: PART III HOW THESEUS SLEW THE MINOTAUR

translation.en: Part 3: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
translation.kr: [3부: 테세우스가 미노타우로스를 물리치다]

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And at last they came to Crete, and to Cnossus, beneath the peaks of Ida, and to the palace of Minos the great king, to whom Zeus himself taught laws.  So he was the wisest of all mortal kings, and conquered all the Ægean isles; and his ships were as many as the sea-gulls, and his palace like a marble hill.  And he sat among the pillars of the hall, upon his throne of beaten gold, and around him stood the speaking statues which Daidalos had made by his skill.  For Daidalos was the most cunning of all Athenians, and he first invented the plumb-line, and the auger, and glue, and many a tool with which wood is wrought.  And he first set up masts in ships, and yards, and his son made sails for them: but Perdix his nephew excelled him; for he first invented the saw and its teeth, copying it from the back-bone of a fish; and invented, too, the chisel, and the compasses, and the potter’s wheel which moulds the clay.  Therefore Daidalos envied him, and hurled him headlong from the temple of Athené; but the Goddess pitied him (for she loves the wise), and changed him into a partridge, which flits for ever about the hills.  And Daidalos fled to Crete, to Minos, and worked for him many a year, till he did a shameful deed, at which the sun hid his face on high.

translation.en: They finally reached Crete and the city of Cnossus, situated below the peaks of Mount Ida.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 이다 산의 봉우리 아래에 있는 크레타 섬의 크노소스에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: There stood the palace of the great King Minos, who learned the laws directly from Zeus.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 제우스에게 직접 법을 배운 위대한 미노스 왕의 궁전이 있었습니다.

translation.en: Minos was the wisest of all mortal kings and had conquered all the Aegean islands.
translation.kr: 미노스는 인간 왕들 중 가장 지혜로웠으며 모든 에게해의 섬들을 정복했습니다.

translation.en: His ships were as numerous as seagulls, and his palace resembled a marble hill.
translation.kr: 그의 함선은 갈매기 떼처럼 많았고, 궁전은 대리석 언덕과 같았습니다.

translation.en: He sat among the hall's pillars on a throne made of solid gold.
translation.kr: 그는 넓은 전당의 기둥들 사이, 순금으로 만든 왕좌에 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: Around him stood speaking statues crafted by the skilled inventor Daedalus.
translation.kr: 그 주변에는 뛰어난 발명가 다이달로스가 만든 말하는 조각상들이 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: Daedalus was the most clever of all Athenians.
translation.kr: 다이달로스는 아테네인들 중에서 가장 손재주가 뛰어났습니다.

translation.en: He invented the plumb-line, the drill, glue, and many woodworking tools.
translation.kr: 그는 추와 송곳, 접착제를 비롯해 나무를 다루는 수많은 도구를 발명했습니다.

translation.en: He also first equipped ships with masts and yards, while his son made their sails.
translation.kr: 또한 그는 배에 돛대와 활대를 처음 설치했고, 그의 아들은 돛을 만들었습니다.

translation.en: However, his nephew Perdix proved to be even more talented.
translation.kr: 하지만 그의 조카 페르딕스가 그보다 더욱 뛰어난 재능을 보였습니다.

translation.en: Perdix invented the saw by copying the jagged backbone of a fish.
translation.kr: 페르딕스는 물고기의 등뼈 모양을 본떠 톱을 발명했습니다.

translation.en: He also invented the chisel, the compass, and the potter's wheel for molding clay.
translation.kr: 그는 끌과 나침반, 그리고 점토를 빚는 물레도 발명했습니다.

translation.en: Daedalus grew incredibly jealous and threw his nephew from the roof of Athena's temple.
translation.kr: 다이달로스는 질투심에 눈이 멀어 조카를 아테나 신전 지붕에서 밀어 떨어뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: But the Goddess pitied the wise boy and transformed him into a partridge.
translation.kr: 하지만 지혜로운 자를 사랑하는 여신은 소년을 불쌍히 여겨 자고새로 변하게 했습니다.

translation.en: That bird now flutters forever among the hills.
translation.kr: 그 새는 지금도 산언덕을 끊임없이 날아다닙니다.

translation.en: After this crime, Daedalus fled to Crete and worked for King Minos for many years.
translation.kr: 이 범죄 이후 다이달로스는 크레타 섬의 미노스에게로 도망쳐 오랫동안 일했습니다.

translation.en: He stayed there until he committed a deed so shameful that the sun hid its face.
translation.kr: 그는 태양조차 얼굴을 가릴 만큼 수치스러운 짓을 저지를 때까지 그곳에 머물렀습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: Then he fled from the anger of Minos, he and Icaros his son having made themselves wings of feathers, and fixed the feathers with wax.  So they flew over the sea toward Sicily; but Icaros flew too near the sun; and the wax of his wings was melted, and he fell into the Icarian Sea.
