But Daidalos came safe to Sicily, and there wrought many a wondrous work; for he made for King Cocalos a reservoir, from which a great river watered all the land, and a castle and a treasury on a mountain, which the giants themselves could not have stormed; and in Selinos he took the steam which comes up from the fires of Ætna, and made of it a warm bath of vapour, to cure the pains of mortal men; and he made a honeycomb of gold, in which the bees came and stored their honey, and in Egypt he made the forecourt of the temple of Hephaistos in Memphis, and a statue of himself within it, and many another wondrous work.  And for Minos he made statues which spoke and moved, and the temple of Britomartis, and the dancing-hall of Ariadne, which he carved of fair white stone.  And in Sardinia he worked for Iölaos, and in many a land beside, wandering up and down for ever with his cunning, unlovely and accursed by men.

translation.en: Daedalus soon had to flee from the anger of Minos.
translation.kr: 이윽고 다이달로스는 미노스의 분노를 피해 달아나야 했습니다.

translation.en: He and his son Icarus made wings from feathers and secured them with wax.
translation.kr: 그와 그의 아들 이카로스는 깃털을 모아 밀랍으로 붙여 날개를 만들었습니다.

translation.en: They flew over the sea toward Sicily.
translation.kr: 그들은 바다를 날아서 시칠리아로 향했습니다.

translation.en: But Icarus flew too close to the hot sun.
translation.kr: 하지만 이카로스는 뜨거운 태양에 너무 가까이 날아올랐습니다.

translation.en: The wax on his wings melted, and he plunged to his death in the Icarian Sea.
translation.kr: 날개의 밀랍이 녹아버렸고, 그는 이카리아 해로 추락하여 목숨을 잃었습니다.

translation.en: Daedalus arrived safely in Sicily, where he crafted many more incredible works.
translation.kr: 다이달로스는 시칠리아에 무사히 도착하여 그곳에서도 수많은 놀라운 작품들을 만들었습니다.

translation.en: He built a massive reservoir for King Cocalus to water the entire land.
translation.kr: 그는 코칼로스 왕을 위해 온 땅에 물을 대는 거대한 저수지를 건설했습니다.

translation.en: He also built an impenetrable mountain castle and treasury that giants could not storm.
translation.kr: 또한 거인들조차 뚫을 수 없는 난공불락의 산성 안 금고도 지었습니다.

translation.en: In Selinus, he captured steam from Mount Etna's fires to create healing vapor baths.
translation.kr: 셀리누스에서는 에트나 산의 열기를 모아 병자들을 치료하는 온천을 만들었습니다.

translation.en: He forged a golden honeycomb where real bees came to store their honey.
translation.kr: 그는 진짜 벌들이 날아와 꿀을 저장할 수 있는 황금 벌집을 만들었습니다.

translation.en: In Egypt, he built the grand forecourt of the Memphis temple and his own statue inside.
translation.kr: 이집트에서는 멤피스 신전의 거대한 앞뜰과 그 안에 자신의 조각상도 세웠습니다.

translation.en: Earlier for Minos, he had carved speaking statues and the beautiful dancing hall of Ariadne.
translation.kr: 이전에 그는 미노스를 위해 말하는 조각상과 아리아드네의 아름다운 무도장을 조각했습니다.

translation.en: He later worked in Sardinia and many other lands.
translation.kr: 그는 훗날 사르데냐를 비롯한 여러 나라에서도 일했습니다.

translation.en: He wandered forever with his brilliant skills, yet remained unloved and cursed by humanity.
translation.kr: 그는 뛰어난 기술을 지니고 영원히 떠돌았으나, 사람들의 사랑을 받지 못하고 저주받았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: But Theseus stood before Minos, and they looked each other in the face. And Minos bade take them to prison, and cast them to the monster one by one, that the death of Androgeos might be avenged.  Then Theseus cried—

translation.en: Theseus stood firmly before King Minos, and they stared into each other's eyes.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 미노스 왕 앞에 당당히 서서 서로의 눈을 응시했습니다.

translation.en: Minos ordered the guards to throw the youths into prison.
translation.kr: 미노스는 경비병들에게 젊은이들을 감옥에 가두라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: He commanded that they be fed to the monster one by one to avenge his son's death.
translation.kr: 그는 아들의 죽음을 복수하기 위해 그들을 한 명씩 괴물에게 먹이로 주라고 지시했습니다.

translation.en: Suddenly, Theseus called out loudly.
translation.kr: 그때 테세우스가 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘A boon, O Minos!  Let me be thrown first to the beast.  For I came hither for that very purpose, of my own will, and not by lot.’

translation.en: Grant me a favor, King Minos! Let me be thrown to the beast first.
translation.kr: 미노스 왕이여, 제게 한 가지 부탁을 들어주십시오! 저를 괴물에게 가장 먼저 던져 주십시오.

translation.en: I came here for this exact purpose by my own choice, not by drawing lots.
translation.kr: 저는 제비뽑기가 아니라 오직 이 목적을 위해 제 발로 찾아왔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘Who art thou, then, brave youth?’

translation.en: Who are you, brave young man?
translation.kr: 용감한 젊은이여, 도대체 너는 누구냐?

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘I am the son of him whom of all men thou hatest most, Ægeus the king of Athens, and I am come here to end this matter.’

translation.en: I am the son of the man you hate most in this world.
translation.kr: 저는 당신이 이 세상에서 가장 증오하는 사람의 아들입니다.

translation.en: I am the son of King Aegeus of Athens, and I have come to end this nightmare.
translation.kr: 아테네의 왕 아이게우스의 아들로서 이 끔찍한 악몽을 끝내러 왔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And Minos pondered awhile, looking steadfastly at him, and he thought, ‘The lad means to atone by his own death for his father’s sin;’ and he answered at last mildly—

translation.en: Minos thought for a moment while staring intently at the young hero.
translation.kr: 미노스는 젊은 영웅을 뚫어지게 바라보며 잠시 생각에 잠겼습니다.

translation.en: He assumed the boy wanted to atone for his father's sins with his own life.
translation.kr: 그는 이 소년이 자신의 목숨으로 아버지의 죄를 속죄하려 한다고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: The king finally answered in a surprisingly gentle tone.
translation.kr: 왕은 마침내 놀랍도록 부드러운 어조로 대답했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘Go back in peace, my son.  It is a pity that one so brave should die.’

translation.en: Go back in peace, my son. It is a tragedy for someone so brave to die.
translation.kr: 평안히 돌아가거라, 내 아들아. 너처럼 용감한 자가 죽는 것은 참으로 안타까운 일이다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: But Theseus said, ‘I have sworn that I will not go back till I have seen the monster face to face.’

translation.en: I have sworn an oath that I will not return home.
translation.kr: 저는 결코 고향으로 돌아가지 않겠다고 맹세했습니다.

translation.en: I will stay until I look this monster directly in the face.
translation.kr: 이 괴물의 얼굴을 똑똑히 마주할 때까지 이곳에 남겠습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And at that Minos frowned, and said, ‘Then thou shalt see him; take the madman away.’

translation.en: Minos frowned deeply at his stubbornness.
translation.kr: 미노스는 그의 고집에 미간을 깊게 찌푸렸습니다.

translation.en: Then you shall see him! Take this madman away.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 그놈을 보게 될 것이다! 이 미치광이를 끌고 가라.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And they led Theseus away into the prison, with the other youths and maids.

translation.en: The guards dragged Theseus into the dark prison along with the other terrified youths.
translation.kr: 경비병들은 겁에 질린 다른 젊은이들과 함께 테세우스를 어두운 감옥으로 끌고 갔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: But Ariadne, Minos’ daughter, saw him, as she came out of her white stone hall; and she loved him for his courage and his majesty, and said, ‘Shame that such a youth should die!’  And by night she went down to the prison, and told him all her heart; and said—

translation.en: However, the king's daughter Ariadne had seen him from her white stone hall.
translation.kr: 하지만 왕의 딸 아리아드네가 하얀 대리석 전당에서 그를 지켜보고 있었습니다.

translation.en: She instantly fell in love with his majestic courage.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그의 기품 있는 용기에 단번에 사랑에 빠졌습니다.

translation.en: She felt it was a terrible crime for such a hero to die.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그런 영웅이 죽는 것은 끔찍한 비극이라고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: Under the cover of night, she secretly visited his prison cell.
translation.kr: 한밤중에 그녀는 남몰래 그의 감옥을 찾아갔습니다.

translation.en: She confessed her feelings to him and urgently whispered her plan.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그에게 자신의 마음을 고백하며 다급하게 계획을 속삭였습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘Flee down to your ship at once, for I have bribed the guards before the door.  Flee, you and all your friends, and go back in peace to Greece; and take me, take me with you! for I dare not stay after you are gone; for my father will kill me miserably, if he knows what I have done.’

translation.en: Run to your ship right now. I have already bribed the guards.
translation.kr: 지금 당장 배로 도망치세요. 제가 경비병들에게 이미 뇌물을 주었습니다.

translation.en: Take all your friends and escape safely back to Greece.
translation.kr: 친구들을 모두 데리고 무사히 그리스로 탈출하세요.

translation.en: Please take me with you! I cannot stay here after you leave.
translation.kr: 제발 저도 함께 데려가 주세요! 당신이 떠난 뒤에 저는 이곳에 남을 수 없습니다.

translation.en: My father will kill me without mercy if he discovers what I have done.
translation.kr: 아버지가 제 행동을 알게 되면 저를 무자비하게 죽이실 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And Theseus stood silent awhile; for he was astonished and confounded by her beauty: but at last he said, ‘I cannot go home in peace, till I have seen and slain this Minotaur, and avenged the deaths of the youths and maidens, and put an end to the terrors of my land.’

translation.en: Theseus stood completely silent, stunned by her breathtaking beauty.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그녀의 눈부신 아름다움에 넋을 잃고 멍하니 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he spoke with absolute determination.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 단호한 결의를 담아 입을 열었습니다.

translation.en: I cannot go home peacefully until I kill this Minotaur.
translation.kr: 이 미노타우로스를 죽이기 전에는 결코 편안히 고향에 갈 수 없습니다.

translation.en: I must avenge the innocent youths and end the terror threatening my land.
translation.kr: 희생당한 젊은이들의 복수를 하고 내 조국을 위협하는 공포를 끝내야만 합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘And will you kill the Minotaur?  How, then?’

translation.en: But how can you possibly kill the Minotaur?
translation.kr: 하지만 대체 어떻게 미노타우로스를 죽이겠다는 건가요?

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘I know not, nor do I care: but he must be strong if he be too strong for me.’

translation.en: I do not know, nor do I care.
translation.kr: 방법은 모르지만 상관없습니다.

translation.en: He will have to be unimaginably strong to defeat me.
translation.kr: 저를 꺾으려면 상상할 수 없을 만큼 강력해야만 할 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: Then she loved him all the more, and said, ‘But when you have killed him, how will you find your way out of the labyrinth?’

translation.en: She loved him even more for his bravery.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그의 용기에 더욱 깊이 빠져들었습니다.

translation.en: But even if you kill him, how will you find your way out of the maze?
translation.kr: 하지만 괴물을 죽인다 해도, 어떻게 그 미궁에서 빠져나올 생각인가요?

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: ‘I know not, neither do I care: but it must be a strange road, if I do not find it out before I have eaten up the monster’s carcase.’

translation.en: I do not know, and it does not matter.
translation.kr: 그것도 모르고, 별로 중요하지도 않습니다.

translation.en: I will figure it out eventually once the monster is completely destroyed.
translation.kr: 괴물을 완전히 쓰러뜨리고 나면 결국 길을 찾아낼 수 있을 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: Then she loved him all the more, and said—‘Fair youth, you are too bold; but I can help you, weak as I am.  I will give you a sword, and with that perhaps you may slay the beast; and a clue of thread, and by that, perhaps, you may find your way out again.  Only promise me that if you escape safe you will take me home with you to Greece; for my father will surely kill me, if he knows what I have done.’

translation.en: Her heart swelled with love, and she looked at him with desperate hope.
translation.kr: 그녀의 가슴은 사랑으로 부풀어 올랐고, 간절한 희망을 담아 그를 바라보았습니다.

translation.en: Fair youth, you are far too bold, but I can help you.
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 너무 무모하지만 제가 도와드릴 수 있습니다.

translation.en: I will give you a sword to slay the beast.
translation.kr: 괴물을 찌를 수 있는 검을 한 자루 드리겠습니다.

translation.en: I will also give you a ball of thread to find your way back out.
translation.kr: 그리고 밖으로 빠져나올 길을 찾을 수 있도록 실뭉치도 드리겠습니다.

translation.en: Just promise to take me to Greece if you escape safely.
translation.kr: 무사히 탈출한다면 저를 그리스로 데려가겠다고 약속해 주세요.

translation.en: My father will surely kill me if he discovers my betrayal.
translation.kr: 아버지가 제 배신을 알게 되면 틀림없이 저를 죽이실 것입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: Then Theseus laughed, and said, ‘Am I not safe enough now?’  And he hid the sword in his bosom, and rolled up the clue in his hand; and then he swore to Ariadne, and fell down before her, and kissed her hands and her feet; and she wept over him a long while, and then went away; and Theseus lay down and slept sweetly.

translation.en: Theseus laughed warmly and told her that he was safe now.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 따뜻하게 웃으며 이제 자신은 안전하다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: He hid the sharp sword under his clothes and gripped the thread.
translation.kr: 그는 날카로운 검을 옷 속에 숨기고 실뭉치를 단단히 쥐었습니다.

translation.en: He swore a solemn oath to Ariadne, bowing to kiss her hands and feet.
translation.kr: 그는 아리아드네에게 엄숙한 맹세를 하며 엎드려 그녀의 손과 발에 입을 맞추었습니다.

translation.en: She wept over him for a long time before quietly slipping away.
translation.kr: 그녀는 오랫동안 눈물을 흘린 뒤에 조용히 빠져나갔습니다.

translation.en: Confident in his victory, Theseus lay down and slept peacefully.
translation.kr: 승리를 확신한 테세우스는 자리에 누워 평온하게 잠들었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And when the evening came, the guards came in and led him away to the labyrinth.

translation.en: When evening arrived, the guards came to lead him into the dreadful labyrinth.
translation.kr: 저녁이 되자, 경비병들이 그를 끔찍한 미궁 속으로 끌고 가기 위해 찾아왔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And he went down into that doleful gulf, through winding paths among the rocks, under caverns, and arches, and galleries, and over heaps of fallen stone.  And he turned on the left hand, and on the right hand, and went up and down, till his head was dizzy; but all the while he held his clue. For when he went in he had fastened it to a stone, and left it to unroll out of his hand as he went on; and it lasted him till he met the Minotaur, in a narrow chasm between black cliffs.

translation.en: He descended into the dark, sorrowful pit, following winding paths through the rocks.
translation.kr: 그는 바위 사이의 구불구불한 길을 따라 어둡고 슬픈 구덩이로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He passed through deep caverns, stone arches, and piles of broken rubble.
translation.kr: 그는 깊은 동굴과 돌로 된 아치, 그리고 무너진 잔해 더미를 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: He turned left and right, climbing up and down until he felt dizzy.
translation.kr: 그는 어지러움을 느낄 때까지 좌우로 돌고 위아래로 오르내렸습니다.

translation.en: But throughout the maze, he kept a tight grip on the thread.
translation.kr: 하지만 미궁 속에서도 그는 실뭉치를 단단히 쥐고 있었습니다.

translation.en: He had tied the end to a heavy stone at the entrance.
translation.kr: 그는 입구에 있는 무거운 돌에 실의 끝을 묶어 두었습니다.

translation.en: He let the string unroll slowly as he ventured deeper into the darkness.
translation.kr: 그는 어둠 속으로 더 깊이 들어갈수록 실이 천천히 풀리도록 내버려 두었습니다.

translation.en: The thread lasted until he finally cornered the Minotaur in a narrow black chasm.
translation.kr: 그 실은 마침내 비좁고 검은 협곡에서 미노타우로스를 몰아넣을 때까지 이어졌습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And when he saw him he stopped awhile, for he had never seen so strange a beast.  His body was a man’s: but his head was the head of a bull; and his teeth were the teeth of a lion, and with them he tore his prey.  And when he saw Theseus he roared, and put his head down, and rushed right at him.

translation.en: When Theseus spotted the creature, he paused in pure shock.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 괴물을 발견하고 순수한 충격에 잠시 멈춰 섰습니다.

translation.en: He had never seen such a terrifying and unnatural beast.
translation.kr: 그는 그렇게 기괴하고 끔찍한 짐승을 본 적이 없었습니다.

translation.en: It possessed the muscular body of a man but the massive head of a bull.
translation.kr: 그것은 인간의 근육질 몸을 가졌지만 거대한 황소의 머리를 하고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Its mouth was filled with sharp lion's teeth designed for tearing flesh.
translation.kr: 그 입에는 살점을 찢기 위한 날카로운 사자의 이빨이 가득했습니다.

translation.en: Seeing the hero, the monster roared deafeningly and charged straight at him.
translation.kr: 영웅을 발견한 괴물은 귀청이 터질 듯 포효하며 그를 향해 곧장 돌진했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: But Theseus stept aside nimbly, and as he passed by, cut him in the knee; and ere he could turn in the narrow path, he followed him, and stabbed him again and again from behind, till the monster fled bellowing wildly; for he never before had felt a wound.  And Theseus followed him at full speed, holding the clue of thread in his left hand.

translation.en: Theseus nimbly dodged the attack and slashed the beast's knee as it passed.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 민첩하게 공격을 피하며 괴물이 지나갈 때 무릎을 베었습니다.

translation.en: Before the monster could turn in the tight space, Theseus struck again.
translation.kr: 괴물이 좁은 공간에서 몸을 돌리기도 전에 테세우스는 다시 공격했습니다.

translation.en: He stabbed the creature from behind repeatedly.
translation.kr: 그는 뒤에서 그 짐승을 쉴 새 없이 찔렀습니다.

translation.en: Experiencing pain for the first time, the monster shrieked and fled wildly.
translation.kr: 처음으로 고통을 느낀 괴물은 비명을 지르며 미친 듯이 도망쳤습니다.

translation.en: Keeping the thread in his left hand, Theseus sprinted after his prey.
translation.kr: 왼손에 실뭉치를 쥔 채로 테세우스는 사냥감을 뒤쫓아 질주했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: Then on, through cavern after cavern, under dark ribs of sounding stone, and up rough glens and torrent-beds, among the sunless roots of Ida, and to the edge of the eternal snow, went they, the hunter and the hunted, while the hills bellowed to the monster’s bellow.

translation.en: The deadly chase continued through endless dark caverns and echoing stone corridors.
translation.kr: 치명적인 추격전은 끝없는 어둠의 동굴과 메아리치는 돌 복도를 지나 계속되었습니다.

translation.en: They raced over rough terrain and dried riverbeds deep under Mount Ida.
translation.kr: 그들은 이다 산 깊은 곳의 거친 지형과 마른 강바닥을 내달렸습니다.

translation.en: The hunter and the hunted climbed to the very edge of the eternal snow.
translation.kr: 사냥꾼과 사냥감은 만년설이 덮인 끝자락까지 기어올랐습니다.

translation.en: The entire mountain shook with the terrified bellows of the wounded beast.
translation.kr: 상처 입은 괴물의 겁에 질린 울부짖음에 온 산이 뒤흔들렸습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: [Picture: Theseus and Minotaur]

translation.en: [Illustration: Theseus fighting the Minotaur]
translation.kr: [삽화: 미노타우로스와 싸우는 테세우스]

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And at last Theseus came up with him, where he lay panting on a slab among the snow, and caught him by the horns, and forced his head back, and drove the keen sword through his throat.

translation.en: Theseus finally caught the beast panting exhaustedly on a snowy stone slab.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 마침내 눈 덮인 돌판 위에서 지쳐 헐떡이는 괴물을 따라잡았습니다.

translation.en: He grabbed the monster's sharp horns and violently bent its head backward.
translation.kr: 그는 괴물의 날카로운 뿔을 움켜쥐고 그 머리를 뒤로 거칠게 꺾었습니다.

translation.en: With one final strike, he drove his keen sword straight through its throat.
translation.kr: 마지막 일격으로 그는 예리한 검을 괴물의 목구멍 깊숙이 찔러 넣었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: Then he turned, and went back limping and weary, feeling his way down by the clue of thread, till he came to the mouth of that doleful place and saw waiting for him, whom but Ariadne!

translation.en: Limping and exhausted, Theseus turned around to begin the long journey back.
translation.kr: 다리를 절며 기진맥진한 테세우스는 기나긴 귀환을 위해 발길을 돌렸습니다.

translation.en: He carefully followed his winding thread all the way to the maze's entrance.
translation.kr: 그는 미궁의 입구까지 구불구불한 실을 조심스럽게 따라갔습니다.

translation.en: When he finally stepped out, he saw Ariadne eagerly waiting for him.
translation.kr: 마침내 밖으로 나왔을 때, 그는 자신을 애타게 기다리고 있는 아리아드네를 보았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: And he whispered ‘It is done!’ and showed her the sword; and she laid her finger on her lips, and led him to the prison, and opened the doors, and set all the prisoners free, while the guards lay sleeping heavily; for she had silenced them with wine.

translation.en: He whispered that the deed was done and showed her the bloody sword.
translation.kr: 그는 임무를 완수했다고 속삭이며 피 묻은 검을 그녀에게 보여주었습니다.

translation.en: She placed a finger to her lips for silence and hurried to the prison.
translation.kr: 그녀는 조용히 하라는 뜻으로 입술에 손가락을 대고 감옥으로 서둘러 갔습니다.

translation.en: She had knocked out the guards with drugged wine.
translation.kr: 그녀는 수면제를 탄 포도주로 경비병들을 기절시켜 둔 상태였습니다.

translation.en: Ariadne swiftly opened the heavy doors and set all the prisoners free.
translation.kr: 아리아드네는 재빨리 무거운 문을 열고 모든 죄수들을 풀어주었습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part III: How Theseus Slew the Minotaur
paragraphs.raw: Then they fled to their ship together, and leapt on board, and hoisted up the sail; and the night lay dark around them, so that they passed through Minos’ ships, and escaped all safe to Naxos; and there Ariadne became Theseus’ wife.

translation.en: Together, they sprinted to their waiting ship and hoisted the sails.
translation.kr: 그들은 함께 기다리고 있던 배로 달려가 돛을 올렸습니다.

translation.en: The thick darkness of the night hid them from King Minos's fleet.
translation.kr: 짙은 어둠 덕분에 그들은 미노스 왕의 함대를 피할 수 있었습니다.

translation.en: They escaped completely safely to the distant island of Naxos.
translation.kr: 그들은 멀리 떨어진 낙소스 섬으로 완벽하게 무사히 탈출했습니다.

translation.en: There, the brave hero Theseus finally married the beautiful Ariadne.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 용감한 영웅 테세우스는 마침내 아름다운 아리아드네와 혼인했습니다.

chapters.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: PART IV HOW THESEUS FELL BY HIS PRIDE

translation.en: Part 4: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
translation.kr: [4부: 오만함으로 몰락한 테세우스]

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: But that fair Ariadne never came to Athens with her husband.  Some say that Theseus left her sleeping on Naxos among the Cyclades; and that Dionusos the wine-king found her, and took her up into the sky, as you shall see some day in a painting of old Titian’s—one of the most glorious pictures upon earth.  And some say that Dionusos drove away Theseus, and took Ariadne from him by force: but however that may be, in his haste or in his grief, Theseus forgot to put up the white sail.  Now Ægeus his father sat and watched on Sunium day after day, and strained his old eyes across the sea to see the ship afar.  And when he saw the black sail, and not the white one, he gave up Theseus for dead, and in his grief he fell into the sea, and died; so it is called the Ægean to this day.

translation.en: But beautiful Ariadne never reached Athens with her husband.
translation.kr: 하지만 아름다운 아리아드네는 남편과 함께 아테네에 도착하지 못했습니다.

translation.en: Some say Theseus abandoned her while she slept on the island of Naxos.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 테세우스가 낙소스섬에서 잠든 그녀를 버려두고 떠났다고 말합니다.

translation.en: Then Dionysus, the god of wine, found her and carried her up to the sky.
translation.kr: 그 후 포도주의 신 디오니소스가 그녀를 발견하여 하늘로 데려갔다는 것입니다.

translation.en: You might see this someday in a famous, glorious painting by Titian.
translation.kr: 언젠가 티치아노가 그린 세상에서 가장 찬란한 명화에서 그 모습을 보실 수 있을 것입니다.

translation.en: Others claim Dionysus drove Theseus away and took Ariadne by force.
translation.kr: 다른 이들은 디오니소스가 테세우스를 쫓아내고 아리아드네를 강제로 빼앗았다고도 합니다.

translation.en: Whatever the truth, in his rush or sorrow, Theseus forgot to hoist the white sail.
translation.kr: 진실이 무엇이든, 테세우스는 서두르거나 슬퍼하느라 하얀 돛을 올리는 것을 잊어버렸습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, his father Aegeus sat waiting on the cliffs of Sunium every day.
translation.kr: 한편 그의 아버지 아이게우스는 매일 수니온 절벽에 앉아 기다렸습니다.

translation.en: He strained his old eyes across the sea to spot the ship from afar.
translation.kr: 그는 늙은 눈을 부릅뜨고 바다 너머 멀리서 배가 오는지 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: When he saw the black sail instead of the white one, he believed his son was dead.
translation.kr: 그가 하얀 돛 대신 검은 돛을 보았을 때, 그는 아들이 죽었다고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: In his overwhelming grief, he threw himself into the sea and died.
translation.kr: 걷잡을 수 없는 슬픔에 빠진 그는 바다에 몸을 던져 목숨을 잃고 말았습니다.

translation.en: That is why those waters are called the Aegean Sea to this day.
translation.kr: 그 바다가 오늘날까지도 아이게우스의 이름을 따서 에게해라고 불리는 이유입니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: And now Theseus was king of Athens, and he guarded it and ruled it well.

translation.en: Theseus was now the king of Athens, and he protected and ruled it well.
translation.kr: 이제 테세우스는 아테네의 왕이 되어 나라를 훌륭하게 다스리고 보호했습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: For he killed the bull of Marathon, which had killed Androgeos, Minos’ son; and he drove back the famous Amazons, the warlike women of the East, when they came from Asia, and conquered all Hellas, and broke into Athens itself.  But Theseus stopped them there, and conquered them, and took Hippolute their queen to be his wife.  Then he went out to fight against the Lapithai, and Peirithoos their famous king: but when the two heroes came face to face they loved each other, and embraced, and became noble friends; so that the friendship of Theseus and Peirithoos is a proverb even now.  And he gathered (so the Athenians say) all the boroughs of the land together, and knit them into one strong people, while before they were all parted and weak: and many another wise thing he did, so that his people honoured him after he was dead, for many a hundred years, as the father of their freedom and their laws.  And six hundred years after his death, in the famous fight at Marathon, men said that they saw the ghost of Theseus, with his mighty brazen club, fighting in the van of battle against the invading Persians, for the country which he loved.  And twenty years after Marathon his bones (they say) were found in Scuros, an isle beyond the sea; and they were bigger than the bones of mortal man. So the Athenians brought them home in triumph; and all the people came out to welcome them; and they built over them a noble temple, and adorned it with sculptures and paintings in which we are told all the noble deeds of Theseus, and the Centaurs, and the Lapithai, and the Amazons; and the ruins of it are standing still.

translation.en: He killed the fierce bull of Marathon that had slain King Minos's son.
translation.kr: 그는 미노스 왕의 아들을 죽였던 마라톤의 사나운 황소를 물리쳤습니다.

translation.en: He also drove back the famous Amazons, the fierce warrior women of the East.
translation.kr: 또한 동방의 용맹한 여전사들인 유명한 아마존 군대도 격퇴했습니다.

translation.en: They had marched from Asia, conquered Greece, and broken right into Athens.
translation.kr: 그들은 아시아에서 진군하여 그리스를 정복하고 아테네까지 쳐들어왔습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus stopped them, defeated their army, and married their queen, Hippolyta.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그들을 막아내어 물리쳤고, 여왕 히폴리테를 아내로 맞이했습니다.

translation.en: Later, he went to fight the Lapiths and their famous king, Pirithous.
translation.kr: 훗날 그는 라피타이족과 그들의 유명한 왕 피리토오스와 싸우러 나갔습니다.

translation.en: But when the two heroes met face to face, they felt an instant bond.
translation.kr: 하지만 두 영웅이 얼굴을 마주하자 그들은 즉시 깊은 유대감을 느꼈습니다.

translation.en: They embraced and became such great friends that their loyalty is still a proverb today.
translation.kr: 그들은 서로를 껴안고 훌륭한 친구가 되었으며, 그 우정은 오늘날까지도 전설로 남아있습니다.

translation.en: Athenians say Theseus united all the scattered towns into one strong nation.
translation.kr: 아테네 사람들은 테세우스가 흩어진 마을들을 하나로 모아 강한 국가를 만들었다고 말합니다.

translation.en: Before this, they had been divided and weak.
translation.kr: 그 이전에는 모두 분열되어 힘이 없었습니다.

translation.en: He did many other wise things, and his people honored him for centuries after his death.
translation.kr: 그는 수많은 지혜로운 업적을 남겼고, 백성들은 그가 죽은 뒤에도 수백 년 동안 그를 존경했습니다.

translation.en: They remembered him as the father of their freedom and their laws.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그를 자유와 법의 아버지로 기억했습니다.

translation.en: Six hundred years later, at the famous Battle of Marathon, soldiers claimed to see his ghost.
translation.kr: 육백 년 후 벌어진 유명한 마라톤 전투에서 병사들은 그의 유령을 보았다고 주장했습니다.

translation.en: They saw him wielding his mighty bronze club, fighting invading Persians for his beloved country.
translation.kr: 그가 굳센 청동 몽둥이를 휘두르며 사랑하는 조국을 위해 페르시아 침략군에 맞서 싸웠다는 것입니다.

translation.en: Twenty years after that battle, his massive bones were supposedly found on the island of Scyros.
translation.kr: 그 전투로부터 이십 년 후, 바다 너머 스키로스섬에서 그의 거대한 뼈가 발견되었다고 합니다.

translation.en: They were far larger than the bones of any normal mortal man.
translation.kr: 그 뼈는 평범한 인간의 뼈보다 훨씬 더 컸습니다.

translation.en: The Athenians brought his remains home in triumph, and the whole city welcomed them.
translation.kr: 아테네 사람들은 승리에 차서 그의 유해를 고향으로 모셔왔고, 모든 시민이 나와 환영했습니다.

translation.en: They built a grand temple over his tomb, decorated with magnificent sculptures and paintings.
translation.kr: 그들은 무덤 위에 웅장한 신전을 짓고 화려한 조각과 그림으로 장식했습니다.

translation.en: These artworks depicted his brave battles against monsters, centaurs, and the Amazons.
translation.kr: 이 예술품들은 괴물과 켄타우로스, 그리고 아마존에 맞서 싸운 그의 용감한 행적을 담고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The ruins of that glorious temple are still standing today.
translation.kr: 그 찬란했던 신전의 폐허는 지금도 굳건히 서 있습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: But why did they find his bones in Scuros?  Why did he not die in peace at Athens, and sleep by his father’s side?  Because after his triumph he grew proud, and broke the laws of God and man.  And one thing worst of all he did, which brought him to his grave with sorrow.  For he went down (they say beneath the earth) with that bold Peirithoos his friend to help him to carry off Persephone, the queen of the world below.  But Peirithoos was killed miserably, in the dark fire-kingdoms under ground; and Theseus was chained to a rock in everlasting pain.  And there he sat for years, till Heracles the mighty came down to bring up the three-headed dog who sits at Pluto’s gate.  So Heracles loosed him from his chain, and brought him up to the light once more.

translation.en: But why were his bones found on the island of Scyros?
translation.kr: 그런데 왜 그의 뼈가 스키로스섬에서 발견되었을까요?

translation.en: Why didn't he die peacefully in Athens and rest beside his father?
translation.kr: 왜 그는 아테네에서 평화롭게 죽어 아버지 곁에 잠들지 못했을까요?

translation.en: It was because his victories made him arrogant, and he broke both human and divine laws.
translation.kr: 승리에 취해 오만해진 그가 신과 인간의 법을 모두 어겼기 때문입니다.

translation.en: He committed one terrible final act that brought him to a sorrowful end.
translation.kr: 그는 결국 자신을 비참한 죽음으로 몰고 간 끔찍한 잘못을 저질렀습니다.

translation.en: He went down into the Underworld with his bold friend Pirithous.
translation.kr: 그는 대담한 친구 피리토오스와 함께 지하 세계로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He wanted to help his friend kidnap Persephone, the queen of the dead.
translation.kr: 죽은 자들의 여왕 페르세포네를 납치하려는 친구를 돕기 위해서였습니다.

translation.en: But Pirithous met a miserable death in those dark, fiery underground realms.
translation.kr: 하지만 피리토오스는 그 어둡고 뜨거운 지하 왕국에서 비참하게 목숨을 잃었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus was chained to a rock, cursed to suffer in everlasting pain.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 바위에 사슬로 묶여 영원한 고통을 겪는 저주를 받았습니다.

translation.en: He sat there for years until the mighty Hercules came down to the Underworld.
translation.kr: 그는 강력한 헤라클레스가 지하 세계로 내려올 때까지 몇 년 동안이나 그곳에 묶여 있었습니다.

translation.en: Hercules was there to capture the three-headed dog that guarded the gates of the dead.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 죽음의 문을 지키는 머리 셋 달린 개를 잡으러 그곳에 왔습니다.

translation.en: He took pity on Theseus, shattered his magical chains, and brought him back to the sunlight.
translation.kr: 그는 테세우스를 가엾게 여겨 마법 사슬을 부수고 그를 다시 햇빛 속으로 데려왔습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: But when he came back his people had forgotten him, and Castor and Polydeuces, the sons of the wondrous Swan, had invaded his land, and carried off his mother Aithra for a slave, in revenge for a grievous wrong.

translation.en: But when Theseus returned, his people had already forgotten him.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스가 돌아왔을 때, 백성들은 이미 그를 잊고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The fierce twin brothers, Castor and Pollux, had invaded his kingdom.
translation.kr: 사나운 쌍둥이 형제인 카스토르와 폴룩스가 그의 왕국을 침략했던 것입니다.

translation.en: They kidnapped his mother Aethra and made her a slave to avenge a terrible wrong.
translation.kr: 그들은 끔찍한 악행에 복수하기 위해 그의 어머니 아이트라를 납치하여 노예로 삼았습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: [Picture: Warriors fighting]

translation.en: [Picture: Warriors fighting]
translation.kr: [그림: 전투 중인 전사들]

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: So the fair land of Athens was wasted, and another king ruled it, who drove out Theseus shamefully, and he fled across the sea to Scuros.  And there he lived in sadness, in the house of Lucomedes the king, till Lucomedes killed him by treachery, and there was an end of all his labours.

translation.en: The beautiful land of Athens was ruined, and a new king ruled in his place.
translation.kr: 아름다운 아테네 땅은 폐허가 되었고, 새로운 왕이 그의 자리를 대신하여 다스렸습니다.

translation.en: This new king chased Theseus away in disgrace, forcing him to flee across the sea to Scyros.
translation.kr: 이 새로운 왕은 테세우스를 불명예스럽게 쫓아냈고, 그는 바다 건너 스키로스섬으로 도망쳐야 했습니다.

translation.en: He lived there in deep sadness at the court of King Lycomedes.
translation.kr: 그는 리코메데스 왕의 궁전에서 깊은 슬픔에 빠져 살았습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, Lycomedes murdered him through cruel treachery, putting an end to all his heroic labors.
translation.kr: 결국 리코메데스 왕이 잔인한 배신으로 그를 살해하면서 그의 모든 영웅적인 업적도 끝이 났습니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: So it is still, my children, and so it will be to the end.  In those old Greeks, and in us also, all strength and virtue come from God.  But if men grow proud and self-willed, and misuse God’s fair gifts, He lets them go their own ways, and fall pitifully, that the glory may be His alone. God help us all, and give us wisdom, and courage to do noble deeds! but God keep pride from us when we have done them, lest we fall, and come to shame!

translation.en: And so it remains today, my children, and so it will be until the end of time.
translation.kr: 아이들아, 이것은 오늘날에도 마찬가지이며 세상 끝날까지 변하지 않을 진리입니다.

translation.en: For the ancient Greeks, just as for us, all strength and goodness come from above.
translation.kr: 고대 그리스인들에게나 우리에게나 모든 힘과 선함은 하늘에서 옵니다.

translation.en: But if people grow arrogant and selfish, misusing their wonderful gifts, they are left to their own paths.
translation.kr: 하지만 사람들이 오만하고 이기적으로 변하여 훌륭한 재능을 남용한다면, 결국 자신의 길을 잃게 됩니다.

translation.en: They will fall pitifully, proving that true glory does not belong to mortals.
translation.kr: 그들은 비참하게 몰락하여 진정한 영광이 인간의 것이 아님을 증명하게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: May we all find the wisdom and courage to perform noble deeds!
translation.kr: 우리 모두가 숭고한 일을 해낼 수 있는 지혜와 용기를 얻기를 바랍니다!

translation.en: But may we also be saved from toxic pride, so we do not fall into ruin and bitter shame.
translation.kr: 하지만 우리가 파멸과 쓰디쓴 수치심에 빠지지 않도록 끔찍한 오만함으로부터 구원받기를 기도합니다.

paragraphs.part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
paragraphs.raw: THE END

translation.en: THE END
